title: Reid's midseason NFL mock draft: 32 prospect landing spots, four QBs and one big trade
summary: Which team could land Drew Mestemaker? Who needs Chris Cole, Ashton Hampton or Jamari Johnson? Jordan Reid projected first-round picks for 2027 -- and a trade.
full_text:
Now that the NFL trade deadline has passed and we're in the second half of the 2026 season , it's a great time to look ahead to the 2027 NFL draft .
Some teams whose playoff hopes are mostly dashed are already fully into the process of evaluating prospects for the draft, which will take place in April in Washington. So why not take our own look at how that draft might turn out?
This latest mock draft factors in a combination of what NFL teams need, my evaluation of production and tape from the 2026 college football season , and conversations I've had with trusted scouts and evaluators. Of course, things will change between now and April -- players will move up and down the board or exit the class entirely by returning to school -- but this is how I see things currently.
The draft order obviously is far from set, so I based this 1-32 on what the order would look like if the season ended today. There have already been six trades in Round 1, and I actually pitched a seventh that could make sense.
How many quarterbacks will make Round 1? Here are my full projections for all 32 first-round picks.
Note: Underclassmen are marked with an asterisk.
Jeremiah Smith , WR, Ohio State*
Smith is the best player in this draft, and as the first wide receiver to go No. 1 since 1996 (Keyshawn Johnson), he would allow the Titans to continue to build around quarterback Cam Ward , the No. 1 pick of the 2025 draft. How special is Smith? He has drawn comparisons to some of the best wideouts of the past quarter century -- including Calvin Johnson, Larry Fitzgerald and Julio Jones -- by NFL scouts.
Smith's 131.7 receiving yards per game ranks second in the FBS, and he continues to thrive despite Ohio State's quarterback issues . Speaking of the Buckeyes, the Titans could reunite Smith with fellow wide receiver Carnell Tate , Tennessee's first pick in 2026. Smith's rare combination of size (6-foot-4 and 225 pounds), speed and power gives him early All-Pro potential and makes him the type of player Ward and the Titans need to further improve their offense.
The Jets have three first-round picks, so I have them sending Nos. 4 and 13, along with a 2028 third-rounder, to the Chargers for the No. 2 selection. New York originally acquired the No. 13 pick in a trade with the Cowboys for defensive tackle Quinnen Williams .
Could this move finally allow the Jets to select their quarterback of the future?
Drew Mestemaker , QB, Oklahoma State*
Mestemaker has progressed from a walk-on who didn't start in high school to my top QB in this class. The Jets have used the past three drafts to establish an offensive base, selecting bookend tackles ( Olu Fashanu and Armand Membou ), wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. and tight end Kenyon Sadiq in Round 1. Along with star wideout Garrett Wilson , they make New York an ideal landing spot for a rookie signal-caller.
Mestemaker excels at pushing the ball down the field, with his 21 completions of 20 or more yards this season ranking eighth in the FBS. His decision-making is inconsistent at times, but Mestemaker is young (he's in his first season as a Power 4 starter) and has the tools to transform the Jets.
Colin Simmons , Edge, Texas*
After drafting 13 players last year, the Dolphins have a foundation of young talent on their roster. Now, Miami needs a star, which Simmons could be on defense. He is arguably the top pass rusher in this class and one of the best in the FBS at generating pressure off the edge. His 10.5 sacks are third most in the country despite him missing two games because of injury . His 20.5% pressure rate ranks fifth in the FBS, and Simmons' powerful hands let him set a violent edge in run defense.
Pairing Simmons with 2024 first-rounder Chop Robinson would give the Dolphins an explosive pass-rush duo for defensive-minded coach Jeff Hafley.
Charlie Becker , WR, Indiana*
The Chargers have been extremely disappointing this season, and their 1-8 start has exposed the need for more talent everywhere. That and the fact that they already have a QB in Justin Herbert are why I had them trade out of No. 2 and add another pick. And we'll use this first pick to get Herbert some help.
Becker is an excellent vertical threat who has 10 touchdowns this season (sixth in the FBS) and can also execute the short to intermediate levels of the route tree. He is tall (6-foot-4) and sure-handed (zero drops on 85 targets this season) with excellent body control and elite hand-eye coordination, allowing him to win in the air on long and contested catch opportunities. Becker would immediately become Herbert's WR1.
Dylan Stewart , Edge, South Carolina*
This season has been a disaster for Philadelphia, but it allows the Eagles to get an elite edge-rushing talent. Stewart is a toolsy and explosive player who has the unique ability to bend around the corner and wreak havoc in the backfield. The 6-foot-5, 250-pounder hasn't had consistent production in college, but his tools and flashes of potential are tantalizing and reminiscent of Brian Burns coming out of Florida State . Stewart will have to answer questions during the predraft process about his production and an in-season suspension , but he's an ideal talent for the Eagles to draft and develop behind Jonathan Greenard , Nolan Smith Jr. and Jalyx Hunt .
Leonard Moore , CB, Notre Dame*
Now that the Jets have traded up to take their quarterback of the future, they could select my No. 1 defensive prospect in this year's class here. Moore's 8.6% target rate is the lowest among all FBS corners this season, and he has allowed only seven completions in eight games. Moore is one of the most consistent cover guys in the country and has the length (6-foot-2, 197 pounds) and ball skills to be a shutdown corner in the NFL. He could start right away at outside corner for New York.
The Cardinals desperately need to add help in the trenches, and Seaton is an upper-tier athlete who is very polished in pass protection. He has allowed only one sack and four pressures this season on 344 pass-blocking snaps. He is more than capable of mirroring and matching edge rushers, though he needs to get stronger and improve his anchor and drive strength. But Seaton would be a plug-and-play starting option at either tackle spot opposite Paris Johnson Jr. , who will be on his fifth-year option in 2027.
With Michael Penix Jr. struggling to find consistency in Year 3, the Falcons could once again be convinced to use the No. 8 pick on a QB -- like they did three years ago with Penix , especially since the Falcons' front office and coach have changed since making that selection. Atlanta has plenty of skill-position talent (RB Bijan Robinson , WR Drake London , TE Kyle Pitts Sr. ) that could enable a young QB to thrive immediately.
Carr is an instinctive passer who consistently has answers and has already been given considerable autonomy in Notre Dame's offense. He doesn't have the high-end traits of some passers in the class (picture a more mobile Kirk Cousins ), but he is polished in many of the skills that are essential to playing the position.
Zereoue Williams , OT, Utah
"I could see him making a rise similar to Kolton Miller " is a text that a scout sent me after watching Williams earlier this season. Miller was drafted No. 15 in 2018 by the Raiders, and Williams could be taken even higher. He is already 24 years old, which is part of why he is receiving some second-round grades from scouts right now. But I'm confident in Williams' tools and ceiling ultimately leading to a big rise; I see a first-round player.
Houston has been trying to fix its offensive line in front of C.J. Stroud for years, and taking Williams at tackle would be a logical follow-up to their selection of guard Keylan Rutledge in the 2026 first round. Williams is one of the best blockers in this class and has upside for more development. He could be the third Utah tackle selected in the first round in the past two drafts.

title: Which team will land the No. 1 draft pick? Our look at a five-franchise race
summary: Five teams have at least 5% odds to land the No. 1 pick in 2027, per ESPN's Football Power Index.
full_text:
The race for the No. 1 pick in the 2027 NFL draft is taking shape now that we're 10 weeks into the 2026 season .
Five teams have at least a 5% chance at landing the top pick, according to ESPN's Football Power Index projections. So we called on our experts and reporters to size up each of those bottom-tier franchises at midseason.
NFL analyst Seth Walder used the FPI to make sense of each of the five teams' schedules the rest of the way. Our NFL Nation reporters looked at the biggest positional needs that could be addressed in the first round in April. And NFL draft analyst Jordan Reid spun it forward and suggested one prospect each front office could consider if it landed that top selection.
Let's start with the Dolphins, who currently have the best odds at the No. 1 pick.
Jump to a team: LAC | MIA | NYJ PHI | TEN
FPI chance to earn No. 1 pick: 41.2% FPI chance to earn top-five pick: 93%
What lies ahead in the schedule? Are they favored in any remaining games?
Not only are the Dolphins not favored by the FPI in a single remaining game this season, but the model also makes them at least a field-goal underdog in every game. Their best chances to win are versus the Jets in Week 12 , versus the Chargers in Week 16 and at the Patriots in Week 18 . But because the FPI believes the Dolphins are the worst team in the NFL, they are not likely to win any of those contests. -- Walder
What is their biggest first-round need right now?
The Dolphins have needs across the board, but if we're narrowing down positions that make sense at their projected draft slot, it's edge rusher, quarterback and wide receiver. Chop Robinson has been excellent this season and could use a pass-rush partner to mix in with Josh Uche . However, pairing wide receiver Caleb Douglas in his second year with another receiver or a rookie quarterback is also tempting. -- Marcel Louis-Jacques
Who is the best prospect fit right now for them at No. 1?
Drew Mestemaker , QB, Oklahoma State. Free agent signee Malik Willis hasn't shown any signs of being the long-term answer moving forward, and Miami could use him as a bridge option. Mestemaker is a young and intriguing passer who won't be ready to start from Day 1; 2026 is only his second season as a starter in high school and college combined. Miami already has a productive foundation of youth, but Mestemaker could provide it the QB necessary to continue its rebuild. -- Reid
FPI chance to earn No. 1 pick: 36.9% FPI chance to earn top-five pick: 92.4%
What lies ahead in the schedule? Are they favored in any remaining games?
There are definitely some winnable games available for the Titans: Week 13 versus the Commanders , Week 15 versus the Colts and Week 16 at the Raiders . The FPI favors the Titans only against the Raiders in Week 16 (the model has fairly low confidence in rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza until proven otherwise), but there is a strong chance Tennessee wins at least one of those three games. Still, Tennessee has the second-best chance to earn the No. 1 pick. -- Walder
What is their biggest first-round need right now?
Pass rusher. Sure, Jacob Martin has gotten off to a great start with a career-high 7.5 sacks so far, but there's no guarantee he'll repeat that success next year, and his deal expires after 2027. Getting a running mate opposite Martin would improve the whole defense and give Tennessee an edge rusher to build its defense around in the future. A game-changing pass rusher would also allow coach Robert Saleh to rush with four and drop seven into coverage, which would help a struggling pass defense. -- Turron Davenport
Who is the best prospect fit right now for them at No. 1?
Jeremiah Smith , WR, Ohio State. Even though the Titans have a huge need at edge -- where South Carolina's Dylan Stewart and Texas' Colin Simmons are my top prospects -- it shouldn't be at the expense of taking Smith, the best player in this class. Smith and Titans WR Carnell Tate are very familiar with each other, combining for 2,118 receiving yards and 21 touchdowns at Ohio State in 2025. Quarterback Cam Ward , who still hasn't solidified whether he's the long-term solution under center, has a risk-taking nature that would pair well with Smith's ability to be a three-level threat. -- Reid
FPI chance to earn No. 1 pick: 7.9% FPI chance to earn top-five pick: 68.7%
What lies ahead in the schedule? Are they favored in any remaining games?
Two games stand out as possible victories: Week 13 at the Cardinals and Week 14 versus the Colts . The FPI considers the Eagles as slight underdogs in both of them. I'll throw out one other game to keep an eye on: Week 18 at the Giants . That's because the FPI is pretty bearish on New York, so it thinks the Eagles have a chance, and the Giants could sit their starters if they have the NFC East wrapped up at that point. -- Walder
What is their biggest first-round need right now?
Offensive tackle. The retirement of future Hall of Fame right tackle Lane Johnson created a major need along the offensive front. Rookie Markel Bell , the team's 2026 third-round pick, had a strong summer and took over when Johnson stepped away in early October, but Bell has yet to solidify himself as the right tackle of the future. The Eagles' long run of success is tied directly to their strength along the fronts. They need to invest early and often in the O-line. -- Tim McManus
Who is the best prospect fit right now for them at No. 1? Jeremiah Smith. Right now, there isn't an offensive tackle worthy of a top-five pick. LSU's Jordan Seaton tops my position rankings right now at No. 11. That puts the Eagles in position to take the best player available, which is Smith in this scenario. He would add another outstanding option to an offense that includes RB Saquon Barkley , WR DeVonta Smith and 2026 first-round pick Makai Lemon . At 6-foot-4 and 220 pounds, Smith can glide past defenders or outmuscle them at the catch point. -- Reid
FPI chance to earn No. 1 pick: 5.9% FPI chance to earn top-five pick: 63.1%
What lies ahead in the schedule? Are they favored in any remaining games?
The FPI favors the Jets to beat the Dolphins -- a high-leverage game for AFC East draft capital -- in Week 12 . But the Jets could also win next week at the Chargers , in Week 15 at the Cardinals and in Week 16 against the Patriots (the FPI is assuming Tommy DeVito as the most likely quarterback in that game). Plus, if the Bills have the AFC's No. 1 seed locked up by Week 18 , it's possible the Jets' season finale in Buffalo could sneakily become a feasible win, too. -- Walder
What is their biggest first-round need right now?
Priority No. 1 is a franchise quarterback. This is their moment. This is why they traded defensive stars Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams in 2025. The objective was to accumulate draft capital for 2027, and now they have the means (three first-round picks) to wheel and deal. After four years of Aaron Rodgers , Justin Fields and Geno Smith -- all stopgaps, to varying degrees -- the Jets want to build around a young quarterback who can grow with the talent already in place. -- Rich Cimini
Who is the best prospect fit right now for them at No. 1?
Drew Mestemaker. At 6-foot-4 and 220 pounds, he is a strong-armed passer with plenty of mobility. Mestemaker still needs to become more consistent with his decision-making, but his tools and potential are an ideal fit for the Jets given the offensive personnel they already have in place. -- Reid
FPI chance to earn No. 1 pick: 5.5% FPI chance to earn top-five pick: 50.8%
What lies ahead in the schedule? Are they favored in any remaining games?
Believe it or not, the FPI favors the Chargers in four games. That includes their upcoming home game against the Jets , the following week's home game against the DeVito-led Patriots, Week 14 at the Raiders and Week 16 at the Dolphins . That's a huge reason the Chargers are in the fifth spot here. -- Walder

title: CB Humphrey apologizes for 'criminals' quip about Baltimore; mayor responds
summary: Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey apologized Wednesday for the derogatory comment he recently made about Baltimore on his podcast.
full_text:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- Outspoken Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey apologized for the derogatory comment he made about the city of Baltimore on his recent podcast.
On an episode of "The Marlon Humphrey Show" released Wednesday, Humphrey took a swipe at the city when asked what Baltimore was best at making.
After first mentioning "The Star-Spangled Banner" and National Bohemian beer, Humphrey quipped, "They're best at making criminals."
After Wednesday's practice, Humphrey said he regretted those remarks.
"I would like to apologize for some comments on my podcast I had to the city of Baltimore," Humphrey said. "As you guys know, I've been here my whole career. Spent lots of offseasons here. Welcomed a son here and I'm an investor in the city. And obviously, I do know the effect that words have and just like to apologize for those comments."
Humphrey received heavy fan backlash on social media Wednesday afternoon. The podcast episode featuring Humphrey's "criminals" comment has since been deleted from his YouTube page.
Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott acknowledged Humphrey's apology in a statement posted to social media , but noted, "a verbal apology is not enough. Baltimore is a city full of young Black boys who look to the Ravens as a beacon of light in their lives and to have someone that looks like them who wears a Baltimore Ravens jersey relegate them to becoming criminals cuts deeper.
"I wonder how he would feel if prominent Baltimoreans used their platforms to imply that Baltimore once produced great defensive backs but we have recently lost our way."
Scott then added, "They wouldn't do that because our team and city are supposed to be united as one. Baltimore versus the world."
Scott concluded his post by inviting Humphrey to sit down with him and some Baltimore citizens "who have re-entered into our community and are now preventing others from making the mistakes they made."
A post shared by Mayor Brandon M. Scott (@mayorbmscott)
Humphrey, 30, is in his 10th season with Baltimore and is the longest-tenured defensive player on the Ravens. The No. 16 selection in the 2017 draft by Baltimore, Humphrey has been to four Pro Bowls, which are the most by a Ravens cornerback.
In recent years, Humphrey has struggled and has drawn the ire of fans. This season, he has given up an NFL-worst 313 yards in coverage in the fourth quarter.
Asked if he understood why fans would be upset with this comment even if he was joking, Humphrey replied, "Yeah, I just apologized ... and that won't really happen again."
Humphrey is in the final year of a five-year, $97.5 million extension. His $26.276 million salary cap hit is the largest for any cornerback in 2026.
Humphrey's slight at Baltimore comes at a time when the franchise is dealing with one of its worst stretches in its history. The Ravens (4-6) have lost five straight, including a 23-20 loss to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers on Monday. Baltimore has also lost seven of its past eight games at home.
Ravens coach Jesse Minter said he would keep any conversations with Humphrey about this matter private.
"Just speaking for myself, I love this city," Minter said. "I know what this city means to me and my family. I take a lot of pride in being here. It's a great city with a bunch of great people. We desperately want to represent this city the right way by how we play most importantly."
This isn't the first time that Humphrey has caused a stir with his podcast. One month ago, Humphrey said safety Kyle Hamilton "knew" he was going to make a game-sealing interception of Atlanta Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa once he replaced injured starter Michael Penix Jr . in overtime. Hamilton later shot down that characterization, describing Humphrey's account as "pretty hyperbolic."
"I think Marlon is very unapologetically himself," Hamilton said Wednesday. "He can be slightly abrasive at times, but that's just him. And talking to his family has always been like that. But we all love Marlon and we appreciate everything he's done for us [and] will do for us. And he's one of us."
Humphrey has been a target of fan criticism over the past two seasons. He has been frequently booed during home games at M&T Bank Stadium.
During the "Monday Night Football" broadcast two days ago, when the Ravens were losing to the winless Chargers, fans could be heard shouting "F--- Marlon Humphrey" as they exited the stadium.
"I love the city. I think I've expressed this many times," Humphrey said. "I want to win in front of the fans just because it's not cheap to be in those seats."
Has the fans' negativity toward him affected his view of them?
"To answer your question," Humphrey replied, "nothing has changed how I feel."
author: Jamison Hensley

title: Giants RB Skattebo to nix backflips in wake of Hutchinson's injury
summary: Giants RB Cam Skattebo said he is holding off on doing any more backflips after Lions DE Aidan Hutchinson suffered a major knee injury while leaping and celebrating a sack.
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo is retiring his trademark celebratory backflip for the time being.
This comes on the heels of Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson suffering a season-ending knee injury while leaping and celebrating a sack Sunday. Hutchinson was placed on injured reserve.
"It's hard to see," Skattebo told reporters Wednesday. "I'm saying, yeah, [no backflips]. Mentally, I'm like, 'I'm not doing that.'
"That s--- ain't going to happen to me."
Skattebo, the Giants starting running back, is coming off a serious ankle injury last year. But he returned for the start of the season and backflipped after scoring in New York's season-opening win over the Dallas Cowboys . He backflipped as recently as Thursday night in a loss to the Washington Commanders .
Skattebo isn't saying he won't backflip again. The likelihood is he will. He has done it his whole life. But he mentioned after the opener that he might put the celebration on the backburner, before it reemerged in Week 10.
Skattebo conceded Wednesday the backflip might resurface "if we go to the playoffs or something."
The backflip was a point of contention throughout the offseason, even before Hutchinson had his mishap. Skattebo did his flip for the first time since the injury after hitting a home run at the Brian Burns Celebrity Softball Game in late May.
Skattebo then stumbled while doing a backflip at Fanatics Fest over the summer, creating a stir.
Giants brass had a conversation with Skattebo afterward. They preferred he didn't do it leading into the season, especially coming off a major injury. They didn't mandate he never do it again.
"The big-picture message is you want to take care of yourself, take care of your team. Do everything you can do to be healthy, be back, be right, be good," Giants coach John Harbaugh said at the start of training camp. "What does that mean? It's not going to be the same situation the next time for anybody. It's going to be different. So, it's really the principle of it."
Skattebo, 24, leads the Giants with 496 yards rushing and four touchdowns on 116 carries so far this season.
Hutchinson, 26, isn't the first player to be injured while celebrating. Former Arizona Cardinals kicker Bill Gramatica tore his ACL while celebrating a made kick against the Giants in 2001. But the current Hutchinson situation has prompted some debate about whether coaches should talk to players about celebrations, potentially banning anything that could be deemed dangerous.
"No, I don't believe that," Lions coach Dan Campbell said. "I think what happened speaks for itself. We're not talking to 8-year-olds here."
author: Jordan Raanan

title: Pettine to take over defensive playcalling for Cowboys; Parker still DC
summary: Christian Parker will remain as the Cowboys' defensive coordinator, but Mike Pettine will call the defense on game day, coach Brian Schottenhiemer said.
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas -- Despite Christian Parker losing playcalling duties after just 10 games, Dallas Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said he believes in his defensive coordinator's future, but he is concerned about the present with his team 4-6 and fighting for contention in the NFC East.
While Parker will retain his title as defensive coordinator, senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine will call the defense for the rest of the season.
"He's still running meetings. He's still leading walk-throughs. He's still doing all of those things," Schottenheimer said. "The only thing that's different is he's not calling the plays on game day."
The Cowboys have turned to Mike Pettine to take over playcalling for a defense that ranks 30th or worse in several key categories this season.
A day after Parker's defense allowed 584 yards, the most given up in a home game in team history, in the 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers , Schottenheimer and Parker had their first discussions about a change in roles. By mid-morning Tuesday, Schottenheimer had made the decision to make Pettine the defensive playcaller for the rest of the season.
"Watching over the past few weeks, looking back at some things, I think that the different perspective was good for us," Schottenheimer said.
Through 10 games, the Cowboys are last in total yards (393.8), last in run defense (154.1) and last in third-down defense (48.8%).
Pettine last called defenses in 2020 as the Green Bay Packers ' defensive coordinator. He served as the coordinator of the New York Jets , with Schottenheimer on that staff, and the Buffalo Bills . In 2014-15, he was head coach of the Cleveland Browns .
He joined the Cowboys before Week 5.
Schottenheimer informed the players of the move at Wednesday's team meeting.
"I was upfront and honest with them. And again, Christian Parker is a huge part of what we're trying to build here and that he is our defensive coordinator," Schottenheimer said. "He is our leader. He is not changing any of those things, but that I do feel that in the best interest of winning that Pett's calling the game is going to help us get to where we want to get to."
Parker became the youngest defensive coordinator in team history when he was hired in January after a two-season run as the Philadelphia Eagles ' defensive passing game coordinator.
He earned the job after an exhaustive search of nine candidates to replace Matt Eberflus after the Cowboys finished the 2025 season as the 30th-ranked defense and gave up 511 points.
There was praise for the hire considering Parker's history with cornerbacks Patrick Surtain II in Denver and Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean in Philadelphia.
Parker changed the Cowboys to a 3-4 front with principles from Vic Fangio's zone-based scheme Parker learned with the Broncos and Eagles.
The Cowboys made a number of moves on defense, including signing safety Jalen Thompson to the biggest free agent deal in more than a decade (three years, $33 million), trading for linebacker Rashan Gary in the offseason and cornerback Joey Porter Jr . in season, and drafting safety Caleb Downs and linebacker Malachi Lawrence in the first round.
There were promising signs in training camp and in joint practices against the Los Angeles Rams and New Orleans Saints , but the Cowboys have allowed more than 20 points in every game, a streak that has now reached 17 games over the past two seasons.
But it has not translated to regular-season success.
In the past three games, the Cowboys have given up six plays of at least 50 yards, including scoring plays of 74, 70 and 66 yards to the 49ers. The Cowboys have given up an NFL-high nine plays of 50 yards or more.
"I think Christian is an incredibly strong and committed man who wants to get it right," Schottenheimer said. "I love the fact that he and I could have the real conversations and honest conversations and we talked through a number of different things. But at the end of the day, this decision was made because again, I do think it gives us the best chance to win. And CP understands that the decision has been made and he wants to help us beat the Titans."
Schottenheimer said the Cowboys' next two games against less-than-stellar offensive teams in Tennessee and the Eagles had nothing to do with the timing.
It was done with an eye toward saving a season.
"If we don't make the playoffs, it's a failure. The season's a failure," Schottenheimer said. "That's what we play for. We play to win and we play to make the playoffs, and we've got seven games left and again, we need to put together a run of success."
The defensive players who spoke Wednesday supported Parker. Defensive tackle Kenny Clark said he was "bummed" for Parker. Downs said the news "hurt his heart."
Downs and Parker have been joined at the hip in meetings and the practice field since the Cowboys selected Downs in the first round. Downs said Parker remained the same energetic coach he was before the move.
"He's still somebody that we're playing for in the building and somebody that we love," Downs said. "He's still in the building, still in the meetings, still talk to him every day ... still one of the people that we're looking to have around. It's like looking to play for one of our sources of motivation."
Clark was with Pettine in Green Bay.
"Coach Pettine, he's a great coach," Clark said. "We're going to be running, doing the same things that we've been doing. It's not a completely new defense. As players, we've got to still be intentional about what we're doing, prepare the right way. It's no magic playcall or nothing that Pett is going to be able to give us. So it's our job to go out there and execute the game plan, whatever it is."
Said defensive tackle Quinnen Williams , "Everything is on us [as players]. We're on the field. No matter what play gets called, no matter who call it, we've got to execute the play. And that's going to be around the NFL, that's going to be youth football, college football, NFL, man. Once the play gets called, no matter who call it, the players on the field got to execute it. And that's what we haven't been doing. We got to do it going forward."
author: Todd Archer and Kimberley A. Martin

title: Niners' Bosa on 4-game sack drought: 'Don't think I'm playing my best'
summary: Niners star Nick Bosa acknowledged his performance this season, including four straight games with no sacks, hasn't been up to his usual standard.
full_text:
COLORADO SPRINGS, Colo. -- After failing to record a sack in his fourth straight game, San Francisco 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa acknowledged Wednesday that his performance this season has not been up to his usual standard.
In the Niners' 46-40 win against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, Bosa played 34 defensive snaps in which he had a pass rush opportunity. He finished with no sacks, one quarterback hit and four pressures while also being called for three penalties, including two for jumping offside.
It's the first time since Bosa entered the league in 2019 that he hasn't had a sack in four straight games in the same season.
"I think in the past when I was younger, it would eat at me a lot more, just strictly the stat aspects," Bosa said after the Niners completed their first practice of the week at the Air Force Academy in preparation for this week's showdown with the Minnesota Vikings . "But now I'm really just focused on the people around me, and if I feel like I'm playing good football, then I really don't care much about the stats. But I don't think I'm playing my best football right now. So that's what gets to me more so than the actual stats."
Bosa is still working his way back from multiple injuries. He missed all but three games in 2025 because of a torn ACL in his right knee. During training camp this year, Bosa participated in individual drills in the opening days but then missed most of the preseason before playing 70 snaps in the first two games of the season.
But before the Niners played the Arizona Cardinals in Week 3, Bosa strained his calf while warming up during a Thursday walkthrough and missed the ensuing five games. Bosa said that injury was a result of overcompensation from his ACL recovery.
Upon returning, Bosa has attempted to fit into new coordinator Raheem Morris' defensive scheme. The system isn't drastically different from what Bosa and other veteran Niners have played in, but has enough nuance that it takes some time to catch up.
Bosa said Wednesday that he also could have done a better job being proactive about learning those details about Morris' defense.
"I think there's a learning curve and ... a lot of guys haven't had many reps in the scheme so far," Bosa said. "I'm trying to break it down to the basics and just kind of get back. I missed a year and then missed camp. I kind of took for granted some of the things that I did automatically, and I thought I could just kind of coast and continue to do those things automatically and focus on other things. But I need to, especially with a newer defense, really hone in on the things that made me the player that I am."
Asked for an example of something he needs to refocus on, Bosa pointed to doing a better job of setting his feet and getting off the ball at the snap, before stopping short of sharing too much for competitive reasons.
"It takes time," Bosa said. "I'm not going to make excuses because nobody really cares. But I'm going to get better and I'm pretty confident in that physically and how I'm playing."
A healthy and productive Bosa, even if not back to his 2022 Defensive Player of the Year level of play would be a boon for a Niners pass rush that has struggled to generate pressure and sacks of late.
In the past three games, the Niners have just one sack and a pressure rate of 25.8% that is 31st in the league in that span. It hasn't been all bad this season for Bosa, who needs three sacks to pass Charles Haley for second-most in franchise history (66.5).
If Bosa had played enough snaps to qualify, his 25% pass rush win rate would rank eighth in the NFL among edge rushers and 11th among all defenders.
Niners coach Kyle Shanahan said he believes Bosa will continue to get healthier, knock off rust and acclimate to Morris' scheme as the year goes on.
"I see Nick working his way back," Shanahan said. "I think that he has a number of plays that look just like Nick and I think he's had a few plays that doesn't. I think Nick's ready to go and I think he's definitely affecting the quarterback and doing some good things out there. ... I'm not worried about Nick. Nick's going to get better each week and he'll eventually get there."
author: Nick Wagoner

title: Sources: Aiyuk contacted Daniels to mend friendship with Commanders star QB
summary: Brandon Aiyuk and Jayden Daniels have patched up their relationship after a falling out earlier this year, sources told ESPN.
full_text:
Brandon Aiyuk and Jayden Daniels have patched up their relationship after a falling out earlier this year, sources told ESPN.
Aiyuk, who was reinstated last week and is attempting to determine his NFL future, reached out to Daniels about a month ago to reconcile with the Washington Commanders star quarterback, according to sources.
The former college teammates' relationship was strained over the summer when Aiyuk criticized Daniels and his mother, Regina Jackson, as part of a series of social media posts.
But sources told ESPN that after talking things out, Daniels was receptive and understanding of Aiyuk.
The NFL reinstated Aiyuk on Nov. 9 after the wide receiver reported for a physical with the San Francisco 49ers , who received a two-game roster exemption to sort through any remaining business with the seven-year veteran. That exemption expires next Monday after San Francisco's Week 11 game against the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City.
Aiyuk took to social media multiple times over the summer to voice his displeasure with the Niners and attempted to goad them into releasing him while also saying he wouldn't "do business" with the team at all. On multiple occasions, he also implied or openly suggested that he wanted to join the Commanders to play with Daniels, with whom he had formed a friendship in their time together at Arizona State.
That friendship was strained by Aiyuk's subsequent social media posts aimed at Daniels, but the pair have since settled those differences. It is unclear whether the recent conversation will have any bearing over Aiyuk potentially joining Daniels and the Commanders.
Aiyuk, 28, has been on the Niners' reserve/left squad list since December, but he took steps toward reinstatement in recent weeks, hiring agent Drew Rosenhaus and filing the reinstatement paperwork in late October.
Aiyuk has not played since tearing the ACL, MCL and meniscus in his right knee on Oct. 20, 2024. The Niners have until Monday to place Aiyuk on their 53-man roster or release him.
author: Jeremy Fowler

title: Eagles' Sirianni sticking with Milton as QB1, Mannion as offensive playcaller
summary: QB Joe Milton will start again for the Eagles on Sunday and Sean Mannion will remain as the offensive playcaller against the Steelers, coach Nick Sirianni said.
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA -- Eagles quarterback Joe Milton will remain the starter and offensive coordinator Sean Mannion will retain playcalling duties as the team comes off the bye looking for an offensive turnaround, coach Nick Sirianni said Wednesday.
The Eagles signed Milton off the Dallas Cowboys ' practice squad in mid-October and thrust him into the starting lineup three weeks later against the New York Giants in place of Tanner McKee . Milton went 18-of-34 for 169 yards with no touchdowns, no interceptions and seven sacks, including one where he lost a fumble. He also ran for 64 yards on nine carries.
"He works extremely hard with everything, really love his approach, like his personality," Sirianni said. "He's a really hard worker, and I really value that."
Mannion, 34, oversaw an offense that led the league in three-and-out percentage (35.7%) and was bottom five in passing (171.7 YPG), rushing (88.6 YPG) and points per game (16.4) through nine games.
Some bumps were expected for Mannion, a first-time offensive coordinator who entered the season with just two years of coaching experience. The job of implementing a new scheme got tougher with the retirement of right tackle Lane Johnson , losing quarterback Jalen Hurts for the season, trade of center Cam Jurgens and multigame absence of wide receiver DeVonta Smith over the first half of the season.
Sirianni said he made no staff changes during the bye week outside of hiring former assistant offensive line coach and run game specialist T.J. Paganetti in a consulting role.
The Eagles (2-7), losers of seven straight games, will host the Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3) on Sunday.
"I think we have a good plan of action moving forward of things we want to do to move forward and to get better. Obviously we haven't been good enough on offense but I like our plan of attack and our process we went through last week," Sirianni said.
"I think [Sean] is very smart. I think he has a great football mind. He thinks through everything."
author: Tim McManus

title: TNF: Texans rule out DE Hunter, RB Marks; Colts rule out CB Ward, starting OTs
summary: The Texans and Colts ruled out several key contributors for their Thursday night matchup.
full_text:
HOUSTON -- Key players for the Houston Texans and the Indianapolis Colts will be out for their AFC South matchup on "Thursday Night Football."
For the Texans, All-Pro defensive end Danielle Hunter is out with a hamstring injury after missing Houston's Week 10 loss to the Cleveland Browns , where they blew a 17-0 lead. That comes on the heels of Pro Bowl linebacker and team leader in tackles Azeez Al-Shaair being placed on injured reserve with a groin injury.
On the offensive side, the Texans will be without running back Woody Marks , who sustained a concussion on a second-down carry in the third quarter against the Browns. Browns defenders Emmanuel McNeil-Warren , Sam Kamara and Quincy Williams collided with Marks, leaving him on the ground for a few minutes.
A potential replacement for Marks is David Montgomery , but he has been out since Week 4 (groin). Montgomery practiced last week, and on Tuesday he said he's "trending in the right direction." He has no injury designation for the game.
Wideout Marvin Harrison Jr . is also out with a hamstring for the second straight game.
On the Colts' side, they will be without Pro Bowl starting cornerback Charvarius Ward , who sustained a knee injury in Sunday's win over the Miami Dolphins and did not practice this week.
Indianapolis also will be missing both starting tackles, a concerning development considering the impact that Houston defensive end Will Anderson Jr . had in the teams' first meeting in September. Left tackle Bernhard Raimann is still being treated for a concussion, and right tackle Jalen Travis will miss his second consecutive game with a knee injury. Tight end Will Mallory will not play because of a hamstring injury.
In the Colts' Week 3 win over Houston, Anderson dominated Indianapolis with 2.5 sacks, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery. He matched a career high with eight pressures in the game.
Cornerback Sauce Gardner , who has been dealing with calf issues off and on since last season, aggravated the injury Sunday and is listed as questionable. Another injury of note is the toe issue that has slowed receiver Anthony Gould . He took over the starting role in the slot after Josh Downs was traded to the Kansas City Chiefs earlier this month. Gould is listed as questionable.
author: DJ Bien-Aime and Stephen Holder

title: Jets QB Smith (ankle) intends to play vs. Chargers: 'That's the plan'
summary: Jets quarterback Geno Smith says he intends to play Sunday against the Chargers despite still walking with a noticeable limp due to an ankle injury.
full_text:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- Quarterback Geno Smith still was walking with a noticeable limp Wednesday, three days after injuring his left ankle, but he intends to play Sunday when the New York Jets try to snap their five-game losing streak.
"That's the plan," Smith said. "Obviously, you've got to take it day by day, but that's the plan."
Smith was listed as a limited participant in practice -- not a regular practice, but an extensive walk-through, as the Jets like to call it. Barring a setback, he expects to face the Los Angeles Chargers (1-8) at SoFi Stadium.
Embattled coach Aaron Glenn said he will let the week play out before announcing his plans. His options are a gimpy Smith or rookie Cade Klubnik , who replaced Smith in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills and was uneven in his NFL debut.
Glenn has made it clear that, even though the Jets are out of playoff contention with a 2-8 mark, he's not interested in turning the season over to the unproven Klubnik for evaluation purposes. Glenn, fighting for his job with a 5-22 record, said it would be "disrespectful" to bench Smith.
Smith has played reasonably well -- he's 19th in Total QBR (53.3) -- but the offense has gone nine straight quarters without a touchdown.
On Sunday, Smith was sidelined in the third quarter and never returned to the game. He went for a postgame X-ray and an MRI exam Monday, which showed no significant damage, a source said.
Smith wouldn't disclose the nature of the ankle injury, except to say it's "a little bit better [than Sunday]. I'm working through it." He took a few big hits in the game, acknowledging other aches and pains.
"Yeah, just working through some things, but just normal football stuff," he said.
When the starter is less than 100%, the distribution of practice reps can become an issue, especially if the backup is a rookie. Klubnik, who played only five series Sunday, had no practice reps with the starters before this week.
Glenn downplayed the matter, saying Klubnik will get a "fair amount of reps" in practice due to competition periods. In the game, the former Clemson star, a fourth-round pick, showed his inexperience. He led one field goal drive but also took three sacks and threw an interception. He completed 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards.
The sense in the locker room is that Smith will play.
"From what I know, Geno feels good to go," wide receiver Garrett Wilson said. "You would have to ask him. ... [but] from what I know, he's good to go. So, I'll say that."
author: Rich Cimini

title: 📊 Tiering all 32 teams' playoff chances, from locks to long shots
summary: We placed all 32 NFL teams into tiers based on their likelihood of making the playoffs, from Super Bowl favorites to the top-draft-pick candidates.
full_text:
The back half of the 2026 NFL season is upon us, and the playoff race is heating up. Though the standings tell us a lot about teams' chances to reach the postseason , they don't tell us everything . Team strength, injuries, tiebreakers, future strength of schedule and more can shift those odds up or down and don't show up in the win or loss columns.
So, ESPN analytics writer Seth Walder placed all 32 teams into eight tiers of playoff hopes, ranging from clear Super Bowl contenders to those already looking ahead to 2027. There is some fluidity in between, because for as confident as we feel about the league right now, things could look quite different once Week 18 rolls around. The tiers are based on information from ESPN's Football Power Index (FPI), betting lines , metrics, health status and some instinct.
Walder ranked the teams within each tier too. All percentages and statistical rankings are through Sunday unless otherwise indicated, and playoff chances are from the FPI.
Jump to a team: ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF SEA | TB | TEN | WSH
Chances to make the playoffs: 99.7% Chances to win the NFC West: 95.5% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 39.9%
Injuries have hit some of the 49ers' best players -- edge rusher Nick Bosa missed five games and wide receiver Mike Evans hasn't played since Week 6 -- but San Francisco is the FPI's Super Bowl favorite for two main reasons. The Niners are basically a lock to reach the playoffs and a heavy favorite to win the NFC West given their lead and head-to-head wins over the Rams and the Seahawks . Brock Purdy entered Week 10 as the No. 1 quarterback in QBR, and he is arguably the league's MVP thus far. Kyle Shanahan might be the Coach of the Year thus far too.
Chances to make the playoffs: >99.9% Chances to win the AFC East: >99.9% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 30.0%
The Bills entered this season as the AFC favorite, and nothing that has happened in the first 10 weeks has dispelled that notion. Their hold on the conference looks even stronger now than it did then thanks to their conference-best record and the Ravens falling out of contention. Buffalo's defense (16th in EPA per play) is still a concern, but quarterback Josh Allen , running back James Cook III and the Bills' offensive line do more than enough damage on offense.
Chances to make the playoffs: 99.9% Chances to win the AFC South: 98.8% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 22.5%
The Jaguars were already playoff locks and clearly one of the top two teams in the AFC before the trade deadline, when they acquired safety Jessie Bates III along with defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux . The Davis deal from the Jaguars' perspective is one of the worst trades in years , but there's also little doubt Jacksonville is better today than it was a week ago. And the Jaguars were great a week ago! The Jaguars rank in the top five in EPA per dropback on offense and EPA allowed per dropback as well as EPA allowed per designed rush on defense.
Chances to make the playoffs: 99.8% Chances to win the AFC West: 44.6% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 15.4%
The Chiefs faced three major questions entering the season:
How would quarterback Patrick Mahomes fare after recovering from a torn ACL suffered last December?
What kind of impact would free agent running back Kenneth Walker III have on the offense?
Could the defense survive the loss of starting cornerbacks Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson ?
The answer to every question has been positive for Kansas City. In particular, Walker has helped transform the Chiefs' rushing attack into a strength. And coordinator Steve Spagnuolo has managed to keep the defense strong too: It ranks sixth in EPA per play.
Chances to make the playoffs: 99.9% Chances to win the AFC North: 93.2% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 19.0%
It's something we've wondered about for years: What would happen if the Bengals could manage to combine a peak Joe Burrow season with simply mediocre defense? Well, we're finding out. Burrow is in the MVP race, and Cincinnati's defense is ranked 11th in EPA per play. Wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have been outstanding and provide a sky-high ceiling for the passing offense. Plus, the Bengals have a very easy schedule the rest of the way.
Chances to make the playoffs: 99.6% Chances to win the AFC West: 55.4% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 9.5%
Somehow, it's working . Despite Bo Nix falling well short of expectations -- he entered Week 10 ranked 24th out of 31 qualifiers in QBR -- the Broncos are a virtual lock to reach the playoffs and have a great shot at winning the AFC West. The defense hasn't quite lived up to its reputation (13th in EPA per play), but Denver also hasn't had All-Pro cornerback Pat Surtain II for every game, either. If the offense can keep its recent momentum (the Broncos have put up 26 points in each of their past three games), Denver can be a threat in the postseason. The Broncos have a soft schedule the rest of the way, too.
Chances to make the playoffs: 97.0% Chances to win the NFC North: 45.9% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 14.4%
Minnesota's trade-deadline deal for quarterback Kirk Cousins breathed new life into its season. That move instantly increased the Vikings' playoff chances from 65% to 83% at the time of the deal, according to the FPI. But that deal was about what comes next. With Brian Flores' incredible defense leading the way, the Vikings can and should have legitimate Super Bowl aspirations. The moment Flores leaves, a real possibility in this upcoming offseason, the team's contention window vanishes, so the Vikings need to take advantage of this opportunity. Minnesota's 30-10 dismantling of the Packers on Sunday only reinforced what a good trade it was.
Chances to make the playoffs: 84.9% Chances to win the NFC North: 20.2% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 11.1%
Chicago entered its bye week as a near lock to reach the playoffs and very much a team that could go all the way. Quarterback Caleb Williams has taken a significant step forward, and the fact that the Bears are 7-2 despite Williams missing three games is a testament to the coaching staff and how strong this team is. Coordinator Dennis Allen was already getting the most out of a lacking defensive roster when the Bears acquired the best defensive tackle in the league in Jeffery Simmons as they prepare for what they hope is a Super Bowl run.
Chances to make the playoffs: 89.4% Chances to win the NFC North: 33.1% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 10.4%
If they played in a normal division, the Lions would be even safer than this, especially after the team's blowout win over the Patriots in Munich on Sunday -- albeit with New England missing quarterback Drake Maye for most of that contest . But Detroit's record has it on the verge of a playoff berth despite playing in a stacked NFC North and with the Seahawks and Rams looming as other wild-card threats. There's little doubt the Lions can score points. But the X factor down the stretch and in the postseason will be their defense, which ranks 23rd in EPA per play and now faces a significant knee injury to star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson .
Chances to make the playoffs: 83.6% Chances to win the AFC North: 4.9% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 1.6%
The Steelers are barreling toward another playoff berth thanks to their running game and defense. No team in the league is more efficient (by EPA per play) on the ground than the Steelers -- hello, Jaylen Warren ! -- and the team's run defense hasn't allowed opponents to rush successfully against them. Getting past the Bengals to win the division will be a tall order, but the fall of the Ravens helps widen the Steelers' path to the postseason.
Chances to make the playoffs: 62.6% Chances to win the NFC South: 62.3% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 5.5%
The FPI believes the Bucs are the best team in the…
author: Seth Walder

title: What has gone right -- and wrong -- for every NFL offensive coordinator, playcaller this season
summary: Here's the good and the bad for each offensive coordinator or playcaller through Week 10, plus keys to their success the rest of the way.
full_text:
We've seen the good and bad of offensive coordinators and playcallers across the league throughout the first half of the 2026 NFL season.
With Dan Pitcher coordinating the offense and coach Zac Taylor calling plays, Joe Burrow has the Cincinnati Bengals ' offense humming. The same goes for Trevor Lawrence and the Jacksonville Jaguars , with Grant Udinski as OC and coach Liam Coen the playcaller. Both QBs are in the MVP conversation.
On the other side of things, the Los Angeles Chargers ' offense under OC/playcaller Mike McDaniel has been a disaster. The Minnesota Vikings had struggled to put points on the board until they acquired QB Kirk Cousins , which had an immediate impact on coach Kevin O'Connell's playcalling in Sunday's win over the Green Bay Packers .
There are eight weeks left this season, and the pressure will continue to build for coordinators and playcallers looking for winning formulas, while those who shine might be in position to become head coaches in 2027.
With that in mind, here is what has gone right, what has gone wrong and the key to the second half for every offense in the NFL.
Jump to: ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF SEA | TB | TEN | WSH
Offensive coordinator: Pete Carmichael
What has gone right? Just about everything. The Bills lead the NFL in scoring and are doing so with a varied attack that features RB James Cook III handling a career-high workload and QB Josh Allen leading his most explosive passing attack since arriving in Buffalo. Most encouragingly, this offense has proved just as capable of winning in slow-paced ball-control games as in up-tempo shootouts.
What has gone wrong? Pre-snap sloppiness is a recurring problem. Between false starts, illegal shifts, delays of game, offsides and too many men in the huddle calls, the Bills are averaging close to three pre-snap offensive penalties per game, and that's not to mention the 132 yards the Bills have had nullified by holding penalties.
Key to second half: Allen has always benefited from the abnormal consistency, continuity and health in front of him on the offensive line. In recent weeks, tackles Dion Dawkins and Spencer Brown and guard Alec Anderson have dealt with injury concerns. Keeping the line together, especially with cold weather coming and how the Bills are already leaning on Cook, is paramount. -- Nick Suss
Offensive coordinator: Bobby Slowik
What has gone right? The Dolphins entered this season vowing to run the ball and they've done so successfully -- remarkably, even without starter De'Von Achane , who tore his left ACL in September. Second-year back Ollie Gordon II has filled in nicely for Achane, at one point scoring a rushing touchdown in four straight games. Miami's offensive line has been physical at the line of scrimmage and leads the league in average rushing yards before first contact per rush attempt.
What has gone wrong? Miami has largely struggled to move the ball consistently through the air, averaging the third-fewest passing yards per game in the NFL this season. Third-round rookie Caleb Douglas looks like a definite starting receiver, but the Dolphins are still looking for consistent production from the rest of the room. Some of that also falls on quarterback Malik Willis , who will be on injured reserve until at least Week 14 with a groin/core injury.
Key to second half: Continue to get receivers Douglas, Chris Bell and Kevin Coleman Jr . involved in the passing game. Their development will be worth keeping an eye on with Willis sidelined and second-year quarterback Kyle McCord starting in his place. With the playoffs out of the picture, the Dolphins' focal point should center on their three rookie receivers and continuing to sharpen their run game. -- Marcel Louis-Jacques
Offensive coordinator: Josh McDaniels
Playcaller: Josh McDaniels
What has gone right? Explosive plays. They are among the league leaders in passing plays of 20 yards or more, and running plays of 20 yards or more. They've also received solid contributions from a young core of players who project to be a big part of their future -- OTs Will Campbell and Caleb Lomu , C Jared Wilson and TE Eli Raridon
What has gone wrong? Too many injuries. WR A.J. Brown sustained a high right ankle sprain in the third quarter of the season opener, which foreshadowed what was to come -- a run of injuries across the offense that has challenged finding continuity and consistency, and now includes Drake Maye . The Patriots are expected to use all eight of their return-from-IR designations and Maye might be done for the season.
Key to second half: Supporting QB Tommy DeVito . He is being thrust into the starting role and that means everyone else needs to raise their level of play to lift him up. The return of starting left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker and No. 2 receiver Romeo Doubs should also help. -- Mike Reiss
Offensive coordinator: Frank Reich
What has gone right? The veteran Reich, in Year 1 with the Jets, has done a nice job of helping QB Geno Smith curb his turnovers. Smith, who had more interceptions (52) than any quarterback from 2022 to 2025, has reduced his picks to three. Smith is having the best statistical season of any Jets QB since Ryan Fitzpatrick in 2015. Reich, himself a former QB, deserves some credit for that.
What has gone wrong? Reich has above-average talent, including gifted skill players in WR Garrett Wilson and RB Breece Hall , and yet the Jets are only 24th in points per game (19.4). The main reasons: poor red zone efficiency (31st), vanilla game plans, questionable halftime adjustments and inconsistency in getting the ball into the hands of their top players.
Key to second half: The Jets can start off by scoring a touchdown; they've gone nine straight quarters without one, tied for the second-longest drought in the league this season. Reich needs to create an identity for the offense. They want to be physical and run-oriented, but they stray from that during games. Another key: Get Kenyon Sadiq more involved. The talented rookie tight end has been a nonfactor over the past seven games. -- Rich Cimini
Offensive coordinator: Declan Doyle
What has gone right? Getting RB Derrick Henry in the end zone. The Ravens have failed to consistently run and throw the ball this season, but Henry continues to pile up touchdowns. By midseason, he recorded his ninth season of 10 or more touchdowns, which ties LaDainian Tomlinson for the most in NFL history.
What has gone wrong? Injuries at quarterback. It's gotten so bad that the Ravens became the third team since 1950 to start four different quarterbacks in four weeks (excluding the 1987 strike season), according to the Elias Sports Bureau. Lamar Jackson is out until at least mid-to-late December after having surgery on his right thumb and Tyler Huntley is out for the season with turf toe. After one start with undrafted Joe Fagnano , Baltimore was in desperation mode when it traded for Jacoby Brissett .
Key to second half: Getting the offense on track with Brissett. Entering Monday night's game, the Ravens had gone four straight games without scoring more than 14 points for the first time in team history. The Ravens have praised Brissett for his ability to drive the ball downfield. Since the start of the 2025 season, Brissett has thrown 33 touchdown passes, which is more than Justin Herbert (32), Baker Mayfield (29) and Jackson (27). -- Jamison Hensley
Offensive coordinator: Dan Pitcher
What has gone right? The team is scoring the ball at an absurd clip. Since Week 5, the Bengals are No. 1 in the NFL in points per drive and scoring touchdowns on a staggering 46.2% of their possessions. QB Joe Burrow is also the league leader in Total QBR during that span and in about every other notable metric.
What has gone wrong? Cincinnati wanted to be a more balanced team that was able to operate under center. That experiment…
author: NFL Nation

title: What we're hearing on Week 11: Buzz off Mendoza's first start?
summary: Could changes be coming in Dallas? And what now for New England? Here's the latest intel.
full_text:
Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season is here, and insiders Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano have been calling sources around the league for the latest news and notable buzz.
First, what are people saying about last weekend's much-anticipated first start for Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza ? What did he show against the Seahawks and what does it tell us about the rest of his season? Then, what are we hearing on the Cowboys' struggling defense and any potential changes on the horizon? What about the Patriots and their sudden downturn in the aftermath of Drake Maye 's injury? And finally, who are the most interesting 2027 free agents and what is the early intel on them?
It's all here, as Jeremy and Dan answer big questions, hand out useful fantasy football nuggets and empty their reporting notebooks heading into Week 11.
Jump to: Mendoza's debut | Cowboys' defense Patriots' concern | 2027 free agents Fantasy advice | More notes, intel
Graziano: They are saying he looked the part and that the moment didn't look too big for him. And that is really what you're looking for if you're starting a rookie No. 1 pick in Week 10 against the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks' defense .
Mendoza obviously has work to do on pre-snap diagnosis and other aspects of the job at this level, but he's not the first quarterback to not see Devon Witherspoon coming on a blitz, and he won't be the last. He clearly offers something with his legs that Kirk Cousins does not at this point, and he made throws outside the numbers that people view as a sign the offense can evolve with him at the helm.
Fowler: People I spoke with saw flashes. Playing Seattle is an arduous task. But Mendoza used his legs to escape congestion, completed passes to 10 different receivers and navigated an offense that was without star tight end Brock Bowers for much of the game. The Seahawks eventually overwhelmed him. He missed a few blitzes and took six sacks. He missed some throws, particularly to the left side of the field. But as one personnel evaluator noted, the game didn't look too big for him and he kept his eyes downfield, whether in the pocket or on the move. The arm strength and mobility are obvious, and those can be assets to the Raiders' offense in the coming weeks and into 2027.
While Cousins probably would have started another week had he stayed, Mendoza was making enough progress behind the scenes that he was going to play soon enough. And he did enough to at least validate that promise.
Graziano: He did, and it will get better. This is quite similar to the situation Eli Manning had as a rookie with the Giants in 2004, when veteran Kurt Warner started the first half of the season and Manning took over midway through. One key difference is that Warner remained on that Giants team for the rest of the season, whereas Cousins is no longer there to be a sounding board for Mendoza. So that's something to watch. But the Raiders have been extremely deliberate about Mendoza's development program, and while yes, his first start came a few weeks earlier than they had planned, they believe he's ready enough. And Sunday's debut didn't cause any fresh concern that I can detect in that building.
It doesn't get a lot easier, with Denver and Cleveland in the next two weeks ahead of the Raiders' bye, but Mendoza has something, and people are excited to see more. It's no coincidence that the NFL flexed that Week 12 Raiders-Browns game into primetime on Tuesday.
Fowler: This is a challenging three-game stretch for a young quarterback. In order for him to survive it, the Raiders must find a way to run the ball more efficiently. How a Klint Kubiak-run offense ranks last in yards per rush at 2.9 is shocking to me, even with the transitional state of the offensive line. The Raiders' backs have a combined two rushing performances of more than 60 yards -- Ashton Jeanty (102) in Week 1 and Mike Washington Jr . (83) in Week 8. That's it. Running the ball well is a staple of the Kubiak system, and if the Raiders are to properly support Mendoza, they must find a way to manufacture explosive plays on the ground.
The rest should come into focus. "Mendoza is a good fit for Klint [Kubiak's] offense," an NFC offensive coach said. "I thought he did well when facing live bullets."
(Update: On Wednesday morning, the Cowboys made a playcalling change , and the below text has been updated to reflect that.)
Fowler: The big shake-up would be changing coaching personnel on defense and based on public comments coming from the Dallas brass this week, it feels like everything is on the table when it comes to defensive coordinator Christian Parker's status. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer and owner Jerry Jones have been noncommittal about Parker. On Wednesday morning, the Cowboys did make a change and gave playcalling duties to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine. Parker was formerly a Pettine understudy in Green Bay.
In talking to people in Dallas, they believe firing coaches wouldn't solve much. Parker is a good young coach. It just hasn't worked out thus far. The personnel on defense, though improved on paper from a year ago, still isn't great and is clearly a year away. Yes, it looks bad -- Christian McCaffrey running untouched upfield twice is a hard image to shake -- but the Cowboys have already tweaked the defensive lineup earlier in the season. Plus, it's tough to make wholesale changes, in part because Dallas is very much alive in a weak NFC East.
Graziano: Agreed. And I believe that's the way the Cowboys see it, too. Jones made some comments on the radio Tuesday hinting about possibly changing defensive playcallers, and Dallas ultimately went that route. But this is very much not an ownership group that likes to make in-season coaching changes, so they would consider it a drastic step to move on totally from Parker now. Also, if Schottenheimer is concerned about his own job security at the end of this season, throwing a second defensive coordinator overboard in two years might not be the best way to project that he has everything under control.
Fowler: The Titans and Eagles are on the schedule over the next two weeks. That could be a stretch for Dallas to get things right, though Cam Ward is improving in Tennessee and that game is hardly a gimme. Playoffs or not, the Cowboys will have serious work to do in the offseason to replenish the defense ... again. Defensive tackle Quinnen Williams is worth building around. He's having a strong season as one of the lone bright spots on that side of the ball. But the Cowboys will need help at all three levels. There are not enough standouts. And they have just four picks in April's draft to change that.
Situating the futures of corner Joey Porter Jr . and wide receiver George Pickens is critical. Franchise-tagging one of them could risk losing the other, and cornerback is a major need for the team, even with Porter in the lineup. Dallas was brimming with confidence defensively coming out of camp, and the good feelings dissipated early in the season. This is going on two years of bad defensive football.
Graziano: It makes you wonder if the organization needs to take a broader look at the way it scouts, acquires and develops defensive talent. The Cowboys seem to need a more coherent overall plan, which admittedly is tough when you change defensive coordinators every year. Since Dan Quinn left to coach the Commanders, they have cycled through Mike Zimmer, Matt Eberflus and now potentially Parker. The criticism of Eberflus last season was that he didn't coach to the specific abilities of his players enough and wasn't flexible in making scheme changes to reflect the players' strengths and weaknesses. But things are worse on that side of the ball this season -- even after Dallas brought in young players it believed would specifically fit what Parker wanted to do.
It's bad there, and there's no evidence that another coordinator change would make things better. The Cowboys might need to…
author: Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano

title: Barnwell debunks a myth: Yes, there are at least 32 starter-level QBs in the NFL at any given time
summary: Finding legit quarterbacks can be tough, and many people think there aren't even enough true QB1s to fill the league's 32 QB1 spots. Is there any validity to that?
full_text:
It has been an absolutely brutal year for quarterback injuries in the NFL. When I wrote about this in September , the 2026 season was already looking as if it could be on the high end for missing signal-callers. And as we hit Week 11, it's almost more difficult to find teams that haven't had to go to their backups than ones who have been able to stick with their starter all season.
Fourteen teams have been unable to play their primary quarterback for more than a quarter of work because of an injury this season. The Bears, Cardinals and Ravens have been forced to turn to their third-string option. As many as seven of the 10 afternoon games Sunday will feature at least one backup quarterback.
Though both the league and its teams are desperate to keep the best quarterbacks healthy, injuries are going to happen. And in just about every case, going from a starter to a backup is going to create problems. Over the past decade -- without factoring in any other information -- teams that got a full game from their starting quarterback and went up against opposition that didn't get a single snap from their preferred starter won nearly 66% of the time.
Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show'
It would be great if teams could turn to a deep pool of backups, but that just isn't the case at quarterback. And there's a phrase that comes up all the time: "There aren't 32 starting-caliber quarterbacks to go around in the NFL." And yes, the reality is that the league rarely, if ever, has 32 quality starters featuring at the same time.
But does that mean that there couldn't be 32 quality starters if they were dispersed around the league's 32 teams? I'm not so sure. There are some gaps in that logic, and it's a topic I've always wanted to explore. The middle of an injury-riddled 2026 season feels like the right time to get there. How many viable starting QBs are typically on NFL rosters at any one time? Is it 20? 30? 40?
I wasn't sure of the answer, but I'm sure we're not considering the question correctly. I'm going to show why that's the case and give my best estimate for how many viable quarterbacks have typically been present on NFL rosters at any one time over the past few decades.
Jump to: Why the argument is flawed True QB1s in a typical season What it means for 2026
The fundamental flaw in the "There aren't 32 starting-caliber quarterbacks" argument is that it evaluates only the 32 quarterbacks who are currently playing in NFL lineups. Even if we ignore injuries and just consider each team's ideal and preferred option heading into 2026, that's still going to leave us with a handful of teams that don't have a quarterback who projects to be even a viable starter, let alone a solid one. At any one time, there are typically going to be at least a couple of replacement-level starters in a starting lineup. By midseason, when injuries have usually hit the league, those concerns feel even more acute.
On the other hand, there are a lot of reasons why the 32 starting quarterbacks in the league at any given time aren't the 32 best options to fill those roles.
Teams aren't as good at identifying the right starting QBs as we'd like to believe. When it comes its quarterbacks, NFL teams are generally meritocratic and able to identify who they should be starting by the end of training camp. But not always.
Some teams are locked into long-term contracts for players and want to give that passer every chance to prove that he's worth his deal. The Browns started Deshaun Watson to open the 2024 season and got historically bad play for seven games before the highly paid veteran tore his Achilles . Jameis Winston isn't a superstar, but the Browns were a much better offense the moment he entered the lineup.
Other teams are operating in the opposite boat and have a young, highly drafted quarterback who isn't very good yet playing ahead of a veteran backup who would be more effective if given the full-time starting role. Also in 2024, the Colts were starting Anthony Richardson Sr . ahead of Joe Flacco for most of the season despite the fact that Flacco had helped lead the Browns to the postseason the previous season. Richardson plays a very different style, but if the goal was just to field the best possible quarterback, Flacco probably should have been the choice.
Teams also just flat-out make evaluation mistakes, even with players they've already seen in their offense. The Vikings chose Kyler Murray , Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer ahead of J.J. McCarthy and then traded their 2024 first-round pick to the Giants, where he has been a much more productive player than any of the signal-callers he had been competing with in camp. I'm sure some of that was a product of not wanting to deal with McCarthy as a third or fourth quarterback, but strictly in terms of on-field performance, the Vikings appear to have chosen the wrong guys.
In the big picture, teams find it even more difficult to identify which quarterback prospects will succeed as they enter the NFL, even when those guys are roughly entering the league within the same tier. In 2018, five QBs came off the board in Round 1. Baker Mayfield , who has been somewhere between a solid starter and a replacement-level passer in his various stops around the league, was the first pick. Sam Darnold , who fits the same mold, was next. Josh Allen , a future Hall of Famer, followed. The Cardinals then chose Josh Rosen , who was out of football after 16 starts, before the Ravens took Lamar Jackson , who will join Allen in Canton one day.
I'll get to later-round picks in a moment, but the idea that the 32 quarterbacks starting around the league at any given time are actually the 32 best quarterbacks in football simply isn't true. And it takes a few seconds to quickly look around the league to see that.
Some teams have no viable quarterback, but others have more than one. There are going to be some QB1s this weekend who either haven't proved themselves to be NFL starters or previously weren't able to perform like one. Players like Tommy DeVito and Joe Milton probably don't qualify as viable starting quarterbacks for the purposes of the statement we're evaluating, even if they're going to be on the field Sunday. Of course, they're replacing quarterbacks who are hurt in Drake Maye and Jalen Hurts , respectively, who would comfortably fit any definition of a quality starter.
Elsewhere, there are teams that haven't needed to turn to a backup but might have two viable starters. The Bengals have Flacco backing up Joe Burrow . Marcus Mariota has been solid behind Jayden Daniels as an injury replacement in Washington. Joshua Dobbs put together an impressive run with the Vikings in 2023 and hasn't been needed behind Jared Goff in Detroit. Murray has been disappointing in Minnesota, but he was a solid starter for the Cardinals over the past half-decade. Drew Lock has been effective filling in for Darnold in Seattle. And Mac Jones was able to sustain the offense for the 49ers when Brock Purdy was injured last season.
Are all of those guys stars? No. But if the goal was to pick the 32 best quarterbacks in football in 2026, backups like Flacco, Jones and Mariota would probably be in that conversation ahead of some starters around the NFL, even though they're backing up other high-profile quarterbacks and aren't currently in starting roles. And we've seen each of those backups push teams to the postseason as starters in the past, which would seem to suggest that they would be viable starters again in the right situation.
Some players would be starter-worthy in certain schemes and ineffective in others.
If we were looking for quarterbacks who would excel in every single scheme and situation, regardless of their individual skill set, that number will be very low. That's also true for many other positions, too, though, and we don't talk about scarcity in those spots in the same way. Guard Kevin Dotson was struggling in a Steelers scheme that asked him to move laterally in a…
author: Bill Barnwell

title: Why can't Anthony Richardson beat out the struggling Daniel Jones as Colts QB1?
summary: Daniel Jones has some of the worst numbers in the NFL, yet Anthony Richardson can't get on the field for the woeful Colts.
full_text:
INDIANAPOLIS -- Indianapolis Colts teammates Anthony Richardson Sr . and Grover Stewart have a playful rivalry that can be seen playing out during practice most days.
Stewart, the 6-foot-4, 314-pound veteran nose tackle who anchors the middle of the defense, warns backup quarterback Richardson that today is the day he'll chase him down when he leaves the pocket.
"Look," Stewart said, "he can move. But I always tell him, 'I'm gonna catch you.'"
"Hey, he's a hard guy to catch," Stewart said. "He's fast. That's a threat right there. Big arm, big legs."
But lately, those practice reps running the scout-team offense are the closest Richardson has come to playing meaningful snaps. That remains true despite starting quarterback Daniel Jones ranking as the NFL's worst starter in numerous major categories, including QBR (30.3) and yards per attempt (5.6). He also leads the NFL in interceptions (12).
Nevertheless, Jones remains the starter heading into Thursday's AFC South matchup against the Houston Texans (8:15 ET, Prime Video). And Colts coach Shane Steichen continues to defend his handpicked starter who enjoyed the best stretch of his career under Steichen in the first half of the 2025 season.
But most of what Jones has displayed in 2026 suggests that last season -- he at one point was the most efficient passer in the NFL -- was the exception, not the rule. Jones posted a 1.7 QBR in Sunday's win over the Miami Dolphins , the worst of any quarterback who has started a game in 2026. He's averaged 135 passing yards in his past four games and hasn't thrown for 200 yards in any game in the last month.
