It is arguably the worst Jones has played in his career, including his six tumultuous seasons with the New York Giants .
But Steichen remains steadfast.
"I think I take everything into account," he said when asked how he determines whether a quarterback change is warranted. "I always go back and look at the film and make sure on this play, was it his fault? Was it someone else's fault? I think there's a lot that goes into it.
"Obviously, the biggest thing is taking care of the football moving forward."
Jones hasn't done the latter, with a 7-to-12 touchdown-to-interception ratio and 13 fumbles over his 23 games as the Colts' starter. To be fair, the Colts are outmanned on offense, especially after trading receivers Josh Downs and Keenan Allen last week and All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson late last month.
But there's no spinning Jones' performance, which was problematic even before the Colts' recent flurry of trades. The Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard on Oct. 19, lost five of their past six games and are four games behind division-leading Jacksonville in the win column. If now isn't the time to try someone else at quarterback, when will it be?
"It's not all about one guy," Steichen said this week. "I think it takes all 11 to do their job at a high level."
It's a level of grace the Colts rarely afforded to Richardson.
The No. 4 overall pick in the 2023 draft, Richardson's arrival in Indianapolis coincided with Steichen's. Together, the team envisioned Steichen doing for Richardson what he'd done for other young quarterbacks such as Justin Herbert and Jalen Hurts while an offensive coordinator for the Chargers and Eagles, respectively.
Steichen, along with Ballard and late owner Jim Irsay, were aligned on the selection of Richardson, who had just 13 college starts at Florida. He was one of the least-experienced quarterbacks ever to be drafted in the first round, but the Colts were undaunted.
Richardson entered his first training camp in competition with veteran Gardner Minshew II . Richardson started the team's preseason opener that summer against the Buffalo Bills and played about a quarter. Two days later, Steichen opened his post-practice media briefing with an announcement: He'd seen enough. Richardson would be the team's Week 1 starter.
Steichen, it seemed, was all-in.
The Colts have traded away several key offensive players, but even before that, Daniel Jones was struggling.
Now, four seasons later, Richardson, who is in the last year of his contract, can't get on the field even when the team's starter is throwing perplexing interceptions and his coach's job is in serious jeopardy .
Looking back, Steichen's belief in Richardson was short-lived. Steichen benched Richardson midway through the 2024 season following a loss at Houston that included the infamous "tap out," with Richardson leaving the game for a play after taking a knee on the field. He later said he was exhausted after the previous play.
Steichen insisted then that backup Joe Flacco gave the Colts the best chance to win -- until that proved not to be true. Three weeks later, Steichen reinserted Richardson into the lineup. He went on to have some promising moments, authoring game-winning drives against the New York Jets and New England Patriots down the stretch.
But Richardson's inconsistency -- he's a 50.9% career passer -- and his many injuries seemed to break Steichen's belief. It was clear to many in the organization that the coach had turned the page on the young quarterback. The Colts signed Jones the following spring and the rest is history. He has since signed a two-year, $88 million contract extension that might be a variable in Steichen's commitment to Jones.
Richardson's performance was more than enough to prompt the Colts to look elsewhere. He was one of the lowest-rated quarterbacks in the league in his lone season as a full-time starter. But the same is now true of Jones, yet Steichen is staying the course.
Steichen recently acknowledged that Richardson's electric running ability could possibly give the Colts a spark. Richardson has 10 rushing touchdowns in 15 career starts.
"That's a real thing," Steichen said. "... We'll look at everything."
The Colts have at least considered it. Richardson, according to multiple sources, currently has a package of plays in the playbook. But the Colts have yet to dust it off. If his exploits against Colts defenders in practice are any indication, perhaps they should.
"He's so explosive," defensive end Jaylahn Tuimoloau said. "I don't think I've ever played against a quarterback that explosive. He gives us great looks on the scout team whenever we go against him."
Richardson showed improvement during the preseason after coming back from a career-threatening eye injury that kept him out for much of last season. Still, it's difficult to imagine a future for him in Indianapolis. Recognizing his status with the franchise, Richardson requested a trade earlier this year. Ultimately, nothing materialized, according to team sources. But that the idea was even broached spoke volumes about Richardson's view of the situation. Now, Ballard, Richardson's biggest ally at Colts headquarters, has been ousted.
Richardson was recently cited for marijuana possession in Carmel, Indiana, and faces a possible four-game suspension for violating the personal conduct policy, but there's no indication that is playing a role in lineup decisions.
"I've just got to keep doing what I've been doing, coming in the building, showing up to work," Richardson said recently. "Just preparing like I was going to be the starter regardless of what decision [Steichen] makes. I've just got to make sure I'm prepared when my number's called."
At this point, it's not clear whether that will ever happen.
author: Stephen Holder

title: Playoff hopes? How Houston has banded together through tough losses
summary: Houston enters "Thursday Night Football" against the Colts with a 32.4% chance of making the playoffs.
full_text:
HOUSTON -- A despondent Kamari Lassiter lumbered into a borderline vacant Houston Texans locker room following a Week 1 loss to the Buffalo Bills .
An hour prior, Bills quarterback Josh Allen floated a 30-yard pass into the end zone with 1:48 remaining in the season opener -- a balloon pass that hit the hands of a falling Lassiter.
The cornerback bobbled it, and the ball slipped out of his grasp and dribbled into the end zone. Laying side by side with the ball, Lassiter clutched it in disbelief.
On the next play, Bills wideout Joshua Palmer spun Lassiter around and Allen zipped a touchdown pass to Palmer to go up 36-31 with 1:36 remaining. Quarterback C.J. Stroud & Co. tried to respond -- marching down the field with the game on the line -- but on third-and-goal, Stroud was sacked and fumbled, dropping Houston to 0-1.
As Lassiter was slouched in front of his locker stall, still sporting his game worn white pants, he took notable pauses in response to questions. He noted that "a lot of the plays that happened" weren't up to the team's standard and his play just wasn't him.
"Yeah, it was really bad for me," Lassiter said. "Man, I just feel like it was just not me. It was just not the best day at all."
How did Lassiter handle a day where he allowed 95 yards in coverage, the game-winning score and a penalty in the second quarter that positioned the Bills on the 1-yard line, resulting in a touchdown? He went nearby to his mom's house and invited safety Calen Bullock and linebacker Jamal Hill over as he paced around in frustration.
He was seeking the kind of brotherhood and unity that has kept a team with Super Bowl hype coming into the season mentally afloat through a disappointing 3-6 start. They have banded together, finding ways off the field to uplift one another.
"Our team is really close," Bullock told ESPN. "Everybody is always kicking it with each other, even outside the building. We all go to dinner. We stay close even when times are hard. We still got each other back, and we bring each other up."
Houston's defense allowed the second-fewest points last season (17.4 per game), but it has allowed 24.3 (18th) in the first half of this season. And most inexcusably, the unit has blown four leads in the waning minutes of fourth quarters and also allowed a game-winning score in overtime against the New York Giants .
Coming off a backbreaking 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns , in which they squandered a 17-0 lead, the Texans are looking to rebound once again -- as they are set to host the Indianapolis Colts (3-7) on "Thursday Night Football" (8:15 p.m. ET, Amazon Prime).
Despite ESPN's Football Power Index giving Houston a 32.4% chance to make the playoffs -- considering the struggles of the AFC compared to the NFC -- coach DeMeco Ryans isn't "discouraged" by the rough start and Stroud believes his team can find a way. With a win, Houston's playoff chances rise to 37%, but with a loss, they drops to 15%.
Not playing meaningful football is an unfamiliar place to these Texans -- three straight winning seasons and postseasons that started with Stroud and Ryans' arrival in 2023.
"What else are we going to do?" Stroud said. "Cry about it and hold our heads down? Woe is us, woe is this team? I don't believe in that. It sucks, yeah, I'm not the happiest camper.
"A motivated Texans is a scary team. It's up to us. We don't need anybody else. That's my message to the guys."
Offensive guard Ed Ingram shot a text to his teammates. He had an idea for a team bonding activity during their bye week: A halloween party.
It was something he and his wife experienced when he was with the Minnesota Vikings , and they wanted to bring that tradition to Houston. They rented out a local restaurant called "King Steak" and had a clown theme night. The costumes were creative, but a highlight for multiple players was offensive guard Wyatt Teller doing the "South Dallas Swag" dance.
A post shared by White Flower Events | Houston Event Rentals | Corporate & Social (@1whiteflowerevents)
"It was a goofy version," Ingram told ESPN with a laugh. "That was probably one of my favorite moments. When you have camaraderie outside the facility, it shows you that it's more than just a job. We're more than coworkers, we're a brotherhood.
"If you can build that environment around here, you can go far -- because when you're on the field, you're not just playing for money, you're playing for the person next to you. We are ready to go out there and die for each other."
Eight players also attended the Ohio State versus USC game during the bye -- with friendly bets on the line. The losers had to wear the opposing school's clothing. That meant Stroud, an OSU alum, had to don the cardinal and gold after the Trojans defeated the Buckeyes 30-18.
"We put belts on the boys," said Bullock, a USC alum. "[Stroud] was on that side, we was on this side. After every touchdown, we celebrated looking at C.J., talking trash to him. They get a first down, he's talking trash to us.
"It got to a point of the game where he disappeared though. It's just stuff like that outside the building, and you see how close we are."
Coming out of the bye week, Houston was able to pick up its third win of the season -- an impressive 44-22 win over the Los Angeles Chargers . That week featured five touchdown passes from Stroud along with eight sacks from the defense and two takeaways. But the biggest highlight of the day was wideout Tank Dell , who scored a 63-yard touchdown in his second game back since a gruesome knee injury in December of 2024 that sidelined him.
When he crossed the end zone, a sea of Texans waited for Dell to reach the sideline to congratulate him.
"You could see the energy shift. Everybody is happy to be here," Dell told ESPN. "Happy to see where we are going and the work that we are putting in. Just creating that relationship, man, that helps tremendously on the field."
The frustrations have been high for the Texans, but not with each other as they've found ways to keep the team chemistry high during the adversity.
"That's been one of our strongest points," defensive end Will Anderson Jr . said. "We've been together. Nobody has been energy vampires."
Still, losing is hard, as shown by Lassiter finding himself in a familiar space following Sunday's game.
He drew a 15-yard unnecessary roughness penalty with 1:18 left in the fourth quarter on second-and-11, giving the Browns a first-and-10 from the Texans' 35-yard line. The third-year corner unintentionally made contact with the helmet of wideout Tylan Wallace while trying to intercept quarterback Deshaun Watson , as both players got their hands on the ball.
"It's very frustrating because it leaves you with indecision," Lassiter said. "I don't know what I'm supposed to do. I'm trying to go get the ball. If he's touching the ball, I'm trying to get the ball out of his hands. We play a violent sport. I don't know, I'm confused."
On the next play, Watson completed a 30-yard dart to tight end Harold Fanning, and running back Quinshon Judkins scored one play later giving Houston 47 seconds to respond.
But the drive ended with the same result as Week 1 did. No points.
Even in the face of adversity, Houston continued to show unwavering loyalty.
"What else are you supposed to do in that position," Bullock said. "You're supposed to just sit there and let them catch the ball?"
Ryans echoed those sentiments during his postgame press conference.
"It's only one way forward, and that's together," Ryans said. "I haven't seen it any other way. Our guys have been very good. Our guys have been together. That's never a message, or it's nothing that I have to talk about."
Just like how Weeks 1 and 10 felt like déjà vu, the Texans are hoping to recreate their 2025 success -- where they turned a 3-5 record into a 12-5 finish with a postseason berth. But they know it's up to them to turn the tide.
"We've put ourselves in this position, so we can't be mad at that," Bullock said. "We…
author: DJ Bien-Aime

title: Falcons seek change, but keep ending up in the same spot
summary: Mediocre record, questions at quarterback, rinse, repeat. Maybe next year the Falcons can start making progress.
full_text:
Bijan Robinson was visibly frustrated. He was in the locker room addressing the media after another Atlanta Falcons loss. The star running back referenced the team's bye this week and how it was time to put up or shut up.
"We have to come together this week and just tell ourselves, is this how we want to end this season and is this how we want to go about the rest of the season with this product or are we going to change and are we going to strain for each other?" Robinson said after a 35-13 home loss to the Kansas City Chiefs last Sunday. "Are we going to go out there and play for each other no matter the situation and just be dominant on the field, man?"
It is an all-too-familiar feeling for Robinson, who has yet to play for a winning team in his four seasons in the NFL.
The Falcons have lost five of their last six games to fall to 3-7. That was their exact record through 10 games last season. Over the previous five seasons, Atlanta has gone 7-10 three times and 8-9 twice. The franchise has not made the playoffs since the 2017 season, the second-longest drought in the NFL after the New York Jets .
The Falcons have been like the football version of Bill Murray's Groundhog Day. There has been a certain sameness to it all across three different coaching staffs and two different front offices.
Head coach Kevin Stefanski, general manager Ian Cunningham and president of football Matt Ryan -- the last Falcons' franchise quarterback from 2008-21 -- took over last offseason. The story, though, remains on repeat: a team good enough to knock off top teams (the Philadelphia Eagles in 2024, the Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Rams in 2025 and the San Francisco 49ers this season) yet one inconsistent enough to suffer seemingly annual blowout losses to the middling Carolina Panthers .
The Falcons offense was supposed to get a facelift this season, a new system led by Stefanski, an offensive guru, and young offensive coordinator and playcaller Tommy Rees. They have gotten some things right, like making quarterback Michael Penix Jr . into a primarily under-center passer with more play-action looks. But the results have been maddeningly similar to where the Falcons were at this time in 2025.
Through 10 games this season, the Falcons have scored 20.1 points per game and have accumulated 327.4 yards per game. Atlanta has an offensive success rate of 40.8% and its EPA per play is -0.16. That latter mark is tied for fifth-worst in the league.
Last season, through 10 games, the Falcons had scored 19.5 points per game and had racked up 332.5 yards per game. The 2025 team had a 43.4% success rate with a -0.07 EPA per play. Eerily similar numbers.
Even if you remove the first two games of this season started by third-string quarterback Cooper Rush , the Falcons stats are only marginally better: 23.1 points per game, 343.8 yards per game, a 41.7% success rate and a -0.08 EPA per play.
There are some positives. Unlike last season when the Falcons were already mathematically eliminated from the playoffs at 3-7, they are still in the division race this season. The entire NFC South is only separated by two games in the loss column. Atlanta closes its season with three straight games against its division rivals.
Also, if you want to look ahead, the Falcons will have more than $140 million in salary-cap space this offseason, the most in the NFL. That will allow Cunningham, Ryan and Stefanski to build the kind of roster they want moving forward. Atlanta could be looking at a top-10 draft pick, as well. The Falcons are currently projected to pick No. 8, a familiar spot, of course, for a franchise that is stuck in a loop. That's where they selected wide receiver Drake London , Robinson and Penix in consecutive years.
Stefanski is not thinking about that right now. Despite trading away starters Jessie Bates III and Ryan Neuzil at the deadline, the Falcons would still love to turn things around and end that eight-year playoff drought. Atlanta heads to face the Minnesota Vikings on the road after the bye.
"With the amount of time that you have [during the bye] and you're not game-planning for the next week, you can really put a fresh set of eyes on it, if you will, and look at areas that we can do better because the truth is we have to do better in multiple areas," Stefanski said. "And then the first part of that is identifying those areas."
Robinson's advice to teammates? Just play more freely. Maybe that's the only way for the Falcons to get out of this rut.
"I told some of the guys, 'Act like it's like street ball out there,'" Robinson said. "You're just free flowing, you know your assignment and just make it happen.
"So that used to be our mentality is just to not worry about anything external, just worry about what we have going on and try to make it better for ourselves and for everybody watching."
author: Marc Raimondi

title: 15 pass catchers you can trust (or not): Should you believe in Diggs, Tyson, Downs?
summary: A look at wide receivers and tight ends who have become start-worthy, and others you should expect less from.
full_text:
With the fantasy football trade deadline looming (Dec. 2), I'll have a column next week on the top candidates to move. So, to build up to the deadline, this is a good opportunity to write about my current trust levels with pass catchers in the league.
These are wide receivers and tight ends who are trending up and those who are starting to lose my trust based on their usage, route deployment and declining production. I'm not saying there are cut candidates in here, as most players still have some level of value, but the point of the column is to give managers the data and analysis they need to make lineup decisions in the critical weeks ahead.
There are 15 players below broken down into four separate categories: pass catchers to trust, not to trust, those to expect less from and also a couple of deeper-league targets.
Stefon Diggs , WR, Washington Commanders
Diggs can still shake coverage. It's on the tape. And he can catch touchdowns, too. Diggs, who has six scoring receptions on the season, now has a TD in three of his past four games. Diggs is also scoring 14.4 fantasy PPG during this stretch, averaging seven targets per game. While Diggs isn't an explosive playmaker at this stage of his career, he has the inside/outside alignment flexibility to gain positive matchups for quarterback Jayden Daniels , plus he is slippery after the catch. With some positive matchups looming (CIN, @ARI, @TEN), I like Diggs as a WR2/flex.
DJ Moore , WR, Buffalo Bills
Moore has been banged up this season, and he has missed time. However, in the five full games Moore has played, he has scored at least 12 fantasy points in four of them, with 16 or more in three. And the one game out of the five full Moore played where he didn't produce double-digit points came in a tough matchup against the Vikings' chaos-creating defense in Week 9. Moore has a touchdown grab in two of his past three games, with a total of three receptions of 20 or more yards during that stretch. Moore has two tougher upcoming matchups (MIA, KC), but as the top target for Josh Allen in Buffalo's explosive offense, he can be trusted as a WR2.
Harold Fannin Jr ., TE, Cleveland Browns
The Browns are on a bye this week, but Fannin should be played in all formats going forward. Fannin, who was started in only 61.2% of ESPN leagues last week, has scored 16.2 fantasy PPG over his last four. And in the three games during that stretch with Deshaun Watson under center, Fannin had at least six targets and 90 yards receiving. Plus, the upcoming schedule, starting in Week 12, is positive (LV, CIN, ATL). Remember, with both Trey McBride and Brock Bowers now working with rookie quarterbacks, Fannin (who is currently TE4 in scoring) has a path to maintain his momentum and finish the season as a top-five tight end.
Parker Washington , WR, Jacksonville Jaguars
Washington's production hasn't been exactly steady (two games with fewer than five points, three with fewer than 15), and he has a catch rate of only 56.3%. However, Washington has scored 28 or more points in two of his past five games, with at least seven targets in four of five. And in coach Liam Coen's offense, the Jags can get Washington in positive one-on-ones, while also scheming open voids in zone coverage. Washington is an easy mover at the release, plus he can scoot after the catch. In this system, with Trevor Lawrence at quarterback, I'd trust Washington as a higher-end WR2.
Jordyn Tyson , WR, New Orleans Saints
Tyson was active last week against the Panthers, only his second game as a pro after suffering a hamstring injury in camp. The rookie first-rounder caught 11 of 13 targets (both team highs), finishing with 80 yards on 32 routes run. Yes, Chris Olave is still the No. 1 option for the Saints, however, Tyson could continue to see more opportunities if teams roll coverage to Olave. Tyson has the high-level playmaking traits to potentially produce breakout weeks. He's a solid fit for coach Kellen Moore's route tree, and his upcoming schedule (@CHI, @CIN, GB, @CAR) could also lead to a heavy passing script for the Saints. Get him in the lineup as a flex.
Josh Downs , WR, Kansas City Chiefs
Patrick Mahomes is going to spread the ball around in Andy Reid's system, which caps the ceiling of his pass catchers. But if you are looking for a player to put in the WR3 or flex spot, Downs looks like a fit. Yes, we have only one game of tape with Downs in a Chiefs uniform (after he was traded from the Colts), but there are a lot of positives after watching him during the win over the Falcons. Downs scored 15.3 points, catching four of five targets for 53 yards (on only eight routes run) and a touchdown on a schemed wheel route. I would expect Downs' usage to climb quickly, as the Chiefs have some big-time upcoming matchups (ARI, @BUF, @LAR, @CIN), plus he has the route traits to uncover for Mahomes at multiple levels of the field.
Jalen Coker , WR, Carolina Panthers
Coker started the season with a career-best 33.8 points in Week 1 versus the Bears, and he caught a total of 16 of 18 targets over his first two games. Since then, Coker has fewer than 10 points in five of seven games played, and he didn't record a reception (on four targets) in the Week 10 win over the Saints. With his low-level production in a struggling Panthers pass game, I can't trust Coker moving forward, despite his physical profile and route traits. He's a deeper-league WR3 at best at this point.
Tyler Warren , TE, Indianapolis Colts

I love the talent and skill set of Warren. That's why I had him ranked as a top-five tight end this summer. However, Warren's production has rapidly declined, as he's scored fewer than 10 fantasy points in three straight games (5.5 PPG). Plus, I don't understand his current route deployment. During this stretch, Warren has seen 20 targets, yet he's averaging only 5.4 air yards per target. He can press the seams, work the corner routes and more. Where is it? This Colts offense (after the trade deadline) has been a rough watch, and Warren's upcoming schedule is daunting (@HOU, @NYG, BYE, PHI). There's a reason he's falling in weekly rankings.
DK Metcalf , Pittsburgh Steelers
I've written about Metcalf before in this space and not much has changed. Yes, Metcalf did score 15.4 fantasy points in the Sunday night loss to the Bengals, cashing in on a fourth-quarter touchdown when the game was in control for Cincy. However, that was only Metcalf's second reception of the night, and he has fewer than 10 points in three of his past five games, despite seeing an average of 7.6 targets in each. With Aaron Rodgers also cooling off, I can't trust Metcalf as more than a boom/bust flex option moving forward.
Emeka Egbuka , WR, Tampa Bay Buccaneers
Egbuka was my guy this summer. I saw breakout potential, but it simply hasn't hit this season. Egbuka missed two games with an injury, and the Bucs have experienced disruption at quarterback due to Baker Mayfield's thumb injury -- and he is questionable again this week (foot). Egbuka (11.1 PPG) has scored fewer than 10 points in two of his last four games, and he has only two touchdown grabs on the season. Another thing working against Egbuka: this Tampa offense has attempted the fewest passes in the league (240). You can still play him, but he needs to remain as a flex option only.
A.J. Brown , WR, New England Patriots
Drake Maye (ankle) could be done for the season and Brown is dealing with yet another injury (hamstring). Brown has played in only four games for the Patriots (6.0 PPG), and he could miss more time. Without Maye, managers must downgrade the entire Patriots pass game with No. 2 Tommy DeVito in line to start in Week 12 versus the Chargers (after the team returns from the bye). When Brown is ready to…
author: Matt Bowen

title: Matchup rankings for Week 11: Why you should start one 49er, but sit another
summary: The most and least favorable matchups in the NFL for this week's games at the four key fantasy positions.
full_text:
Beware the seafaring teams.
The Minnesota Vikings , Seattle Seahawks and Tampa Bay Buccaneers have been head and shoulders the toughest overall matchups for fantasy football opponents all season, and they should be almost universally avoided at this stage. (Sorry, Miami Dolphins , but ... better luck next year?)
In addition to their positional ratings over the past five weeks alone that we'll get to shortly, the Vikings, Seahawks and Buccaneers have been, with one exception, top-seven schedule adjusted defenses against quarterbacks, running backs, wide receivers, WR1s and tight ends. The Buccaneers grant that one exception, ranking 21st for the season against tight ends, so... fire up Sam LaPorta ? (Or don't, for reasons we'll also get to a little later on.)
As we've seen this past week with the once high-flying Green Bay Packers , no one is safe from the dreaded Vikings matchup. None of Jordan Love , Matthew Golden or Christian Watson exceeded 12 fantasy points in Week 10, and over their past five games, only four players reached even the 17-point plateau against the Vikings: Jonathan Taylor (Week 7), Jahmyr Gibbs and Jameson Williams (Week 8) and James Cook III (Week 9).
That's a critical takeaway considering how prominent the Vikings' Week 11 matchup. They'll visit a San Francisco 49ers team that ranks first in total yards per game (399.8) and third in points per game on offense (29.7), and whose starting running back ( Christian McCaffrey ) just scored the season's highest single-game fantasy point total (46.3). It's quite a matchup and in primetime, no less.
This isn't a mandate to bench McCaffrey. But it's that suboptimal matchup that influences lineup strategy. Going more risk/reward from your other lineup spots, fading in Daily Fantasy and certainly steering clear of McCaffrey's teammates where possible ... it's all on the table.
It's a similar case with the Detroit Lions and the aforementioned Gibbs, as they go up against the massively underrated Buccaneers defense. Again, don't sit him and aim to surround him with higher-ceiling, plus-matchup players who can help make up any of the No. 1 fantasy football player's matchup deficiencies.
Here are this week's Matchup Rankings, to help give you a head start on finding those matchup-driven values. If you're curious about the methodology behind these rankings, select here for a handy primer.
Matchups highlight: Tyler Shough , New Orleans Saints (at Chicago Bears ). Though his performance has cooled from his scorching-hot September that had him on the doorstop of weekly fantasy QB1 status, Shough has had his moments thus far as an NFL starter. Since Week 9 of last season, his five game-winning drives are tied for fifth most in the league and he has a better-than-league-average 97.1 passer rating while trailing in the second half or overtime. Shough's moxie under pressure could prove especially advantageous in a Bears matchup -- one that has been extremely favorable for quarterbacks in all game situations -- being that his Saints are 6.5 point underdogs in a game with a 48.5 over/under.
Dak Prescott , Dallas Cowboys (versus Tennessee Titans ) Kirk Cousins , Vikings (at 49ers, "Sunday Night Football")
Matchup to avoid: Brock Purdy , 49ers (versus Vikings, SNF). Where the aforementioned McCaffrey gets a pass on the matchup, Purdy isn't so fortunate. Fantasy's No. 3 quarterback in scoring has fallen into his matchups, as his two 30-plus-point performances came in his two most favorable (ARI, @DAL), while he scored 16.16, his second-worst total all year, in his least favorable (@SEA). And this is a terrible one, against which top-12 quarterbacks (going by points per game) Josh Allen , Jordan Love , Jared Goff and Caleb Williams averaged 10.1 fantasy points with a 12.86 max (Allen's, in Week 9). Additional note: Goff gets an unfavorable Buccaneers matchup this week, but as the QB11 in scoring, he's a lower-tier sit.
"DEF to avoid" and "DEF to exploit" columns rank team defenses in terms of strength of matchup; "Opp.": Week 10 opponent; "Rk": Matchup ranking, where 1 is the toughest defense and 32 is the easiest defense to face; "Adj. FPA": The number of fantasy points that defense added or subtracted from its opponent.
Matchups highlight: Jonah Coleman , Denver Broncos (versus Las Vegas Raiders ). His ascent to the top of the Broncos' depth chart has been quick and decisive. In Weeks 8-9, he played 75% of the offensive snaps and had a 56% rushing share, with which he averaged 19.6 fantasy points. Now fresh off the bye week, Coleman draws a matchup with the Raiders in a game where his Broncos are heavily favored, making him a clear-cut fantasy RB1. The Raiders have seen an opposing running back score in excess of 17 fantasy points in five of their past six games, and in the one in which they didn't, the Seahawks' Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price combined for 20.8 points despite failing to see a single goal-line carry or target.
Tony Pollard , Titans (at Cowboys) Omarion Hampton , Los Angeles Chargers (versus New York Jets ) David Montgomery , Houston Texans (versus Indianapolis Colts , "Thursday Night Football")
Matchup to avoid: Ollie Gordon II , Dolphins (at Buffalo Bills ). Neither Gibbs nor McCaffrey is a sit-him in "Bye-mageddon" Week 11, but Gordon, despite being a difficult player to bench with a depleted positional pool, might as well be. The opposing Bills are scorching hot defensively, limiting opponents to a league-low 9.3 points and second-lowest 232.7 total yards per game in three weeks since their bye, and they held opposing No. 1 running backs to 10.6 fantasy points and 11.3 touches during that time. The Bills began the week 11.5 point favorites, meaning this might be the fourth straight week their opponent faces negative game script.
"DEF to avoid" and "DEF to exploit" columns rank team defenses in terms of strength of matchup; "Opp.": Week 10 opponent; "Rk": Matchup ranking, where 1 is the toughest defense and 32 is the easiest defense to face; "Adj. FPA": The number of fantasy points that defense added or subtracted from its opponent.
Matchups highlight: Carnell Tate , Titans (at Cowboys). It speaks volumes about the poor quality of the defenses that a game featuring two teams with a combined 5-14 record has the week's highest over/under (54.5 points). For the season, the Cowboys have been the fifth most-favorable matchup for an opposing wide receiver (+4.5 Adj. FPA), and sixth most for WR1s (+2.5) and in the past four weeks alone, Makai Lemon , Michael Wilson and Deebo Samuel Sr . has each scored at least 19 fantasy points against them. Tate, who missed the Titans' past two games with a shoulder issue, is expected back in time to assume WR1 duties in this plus matchup. But if he's unable to go, Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike would become WR3/flex options.
Garrett Wilson , Jets (at Chargers) George Pickens , Cowboys (versus Titans) Stefon Diggs , Washington Commanders (versus Cincinnati Bengals , Monday Night Football)
Matchup to avoid: Emeka Egbuka , Buccaneers (at Lions). The Lions, specifically against wide receivers, have one of the most interesting early-season/recent splits I've seen in recent memory. From Weeks 1-5, their Adj. FPA was +8.3, second-most in the league. In five weeks (and four games) since, that number is minus-9.0 and is third fewest . That coincides with the healthy return of Brian Branch , granting the Lions more opportunities to key on the opposing No. 1 receiver. WR1s have averaged only 8.5 fantasy points and 6.5 targets against the Lions the past four weeks, and Egbuka's team-leading 28% target share when he's on the field makes him their probable focal point defensively.

title: Kyle Shanahan on the Brian Flores defense: "It's not just a fad"
summary: 49ers coach says the Minnesota defense puts pressure on everyone involved.
full_text: '' 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan has never beaten a Brian Flores defense. Which might be the most impressive thing that can be said about the Brian Flores defense. They meet again on Sunday night in Mexico City, when Shanahan's 49ers play the Vikings, whose defense is coordinated by Flores. “He's more unique than all the other 31 guys," Shanahan told reporters on Wednesday regarding Flores. "He's the one guy who commits to this and it's not just a fad for these nine games or whatever. He's been doing it his whole time in Minnesota. He did the same thing in Miami. He's as good as it gets at that stuff. "Anybody who lives in that world as much as he does, it's usually a matter of time. I think offensive coaches used to like to say that early on, but it's too many years of it and it’s too many games in this year that they're sound. They put so much pressure on the quarterback, the play-caller, the O-Line, the receivers, on everybody. A lot of times when you go into an NFL game, the pressure's really on people on third down and stuff like that because those are things where everything can come and when you play against Brian it's 70-straight plays of that.” It's not easy to beat in part because it's almost impossible to simulate in practice. As Devin McCourty has said, you think you have a plan and then the game starts and everything changes. It changes in part because Flores seems to be constantly self-scouting and adjusting, defying the films to create pressure in new ways. The goal is to eliminate the offense's built-in advantage that comes from knowing what the play will be by creating confusion for the entire offense. Who's rushing? Who's dropping into coverage? Who do I block? If that guy doesn't rush, what do I do? It makes for a compelling chess match, with the 49ers needing to find a way to get the Minnesota defense on its heels. A strong running game is a must. Wearing down the defense physically is required. When inevitable passing situations arise, the quarterback needs to quickly find the open man (if there is one) and get the ball out before the walls close in. Sometimes, they close quickly. The strategy results in plenty of guys getting a free run at the quarterback, forcing a deer-in-the-headlights response — right before impact.
author: Mike Florio

title: Diego Pavia is the first pick in the UFL draft
summary: Quarterback Diego Pavia went unselected in the 2026 NFL draft.
full_text: Quarterback Diego Pavia went unselected in the 2026 NFL draft. Seven months later, Pavia became the first pick in the UFL draft. The Columbus Aviators made Pavia the top selection. It's no surprise. He'll create buzz. He'll sell tickets. At some point, he'll have to show that he can compete with a level of football that isn't all that far below NFL quality. Every year, plenty of UFL players play their way into NFL opportunities. Pavia can, too. He'll get his chance. What he does from there is entirely up to him. Despite finishing second in the 2025 Heisman Trophy voting, no team picked Pavia in April. He initially was invited to participate in the Ravens' rookie minicamp before being added to the 90-man roster on a tryout basis. Pavia participated in the offseason program. He was released not long before the start of training camp. He has had no NFL opportunities since then.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cam Ward: Shift in offensive philosophy "what we all wanted"
summary: Titans head coach Robert Saleh said earlier this week that the Titans recently shifted their offensive philosophy to put more on quarterback Cam Ward's plate over the rest of the season.
full_text: Titans head coach Robert Saleh said earlier this week that the Titans recently shifted their offensive philosophy to put more on quarterback Cam Ward's plate over the rest of the season. Saleh said the move was made "to be fair to Cam" as the team assesses his standing as their quarterback of the future. The early returns have been promising. Ward is 74-of-110 for 716 yards, four touchdowns and two interceptions while also running 12 times for 85 yards. On Wednesday, Ward said "it's a lot more up-pace and what I like" while adding that he isn't the only member of the offense who has been pleased by the change. "It's what we all wanted , though," Ward said, via the team's website. "Because we know what makes us go as an offense, and it is going to continue to do good things for us in the future." The shift in style hasn't resulted in any wins yet, but continued growth from Ward is the likeliest path to the Titans improving on that front as well before the year is out.
author: Josh Alper

title: CB Mike Jackson says he's ready to return to Panthers lineup
summary: The Panthers are set to get a key piece of their secondary back for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
full_text: The Panthers are set to get a key piece of their secondary back for Sunday's game against the Ravens. Mike Jackson has been out since having core muscle surgery after Week 3, but has been back at practice for the last couple of weeks. On Wednesday, Jackson proclaimed himself ready for a return to the lineup as the Panthers try to improve to 5-5 on the season. "I'm game ready, so I'll be out there on Sunday," Jackson said, via Mike Kaye of ESPN.com. The Panthers also lost Jaycee Horn to a quad injury in Week 3 and the dual injuries thinned out the team's cornerback corps. Getting both of their starters back for the stretch run would be a shot in the arm to Carolina's chances of a second straight division title.
author: Josh Alper

title: John Harbaugh: The sacks are going to come for Abdul Carter
summary: Giants linebacker Abdul Carter scores well in a number of metrics that measure pass rush, but that hasn't shown up in the ones that's most obvious to those watching the game.
full_text: ' Giants linebacker Abdul Carter scores well in a number of metrics that measure pass rush, but that hasn't shown up in the ones that's most obvious to those watching the game. Carter has two sacks and eight quarterback hits in nine games this season and he has not had a sack in the team's last four games. Some of that is related to increased double teams coming his way in the wake of Brian Burns's season-ending torn ACL, but any explanation falls short for those who have been wanting to see Carter overwhelm offenses since he joined the Giants as the third overall pick in 2025. On Wednesday, Giants head coach John Harbaugh said "we want sacks" when asked about Carter but that he's confident they'll start to come because of what he sees from Carter's tape. "He's a disruptive guy. I promise you they're accounting for him," Harbaugh said, via a transcript from the team. "And the sacks are just going to come. You've got to go play football. I mean, you can have a bunch of sacks and really not be playing that good too. We've seen that before too. So he's that kind of player. He's a disruptive player. He's a game changer, game wrecker, and I think there's going to be a lot of game wrecks in his future." The Giants face the Jaguars this weekend and that's the start of a tougher run of opponents than the ones they faced thus far. That makes it an ideal time for Carter's effort to translate to the kind of big plays that can swing games in their direction.
author: Josh Alper

title: Myles Price, NFL's top punt returner, shows he can make an impact on Vikings' offense, too
summary: The Vikings have a big weapon on special teams in return man Myles Price, who is leading the league in punt return average, total yards and touchdowns, and is third in the league in both kickoff return average and total yards.
full_text: ' The Vikings have a big weapon on special teams in return man Myles Price, who is leading the league in punt return average, total yards and touchdowns, and is third in the league in both kickoff return average and total yards. But on Sunday against the Packers, Price showed that he can make an impact on offense, too. In the Vikings' win over the Packers, Price got a career-high 33 snaps on offense, and he responded by catching four passes, including the first touchdown of the game on a 38-yard pass from Kirk Cousins. Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell told Paul Allen that the decision to give Price so much playing time was mostly because of injuries to starting receivers Jordan Addison and Jauan Jennings, but with the way Price performed, he'll get more playing time on offense going forward. "We want to continue to find ways to get Myles involved in the offense," O'Connell said. O'Connell said that when the Vikings are as thin at wide receiver as they were on Sunday, there are concerns about getting anyone else injured, and he was worried about seeing Price take hits in the return game. "With all the injuries the other day, we had no way of getting another player up," O'Connell said. "There was not another body to have, so we actually went into the game for the first time since I've been here with four receivers up. Every time Myles returned a ball, you felt like we could be out of 11 personnel altogether here on one play. He did get banged up a couple times, we tried to feature the bigger groupings, and luckily he was able to return." Ultimately, O'Connell believes that when Price has the ball in his hands in the open field, he can make big plays whether on offense or special teams. "Myles is a guy that we feel very strongly about making that last move, making that last man miss, and being able to score," O'Connell said. Expect to see Price do more of that for the rest of the season.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Joe Burrow can become the first QB ever with 4+ touchdowns in 6 consecutive games
summary: Burrow and Peyton Manning are the only QBs ever with 4 TDs in 5 straight games. If Burrow does it again on Monday night, he'll be the first in NFL history to do it in 6 straight games.
full_text: '' Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is on a remarkable streak of four-touchdown games. If he does it again on Monday night, he'll do something no player in NFL history has done before. Burrow has at least four touchdowns (combined running and passing) in each of the last five games. A four-touchdown game against the Commanders on Monday night would give Burrow an all-time NFL record six straight four-touchdown games. Currently, Burrow and Peyton Manning are tied for the record, with five consecutive four-touchdown games. Manning did it in 2004 with the Colts. Burrow's last five games have featured: Four touchdown passes in a 38-18 win over the Steelers. Three touchdown passes and one touchdown run in a 34-17 win over the Falcons. Five touchdown passes and one touchdown run in a 43-36 win over the Titans. Four touchdown passes in a 35-13 win over the Ravens. Four touchdown passes in a 31-24 win over the Dolphins. Burrow is the MVP favorite , and with 2,795 yards and 27 touchdown passes through nine games this season, he's closing in on 3,000 yards and 30 touchdowns, which only four quarterbacks have done within their first 10 games of a season: Tom Brady in 2007, Aaron Rodgers in 2011, Manning in 2013 and 2014, and Patrick Mahomes in 2018. That's good company for a quarterback to be in, and Burrow is playing right now at a level few quarterbacks have ever reached.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Sean Payton won't use Aidan Hutchinson injury as a teaching moment
summary: Lions coach Dan Campbell has made his position clear regarding player celebrations, in the aftermath of defensive end Aidan Hutchinson's season-ending knee injury.
full_text: Lions coach Dan Campbell has made his position clear regarding player celebrations, in the aftermath of defensive end Aidan Hutchinson's season-ending knee injury. Campbell will not tell his players to stop celebrating. Broncos coach Sean Payton agrees with Campbell's position. “I’m kind of with Dan," Payton told reporters. "I saw the final comments. We’re teachers and we’re constantly… But we’re going to walk out of the doors, and there’ve been a lot of celebrations. I’m kind of with Dan there where it’s unfortunate. Two good players got hurt on the same play, and I think that there are a lot of other things that I would put on tape on a Friday, Saturday that are [teaching moments]. That I wouldn’t put that on.” For starters, any non-contact ACL tear quite possibly is the result of a partially torn knee ligament that was on the brink of fully tearing. If Hutchinson's ACL tear hadn't happened when he landed after jumping to celebrate a sack of quarterback Drake Maye, it could have happened on the next play. Or the next. And it's impossible to expect players to not celebrate. A great play is the product of hours of work and effort and discipline, most of which happens away from the public eye. In the arena, with thousands cheering and millions watching on TV, how can the human beings inside the uniforms be expected not to display human emotion? Injuries happen in football. The vast majority happen during a play. Some happen after a play. It's unreasonable to reduce it to none; the players shouldn't be expected to minimize or eliminate the happiness they experience when everything they've done privately culminates in a public moment of achievement.
author: Mike Florio

title: Nick Bosa: I don't think I've played my best football
summary: 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa's only stats in Sunday's 46-40 win over the Cowboys were one quarterback hit, four pressures and three penalties in 34 snaps.
full_text: 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa's only stats in Sunday's 46-40 win over the Cowboys were one quarterback hit, four pressures and three penalties in 34 snaps. It was his fourth consecutive game without a sack, a first in his career. "I think in the past when I was younger, it would eat at me a lot more , just strictly the stat aspects," Bosa said Wednesday, via Nick Wagoner of ESPN. "But now I'm really just focused on the people around me, and if I feel like I'm playing good football, then I really don't care much about the stats. But I don't think I'm playing my best football right now, so that's what gets to me more so than the actual stats." Bosa exited the injury report in Week 10. But he has worked his way back from the torn ACL in his right knee in Week 3 of the 2025 season and a calf injury in Week 3. He has played catch up with new coordinator Raheem Morris' scheme. "I think there's a learning curve and . . . a lot of guys haven't had many reps in the scheme so far," Bosa said. "I'm trying to break it down to the basics and just kind of get back. I missed a year and then missed camp. I kind of took for granted some of the things that I did automatically, and I thought I could just kind of coast and continue to do those things automatically and focus on other things. But I need to, especially with a newer defense, really hone in on the things that made me the player that I am." Bosa's last double-digit sack season was 2023 when he had 10.5. He totaled nine sacks in 14 games in 2024 and two in three games in 2025, with none this season. "I'm not going to make excuses because nobody really cares," Bosa said. "But I'm going to get better and I'm pretty confident in that physically and how I'm playing."
author: Charean Williams

title: Brock Bowers did not practice Wednesday with ankle, quad injuries
summary: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak called tight end Brock Bowers "day-to-day" earlier this week, but Wednesday was not the day.
full_text: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak called tight end Brock Bowers "day-to-day" earlier this week, but Wednesday was not the day. Bowers did not practice with ankle and quadriceps injuries. He left Sunday's game after only 11 snaps with his ankle injury. Bowers has been on the injury report most of the season with hamstring, calf and knee issues. He leads the Raiders with 50 catches, 676 receiving yards and six receiving touchdowns this season. Defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway (stinger) also didn't practice. Defensive tackle Folorunso Fatukasi (toe) and kicker Matt Gay (hip) were limited. Defensive tackle Thomas Booker (ankle) and tight end Ian Thomas (calf) were full participants.
author: Charean Williams

title: Mike Evans, Dre Greenlaw don't practice Wednesday, 49ers hope they can on Thursday
summary: Wide receiver Mike Evans didn't travel with the 49ers for last Sunday's game in Dallas, but he was in Colorado Springs with the team as they prepare for their game against the Vikings in Mexico City.
full_text: Wide receiver Mike Evans didn't travel with the 49ers for last Sunday's game in Dallas, but he was in Colorado Springs with the team as they prepare for their game against the Vikings in Mexico City. Evans remained out of practice due to the Achilles injury that has sidelined him for the last three games. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said that he hopes Evans will be able to get back on the field on Thursday. Linebacker Dre Greenlaw (neck, rest) was also out of practice and Shanahan hopes that he'll be able to work on Thursday as well. Running back Christian McCaffrey and left tackle Trent Williams both had rest days on Wednesday. Safety Ji'Ayir Brown (ankle), linebacker Luke Gifford (chest), cornerback Renardo Green (back), quarterback Mac Jones (illness), defensive end Khalid Kareem (ankle), safety Siran Neal (knee, foot), and cornerback Upton Stout (shoulder, neck) were limited participants. The 49ers listed cornerback Nate Hobbs (adductor), long snapper Jon Weeks (chest), defensive tackle C.J. West (knee), and defensive end Mykel Williams (hand, ankle) as full participants.
author: Josh Alper

title: Steelers-Bengals on Sunday Night Football draws 21.519 million viewers
summary: The game was never competitive.
full_text: '' The game was never competitive. That didn't stop a huge crowd from tuning in. Via Nielsen, Sunday night's blowout win by the Bengals over the Steelers, 38-18, nevertheless averaged 21.519 million viewers. The Bengals took charge from the get-go, and never relented. By halftime, the Bengals led 24-3, and they had outgained the Steelers, 337 yards to 40. By the end of the third quarter, the Bengals had stretched the lead to 31-3. This weekend, the 7-2 Vikings face the 8-1 49ers on Sunday night in Mexico City. The game has massive postseason implications for both teams, and ramifications up and down the NFC playoff tree.
author: Mike Florio

title: Marlon Humphrey apologizes for saying Baltimore is "best at making criminals"
summary: Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey found himself in some hot water for comments he made about Baltimore on Wednesday.
full_text: ''' Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey found himself in some hot water for comments he made about Baltimore on Wednesday. During a since-deleted episode of his podcast , Humphrey said "they’re best at making criminals " when asked what the city is best at making. Humphrey's words were met with an angry response in the city and he tried to walk them back with an apology while speaking to reporters after practice. “As you guys know, I’ve been here my whole career ,” Humphrey said, via Jeff Zrebiec of TheAthletic.com. “Spent lots of offseasons here, welcomed a son here. I’m an investor in the city, an investor in different areas (and) parts of the state. Obviously, I do know the effect that words have, and just would like to apologize for those comments.” Humphrey's apology was noted by Baltimore Mayor Brandon M. Scott, who wondered in a social media post how Humphrey would respond "if prominent Baltimoreans used their platform to imply that Baltimore once produced great defensive backs but we have recently lost our way." Scott added that "a verbal apology is not enough" for those who look up to Ravens players and invited Humphrey to meet with people in the city working on "preventing others from making the mistakes they made."

title: Cam Skattebo says he's done doing backflips after Aidan Hutchinson injury
summary: Giants running back Cam Skattebo's penchant for backflips became a talking point during his recovery from last season's ankle injury, but he resumed doing them after touchdowns upon his return to action this fall.
full_text: Giants running back Cam Skattebo's penchant for backflips became a talking point during his recovery from last season's ankle injury, but he resumed doing them after touchdowns upon his return to action this fall. Skattebo said that those days are now done, however. Skattebo said on Wednesday that he's retiring the celebration in the wake of seeing Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson tear his ACL after a post-sack celebratory leap last Sunday. “It’s hard to see ,” Skattebo said, via Ryan Dunleavy of the New York Post . “I’m saying yeah [no more]. Mentally, I’m like, ‘I’m not doing that.’ That ain’t going to happen to me.” Skattebo did reserve the right to bring the celebration out of retirement "if we go to the playoffs or something," but it seems any touchdowns in the immediate future will be marked with a more reserved reaction.

title: Vikings won't put Jordan Addison on IR

full_text: When Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell announced that wide receiver Jordan Addison needed thumb surgery earlier this week, he said that an injured reserve stint was a possibility. O'Connell offered a positive update on Addison's outlook on Wednesday. Addison had the operation and doctors have given the Vikings hope that he'll be back before missing four games. title: Brian Schottenheimer: Christian Parker still has a bright future with the Cowboys
summary: Brian Schottenheimer confirmed Mike Pettine will take over as the Cowboys' defensive play-caller on Sunday.
full_text: Brian Schottenheimer confirmed Mike Pettine will take over as the Cowboys' defensive play-caller on Sunday. He replaces defensive coordinator Christian Parker, who will retain his title. "Christian Parker is a huge part of what we're trying to build here and that he is our defensive coordinator," Schottenheimer said Wednesday, via Todd Archer of ESPN. "He is our leader. He is not changing any of those things, but I do feel that in the best interest of winning that Pet's calling the game is going to help us get to where we want to get to." Schottenheimer said Parker would continue running meetings and leading walkthroughs, but the Cowboys needed "a different perspective" on game day. Parker, 34, arrived in January as a first-time play caller, leaving Philadelphia after two seasons as the Eagles' defensive passing game coordinator. The Cowboys, though, rank last in yards (393.8), last in run defense (154.1) and last in third-down defense (48.8 percent). They are 30th in scoring (28.2). Pettine arrived before Week 5 as a senior defensive assistant to help Parker, whom he brought into the NFL with the Packers in 2019. He was defensive coordinator with the Jets, when Schottenheimer was on staff, and also served in that role with the Bills and Packers. Pettine was head coach of the Browns from 2014-15. "When I look at this situation, we're all committed to trying to get it right," Schottenheimer said, "and so we're making adjustments like we've made. We've made adjustments. We've adjusted some scheme. We've adjusted some personnel. We've adjusted some play time. This is just another adjustment where we're trying to get right." Schottenheimer made clear several times that he still believes in Parker and still believes Parker has a future with the Cowboys. "CP has a very, very bright future as a coach, but more specifically, a very bright future here as our defense coordinator," Schottenheimer said.

The Chargers were favored in the first two weeks of the season, by 9.5 against the Cardinals in Week 1 and by 6.5 against the Chargers in Week 2. They lost both games by 12, and since then they've been underdogs every week. This is the ninth time this season the Jets have been underdogs. They were last favored in Week 7, when they were favored by four points over the Dolphins but lost 28-25. In a game between two of the worst teams in the league, someone has to win, and the betting odds say that someone will be the Chargers.
