title: Agent's Take: Breaking down Dolphins' historic dead money and where they go from here
summary: Miami's $188.88 million in dead money is unprecedented, but a number the Dolphins felt was necessary to rebuild
full_text:
NFL teams have become increasingly comfortable with significant amounts of dead money, meaning salary cap charges for players that are no longer on a team's roster. Just look at the Miami Dolphins .
Under general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan and head coach Jeff Hafley, who were both previously with the Green Bay Packers before being hired in January, the team is taking dead money to an extreme. The new regime has an unprecedented $188.88 million in dead money as of Week 10's loss to the Indianapolis Colts .
However, there's a method to Sullivan's madness as the Dolphins are in teardown mode after a 7-10 record in 2025 with a high-priced roster.
"There are two philosophies that you can subscribe to in the National Football League: You pay as you go or you're living on credit," Sullivan said during the offseason. "If we keep living on credit, we're never going to get healthy. …We can't get there unless we kind of take it on the chin this year. We're not going to live like this every year. But this year we had to move like this to get back within a healthy salary cap."
Miami's $188.88 million is easily the most dead money in NFL history for a league year. The record-breaking amount has put the Dolphins at a distinct financial and competitive disadvantage, so it's no surprise that Miami is in a three-way race with the Los Angeles Chargers and the Tennessee Titans for the first overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft . Each team has a 1-8 record.
So where does Miami go from here with its mess of dead money? Let's dive in.
Miami's $188.88 million in dead money is on par with the league-wide salary cap in 2019, which was $188.2 million (the current salary cap is $301.2 million). Each team's actual salary cap (known as the adjusted salary cap) typically differs from the NFL's set amount because unused cap room can be carried over from one year to the next, and other adjustments can further increase or decrease cap space.
The Dolphins have a $308.878 million adjusted salary cap for 2026, and dead money takes up an unheard-of 61.15% of that number. Just under $120 million in cap space is available for the actual roster, thanks to dead money. Essentially, the Dolphins are building a team this year under salary cap constraints from 15 years ago — the league-wide salary cap was $120.375 million in 2011 following 2010's uncapped year.
Most of Miami's dead money comes from just a handful of players. The Dolphins have four of 2026's biggest dead-money charges from the following players (league ranking is in parentheses):
Inside Tua's dead money: As expected, the new regime went in a different direction at quarterback. Tagovailoa was benched and demoted to third-string quarterback by former Dolphins head coach Mike McDaniel after 14 games last season. He had three years remaining on the four-year, $212.4 million contract extension averaging $53.1 million per year, signed in July 2024, when he was released in March with a post-June 1 designation.
The total dead money for parting ways with Tagovailoa is $99.2 million, a record for dead money associated with a single-player contract. The post-June 1 designation allows the Dolphins to take Tagovailoa's $99.2 million of dead money over two years, 2026 and 2027. Only the current year's prorated bonus amount counts toward the cap for players released with a post-June 1 designation. The acceleration in future contract years is delayed until the following league year (2027 in this case), which will begin next March 11.
The dead money for Tagovailoa is so much because his $54 million base salary (for 2026) was fully guaranteed. Now, prior to his release, the Dolphins decided to avoid his 2026 dead money from reaching $67.4 million. The team exercised an option for a dummy/voiding 2030 contract year by making a $15 million payment (i.e., an option bonus). Once it did so, the option bonus was prorated to $3 million annually against Miami's salary cap from 2026 through 2030. The dead money charges would have been $67.4 million in 2026 and $31.8 million in 2027 if the option had not been exercised, instead of the actual $55.4 million and $43.8 million.
The Dolphins got minimal cap relief from releasing Tagovailoa. His 2026 cap number was $56.3 million, freeing up $867,647 of cap space.
The $55.4 million in 2026 is a record for dead money tied to an individual player in a single league year. It's also a little over $7 million more than 2026's highest cap number, held by Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford at $48.3 million.
Tyreek Hill: Next up was Hill. His $51.1 million 2026 cap number was untenable even before the gruesome left knee injury he suffered early in the 2025 season. Hill was released before a $5 million roster bonus was due on the third day of the 2026 league year (March 13) and $11 million of his unsecured $29.9 million 2026 base salary became fully guaranteed. That resulted in $22.9 million in 2026 cap savings.
There's only one 2026 wide receiver cap hit bigger than Hill's: Chris Godwin 's $33.7 million with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .
Jaylen Waddle: Waddle and a 2026 fourth-round pick were dealt to the Denver Broncos for a 2026 first-round pick (30th overall), a 2026 third-round pick, and a 2026 fourth-round pick. The Dolphins escaped the three-year, $84.75 million extension, which made Waddle the NFL's highest-paid No. 2 wide receiver at $28.25 million per year upon signing in June 2024. The Dolphins lost $11.60 million of 2026 cap space from trading Waddle, considering he was counting $11.63 on Miami's books before he was dealt.
Jalen Ramsey: Ramsey's $20.9 million comes from a June 2025 trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers, where the Dolphins acquired safety Minkah Fitzpatrick and a 2027 fifth-round pick for him, tight end Jonnu Smith, and a 2027 seventh-round pick. Since the trade occurred after June 1, the prorated bonus amount from Ramsey's 2026 through 2028 contract years became 2026 cap charges.
These four players combined account for just under $127.5 million of the dead money. That's slightly over two-thirds of the Dolphins' total amount.
The Dolphins have three other dead-money charges over $10 million: safety Minkah Fitzpatrick ($13 million), edge rusher Bradley Chubb ($11 million) and offensive tackle Terron Armstead ($10.7 million). Collectively, those seven players are responsible for a little less than $162.5 million (or 86%) of Miami's dead money.
The only significant cash from Miami's dead money is Tagovailoa's. That's $52.9 million rather than $54 million because his salary guarantee has an offset clause allowing the Dolphins to reduce the money owed to him. It's reduced by the one-year contract he signed with the Atlanta Falcons at his $1.215 league minimum salary. The other six major dead money charges are just prorated bonus amounts.
The Dolphins made one important free-agent acquisition with their limited budget. The new regime signed Malik Willis , who was Green Bay's backup quarterback to replace Tagovailoa. Willis signed a three-year, $67.5 million contract with $45 million fully guaranteed in March. At $22.5 million per year, Willis is quite affordable for a starting quarterback, although he is the Dolphins' highest-paid player.
The 2025 average salary for starting quarterbacks, excluding those on rookie contracts which are strictly determined by draft position, was slightly over $44 million per year according to NFLPA data. Willis' 2026 cap number is $5.7 million.
There was some speculation that Willis could be benched before landing on injured reserve with a groin injury from Week 9's loss to the Detroit Lions . Surgery may be required, which would likely end Willis' season.
The Dolphins have 14 players on one-year contracts this season. The largest is tight end Greg Dulcich 's worth $3.25 million. The other 13 are at or slightly above league minimum salary.
The teardown didn't preclude the Dolphins from extending the contracts of key veteran players. Sullivan identified running back…
author: Joel Corry

title: With Kyle Shanahan and Brian Flores, Vikings-49ers will be a matchup for the modern NFL
summary: The winner of the battle between Kyle Shanahan and Brian Flores could define what the NFL becomes schematically
full_text:
In the long-running anime One Piece, there's an incident at the World Government headquarters, Marineford, known as "The War of the Best." The strongest pirates in the world of One Piece fought the strongest Marines the World Government had to offer, and it ultimately became the most important arc in the One Piece world, shaping the direction of the story that's still being told today.
In the NFL , it feels like we have a game every year that is similar to War of the Best -- two titans facing off against each other, where the outcome will shape the next wave of the NFL on both sides of the ball:
Kyle Shanahan vs. the Legion of Boom in 2016.
Sean McVay vs. Vic Fangio, then Bill Belichick, in that year's Super Bowl .
Andy Reid vs. Lou Anarumo in the second half of the 2022 AFC Championship.
Sean McVay vs. Mike Macdonald last season.
This year, the new NFL meta will be defined Sunday night in Mexico City, where the San Francisco 49ers and Shanahan will face the Minnesota Vikings and defensive coordinator Brian Flores in one of the most anticipated matchups of the year. Both the Niners' offense and Vikings' defense are resetting what their respective sides can and should do, and seeing which side blinks first could be a blueprint for how offenses and defenses attack each other in the near future.
If we recall a story I wrote earlier this season , NFL teams are blitzing at an astronomical rate. Over ten weeks, defenses league-wide have a 32.3% blitz rate, the second-highest since 2010 and one of only four seasons with a blitz rate over 30% (2011, 2013, and 2010). The number jumps even higher when teams go under center to an astounding 50.5%, the highest since 2010 and the only season TruMedia has recorded in that time period with a blitz rate over 50% against under-center offenses. When these defenses blitz, they have a 54.9% defensive success rate overall, and that number drops to 50.1% when offenses are under center.
At the forefront of this are Flores and the Minnesota Vikings, who are redefining what it means to be aggressive. The Vikings currently sit with an absurd 72.6% blitz rate, by far the highest for any team through 10 weeks since 2010. In fact, you have to go all the way back to the 2006 Miami Dolphins to find a team that went higher than that (what was Nick Saban cooking in 2006?). The way that Minnesota can dictate the flow of not only a play, but the entire game through their pressure looks that completely stymie opposing offenses.
The Vikings are essentially playing rock-paper-scissors on every play, daring you to throw anything other than rock. One way they can dictate the flow is by forcing teams to leave extra pass protectors in to help against pressure looks.
Imagine you're Packers quarterback Jordan Love . You come to the line of scrimmage, and this is what you see:
The alarm bells are ringing. This is the most obvious Cover 0 all-out blitz look, eight guys up at the line of scrimmage. The common answer for the Packers and Love has been to keep the RB and TE in the protection, calling it max protection. This is the Packers throwing rock, hoping to catch the Vikings in a Cover 0 look and hit them for an explosive.
The Vikings actually spin everyone out of this except the four defensive linemen and run Cover 3, frazzling Jordan Love before he ends up throwing it 10 yards short of the first-down marker on third down. The Vikings got the Packers to throw rock, then they throw paper.
This ability to force offenses to keep seven people in to protect the QB is unprecedented at the NFL level. According to Sumer Sports, the 2026 Vikings are facing dropbacks where all five eligible receivers are out to catch a pass on 35.7% of their dropbacks, the lowest in the NFL by a significant margin. They're the only team in the NFL below 50% in that metric, with the New York Giants in second place…at 58.5%! Flores and the defense force offenses to play a completely different sport when they play Minnesota, using pressure to dictate the terms of the passing game. They force you to waste backs and tight ends in pass protection, then force you to play with a hand behind your back.
If you want to get four out in the passing concept, good luck, because that doesn't work either.
Welcome to hell https://t.co/dEC8w0gUok pic.twitter.com/QVqDriBZlP
You're probably wondering, "Yes, the Vikings defense is amazing, but what does that have to do with the 49ers and how this will decide the state of NFL schematics?" The answer lies in the protection plans. The Vikings see the lowest amount of five-out in the passing concept in the NFL. Well, guess which team leads the NFL in percentage of dropbacks with all five eligible receivers out in the passing concept? That's right, Kyle Shanahan and the San Francisco 49ers.
I'd describe the Niners' offense as "malleable." They can use multiple players in multiple ways, keeping their best players on the field while putting linebackers in a blender. They do that by getting all five guys out in the passing concept. If we include chip blocks, the Niners get all five eligibles out at an 80.1% clip, the highest in the NFL (not including chips, that number drops to 60.8%, second in the NFL behind the Pittsburgh Steelers ). Against pressure looks where linebackers are mugged, or showing that they're blitzing, the 49ers like to get everyone into the concept and spread teams out. The Niners (and Bengals as well) are zagging when everyone else is zigging, spreading out and getting five eligibles into the concept against the blitz.
With simulated pressures, there's always a law of equivalent exchange: for every guy you add, a guy has to drop. For most defenses to stay structurally intact while showing these pressures in two-high shells, someone has to drop from the defensive line. Shanahan knows this, and knows he has the personnel to live in five-out looks (we'll get to that later). If we're going to the rock, paper, scissors comparison again, the Niners are choosing to throw paper instead of rock, because if they can find the weakest point in the pressure, they'll hammer it.
This 3rd down against the Cowboys is a great example. Dallas lines up in a pressure look that has seven at the line of scrimmage. The Niners see this and have five guys as eligible route runners. Instead of checking into max protection, they stay with what they have, giving RB Christian McCaffrey a choice route on the backside. Cowboys spin out and drop into Cover 2, but CMC has already found the hole, and Brock Purdy finds him to move the chains.
DAL comes out with 7 up at the LOS on 3rd down, but drop everyone into the coverage. SF gets 5 out into the look, and run CMC on a choice route underneath that picks up the first down. Their ability to get 5 out into the concept is huge against pressure looks pic.twitter.com/L9sYfVOUuJ
This touchdown for McCaffrey against the Raiders is another way that the 49ers can undress the pressure looks by getting five receivers out into the concept. San Francisco motions FB Kyle Juszczyk into the backfield, then bumps him out right before the snap. The Raiders' secondary bumps with him, then sends the blitz while dropping the 2 DTs. However, LB Quay Walker hesitates just a little bit on his blitz, giving McCaffrey enough time to get wide open.
The reason the 49ers can live this way is not only because of Kyle Shanahan, but because of the personnel on the field. LT Trent Williams is a mute button at left tackle. Having him on the field lets the rest of the line slide the other way and leave Williams on an island. Having McCaffrey also helps in a big way: a guy who can run the offense as well as anyone and run choice routes against zone coverage. But this all comes together because of Brock Purdy and his ability to create out of structure. If the Niners go to five-man protection, and there's someone hot off the edge, Purdy is trusted to make them miss and extend the play. That's why he became the starter in the first place: he can…
author: JP Acosta

title: NFL Week 11 upset alert: Two straight losses for Steelers? Can Titans shock Cowboys?
summary: The Jets could also send the Chargers back into the loss column
full_text:
As expected, following a Week 9 where favorites owned the slate, underdogs bit back in Week 10. In turn, we were fortunate enough to pinpoint a trio of them in our five upset alert picks last week, so you had a peek behind the curtain on those favorites falling if you were with us.
We accurately highlighted the Commanders chances of heading into MetLife Stadium and beating the Giants , the new-look Vikings beating the Packers at Lambeau Field now that Kirk Cousins is in the fold, and Carolina taking down the Saints at the Superdome. We whiffed on the Patriots and Steelers as possible upset candidates, but three out of five ain't too shabby if you ask us.
Now, we turn our attention to Week 11, which is sort of a wonky slate. On top of featuring the fewest number of games (13) as six teams are on the bye, it also includes some hefty spreads. As of Wednesday morning, when this is being written, there are five double-digit spreads, including favorites like the Chiefs and Bills, who are laying over two touchdowns. That makes it a little more difficult to find those potential upsets, but they're there, and we've highlighted five favorites who could fall by the time Week 11 concludes.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
The Cowboys play up or down depending on the competition. This season, their defense has remained abysmal, ranking last in the NFL in total yards allowed per game (393.8) and in rushing yards allowed per game (154.1). That last figure could be a key factor in Tennessee's chances of pulling off the upset. Tony Pollard , who began his career with the Cowboys in 2019, could enact some revenge on his former team as he's been one of the hottest running backs in the NFL as of late. Over his last three games, Pollard has rushed for 279 yards, recorded 112 receiving yards, and totaled six touchdowns. Last week, the 49ers ran for 214 yards and three touchdowns against the Cowboys' defense.
Sure, the change from Christian Parker to Mike Pettine as the defense play-caller could give Dallas a boost, but it might not be an immediate change. If Tennessee can continue to find success on the ground with Pollard in a favorable matchup, a ball-dominant game script could be the recipe for a shocking upset.
Meanwhile, AT&T Stadium hasn't been too kind to the Cowboys either, allowing 31.8 points per game over their last six games in which they are 1-5.
Yes, Baker Mayfield is at risk of missing this game due to a foot injury. However, Jalon Daniels is no stranger to coming in under duress for Mayfield, as he's already made three starts this season. That includes an upset win on the road against Dallas in Week 5. Moreover, Mayfield hasn't been lights-out this season, ranking fourth-worst in EPA per dropback among qualified QBs through Week 10 since 2000. He also has a league-worst 28% completion rate on throws of 15-plus air yards this season. That isn't meant to dump on Mayfield per se, but to highlight that Tampa might be able to win this game regardless of who is under center.
After all, the Buccaneers are a run-first offense this season, leading the league in rushing yards per game (163.9) and tied for the lead in yards per rush (5.0). Meanwhile, the defense is allowing the fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL (79.1), which will be particularly helpful as they look to contain a high-octane Lions offense that's spearheaded by Jahmyr Gibbs . When it comes to the Lions' passing attack, Jared Goff has been a little loose with the football, throwing an interception in three straight games entering Week 11. That could also play into Tampa Bay's hands as its 16 interceptions in the season lead the league.
The Lions are also in a tough spot regarding the scheduling of this game. The Bucs will be well-rested after their bye, while Detroit returns from an international game in Munich, Germany, in Week 10.
The Chargers finally got into the win column on Monday after taking down the Ravens in Baltimore. However, a winning streak might not be in the cards for L.A. as they host the Jets. On top of playing on a short week, it's still hard to buy into the Chargers at this point. The loss might speak more to where the Ravens are at currently without Lamar Jackson than L.A. turning a corner. In that victory on Monday, they were just 2-for-13 on third down while Justin Herbert didn't light it up through the air either, tossing for 129 yards, no touchdowns, and no picks. This is still not a great football team.
The Jets aren't that much better, but I did think they gave Buffalo a game in the first half of their Week 10 defeat before things fell off over the final two quarters. Geno Smith was also in and out of the lineup due to injury, but reportedly is on the mend and should play on Sunday. They have enough talent on both sides of the ball to absolutely go into SoFi Stadium and walk away with a win.
The international tour for the NFL brings us to Mexico City this week for a primetime doozy between the Vikings and 49ers. Given how well both of these teams have played this season, this could very well be an NFC Championship preview.
While his numbers didn't jump out of the box score, I thought Kirk Cousins was sharp in his first game back with the Vikings after being acquired at the trade deadline. He gives the Minnesota offense some much-needed stability under center, and it's no surprise to see them post their second-highest scoring day of the season with him in the fold. This will be an opportunity for Cousins to bounce back against San Francisco, as he threw three interceptions against them back in Week 9 when he was still quarterbacking the Raiders . Some could see that poor showing as a bad sign for Cousins, but you can also see it as him having very recent familiarity with how they plan to attack him.
Of course, the true main event for this game will be Minnesota's defense against the 49ers offense. The Vikings are the best scoring defense (14.0 PPG allowed) in the NFL this season, while San Francisco is the second-best scoring offense (31.2 PPG). This is also a historically great matchup in the red zone, with the Vikings defense holding opponents to a 25% touchdown rate in the red area while the 49ers are scoring touchdowns on 83% of their trips. Both are the best of any team in a season since 2000.
This shows how razor-thin the margins are in this game, and it might be worth simply going with the underdog in Minnesota for value. It's also worth noting that Brock Purdy is 0-2 in his career against the Vikings, with his teams averaging 17 points per game as he's committed four turnovers.
History is not on the Steelers' side in this matchup, as they've lost 11 straight road games against the Eagles. The last time they won was back in 1965 at Franklin Field. Given the slew of injuries that have impacted Philly this season (namely to quarterback Jalen Hurts ), this could present a golden opportunity to snap that streak, but it's certainly not an automatic, considering how Pittsburgh looked on Sunday night.
The Bengals steamrolled the Steelers in primetime. While Joe Burrow can make any defense look foolish, the big concern for Pittsburgh was its inability to do anything on offense. They managed just 18 points and averaged 3.8 yards per play. If that's who they are in this matchup against the Eagles, Joe Milton and Co. will be able to hang around.
Philadelphia will also be well-rested for this matchup after its bye. Over his tenure as head coach, Nick Sirianni is 5-0 in his regular-season career coming off the bye.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: 49ers might have just outsmarted the Vikings with unique travel plan for Week 11 NFC showdown in Mexico City
summary: The 49ers-Vikings game will be held at an elevation of almost 7,400 feet. The two teams are taking an opposite approach with their preparation
full_text:
For the second time this season, the San Francisco 49ers are set to play an international game, and once again, their travel schedule could end up being a key factor in the game's outcome.
Back in Week 1, the 49ers were sent to Australia to play the Rams , and the two teams took opposite approaches to travel. The 49ers headed to Melbourne a full week before the game while the Rams showed up just 24 hours before kickoff. By the time the game kicked off, the 49ers were fully acclimated to the 17-hour time difference, and it showed: San Francisco won 27-7.
The 49ers outsmarted the Rams with their travel plan in Week 1, and they might try to do the same this week against the Vikings in Mexico City.  Mexico's capital creates a unique challenge for NFL teams because it sits at an elevation of about 7,350 feet. To put that in perspective, Denver has the highest altitude of any NFL city at 5,280 feet, over a quarter-mile of elevation below what the 49ers and Vikings will be dealing with in Mexico.
When you're playing at an altitude that high, it's not easy to get acclimated, so the 49ers have decided to spend their entire practice week in Colorado Springs at Air Force Academy's Falcon Stadium, which sits at 6,621 feet .
Niners coach Kyle Shanahan was raised in Denver, so he knows how difficult it can be to adjust to high altitude, which is why he decided to move the team's base to Colorado this week.
"I think it helps," Shanahan said this week, when discussing practice at a higher altitude. "I grew up mainly in Denver, and I always know how bad it would be for me. It didn't matter how good a shape you're in. Like, when I came home from college, you'd run up the stairs and be out of breath. It takes some time to get used to it. It just is what it is with altitude. I know when you go to play in Denver, it's always a challenge, and I know Mexico City's higher than Denver. It's not make-or-break by any means, but I do think it makes you a couple percent better."
The 49ers have shown that they're willing to adjust their travel plan for the chance to be a "couple percent" better. They did it for Australia, and now, they're doing it for this trip. This will mark the NFL's first game in Mexico City since 2022, and the 49ers also played in that game. Four years ago, they also spent a full week in Colorado before heading to Mexico, and it apparently helped, because they ended up beating the Cardinals 38-10.
On the Vikings' end, they won't be making any changes to their practice location to prepare for the high altitude in Mexico. Instead, the Vikings will spend the week at their practice facility in Eagan, Minnesota, which sits at an altitude of 945 feet.
Minnesota might not be adjusting its travel schedule, but the team did install an altitude chamber to help players acclimate.
Rather than leaving Minnesota to train at altitude before Sunday night’s game in Mexico City, the Vikings built an altitude chamber in Eagan, where players can get familiar with the effects of working in thinner air before Sunday’s game at 7,200 feet (photos courtesy of the… pic.twitter.com/b9FWMF3KxJ
The chamber allows the players to get a workout in at a "high" altitude, but riding a stationary bike or running on a treadmill isn't exactly the same thing as practicing actual football.
Defensive coordinator Brian Flores previously coached a game in Mexico City as a member of the Patriots ' coaching staff in 2017 — a game New England won 33-8 over the Raiders — so he has some first-hand experience with what the trip will be like. During an interview on Tuesday, Flores admitted he'll probably have to change his substitution patterns since the high altitude will likely cause his players to get winded faster.
"There's less oxygen, it's a tough place to play," Flores said of Mexico City . "It's certainly taxing. As a staff, we're already talking about, 'Hey, we're going have to rotate these guys and everybody's going to have to be ready to play.' And so, yeah, it's certainly something that we're going to have to deal with."
Flores has faced Shanahan three times as a head coach or defensive coordinator, and he's won all three games, but this presents a different challenge. The Vikings have had the best defense in the NFL this year, but it will be interesting to see if the altitude changes that. If the defense is winded, it will be tough for them to keep up with San Francisco's offense.
Although the 49ers should be acclimated to the altitude by the time they arrive in Mexico City, the same can't be said for Minnesota. The Vikings will be stealing a page from the Rams' playbook when it comes to traveling this week. The Rams showed up in Australia one day before the game, and that's exactly what the Vikings plan on doing, with the team arriving on Saturday .
This a huge game that could ultimately decide the No. 1 seed in the NFC and the 49ers have decided not to leave anything to chance. The 49ers and Vikings kick off at 8:20 p.m. ET on Sunday night in what will be the final international game of the NFL season.
author: John Breech

title: Why Jaguars' Trevor Lawrence has legitimate 2026 NFL MVP case, is destined to win one at some point
summary: Across Lawrence's last 17 regular season games, he has 15-plus wins and 45-plus TD. He is only 1 of 10 QBs to achieve that feat
full_text:
Entering the 2026 NFL season, Jacksonville Jaguars Pro Bowl quarterback Trevor Lawrence was underrated . With the Jaguars off to a 7-2 start and first place in the AFC South division once again, the secret's out: Lawrence is a legitimate NFL MVP candidate.
Yes, it may be weird to read the words "NFL MVP candidate" next to the quarterback of the Jaguars, which is understandable. Jacksonville is the only current franchise in the league that has never had a player receive a first-place MVP vote. However, Lawrence is performing like an MVP-caliber quarterback for a Jaguars team whose 7-2 record is tied for the next-best record in the NFL, behind only the 8-1 San Francisco 49ers and the 8-1 Buffalo Bills . It's just the third time in franchise history the Jaguars have started 7-2 or better through their first nine games, and the first time since 1999, according to Stathead. Among qualified quarterbacks, Lawrence ranks top-five in the league in pass yards per attempt, passing touchdowns, passer rating, success rate, and EPA (expected points added) per dropback, plus a top-10 finish in touchdown-to-interception ratio and completion percentage, per NFL Next Gen Stats.
Expected points added (EPA) per dropback
That's why DraftKings Sportsbook is currently giving him the fourth-best odds (+550) to take home the NFL MVP hardware entering Week 11. The only three players with better odds are Joe Burrow (-125), Josh Allen (+370), and Brock Purdy (+450). However, Lawrence is also racking up eye-popping numbers in an offense without any other established NFL stars, unlike the three quarterbacks ahead of him. Burrow has five-time Pro Bowler Ja'Marr Chase and Pro Bowler Tee Higgins at wide receiver, plus four-time Pro Bowler Orlando Brown Jr. at left tackle. Allen has 2025 NFL rushing champion James Cook at running back and five-time Pro Bowler Dion Dawkins at left tackle. Purdy has 2023 NFL Offensive Player of the Year Christian McCaffrey at running back, seven-time Pro Bowler George Kittle at tight end, and arguably the best left tackle in the NFL since 2010 in 12-time Pro Bowler Trent Williams .
Close your eyes and think. Who is the most accomplished Jacksonville offensive player outside of Lawrence? Running back Bhayshul Tuten is in just his second NFL season and his first as a lead back. No. 1 wide receiver Parker Washington , a 2023 sixth-round pick, is in his fourth NFL season and has never recorded a 1,000-yard receiving season -- he is well on pace to do so for the first time in 2026 with 645 yards receiving in the first 9 games of the year, which ranks 16th in the league. None of his offensive linemen have ever earned a Pro Bowl selection. Lawrence is uplifting a cast of solid, budding young talent and producing at an elite level similar to, or better than in some metrics, the other quarterbacks up for NFL MVP through 10 weeks.
This first-half performance in 2026 isn't a fluke either. Once Lawrence adjusted to coach Liam Coen's scheme halfway through 2025, their first season together, he led the entire NFL in total touchdowns with 24 across the last eight games of the 2025 regular season, a span in which Jacksonville went a perfect 8-0 to finish 13-4 and win the AFC South. Lawrence's 38 total touchdowns ranked as the third-most in football last season behind only the league's last two MVP winners: Matthew Stafford (46) and Josh Allen (39). That's how he finished fifth in 2025 NFL MVP voting, behind only Stafford, Drake Maye , Allen, and McCaffrey last season.
Across the final six games of the 2025 season, Lawrence produced a ridiculous 19 total touchdowns to just one turnover. That feat made him just the third player in NFL history to record 19-plus total touchdowns and one or fewer turnovers in the final six games of a season. The other two players to do so are 2019 Drew Brees (20 total touchdowns to one turnover) and 2020 NFL MVP Aaron Rodgers (21 total touchdowns to one turnover). Combining the second half of last season and the first half of this season, Lawrence has 15 wins and 45 total touchdowns in his last 17 regular-season games. He's been one of the NFL's best for the last year's worth of regular-season games.
* Minimum 4 starts in span
How rare is 15-plus wins and 45-plus total touchdowns in a 17-game span? According to CBS Sports Research, Lawrence is just the 10th quarterback in league history to do it, and the previous 9 all won NFL MVP honors at some point in their storied careers.
15-plus wins and 45-plus TDs in a 17-game span, NFL history
* All won NFL MVP in their career besides Lawrence
It will likely take Lawrence repeating his second-half effort from 2025 once again in 2026 to swipe the league MVP award out of Burrow's hands, but there's a chance he could do just that. If 2026 isn't the year Lawrence takes home NFL MVP honors, it's coming in the not-so-distant future.
author: Garrett Podell

title: Cowboys make defensive coaching changes, name Mike Pettine as play caller as struggles continue
summary: Christian Parker will remain on as the defensive coordinator, at least in title
full_text:
Three days after surrendering 584 yards — most ever in a home game — in a 46-40 loss to the 49ers , the Cowboys are making a big change in their defensive coaching responsibilities. Senior defensive analyst Mike Pettine will call defensive plays for Dallas, starting this weekend against the Titans , though first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker will retain his job, CBS Sports' Garrett Podell has confirmed .
Sunday's performance was far from a one-off, as Dallas' defense ranks last in yards per game allowed (393.8), tied for last in points per game allowed (28.2) and 31st in yards per play allowed (6.2).
Against San Francisco, Dallas gave up three plays of 50+ yards — all for touchdowns. On the season, Dallas has allowed nine plays of 50+ yards, four more than any other team.
Monday, coach Brian Schottenheimer said the organization was "still in the process of going through all the film and evaluation" when asked about a change at defensive coordinator. Team owner Jerry Jones then hinted at a potential change Tuesday.
"We're talking about that, but I'm not going to talk about that here, but we are talking about those things," Jones said Tuesday on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas on Tuesday, via The Dallas Morning News .
Dallas is currently 4-6, with the defense largely to blame. The Cowboys' offense, in stark juxtaposition to the defense, ranks top 10 in yards per game, points per game and points per drive. After entering the season with high expectations, Dallas is fighting to simply stay in the playoff race, two games behind the Giants in the lowly NFC East.
The Cowboys initially brought Pettine, 60, aboard last month after Dallas' slow start on defense. He has not called plays since 2020, when he was the Packers ' defensive coordinator. Green Bay finished ninth in total defense and 12th in scoring defense that year. Since then, he has bounced around, spending 2021 as a senior defensive assistant with the Bears and 2022-25 as a Vikings assistant head coach, working with outside linebackers in 2024 and 2025.
This is a considerable demotion — not in title, but certainly in responsibilities — for Parker, 34, who came to Dallas this season highly regarded after doing strong work as the Eagles ' defensive backs and pass game coordinator from 2024-25.
Pettine has considerable history with both Schottenheimer and Parker. He spent 2009-11 as the Jets ' defensive coordinator while Schottenheimer was New York's offensive coordinator. When he was with Green Bay, Pettine gave Parker his first NFL job as a defensive quality control coach.

title: Why Seahawks' Jaxon Smith-Njigba may go back-to-back as NFL Offensive Player of the Year
summary: The league might be witnessing the greatest season ever by a wide receiver, which could earn him the first back-to-back OPOY honors in a quarter century
full_text:
Greatness is unfolding in the Pacific Northwest. Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba is in the midst of a potentially legendary season — one unlike any in NFL history.
A year after he blossomed into a superstar, Smith-Njigba is on pace to break the league's single-season receiving record and could become the first player to win Offensive Player of the Year in consecutive seasons since Marshall Faulk rattled off three straight award wins from 1999 to 2001.
Before Faulk, only Earl Campbell (1978-1980) had achieved the rare feat of winning OPOY multiple years in a row. Both of them were running backs, so Smith-Njigba would be the first wide receiver to pull it off if he secures the trophy come February.
Considering the award has only gone to a wide receiver six times since its inception in 1972, Smith-Njigba's victory last year was a rarity in the first place. To up the tally to seven wide receivers and account for two of them, in back-to-back years, would put him in a league of his own in the award's history.
Smith-Njigba leads all players this season in receptions (79), receiving yards (1,207) and receiving touchdowns (10) heading into the Seahawks' Week 11 bye. Let it not be forgotten that he is fresh off a Super Bowl title, too. At just 24 years old, he has already accomplished more at both an individual level and team level than most wide receivers dream of. As far as wideouts go, it's JSN's world, and everyone else is living in it.
When the Seahawks traded D.K. Metcalf in 2025, they did so clearly knowing that Smith-Njigba was ready to handle the lion's share of targets on their offense. He had already proven capable of reaching the 100-catch mark with Metcalf in the group, so the expectation was that he would take the next step as the bona fide No. 1 weapon among Seattle wide receivers. The Ohio State product did just that when he rolled to the league's receiving title in 2025.
One year later, Smith-Njigba is not only on track to repeat as the NFL's most productive pass-catcher, but he is also on pace to beat Calvin Johnson's record for the most receiving yards in a single season. He does have the benefit of a 17-game season whereas Johnson played during the 16-game era, but that is not to discredit the historic heights he could reach by the end of the campaign.
Jaxon Smith-Njigba's current pace
Again, the breakout season Smith-Njigba strung together last year in the wake of the Metcalf trade placed him at the top of the 2025 yardage standings. Stack that season with the even greater 2026 production, and the result might end up being the best two-year run by a receiver the sport has ever seen
Jaxon Smith-Njigba's current pace
Even if he slows down over the final seven games of the year, Smith-Njigba has already done enough through the first 10 to put himself in rare company. He became the fourth player in NFL history and the first since the 1970 merger to rack up 1,200 yards and 10 touchdowns in the first 10 games of a season. The last time that occurred was 65 years ago.
In college football , there is the "Heisman moment." Whatever the Offensive Player of the Year equivalent of that is, Smith-Njigba just had his. In the Week 10 win over the Las Vegas Raiders , he turned in the greatest quarter of his career and highlighted it with a ridiculous play that stands competitively among the best he has ever recorded.
The third quarter of that triumph at Allegiant Stadium was special. Smith-Njigba amassed 144 yards and became the first Seahawk to tally 128+ receiving yards in a quarter. When he tacked on more in the next period, he entered another new echelon as the first Seattle player with 150+ receiving yards in a half in the play-by-play era, which dates back to 1991.
Nearly half of his third-quarter yardage came on one single play: A 71-yard burst to the end zone.
BIG PLAY JSN 😮‍💨 @jaxon_smith1 71 YARDS TO THE HOUSE. 📺: @NFLonCBS pic.twitter.com/0sDwRbuiOK
Smith-Njigba slipped while running his route, immediately stood back up, spun past a defender, beat two safeties to a deep ball and sprinted 40 more yards to the goal line. If the slip at the start of the route was accidental, then credit to him for bouncing back to complete a monster play. If it was intentional to get the safety to bite, then it was a masterclass in baiting a defender out of position. Either way, it belongs on his career highlight reel.
So often in this league, when a starting quarterback goes down with an injury, his top wide receiver's production falls off a cliff. Look at what happened in Minnesota when Justin Jefferson dealt with a revolving door at quarterback, or what Zay Flowers continues to experience in Baltimore amid Lamar Jackson's absence.
Smith-Njigba has actually been better with his No. 2 quarterback than with his starter.
Sam Darnold has been in and out of the lineup due to multiple injuries, which thrust Drew Lock into action during the season opener, Week 2 and each of the last two games. The two longest touchdowns of Smith-Njigba's career came with Lock, not Darnold, operating the offense: last week's 71-yard explosion and an 81-yard score in the second game of the year.
Here is how Smith-Njigba's production stacks up by quarterback:
Opposing defenses cannot stop Smith-Njigba. Apparently, quarterback injuries can't either. He is operating in a different universe from every wide receiver in the NFL and may be recognized for it at the end of the year with another piece of hardware in his already stocked trophy case.

title: Sorting 9 struggling franchises into tiers, from hopeless to hopeful: When will Jets end drought?
summary: At least one multi-year playoff drought will end in 2026, but others are only bound to get longer
full_text:
The last time the New York Jets made the playoffs was all the way back in 2010. Their 15-year postseason drought is the longest in franchise history and by far the longest active streak in the NFL . The Atlanta Falcons own the second-longest run without a playoff berth at eight years, and nine different teams own droughts of at least three seasons. Through 10 weeks in 2026, a couple of those squads appear poised to snap their dry spells. But others are destined to watch the postseason from home yet again.
Reasons for hope exist inside most of these downtrodden teams who have waited at least three years for a return to the Super Bowl hunt. Emerging or solidified franchise quarterbacks, superstar talent and renowned coaches are the best foundational pieces to own on the road back to competitiveness.
For the franchises that lack those puzzle pieces, however, the outlook is far bleaker.
Below are the nine teams with the longest postseason droughts sorted into tiers from hopeful to hopeless.
The two most aggressive sellers at the trade deadline are in the earliest stages of a rebuild. Yes, even the Titans , who started theirs back in 2023.
Tennessee whiffed on their first swing at a franchise quarterback when Will Levis did not work out, which essentially reset the clock on their rebuild. Then they made a second coaching change in two years by bringing in Robert Saleh, which amounted to another overhaul. The Jeffery Simmons and Amani Hooker trades this month moved a franchise legend and the NFL's most prolific defender at forcing interceptions and set the roster's talent back again. All the while, the product on the field has not improved one bit. Since Mike Vrabel's exit in 2023, the Titans have not won more than three games in a season. They are on pace for two this year. And while there are fun young weapons on the offense, it is still unclear whether Cam Ward is the answer at quarterback.
The Colts gutted their roster save for Jonathan Taylor , Sauce Gardner and Daniel Jones , and more moves could be on the way in the offseason. They have an opening at general manager, might be in search of a new coach in a couple of months, are devoid of talent at wide receiver and probably need to change things up at quarterback considering Jones' dreadful production in his first year back from a torn Achilles. This will get worse before it gets better. And on top of all that, they do not have a 2027 first-round pick.
Geno Smith and recently traded Jacoby Brissett are classic veteran bridge quarterbacks whose job is to keep their teams somewhat competitive until they draft their replacements. The Cardinals already moved on from Brissett and are taking a look at the future with Carson Beck , and he did not look the part of a future starter in his debut in Week 10. Both them and the Jets will shop for a signal-caller in the draft.
The quarterback Arizona selects will have an elite receiving tight end in Trey McBride , which will give that incoming rookie a premier safety valve as he gets his feet wet. If and when Jeremiyah Love gets and stays healthy, there is tremendous upside at running back, too. The Cardinals need to upgrade their receiving unit to aid their next quarterback, though. Decisions await on the other side of the ball, where Budda Baker and Josh Sweat remain locked in as two veteran leaders after the Cardinals elected to keep them at the trade deadline.
Years of mediocrity and the NFL's longest playoff drought helped the Jets stockpile young talent, so the quarterback they select might inherit an even better situation than the one in Arizona. The offensive skill positions are flush with rising standouts and established stars. David Bailey is a tremendous building block for the defense as the league leader in forced fumbles with five and a havoc-wreaker with 7.5 sacks as a rookie. The Jets just need to finally hit on a quarterback and ace the coaching hire that feels destined to come with Aaron Glenn on perhaps the hottest seat in the NFL.
Each of these teams own the same blueprint: A developing young quarterback who may be their long-term solution, at least one offensive star or superstar and enough promising or established tertiary weapons to keep them out of the league's basement.
The Saints have trailed at some point in all 26 games of Kellen Moore's tenure. That appalling reality does not instill much confidence that he is the right man for the job. A porous defense is largely to blame for this year's issues, as it ranks 29th in yards allowed per game, 26th in scoring and 23rd in EPA per play allowed. Between that and the musical chairs the Saints have played at running back, the positives that continue to come out of Tyler Shough and his receivers only go so far.
Las Vegas was among the most pleasant surprises of the season's first half, although the luster wore off in the weeks leading up to the Kirk Cousins trade. It was obvious in the first few weeks of the season that Klint Kubiak was an excellent hire and that if Fernando Mendoza delivers on his promise as the No. 1 pick, it will not take long for the Raiders to make noise. Brock Bowers ought to aid Mendoza's development, but they are still in desperate need of wide receiver help and must build around Maxx Crosby on defense.
The combination of Bijan Robinson and Drake London is a legitimate championship-caliber duo that the Falcons hope does not go to waste. Even some locked-in playoff contenders would gladly take Atlanta's skill position weapons over their own. The key for coach Kevin Stefanski is to mold Michael Penix Jr . into at least an upper-half-of-the-league quarterback and field a defense strong enough to maximize the elite playmaking ability on the more loaded side of the ball. That latter task got a little tougher when the Falcons traded Jessie Bates III , though.
Jaxson Dart's season-ending injury in Week 2 will always make this a "what could have been" season for the Giants . How much they accomplish in the second half of the campaign will determine how much excitement will exist for Year 2 of the John Harbaugh era when Dart returns to action.
Harbaugh is a strong candidate for Coach of the Year and continues to make the most of a rough situation without his starting quarterback — so much so that the Giants, even on the heels of a disappointing loss, are in the driver's seat in the NFC East. He could be set for a lengthy tenure in New York if everything goes according to plan. He and Joe Schoen will work together to add even more talent to this roster after the latter turned in a couple of highly fruitful drafts and loaded the squad with some of the league's most exciting young players like Malik Nabers , Abdul Carter and Arvell Reese .
This version of the Bengals is the one the franchise had to have envisioned when Joe Burrow led his 2022 team to the Super Bowl. It just took a few years to manifest. Now that it has arrived, Cincinnati might not just get back to the Super Bowl; it could win it.
Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase , Tee Higgins and Chase Brown were never the problem. All the reasons behind the three-year playoff drought had to do with either injuries or the defense. In 2026, the stars have stayed healthy, and the commitment to fixing the defense has paid off. The Bengals spent all offseason trading for, signing and drafting impact players on their weaker half of the roster. Dexter Lawrence . Boye Mafe . Bryan Cook . Each of them, along with others, has taken the unit to a new level. Consistency still lacks a bit, but the highs are higher than at any other point during the Burrow era. If the defense peaks down the stretch, nobody will be able to keep up with the third-highest-scoring team in football.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Predicting full 14-team NFL playoff bracket heading into Week 11: AFC field seems set, Packers miss out
summary: For the first time this season, we have the same Super Bowl matchup two weeks in a row
full_text:
Heading into Week 11, the NFL playoff race is supposed to be heating up, but it might actually be cooling down, at least in the AFC.
Several things happened in Week 10 that make it feel like the AFC playoff field might be set. For one, Drake Maye went down with a potentially season-ending injury , and because of that, the Patriots (5-5) are now a long shot to make the playoffs. Also, the Browns pulled off a stunning comeback win over the Texans , putting Cleveland in firm control of a wild card spot.
According to our projection, the AFC's seven-team playoff field is all but set. So who's projected to get in? Glad you asked.
To help us figure that out, we had our analytics expert, Stephen Oh, simulate the rest of the 2026 season. There are 122 games left on the regular-season schedule, along with 13 playoff games, and Oh simulated all of them. Not only did he project all eight division winners and the 14 playoff teams, but he also crowned a Super Bowl champion.
With that in mind, let's get to the projections. And just as a reminder, we're projecting what the NFL playoff field will look like at the end of the season. This is NOT the current playoff standings.
The biggest win in Week 10 was probably the Browns' wild comeback victory over the Texans. With Cleveland's win, the Browns are now projected to get the seventh seed in place of Houston, who was there last week.
Here's the projected AFC playoff field (with each team's current record): 1. Bills (8-1) -- AFC East champion 2. Jaguars (7-2) -- AFC South champion 3. Bengals (7-2) -- AFC North champion 4. Chiefs (7-2) -- AFC West champion 5. Broncos (7-2) 6. Steelers (6-3) 7. Browns (6-4) JUST MISSED: Patriots (5-5), Texans (3-6)
BREAKDOWN: According to our projection, the AFC playoff field is basically wrapped up. That's right, we're only in Week 11, but our model feels pretty strongly that these will be your seven playoff teams. The model has given up on the Patriots because they just lost Drake Maye, the Ravens have been left for dead after losing to the Chargers , and even if the Texans somehow rebound to get to 10 wins, they're in a spot where they would lose almost any tiebreaker (they've already lost to the Bills, Bengals and Browns, so the head-to-head tiebreaker is out the window). They do play the Steelers in Week 13, and at this point, that's essentially a must-win game for Houston.
The addition of Kirk Cousins has caused a ripple effect in the NFC North. After watching Cousins lead the Vikings to a win over the Packers in Week 10, our computer now projects the Vikings will win the NFC North (the Lions were projected to win it before the Cousins trade).
Here's the projected NFC playoff field (with each team's current record): 1. 49ers (8-1) -- NFC West champion 2. Vikings (7-2) -- NFC North champion 3. Giants (5-3-1) -- NFC East champion 4. Buccaneers (3-6) -- NFC South champion 5. Lions (7-2) 6. Bears (7-2) 7. Seahawks (6-4) JUST MISSED: Packers (6-4), Rams (6-4)
The most interesting part of the NFC projection is that we have the Packers and Rams both reaching 10 wins but still missing the postseason. To add insult to injury, our projection has the Buccaneers (8-9) and Giants (8-8-1) both finishing at .500 or below, yet still getting in as a division winner.
AFC breakdown: The AFC wild card round would be must-see TV with two huge divisional showdowns. The Bengals just destroyed the Steelers in Week 10, and the computer has them once again winning in the postseason. The juiciest game in the AFC would come in Kansas City, where the Chiefs would edge the Broncos in a thriller. As for the other game, the computer is predicting a short playoff run for Cleveland.
NFC breakdown: We didn't see a single home team lose in the AFC wild card round, but in the NFC, things are much different, with the home teams going a combined 1-2. The NFC North sends three teams through to the divisional round, becoming just the fourth division in the Super Bowl era to pull that off. This round also sees the elimination of the Seahawks, which means the NFL will crown a new champion.
AFC breakdown: Our projection has the Bills beating the Chiefs, but I'll believe it when I see it. On paper, the Bills might have the better overall roster, but that never seems to matter when these two teams meet in the postseason. Patrick Mahomes is 4-0 all-time against Josh Allen in the playoffs, and if our projection is right, Allen's drought will finally end here. As for the other game, the Jags beat the Bengals in Cincinnati earlier this year, and our projection has the Jags earning the win again in Jacksonville.
NFC breakdown: We get total chaos in the NFC with two crazy games that end up going down to the wire. Kirk Cousins leads the Vikings to their first NFC title game appearance since 2017 while the 49ers edge the Bears in a thriller.
If you're scoring at home, we are now down to four teams: three teams that have never won a Super Bowl (Bills, Jaguars and Vikings) and one team that hasn't won a Super Bowl in over 30 years (the 49ers' last title came in 1994)
We've been doing a projection every week since the start of the season, and here's a look at the projected Super Bowl each week.
For the FIRST time all season, our computer has projected the same Super Bowl matchup for TWO straight weeks. The Bills have been projected to win the Super Bowl for four straight weeks and that's mostly because the computer loves them. Our model gives the Bills an 18.27% chance of winning it all, which is incredibly high, especially given that no other team is above 11%.
author: John Breech

title: Week 11 picks, best bets: Lowly Jets send Chargers back into loss column, Titans cover vs. Cowboys
summary: Tyler Sullivan picks every game on the Week 11 schedule, including five locks against the spread
full_text:
You all remember the No. 1 rule about Fight Club, right? You don't talk about Fight Club.
There's a similar philosophy/mantra in the gambling space. You do not, under any circumstances, bring up the fact that you're on a heater, for fear of jinxing it. You simply don't acknowledge it, continue going about your business and pray that the good times keep rolling.
With that in mind, I'm not going to tell you that I went 11-3 (ATS and straight-up) over the Week 10 slate, which included a near-perfect 4-1 ATS record in my five locks of the week. And I'm certainly not going to highlight that I'm currently on a 26-3 moneyline run over the past two weeks, along with a 7-3 ATS mark on my locks.
Again, I'm NOT telling you this. Why would I? Nope. All we need to do now is roll up our sleeves, pick up our lunch pail and keep it moving into Week 11. Because there isn't much else to talk about.
Note : Atlanta, Cleveland, Green Bay, Los Angeles ( Rams ), New England and Seattle are on the bye in Week 11.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
I think Dallas is one of those teams that plays up or down to their opponent. So while it may have gone toe-to-toe with the 49ers last week, I wouldn't be surprised in the slightest to see the 1-8 Titans hang around. In fact, I'm betting they will. Tennessee is a respectable 3-1 ATS on the road this season. Conversely, AT&T Stadium hasn't been much of an advantage for Dallas, as it is 1-3 ATS at home.
Over their last three games, the Titans offense has also been pretty solid, averaging 5.8 yards per play. That's the sixth-highest in the NFL over that stretch. A large part of that success has been thanks to the ground game, as they are averaging 5.4 yards per carry. The only team better than them is the 49ers, who just ran for 214 yards and three touchdowns against this Dallas defense in Week 10. The Cowboys' defense is showing no signs of improvement, as their 6.1 yards allowed per play are the sixth-highest in the NFL season. At the very least, the backdoor will be left wide open.
Projected score: Cowboys 30, Titans 23 The pick: Titans +8
Los Angeles finally got a win, snapping an eight-game losing streak to start the season and an 11-game skid dating back to last year (including playoffs). This moment in the winner's circle, however, will be short-lived. With Geno Smith reportedly avoiding a major injury , that only strengthens my faith that the Jets will take down the Chargers on Sunday. I assume Smith plays, and with him under center, the Jets have been solid.
Moreover, I thought New York's defense largely hung around against Buffalo last week before the wheels fell off in the second half. Justin Herbert is not Josh Allen , nor is Omarion Hampton James Cook, so the Jets' defense should be able to keep this offense in check for four quarters. New York also has the rest advantage after LA played in Baltimore on Monday night.
The Chargers have yet to record an ATS win (0-4) at home this season
Projected score: Jets 24, Chargers 20 The pick: Jets +3.5
The Jaguars are a freight train right now. Over their three-game winning streak, Jacksonville is averaging 38.3 points per game. For the season, they're averaging 6.0 yards per play (tied for fifth-highest in the NFL), a 46.8% conversion rate on third down (third-highest) and 8.7 yards per pass attempt (second-highest). Trevor Lawrence is playing at an MVP level, while running back Bhayshul Tuten is in the midst of a full-blown breakout. Over the winning streak, he's rushed for 221 yards and three touchdowns, while adding 80 yards and a touchdown on five receptions.
Meanwhile, Jacksonville's defense is about to get a boost this week as two of their trade deadline acquisitions (safety Jessie Bates III and defensive tackle Jordan Davis ) are all set to make their debuts after Liam Coen gave them Week 11 off to get acclimated.
While New York does boast a defense that is allowing just 305.7 total yards per game this season (fifth-best in the NFL), the Jaguars feel like an entirely different animal to overcome. I also believe Jacksonville's defense, which is allowing 4.7 yards per play over the last three games (tied for fifth-lowest in the NFL), can contain a J.J. McCarthy-led Giants offense that still gives me pause.
When you look at the trends, the Jaguars have given bettors confidence to back them on the road this season. As the away team, Jacksonville is 3-1 ATS with a 9.5-point average margin of victory, the third-highest in the NFL.
Projected score: Jaguars 33, Giants 21 The pick: Jaguars -6
Fernando Mendoza actually played pretty well given the circumstances, in my opinion. The No. 1 overall pick was making his first career start against one of the toughest defenses in the NFL: the Seahawks . Naturally, he looked like a rookie quarterback at times, completing 17-of-29 for 143 yards, no touchdowns, and no interceptions. He was also sacked six times. That said, he showed some flashes, including a touchdown run on his first possession of the afternoon. While Mendoza has a bright future in front of him, his baptism by fire will continue in Week 11 as he and the Raiders travel to Denver to face a Broncos team that was on the bye in Week 10.
Denver is 3-0 coming off a bye under head coach Sean Payton, and its pass rush could prove to be the difference in this game and keep Las Vegas outside of the number. This season, Denver is second in the NFL in pressures (159) and tied for the ninth-most sacks in the league (26), according to TruMedia. At home, this feels like a recipe for Mendoza to be under siege early and often, allowing Bo Nix and the Broncos offense to simply take advantage of what has been a poor Vegas defense. Coming into Week 11, the Raiders are tied for the most points per game allowed (28.9) in the NFL.
Projected score: Broncos 27, Raiders 16 The pick: Broncos -10
There are a lot of big spreads this week, so we're naturally going to see some teams creep through the back door. I think New Orleans could be one of them. The Saints are tied for the second-most pass attempts per game (38.1) in the NFL this season. That number jumps to a league-high 39.5 when they're on the road. That should only continue in this matchup against Chicago as they try to keep up with Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams on the other side.
The Saints' passing attack is also getting a midseason boost with the return of first-round rookie Jordyn Tyson . Over the first two games of his career, the No. 8 overall pick has looked like the real deal, including an 11-catch, 80-yard outing last week in the loss to Carolina. Paired with Chris Olave , that's a nice one-two punch for Tyler Shough to get us to a cover. Speaking of covers, that's all New Orleans has done this season, as they're the only team in the NFL without an ATS loss on the road so far in 2026 (3-0).

title: Prisco's Week 11 NFL picks: Texans edge Colts on 'TNF,' Cowboys rout Titans, 49ers over Vikings
summary: Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 11 picks, including the Jaguars to handle the Giants on the road
full_text:
Stacking winning weeks is always a good feeling when it comes to picking NFL games .
I did that the past two weeks.
After a good Week 9 picking games, I was solid again in Week 10. I went 9-5 against the spread and 8-6 straight up. I'll take it. Two weeks in a row. Wow.
The records after 10 weeks are now 95-54-1 straight up and 68-79-3 ATS. Climbing out of a huge hole, ATS has me now visibly seeing the .500 mark.
Let's hope the hot streak stays as we move towards Thanksgiving. There are a ton of big spreads this week, so watch out. The dogs might be barking.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
If the Texans are to have any chance of making the playoffs, they have to win this one. The Colts are pretty much done, but they beat Miami last week. Daniel Jones struggled in that one, but the Texans' defense has really struggled. Look for the Colts to hang around here, but the Texans will win it.
Miami is playing consecutive road games after losing at Indianapolis, while the Bills are home for the first time after two road games. The Bills are playing better on defense in recent weeks against some lower-level quarterbacks. They get another one here in backup Kyle McCord . The Bills will score, as Josh Allen always plays well against Miami, but Miami stays around.
Pick: Bills 31, Dolphins 19
The Bears are off a bye, while the Saints lost to the Panthers last week. Chicago is much improved on defense. With the Saints unable to run the ball, it will put a lot of pressure on Saints quarterback Tyler Shough . Caleb Williams will bounce back from his four-interception game last time out against Tampa Bay and will play well here. Bears take it.
The Cowboys are bad on defense, but the Titans haven't exactly lit it up on offense. Cam Ward has played better as of late. Even so, look for the Cowboys offense to have a big day throwing it against a Tennessee defense that struggles against the pass. Dak Prescott will put up big numbers.
Pick: Cowboys 37, Titans 23
The issue here is whether Baker Mayfield will play for the Bucs. If not, they will have big problems. The Lions are back home after beating up the Patriots in Germany last week. The offense was dominant that day, but this Tampa Bay defense is playing well. That will keep them in the game, but the uncertainty at quarterback will be too much to overcome.
Carson Beck makes his first road start for the Cardinals and this is as tough as any place in the league to do so. The Chiefs are coming off an impressive road victory in which Patrick Mahomes threw five touchdown passes. The defense is third in the league in scoring. That will make for a tough day for this limited Arizona offense. Blowout.
Pick: Chiefs 33, Cardinals 14
The Eagles are coming off a bye, while the Steelers are coming off a loss to division-rival Cincinnati. The Eagles are a shell of the team they were early in the season because of injuries and trades. This battle of Pennsylvania has lost some luster. Look for the Steelers to bounce back with a tough defensive effort against an undermanned offense, and Aaron Rodgers will play well.
Pick: Steelers 26, Eagles 13
Both of these teams are in desperation mode when it comes to needing victories for the postseason. The Ravens lost at home Monday night to the previously winless Chargers and now have to head out on the road on a short week. That's tough. The Panthers played better defense last week against the Saints, which will help them here. Carolina wins it late, but it's close.
Pick: Panthers 23, Ravens 22
The Chargers won for the first time on Monday night, beating the Ravens on the road. They actually showed some offensive life in that game. The Jets have defensive issues, which the Chargers can take advantage of here. Quarterback Geno Smith is banged up for the Jets, which could mean rookie Cade Klubnik makes his first NFL start. Look for the Chargers to take advantage if that is the case as they get to 2-8 behind another solid showing by the offense.
Pick: Chargers 28, Jets 24
Fernando Mendoza will be making his first road start, which can be tough for a rookie. But it's also against a really good defense coming off a bye in a tough place to play. That's a real challenge. Look for the Broncos to get after him in this one. The Raiders ' defense isn't playing well, so maybe it's just what Bo Nix needs. Broncos big.
Pick: Broncos 31, Raiders 14
This is a big game for both teams. The Jaguars are 7-2 and playing as well as any team in the league. But they are playing consecutive road games against a Giants team pushing for a division title. This game will be decided by the Giants' defense against the Jaguars' offense. I think the Jaguars get the better of it. Look for them to run it well with Bhayshul Tuten .
Pick: Jaguars 26, Giants 17
This is the best game of the week, featuring two of the NFC's best. The 49ers beat Dallas last week, while the Vikings beat the Packers in Kirk Cousins ' first game back with the team after being traded by the Raiders. This will be about the 49ers offense vs. Brian Flores' defense. I think Kyle Shanahan will get the best of it as the 49ers keep rolling. Big day for Christian McCaffrey running it.
Pick: 49ers 23, Vikings 16
The Bengals are rolling on offense as Joe Burrow pushes toward the MVP. The Commanders have had problems against the pass, ranking 31st in the league, which has to have Burrow and the offense ready to go. Jayden Daniels won't keep up, but it's close. The Bengals keep rolling.
Pick: Bengals 34, Commanders 30

title: Are the Cardinals done for the season? Where do they go from here?
summary: The Arizona Cardinals are one of the worst teams in the NFL in 2026. There. We said it. Nobody in the media can sugar-coat this any longer. They are bad. Really bad. The only silver lining is that quality help is on the horizon in that Arizona should be selecting most likely in the Top-5 […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 18: Head coach Mike LaFleur of the Arizona Cardinals looks on against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals are one of the worst teams in the NFL in 2026. There. We said it. Nobody in the media can sugar-coat this any longer. They are bad. Really bad. The only silver lining is that quality help is on the horizon in that Arizona should be selecting most likely in the Top-5 of April’s NFL Draft. RELATED: WINGARD AND BURCH LAND ON IR So, what now? The Cardinals are 3-7-0. It is inconceivable to think that with seven games remaining on the schedule that a team has tapped out and is done for, but Arizona is not good. Currently, the Cardinals own the #6-#8 pick in the draft. If the draft were today, a coin flip would decide slots six through eight. This draft order will change at season’s end. The Tennessee Titans, Miami Dolphins, Los Angeles Chargers, Philadelphia Eagles, and New York Jets all have a worse record while the Atlanta Falcons and Indianapolis Colts have the same record as Arizona. But consider that the Cardinals are a victim of circumstance. Mainly, injuries. Both OT Paris Johnson and CB Will Johnson have the ability to become Pro Bowl material. Yet, both was inserted on IR early in the season. Losing these two players alone has made both the offense and defense less of a threat. These are major losses. It is the equivalent to losing your best starting pitcher and your clean-up hitter all in one failed swoop. Right now, there are 16 players on IR, of which 10 were starters. What percent is that out of 22 starters? 45%? Name any club that can play without almost half their starting lineup, and still win games. Anyone? But it is what it is. Whoever invented the saying, “The next man up” never coached the Cardinals. Last year it was more of the same. At season’s end, 26 warm bodies filled up the IR room. They had to bring in more chairs to fit everyone. The entire running back room was decimated and towards the end this group was completely backups and practice squad guys. Players who were free agents the entire season were suddenly getting calls from Arizona late in the year to suit up and play in order to fill positions of guys who were hurt. Now don’t take this analogy the wrong way. The Cardinals aren’t losing any games on purpose in order to secure a better draft slot. The word “tanking” is not a real thing in the NFL. For every NFL player who plays badly during the final stretch, his job is on the line whether with Arizona or the next team he hopes calls his agent. Coaches do not lose games intentionally. With all of the off-field functions that take place during the offseason where every head coach, assistant coach, GM, and scouts attend such as the Senior Bowl, the Combine, and owner’s meetings, being the head coach of a losing team is embarrassing. Now, they may play their second stringers more when they realize they have no chance at the postseason, but that is similar to college where you play guys instead of seniors to get them used to playing in live action to prepare them for when their time arrives. When playing, Arizona’s players still have fight in them. It’s just the current roster is now comprised of a lot of non-starters and even some practice squad guys. It’s not like they aren’t trying; they couldn’t beat out the starters and now have the job by default. They weren’t good enough, but now they are necessary in order to fill positions. And it’s not like it was this way all season. Not at all. They beat the Los Angeles Rams and moved the ball up and down the field all game long, but just couldn’t score touchdowns. But now, both sides of the ball are decimated with injuries, and it looks like they are running on three wheels in a NASCAR race. Getting killed by the Rams two weeks ago, and being completely inept against the Seattle Seahawks last week shows that their season is over. So, what should the Cardinals do going forward? Here at ROTB , we made a list of suggestions: Continue to play Beck It is not known if Gardner Minshew will return off of IR this year. He underwent season-ending surgery on Monday, November 16, 2026, to repair a torn ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) in his right elbow, which just happens to be his throwing arm. Most likely, he won’t be playing again this season. In several 2027 NFL mock drafts, most have the Cardinals taking a quarterback in the first round. The names listed are Notre Dame’s C.J. Carr, Darian Mensah of Miami, and Drew Mestemaker of Oklahoma State. Okay, that is if the Cardinals actually need a quarterback. Maybe Beck is that guy. Maybe not? One thing the coaching staff needs to know is if Beck is their starting quarterback going forward, or in the future at some point. It is a possibility that Minshew heals up and comes back next year and is named the starter when training camp has concluded. This would mean that Beck is being assigned for more development. If so, the team would not need to use a valuable first round draft pick on a player they don’t need. Wouldn’t using that pick on an offensive tackle or an elite pass rusher be more prudent instead of yet another developmental guy who won’t help the 2027 roster at all? If a quarterback is needed, Arizona could select Austin Simmons of Missouri in Round 2 or South Carolina’s LaNorris Sellers in Round 3. But Beck was a third-round draft pick. Makes no sense to bring in another guy at almost the same draft position. The coaching staff will find out in the last seven games what the team has in Beck. That information will become invaluable come April. Keep the starters going along the offensive line Knowing the season is pretty much a done deal will make the coaching staff want to insert the second and third teamers more and more in every game. That is all fine and dandy, but not along the offensive line. If wholesale changes become the trend for the Cardinals along the offensive line, it will devastate the development of Beck. The coaching staff will need a good evaluation of Beck going into this year’s draft. They won’t have the true aspects of his playing time if all he is doing is running for his life, being flushed from the pocket, or sacked all the time. Not to mention it would probably give Beck this gun-shy mentality that no quarterback needs. Beck will need positive affirmation. That means a clean pocket that doesn’t collapse almost instantly so that he can read the defense and go through his progressions. This is a guy who threw for almost 4,000 yards in two of his last three college seasons, and had a 72.4% completion ratio as a senior. So, the dude can play. But that takes being able to sit back in a pocket and see his receivers. Yes, the left tackle situation is always in a state of flux with Paris Johnson injured and on IR, followed by the injuries to rookie Jayden Williams who was subbed with Josh Fryar. And RG Isaiah Adams has been a roller coaster while C Hjalte Froholdt didn’t play in Beck’s debut because of being in concussion protocol. Maybe substitute Jon Gaines for Adams, and perhaps give former first round draft pick Jedrick Wills a try at left tackle, his natural position while at Alabama. Regardless, do everything possible to keep this group upright and rigid. Beck will need all the help he can muster. Give Mike LaFleur some time There are rumblings that LaFleur’s time in the desert might be a one-off. It has happened many times in this league. LaFleur came from a very prominent coaching tree. Both the Rams and San Francisco 49ers are offensive juggernauts. The 49ers currently own the Number 1 seed in the NFC. LA started off 2-4-0 and now have won their last four games and are listed as a playoff seed. These two teams can score points. Only the Buffalo Bills have scored more points than San Fran (281). That isn’t by chance, but a carefully laid out plan with a great…
