title: 2027 Bears mock draft: Finding a running mate for Jeffery Simmons
summary: The Bears have a 7-2 record coming out of their bye week, and as their Week 11 matchup approaches against the Saints, their focus is heavy on the rest of the regular season and an expected postseason appearance, more so than what pick they’ll have in the 2027 NFL Draft. That said, preparing for the […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS - NOVEMBER 14: Miami defensive lineman Ahmad Moten Sr. (99) celebrates after coming up with what was originally ruled a fumble, and later an incomplete pass, in the fourth quarter as the Miami Hurricanes faced the Duke Blue Devils on November 14, 2026, at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, FL. (Photo by Samuel Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Bears have a 7-2 record coming out of their bye week, and as their Week 11 matchup approaches against the Saints, their focus is heavy on the rest of the regular season and an expected postseason appearance, more so than what pick they’ll have in the 2027 NFL Draft. That said, preparing for the draft is a year-round process, and for those interested in the upcoming class and which positions Chicago could focus on, I have you covered with another mock draft. For the sake of introducing you all to more draft prospects, I will not re-use any players from my last mock draft here at Windy City Gridiron . Those players are as follows: Zabien Brown, CB, Alabama Mateen Ibirogba, DT, Texas Tech Antwan Raymond, RB, Rutgers Tobi Osunsanmi, EDGE, Indiana Aidan Banfield, OG, North Carolina As always, I made these selections and simulated the picks of the 31 teams around me using PFN’s free mock draft simulator , which recently underwent a fresh interface update. The picks are as follows: Round 2: Ahmad Moten Sr., DT, Miami (FL) The Bears made a massive splash trading for Jeffery Simmons a few weeks before the trade deadline, but he could use another upgrade alongside him on the defensive interior. Grady Jarrett is a potential cap casualty this offseason, and they don’t have another else who’s proven as even a high-level backup defender up the middle. Ahmad Moten Sr. is a defensive tackle who can get it done on all three downs. He’s quick off the snap, low to the ground, powerful in his lower half, and has a diverse arsenal of moves he can use to stack and shed blocks. He has the explosiveness to stress out interior defensive linemen as an immediate backfield penetrator, too. Though his pass-rushing efficiency has dipped in 2026 compared to 2025, he’s a pro-ready run defender with the athleticism to project as a true three-down defender. Round 3: DJ McKinney, CB, Notre Dame As things stand, the Bears will likely need to find a new starting cornerback in the 2027 offseason. Kyler Gordon and Malik Muhammad project as safe bets to return next year, but Jaylon Johnson is a potential cap casualty, and Tyrique Stevenson is in the last year of his rookie deal. With their play so far this season, neither can be relied upon too heavily as long-term fixtures in the starting lineup. At 6’1” and 190 pounds, DJ McKinney is a lengthy cornerback with the physical profile to project as a future NFL starter along the boundary. A three-year full-time starter in college who shined at Colorado before transferring to Notre Dame for his 2026 season, McKinney is a competitive cornerback with a large catch radius, and he’s super twitched-up for his size, changing direction well and sinking his hips into his transitions. Though his tackling form can be inconsistent, he shows willingness in run support, and with some better ball-tracking skills, he has some serious potential on Day 2. Round 5 (via Falcons): Luke Montgomery, OG, Ohio State All things considered, the Bears have a strong offensive line with solid depth, but Joe Thuney won’t be around forever. He turned 34 years old on Thursday and has more football behind him than ahead of him. Luke Montgomery is a player I think would benefit from backing up as a rookie but has NFL starting-caliber tools. He’s a savvy, refined lineman who lands his strikes accurately, buries defenders in the run game, and keeps his head on a swivel in pass protection. It also helps that he has taken reps at both guard spots and both tackle spots during his time at Ohio State, giving him key versatility that should help him get playing time. Round 6: Raylen Wilson, LB, Georgia An All-SEC freshman in 2023 with two years of starting tape at the SEC level, Raylen Wilson moves with a calculated, yet aggressive edge in pursuit. He has sharp pre-snap instincts and takes precise angles to the ball carrier in run support, and his straight-line speed helps him chase down running backs with ease. Though he won’t wow you taking on blocks, I think Wilson is a perfectly capable linebacker with the potential to be a good LB3 in a defensive rotation as either a backup WILL or MIKE. Round 7: Melkart Abou Jaoude, EDGE, North Carolina Melkart Abou Jaoude was a second-team All-ACC member for North Carolina in 2025, leading the conference with 10.5 sacks. Though his production has dipped this year, he’s also battled through an injury, playing with a club on his hand. The 6’5”, 260-pounder from Lebanon has impressive pop in his hands and good length, which helps him keep offensive tackles at bay. He has a high pass-rushing IQ and good anchor strength, and his ability to win the leverage battle is reflective of his district championship-winning days as a high school wrestler. Abou Jaoude doesn’t have the elite burst and flexibility to project as an NFL starter, but I like him a lot as a depth addition late on Day 3.

title: Chicago Bears 1-on-1: Can Theo Benedet neutralize the Saints’ Chase Young?
summary: On paper, the New Orleans Saints might be the worst team the Chicago Bears have faced since Week 4 against the New York Jets. The Saints rank 15th in the league in scoring offense at 22.4 points per game. They are 25th in the league in scoring defense at 26.2 ppg allowed. They are an […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - NOVEMBER 15: Chase Young #99 of the New Orleans Saints pumps up the crowd during the second half of a game against the Carolina Panthers at Caesars Superdome on November 15, 2026, in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images On paper, the New Orleans Saints might be the worst team the Chicago Bears have faced since Week 4 against the New York Jets. The Saints rank 15th in the league in scoring offense at 22.4 points per game. They are 25th in the league in scoring defense at 26.2 ppg allowed. They are an average to below-average team, but they might yet surprise the Bears. The Saints still have a lot to play for, despite their 3-6 record. They remain only one game back in the paltry NFC South, and remain in the upswing of a franchise rebuild eager to get a taste of the postseason. Their star player right now is WR Chris Olave, who is 8th in the NFL with 764 receiving yards. He has turned into a true WR1 in his age 26 season. If after Chris Olave you are struggling to name many Saints players, that’s understandable. Their roster is young and lacking in top-end talent. But there is something lurking beneath the surface that the Bears need to take very seriously. New Orleans has two of the top four sack leaders in the NFL right now, with DE Carl Granderson boasting 8.5 sacks and his foil Chase Young sporting 8 sacks. 16.5 sacks between two players 9 games into a season is not a coincidence. While Granderson may have the higher count presently, he typically lines up on the right side and will face Darnell Wright, who is… really freaking good. It’s no given, but I think that Wright should be able to hold his own. On the other side, though, is the far more interesting matchup. Chase Young, the revived 2nd overall pick in the 2020 draft, has found a new home in New Orleans and has really turned into one of the premier pass-rushers in the league. He gets the opportunity to line up on the Bears left side, which will likely be manned by Theo Benedet. Benedet is hitting a stride himself and holds the 3rd best OT pass blocking win rate in the league entering Week 11 at 92%. He has earned the right to start at LT until Ozzy Trapilo can prove himself to be healthy enough to play like he did in 2025. Still, Chase Young’s physicality is elite. Just look at what he did against highly touted rookie Spencer Fano. Chase Young vs Spencer Fano. The former 2nd overall pick (2020) gave the Browns rookie LT SERIOUS problems 👀😳 pic.twitter.com/FwjyMAhtj3 — Rookie Watch (@RookieWatxh) November 9, 2026 Benedet, as we know, was not a high-end draft pick. And while he has improved drastically in his third season with the Bears, he will have his hands full going up against Young. If the Bears are to win on Sunday, devising a plan to help Benedet will be crucial. It will also be important for Theo to step up and win 1-on-1s when his number is called.

title: From dreams to pay dirt: Dohnte Meyers delivers for Bengals
summary: Dohnte Meyers once delivered dinner to pay for a football dream. Sunday night, he delivered a touchdown in the Cincinnati Bengals’ biggest win of the season against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Somewhere between those deliveries came a $100 tryout, a broken hand, shoulder surgery, and a championship in Canada. Now, the receiver who kept finding reasons […]
full_text: Dohnte Meyers once delivered dinner to pay for a football dream. Sunday night, he delivered a touchdown in the Cincinnati Bengals ’ biggest win of the season against the Pittsburgh Steelers . Somewhere between those deliveries came a $100 tryout, a broken hand, shoulder surgery, and a championship in Canada. Now, the receiver who kept finding reasons to keep going has another milestone: his first NFL touchdown. Meyers caught a 15-yard scoring pass from Joe Burrow just before halftime in Cincinnati’s 38-18 victory, helping send the Bengals into the locker room with a commanding 24-3 lead. He finished with two receptions for 20 yards and that score while drawing a key pass interference penalty that led to another Bengals touchdown as well. He added two kickoff returns for 58 yards, including a 39-yarder. On a night when Burrow threw for 409 yards and Ja’Marr Chase piled up 231 receiving yards, Meyers’ contribution could easily get buried in the box score. His journey deserves a little more attention. The Georgia native began his college career at Presbyterian before transferring to Division II Delta State, where he caught 120 passes for 1,542 yards and 13 touchdowns across two seasons. Those numbers earned him an opportunity to pursue professional football, but no guarantee of a place in it. After going undrafted in 2023, Meyers attended Atlanta’s rookie minicamp but failed to land a roster spot. He returned home, trained, and worked DoorDash and Uber Eats to help finance his preparation. When Saskatchewan held an open tryout in Atlanta, he paid $100 to get his shot. Canada soon discovered what the NFL had overlooked. Meyers opened his CFL career in 2024 with consecutive 101-yard receiving performances against Ottawa and Montreal, becoming the first Roughrider to reach 100 receiving yards in each of his first two CFL games. He totaled 24 receptions for 349 yards and a touchdown that season. Even that breakthrough came with a price. A broken hand delayed his debut, and a separated shoulder ended his season just as he was establishing himself. His response in 2025 was emphatic: 65 catches, 1,056 yards and eight touchdowns in 15 games. He finished seventh in the CFL in receiving yards and tied for fourth in touchdown receptions, turning an intriguing introduction into a full season of production. Then he helped deliver a championship. His crucial 21-yard reception in the Western Final set up Saskatchewan’s winning touchdown and a trip to the Grey Cup. Meyers followed with four catches for 76 yards in the championship game as the Roughriders defeated Montreal. Cincinnati signed Meyers in January to a futures contract, and it’s proven to be one of the Bengals’ biggest moves in an offseason full of big ones. Sunday offered yet another reason to appreciate that decision, but it takes more than one touchdown to establish yourself in the NFL. Meyers has already shown what can happen when he gets an opportunity.
author: John Acree

title: Bengals will ‘evaluate’ future trades in wake of Austin Ebiketie debacle with Eagles, per report
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are 7-2 and in firm command of their own destiny. So, the trade-deadline snafu that saw the Bengals […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals are 7-2 and in firm command of their own destiny. They’re riding a five-game win streak, the offense is firing on all cylinders, and the defense has vastly improved over the last several weeks, finally resembling the championship-caliber unit fans have been begging for. So, the trade-deadline snafu that saw the Bengals agree to terms with the Eagles for edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie just to back out after they found out (from a guy on Twitter) they’d lose the third-round compensatory pick they earned from allowing Trey Hendrickson to walk is forgivable. And it will definitely be forgivable if they learn from their mistake. According to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler, a source close to the Bengals revealed the team is going to adjust how they do things in the future. “We can try to accelerate the process of determining how contracts are treated [by the league],” the source told Fowler. First, the front office had an incredible offseason by trading the No. 1o overall selection for Dexter Lawrence, and bringing in the free agent class that includes Boye Mafe, Jonathan Allen and Bryan Cook. They also tried to make a mid-season trade before the deadline to grab a guy they hoped could push their defense over the edge. These are not moves we’re used to seeing from the Bengals’ front office, and I want to acknowledge that. They deserve a ton of credit for the 7-2 record. Having said that, they did get some egg on their face by not verifying what would happen to their extra third-round pick before they started to move forward with the trade. If they learn from their mistake and change the way they do some things, they’ll be all the better for it. Baby steps in the right direction will still take the Bengals closer to where they want to go.

title: Bengals News: Ravens fans lamenting Trey Hendrickson signing
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals’ fans have a very volatile relationship with their front office. A pretty big episode came over the past few offseasons with pass rusher Trey Hendrickson and the contract saga. At first, it seemed fans were more frustrated that Cincinnati couldn’t seem to get a deal done with a player who had just […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 1: Trey Hendrickson #91 of the Baltimore Ravens looks on against the Buffalo Bills during an NFL football game at Highmark Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cincinnati Bengals’ fans have a very volatile relationship with their front office. A pretty big episode came over the past few offseasons with pass rusher Trey Hendrickson and the contract saga. At first, it seemed fans were more frustrated that Cincinnati couldn’t seem to get a deal done with a player who had just led the league in sacks while also having back to back 17.5 sack seasons. Ultimately, the two sides came to an agreement on a one-year deal for 2025, but both sides were eager to part ways following a season where Hendrickson struggled with injuries. Eventually, over that holdout more fans became annoyed with Hendrickson’s seemingly wanting to draw as much of it out in the media as possible. But it was worse when he landed with a divisional rival, the Baltimore Ravens. Still, at this point Bengal fans had seen the cracks in the armor. At his age, he was a liability against the run, and his style of being a high motor pass rusher would be harder and harder to be productive as he got older and injuries piled up. Now that we have finished Week 10, Ravens’ fans are done with the signing altogether . The exact issues have been popping up that worried not only Cincinnati’s front office, but the fanbase as well. He has seven solo tackles and two sacks on the year. Not exactly what you are looking for from a player you are giving almost $28 million a year for. At least he may not demand another new contract next season. Bengals News Bengals’ Joe Burrow, Lions’ Jahmyr Gibbs highlight Players of the Week This is his second time in four weeks winning the award. It is ironically his fourth week in a row of recording four touchdowns. You light up a divisional rival in a game where you are playing for the top spot you deserve this award. ‘Apparently there was a tweet online or something?’ – Ebiketie on cancelled Eagles-Bengals trade It has to be one hell of a feeling being told you are about to uproot your life and career, and then not even hours later be told “oh never mind you’re staying.” Arnold Ebiketie may forever be known as that guy who had his trade called off because of a complex rule involving compensatory picks. Inside The Defense: A Look At How Safeties Jordan Battle And Bryan Cook Are Putting It All Together The Madrid game really seemed like when this defense came together and finally started to gel a bit more in the back seven. Cook is looking more like the player we expected and Battle hasn’t been missing a bunch of tackles. These guys are going to be very important come playoff time facing the top quarterbacks and offenses in this conference, so hopefully it keeps up. NFL News NFL QB rankings, Week 11: Kirk Cousins climbs; Josh Allen slips from top three There is no guessing where Burrow falls on this list. He remains at top as Brock Purdy and Patrick Mahomes shoot up to right behind him. However, if Burrow even partially keeps up the pace he is on then it may as well be a battle for second place. NFL Power Rankings, Week 11: Vikings vault into top five; Browns, Rams and Commanders on the rise Credit where credit is due. Nick Shook has constantly been higher on this Cincinnati team than most. He had the Bengals at No. 5 going into last week when most were still debating if they were even in the Top 10. Now at No. 4 they only trail the San Francisco 49ers, the Buffalo Bills and Jacksonville Jaguars. Giants’ Cam Skattebo retiring back flip celebration following Aidan Hutchinson injury: ‘That ain’t going to happen to me’ What happened to Hutchinson was very unfortunate, but jumping during a celebration isn’t some wildly irresponsible thing. Now, what Skattebo was doing absolutely falls under wildly irresponsible celebrations. So if that happening led to Skattebo calling off his backflip, then cool good for him. But they are far from equal in how reckless they were.

title: AFC North Roundup: Bengals cruise to division lead; Browns stay in playoff hunt
summary: Even with three teams still firmly in playoff contention, the AFC North race officially has a new favorite, while another team’s playoff hopes are all but officially over. With Cincinnati, Cleveland, and Pittsburgh all multiple games over .500 entering Week 11, there’s a very real chance we’ll see all three teams in the 2026-27 NFL […]
full_text: Even with three teams still firmly in playoff contention, the AFC North race officially has a new favorite, while another team’s playoff hopes are all but officially over. With Cincinnati, Cleveland, and Pittsburgh all multiple games over .500 entering Week 11, there’s a very real chance we’ll see all three teams in the 2026-27 NFL Playoffs. As for the Ravens, their latest defeat effectively eliminated them from postseason contention. Here’s a look at what took place in Week 10 for the AFC North. Bengals steamroll Steelers Cincinnati brought the fireworks. Pittsburgh supplied the audience. With first place in the AFC North at stake Sunday night, the Bengals overwhelmed the Steelers, 38-18, improving to 7-2 with their fifth consecutive victory. Pittsburgh slipped to 6-3 after spending much of the evening trying to keep a divisional showdown from becoming an even bigger embarrassment. The final margin hardly captures how thoroughly Cincinnati controlled the game, which stood at 24-3 by halftime and 31-3 entering the fourth quarter. Joe Burrow gave Pittsburgh almost no room to breathe. He completed 35 of 44 passes for 409 yards and four touchdowns without an interception, piling up 302 yards and three scoring passes before halftime. Against a defense that had been one of the best in the NFL over the past four weeks, Cincinnati’s quarterback repeatedly delivered. The Bengals have now scored at least 30 points in five consecutive games, establishing a franchise record and giving their winning streak some serious offensive muscle. Ja’Marr Chase was the problem Pittsburgh never solved. His 11 receptions produced 231 yards, including a 53-yard gain that helped set up Cincinnati’s second touchdown. Chase Brown caught touchdown passes of two and four yards, while Drew Sample and Dohnte Meyers also scored through the air. That distribution made the Bengals especially difficult to contain: Chase could rip apart the coverage between the end zones, and Burrow had several other answers when Cincinnati reached scoring territory. The defense made sure Burrow’s production came with a comfortable cushion. Cincinnati limited Pittsburgh to 222 total yards and 17 first downs while generating three sacks. Jonathan Allen, Myles Murphy and Boye Mafe each brought down Aaron Rodgers, whose passing line finished at 16 completions in 32 attempts for 145 yards. Pittsburgh managed only a field goal through three quarters, leaving its offense with far too much ground to cover when the touchdowns finally arrived. Rodgers connected with DK Metcalf and Pat Freiermuth for fourth-quarter touchdowns, but Cincinnati answered the first of those scores with a one-yard Samaje Perine touchdown run. The Bengals finished with a 484-222 advantage in total offense and held the ball for 35:09. Those numbers tell the story of a team that dictated the evening on both sides of the ball. Browns do it again vs. Texans Deshaun Watson led Cleveland to its sixth come-from-behind victory of the season en route to a 27-24 win over Houston that pushed the Browns’ record to 6-4. Cleveland spotted the Texans a 17-0 lead as C.J. Stroud threw early touchdown passes to Nico Collins and Xavier Hutchinson, but the Browns gradually erased the deficit. Touchdown runs by Deshaun Watson and KC Concepcion, along with a pair of Andre Szmyt field goals, produced 20 consecutive points and a three-point Browns lead entering the fourth quarter. Houston regained the advantage on Stroud’s 11-yard touchdown pass to Dalton Schultz, forcing Cleveland to mount one more rally. The decisive opportunity came with fewer than two minutes remaining and the Browns starting at Houston’s 49. Harold Fannin Jr. delivered the biggest gain, taking a reception 30 yards to the Texans’ five-yard line. Quinshon Judkins finished the drive on the next snap, scoring with 53 seconds remaining to put Cleveland ahead for good. The Browns still needed their defense to protect the lead, and Denzel Ward and Donovan McMillon supplied late pass breakups, with McMillon’s coming on fourth-and-20 to end Houston’s hopes. Cleveland remained unbeaten at home, while the Texans fell to 3-6. The victory kept the Browns within reach in the AFC North and served as a reminder that Cleveland remains part of the divisional conversation. Ravens suffer crippling loss vs. Chargers The Los Angeles Chargers snapped an 11-game losing streak Monday night, beating the Baltimore Ravens 23-20 for their first win of the season. Los Angeles outrushed Baltimore 160-16 and held Derrick Henry to 10 yards on 10 carries. Justin Herbert opened the scoring with a 22-yard touchdown run, and Omarion Hampton scored from the 1 on fourth down to give the Chargers a 17-7 lead late in the first half. Jacoby Brissett threw for 340 yards in his Ravens debut with Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley both on injured reserve. Baltimore went three-and-out on its first three possessions, but Henry scored twice, cutting the deficit to 23-20 with 10:23 remaining. Herbert finished with 129 passing yards and 51 rushing yards and went without an interception for the first time this season. The Ravens were approaching field-goal range with 2:03 left when Tarheeb Still stripped Zay Flowers after a catch near the Chargers’ 45-yard line. Elijah Molden recovered, and Herbert found former Raven Charlie Kolar for a first down to seal the win. Baltimore dropped to 4-6 with its fifth straight loss that likely ends their slim postseason dreams. AFC North Standings for Week 11

title: 3 reasons why the Bengals will beat the Commanders on MNF, and 3 reasons they won’t
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals did it! They not only got revenge on their hated division rival for their Week 3 defeat, but they absolutely dominated the Pittsburgh Steelers from the first snap to the last. They won the game 38-18, and 15 of those 18 points were from garbage time scores. So even though the Bengals […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals did it! They not only got revenge on their hated division rival for their Week 3 defeat, but they absolutely dominated the Pittsburgh Steelers from the first snap to the last. They won the game 38-18, and 15 of those 18 points were from garbage time scores. So even though the Bengals won by 20 points, the game wasn’t even that close. Now they travel to Landover, Maryland, to face the Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football. The Bengals last played the Commanders in 2024, when Jayden Daniels and the Washington offense beat the Bengals in a shootout, 38-33. What will happen on Monday night? Here are three reasons the Bengals will win on Monday Night Football, followed by three reasons they won’t. The Bengals will win because…. They’re a better team from top to bottom. This is a fact. The Bengals have a more talented roster, and that more talented roster is playing at a higher level than the Commanders are likely even capable of. The Commanders’ offense has scored over 30 points just once this season, and that was in Week 3. The Bengals have scored at least 30 points in five consecutive games, and Joe Burrow is leading the pack for NFL MVP at this point in the season. And then there’s Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, who have time to do their thing because the offensive line is doing a good job at protecting the quarterback. The Bengals scored seemingly at will on Sunday Night Football against a defense that has been playing good football over the prior month. The Commanders are talented—there isn’t a team in the league that doesn’t have talent all over their roster. But they’re not nearly as loaded as the Bengals. Nobody is. It’s not a tough matchup on the secondary. The Bengals’ secondary could use a little work, and the defensive front is really pulling a lot of the weight. However, for the second week in a row, the Bengals’ secondary will be matching up against a receiving corps that has seen better days. Terry McLaurin, the Commanders’ WR1, is on IR for the reason of the year, which means Washington’s top wide receiver is likely an over-his-prime Stefon Diggs. Similarly to their game plan against the Steelers, Al Golden will likely feel comfortable leaving his corners and safeties on islands against the Commanders’ receivers, allowing the defensive line and linebackers to focus on the run game and rushing the passer. The Commanders’ struggle against the pass. I mean, nobody doesn’t against the Bengals, right? The thing is, the Commanders are coming into Week 11 allowing the 10th most yards through the air in the league. Outside the Cowboys and Rams, though, the passing attacks of every team they’ve played have been mediocre at best. The Bengals have the most potent passing attack in the NFL. On top of that, the Commanders’ defense blitzes at the third-highest rate in the NFL. On Sunday night, the Steelers blitzed Burrow 12 times. Burrow went 12 for 12 for 186 yards. View Link The Bengals won’t win because….. There is such a thing as an emotional hangover. How many times have we seen a team blow out a rival one week just to lose to an inferior team the next week? It happens multiple times every season. The season is short—compared to the NHL, NBA, and MLB, it’s pathetically short—but it’s not short enough that the eventual Super Bowl winner can’t drop a non-conference game they should have won earlier in the season. Only one team has been perfect coast-to-coast, and the only team I remember being perfect in the regular season was the ‘07 Patriots, and we know what happened to them. The Bengals won the big one on Sunday Night Football, and as much as I’d love to see them go 8-2 for the first time since the 2015 season, it wouldn’t shock me if they looked like a different team on Monday. It just happens sometimes. Jayden Daniels could be a matchup problem. Do you remember when I said the Bengals’ secondary doesn’t have too tough a matchup on Monday Night Football? Well, even the worst receiving corps in the NFL can figure out a way to get open if the quarterback is able to extend the play. No corner can stay on a receiver’s hip for more than a few seconds. If the Bengals’ defensive line can’t put pressure on Daniels, it could be a big problem for the secondary. Daniels is one of the most athletic quarterbacks the Bengals will face all season long. If he gets out of the pocket, not only could he punish the Bengals with his legs, but he can buy time to find a receiver downfield. He’s perfectly capable of making any throw required of him, and if the Bengals can’t keep him in a pocket they can close around him, the secondary could have a long day. The Bengals’ opponent has a rest advantage…again. The Steelers were coming off their bye week and still lost to the Bengals, who were coming off an international trip. The Bengals absolutely overcame that situation, thanks to leadership from Zac Taylor and the rest of the staff that got the players from Cincinnati to Madrid and back without skipping a beat. Can they do it again? They’ll have an extra day, going from Sunday Night Football to Monday Night Football, but the Commanders will be coming off a Thursday Night Football game. This gives them 11 days to the Bengals’ 8. It’s not a huge difference, but sometimes it’s the little things that make big differences in NFL games. Why do you think the Bengals will win or lose? Sound off!

title: Buy or Sell: 15 hot takes on the Cincinnati Bengals
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are on fire. They’re riding a five-game win streak, have the best offense in the league, Joe Burrow is playing out of his mind, and they just dominated the Steelers at home in front of a national audience. So, yeah. Things are pretty great right now in the Queen City. Below are […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals are on fire. They’re riding a five-game win streak, have the best offense in the league, Joe Burrow is playing out of his mind, and they just dominated the Steelers at home in front of a national audience. So, yeah. Things are pretty great right now in the Queen City. Below are 15 hot takes from across the internet, and some I’ve whipped up on my own. I’ll share whether I’m buying or selling, but I want to see what you think. Sound off! Joe Burrow is going to win the 2026 NFL MVP. Burrow is playing lights out. He is responsible for at least four touchdowns in each of the last five games, and has been able to guide the Bengals to almost score at will since mid-October. He does have the best wide receiver duo in the NFL, but he’s putting the ball only where they can catch it, and he’s leading the best offense in the NFL. If things continue to go this way, he’ll be a shoo-in. My take: Buy. If I were a betting man, I’d place a wager. The Bengals have the best offense in the NFL. Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have been lights out. Against the Steelers’ vaunted defense, Burrow threw for 337 yards and three touchdowns. In the first half. At that point in the game, the Steelers only had 40 yards and mustered just three points. The game was over then and there. My take: Buy Bengals should be favorites to represent AFC in the Super Bowl They’ve come a long way since we were questioning what was going on in their back-to-back losses in Weeks 3 and 4. The defense still has some growing to do, though—especially the secondary. I think they’re close, and by the time the season comes to an end, hopefully it’s a yes. My take: Sell, for now Amarius Mims will be an All-Pro this season. Mims has taken 381 pass-blocking snaps, and he’s only given up six pressures (per PFF). He has the third-highest pass-rush efficiency and has been nothing short of the second coming of Big Willie Anderson. The Bengals have been able to leave Mims all alone on an island against some of the league’s best pass rushers, and he’s absolutely shut them down. My take: Buy Zac Taylor deserves serious consideration for Coach of the Year. He will be in the conversation because the Bengals are 7-2 and are among the small list of teams that can be considered true contenders. He flawlessly guided the Bengals through an international trip, and then brought them right back home to blow out the Steelers, who were coming off their bye week. That alone is pretty incredible. My Take: Buy Ja’Marr Chase is already the greatest wide receiver in Bengals history. Can it be that after just six seasons in the league, we can crown Chase as the greatest receiver in the franchise’s history? And to be clear, the Bengals have a long list of amazing wide receivers—it’s kind of their thing. Chase has 7,715 receiving yards, which is the third most in franchise history behind AJ Green (9,430) and Chad Johnson (10,783). He’s fourth in franchise history in touchdown receptions with 61, but the leader, also Johnson, has 66. It wouldn’t be surprising if Chase was the new record holder before we get to December. Chad is great, but…. My Take: Buy The Bengals don’t need a top-10 defense to win the Super Bowl. With the best offense in the NFL, maybe the Bengals’ defense only needs to be okay. Maybe they can be near the middle of the pack, or possibly even closer to the bottom than the top. As long as it’s not the worst, right? No, we’ve seen that movie. My Take: Sell Boye Mafe was Cincinnati’s best offseason acquisition. The Bengals signed Mafe for less than the Ravens were willing to pay Trey Hendrickson, and it has been a great decision, rivaling some of the top free-agent acquisitions they’ve made over the last dozen years. But while it was special, the trade for Dexter Lawrence was a generational thing. My Take: Sell The Bengals will finish the regular season with at least 13 wins. The best regular-season finish the Bengals have had was 12-4. They’ve done that four times in team history (2022, 2015, 1988, 1981), and 13 wins would set a new record. It would also possibly put the Bengals in contention for the No. 1 overall seed in the playoffs, meaning the AFC Championship Game will be played in Cincinnati (hopefully). My Take: Buy Tee Higgins would be a top-five receiver if he were another team’s WR1. I’m not going to spend too much time on this. It’s a yes. The only reason Higgins isn’t WR1 is he plays on the same team with the best wide receiver in the NFL. Think of him as the Cris Carter to Chase’s Randy Moss. My Take: Buy The Bengals will sweep their remaining AFC North games. This, I think, will come down to the Browns. The Ravens aren’t going to be able to overcome the injuries they’ve suffered, and it’s the Browns who are 6-4 that pose the biggest threat to the Bengals in the AFC North. They’ve had the Bengals’ number over the past few years, but that’s a monkey the team has been able to shed as of late. I don’t think Cleveland can keep up with Cincinnati’s offense. My Take: Buy The Bengals’ offensive line is the best it’s been in the Burrow era. Burrow has been one of the most hit quarterbacks since he was drafted in 2020, which is one of the reasons he’s spent so much time on the IR in his career. For the first time, he came into a season with the same five starters on the offensive line in front of him as he had the season before. And they’ve played like it. He has been able to operate from a clean pocket, or has at least had the time to step up to find a receiver. He has only been sacked 16 times, which is the sixth fewest in the league. My Take: Buy The Bengals will regret not making a bigger move at the trade deadline. Yeesh. The Bengals thrashing the Steelers on Sunday Night Football may not have completely washed away the bad taste in the mouths of fans created by the front office’s blunder at the trade deadline. Here’s the thing: The Bengals absolutely have the talent on their roster to win the Super Bowl. If they don’t, though, will we look back at the trade deadline as the reason why? My Take: Sell……. I hope Anything short of reaching the AFC Championship Game would make this season a disappointment. I came into the season thinking the Bengals needed to win at least one playoff game for me to be satisfied in the direction Taylor and his staff were taking the team, and anything short of that should result in his termination. My opinion on the matter has changed somewhat, though. They’re too good to win on Wildcard Weekend just to get bounced by a less-talented team in the divisional round. So yeah, not getting a chance to represent the AFC in the Super Bowl would be a big disappointment. My Take: Buy This is the best Bengals team in franchise history. The Bengals have been to three Super Bowls, and they’ve unfortunately lost all three. It’s difficult to even compare those three teams to each other because there were over 30 years between the second and third teams to reach the ultimate game. So it’s hard to compare this team to those teams too. They’re exciting, for sure. I don’t know if I can say they’re the best, though. Yet. My Take: Sell, hopefully just for now Now, discuss in the comment section. Do you buy or sell the 15 lukewarm-to-hot takes above? Sound off!

summary: The riverfront of the city of Cincinnati has undergone some major changes over the last 40 years. full_text: The riverfront of the city of Cincinnati has undergone some major changes over the last 40 years. From a series of parking lots between Paycor Stadium and Great American Ballpark to The Banks, the area between the two professional sports franchises’ respective homes has been transformed into a place people actually want to be. One major issue the city faces, though, is a lack of places to host large events. Sure they have Heritage Bank Arena, but it’s old and run down, and it just doesn’t have a very large seating capacity. The city and county could bring in a ton of revenue if they could attract some major events. Luckily for the denizens of the Greater Cincinnati Area, Hamilton County has begun the search for a partner to help bring major events to Cincinnati at Paycor Stadium. So that band you like that’s going to be touring in the next couple of years, maybe they’ll make a stop down on Pete Rose Way. “This is about maximizing the return on investment for the taxpayer,” Hamilton County Commissioner Denise Driehaus, according to the county’s website . “By attracting more events to Paycor Stadium, we can generate additional revenue while supporting jobs, tourism and local businesses.” Here’s what else is going on: NFL snubs Bengals’ red-hot offense and flexes AFC North rival into Week 12 primetime slot instead The league has flexed the Cleveland Browns’ Week 12 home game against the Las Vegas Raiders to “Sunday Night Football.” The move bumps the Los Angeles Chargers’ matchup with the New England Patriots out of the primetime slot. It’s time: This is finally the year Bengals star Joe Burrow wins his first MVP award For the first time in his seven-year career, the Cincinnati Bengals star quarterback has the inside track to winning his first NFL MVP award. The Bengals demolished the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday night, 38-18. Bengals Release Uniform Combination for Week 11 Against Commanders The Bengals head to Washington for their third straight national game as they play the Commanders on Monday Night Football. Joe Burrow’s Big Night and a Shut-Down Defense Earn Bengals an ‘A+’ Grade Against Steelers Burrow was money through the air, Ja’Marr Chase ran circles around Pittsburgh’s defenders, and the defense shut Aaron Rodgers down for three straight quarters. Cincinnati also pushed its winning streak to five games while climbing to 7-2. Zac Taylor’s squad now hits the road for a Monday Night Football trip to Washington.

full_text: The AFC playoff picture is beginning to take shape as the season progresses. Several of the division leaders are starting to separate themselves, like the Buffalo Bills in the AFC East. Beyond those division contenders, the competition for the wild card spots is getting particularly interesting. If the playoffs started today, the division winners would be the Buffalo Bills, Kansas City Chiefs, Jacksonville Jaguars, and Cincinnati Bengals. The wild card spots would go to the Denver Broncos, Pittsburgh Steelers, and Cleveland Browns. The next teams on the bubble would be the New England Patriots, Las Vegas Raiders, and Baltimore Ravens. Three of the four AFC North teams would currently be in the playoffs, with just the Ravens on the outside looking in. With several games remaining between AFC North teams, a lot can still change in the division. At this point, it seems likely that the Broncos, Steelers, and Browns will claim the final three spots, but the Patriots could still sneak in. They have some challenging opponents remaining on their schedule, such as the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs, but they also have some very winnable games against teams like the Los Angeles Chargers and Miami Dolphins. The first is the opening drive of the game. Cleveland has allowed a scoring drive in nine games, including six touchdowns, which, coupled with the slow starts from the offense, have left the Browns playing from behind each week. The second has been the run defense, which has been porous, even by the low standards of the Browns. While Cleveland’s defense shouldn’t expect an easy game against anyone, it has a chance to stabilize the run defense in the first two games after the bye against the Raiders and Cincinnati Bengals, though it still faces some tricky matchups. title: Browns roster seen as the best fit for one of the best 5 free agents left in the NFL
summary: As every Cleveland Browns fan knows, the roster is never finished being adjusted under GM Andrew Berry. That doesn’t mean every move works out or is even a big one, but Berry’s time with the Browns has seen consistent movement with the 53-man roster as well as the practice squad, including multiple moves during the […]
full_text: As every Cleveland Browns fan knows, the roster is never finished being adjusted under GM Andrew Berry. That doesn’t mean every move works out or is even a big one, but Berry’s time with the Browns has seen consistent movement with the 53-man roster as well as the practice squad , including multiple moves during the team’s bye week . Cleveland didn’t make any moves at the NFL trade deadline, leaving concerns about the team’s edge rush and tight end groups to continue to linger into the second part of the 2026 NFL season, while the Browns compete for an AFC playoff spot . With the trade deadline having passed, NFL free agency looks a little different now. All players are waived, giving teams a chance to claim them no matter what their experience in the league is. Prior to the deadline, players with four or more years of service become street free agents with a chance to sign with whatever team they please. The Athletic put together a list of the top five free agents left on the market, with two players who could help Cleveland’s roster, including DE/OLB Leonard Floyd. Floyd was noted as a perfect fit for the Detroit Lions after they lost star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson for the season, leaving TE Will Dissly to be connected to the Browns: At 6-4, the Browns are perhaps the biggest surprise of this season. One of their top needs heading into the trade deadline was blocking at tight end. They did not make a deal. Harold Fannin Jr. is an emerging star as a receiver, but blocking is not necessarily a strength of his game. Dissly has been a proven run blocker over time with the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Chargers. He battled injuries in 2025 with the Chargers, leading to his release with a failed physical in the spring. If healthy, Dissly would fill a need for the Browns, who rank 25th in EPA per designed rush this season, according to TruMedia. Dissly was a fourth-round pick of the Seattle Seahawks in 2018, playing six seasons in the Pacific Northwest before joining the Los Angeles Chargers. A strong blocker, Dissly’s best receiving year came in 2024 when he caught 50 passes for 481 yards. Finding snaps for Dissly could be difficult for HC Todd Monken, with WRs KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston, and Jerry Jeudy alongside TE Harold Fannin Jr. and RB Quinshon Judkins getting a majority of the specialist snaps. Do you think Dissly could be helpful to the Browns roster and final push this season, or should Berry hold tight with most of the players he currently has? Join the conversation! full_text: As the Cleveland Browns enjoy whatever break HC Todd Monken gives them during their bye week , Sunday Night Football against the Las Vegas Raiders looms in Week 12 . title: Grading the Browns offense during their midseason bye week
summary: Describing the Cleveland Browns offense from last season is easy; to sum it up, it was abysmal. Top to bottom. From the offensive line, quarterback, skill positions, everything was bad. GM Andrew Berry spent the entire offseason rebuilding the entire unit. With the team entering their bye week, we will give a grade to the […]
full_text: Describing the Cleveland Browns offense from last season is easy; to sum it up, it was abysmal. Top to bottom. From the offensive line, quarterback, skill positions, everything was bad. GM Andrew Berry spent the entire offseason rebuilding the entire unit. With the team entering their bye week , we will give a grade to the 2026 Browns offense that was created out of all those moves. Browns roster, offense: What has changed? Everything. Last year, Cleveland’s offense was towards the bottom in every statistical category. Despite the young pieces with running backs Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson, tight end Harold Fannin Jr and a reliable veteran wide receiver, Jerry Jeudy, it didn’t have much success overall. The offensive line was older and less effective, and the quarterback play was below average. Berry spent the entire offseason rebuilding this offense. Fired head coach Kevin Stefanski; hired Todd Monken Traded for right tackle Tytus Howard, signed left guard Zion Johnson, center/guard Elgton Jenkins, drafted rookie left tackle Spencer Fano and right guard Austin Barber Drafted rookie wide receivers KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston It was a lot of work, but Berry did what was necessary to improve one of the worst offenses in the league last season. Comparing the numbers from last year’s offense at the bye week to this year’s offense, you can see a stark difference, even if it still ranks in the bottom half of the league: Browns Offense pre-bye (last season) 31st in offensive EPA per play 32nd in offensive success rate 32nd in Dropback EPA/per play 13th in Offensive Rush EPA per play 32nd in Dropback Success Rate 31st in Rush success rate Browns offense pre-bye (2026 season) 23rd in EPA per play 23rd in Offensive Success Rate 22nd in Dropback EPA/per play 27th in Rush EPA/per play 20th in Dropback Success Rate 21st in total offense 23rd in Rush Success Rate Having better offensive personnel has something to do with the numbers looking better, but it is a night-and-day difference from last season. The one thing that the team lacked last season was generating explosive plays in the passing game, rookies Concepcion and Boston have changed that. Fannin has also been a part of a somewhat revitalized passing game, giving Cleveland something with those three in the skill position room. The one thing that the team has lacked for years is competent quarterback play. Going into the season, the Browns quarterback room was considered a major weakness. Granted, it still is because there is no long-term solution on the roster, but the room has some form of stability from an unlikely individual. Going back to the offseason, many believed that second-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders would be the starter for the entire season. However, quarterback Deshaun Watson took the job despite his tenure in Cleveland not being what he envisioned. Many believed that Watson was done after how he lashed out at the fanbase after the second preseason game in which he was booed. Fast forward to now, Watson is playing better than he did in 2024. Head coach Todd Monken has something to do with that: #Browns HC Todd Monken on how Deshaun Watson has turned things around from the Bills preseason game where he called out fans who booed him: "When we met after that, it really wasn't about his physical traits; it was really where you are mentally and emotionally…'Did you get… pic.twitter.com/aAhPQt54Kh — Camryn Justice (@camijustice) November 16, 2026 Monken had an honest conversation with Watson, and it appears to have benefited the quarterback, and his play looks different than before. Playing with more confidence, better pocket presence, utilizing his legs, and showing signs of how he looked in Houston. Granted, Watson hasn’t been perfect, but the Browns have lacked competent QB play last year, and Watson is giving the team that now. In terms of the offensive line, the unit has been better than expected. Fano has been sensational. The same can be said for Barber. Johnson, whom Cleveland paid in free agency, has been better than people give him credit for. Jenkins and Howard have been the subject of criticism (unfair at times), but they are providing stability at their respective positions. What needs to improve? Two things come to mind: The running game hasn’t materialized this season. At times, it feels as if the running game is coming along until it reaches a roadblock. It could improve after the bye week or possibly next season. For the running game to work effectively, the offensive line has to be better, and the backs have to improve as well. Whether it’s opening up rushing lanes consistently or the running back having better vision, the running has to get better. The second thing is the slow starts, which have also been a common theme. It’s more of a recurring theme. The offense simply has to get out of the gate faster and not wait until the game is out of reach to start executing. Going no-huddle or tempo could be easy fixes, but the slow starts offensively have to stop. Grade Overall, the Browns offense has flaws, but this is a unit that is 10x better than last season. Competent QB play, quality talent at the skill positions, a competent offensive line, and a good offensive coordinator are all Cleveland needed. The QB position isn’t solved long-term, but overall this unit is competent and has made massive improvements from last year. Grade: C-, maybe a C How would you grade the Browns offense going into their bye week? Join the conversation! title: Rock bottom is near if Cowboys can’t get back on track vs. Titans
summary: It shouldn’t exactly be hard to find reasons to expect the Dallas Cowboys to play well against the 1-8 Tennessee Titans this Sunday, especially after (in the biggest vacuum of all time) a one-score loss to the NFC leading San Francisco 49ers, yet that is where expectations currently sit going into Thanksgiving week for Brian […]
full_text: Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images | Getty Images It shouldn’t exactly be hard to find reasons to expect the Dallas Cowboys to play well against the 1-8 Tennessee Titans this Sunday, especially after (in the biggest vacuum of all time) a one-score loss to the NFC leading San Francisco 49ers, yet that is where expectations currently sit going into Thanksgiving week for Brian Schottenheimer’s team. The elephant in the room is that coaching is far and away the Cowboys biggest problem right now, and for fans that believe this to be the case, following the trends of opposing coaches the team has gone against this season tells an interesting story. It all started with a loss to the New York Giants to start the John Harbaugh era in New Jersey with a bang. This early separation between the Giants and Cowboys has held up as the Giants continue to lead the NFC East, and the Cowboys look more and more like pretenders to catch them by the week. The streak of playing against other defensive-minded head coaches continued after week one, as the Cowboys drew their own former defensive coordinator Dan Quinn at home in week two. Given the way the Cowboys defense has played in their last two home games against NFC West opponents, it feels more accurate than ever before to say the Cowboys benefited greatly from the Commanders losing starting QB Jayden Daniels in this game. Nonetheless, that week two game is in the books as a win for Schotty against a defense-first head coach. The same goes for week four, when Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb put their hero capes on to beat DeMeco Ryans and the Houston Texans. In between the Commanders win and this AFC South win, the Cowboys dropped a game to another defensive coach in his first season with the team, leaving the win on the doorstep in Brazil to Jesse Minter and the Ravens. Immediately after the Texans win came another letdown against a defensive coach, losing at home to the winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Todd Bowles. Another first-year head coach put the Cowboys back in the loss column in week eight when Mike LaFleur became the latest Cardinals head coach to apparently own the Cowboys, and it took returning to AFC South play to get back in the win column – again by a narrow margin – in week nine at the Colts. Now, the next opponent for the Cowboys is Robert Saleh’s Titans. Another test at home, where the Cowboys are 7-14-1 to date since 2024, and have lost their last two at home to the Titans. Another defensive head coach, but this time one with the worst possible track record against the Cowboys. On the other side of the ball, another running back to deal with in former Cowboy Tony Pollard, who has touchdowns of 32, 40, and 36 yards in his last three games. Brian Daboll, the former Giants head coach before Harbaugh, is the one getting the ball to Pollard and calling plays for the Titans offense. He’ll be doing so in AT&T Stadium for the first time since week two of last year, when the Giants led by Russell Wilson put up 37 points in an overtime loss. Daboll is 0-7 in his last seven games coached against the Cowboys, which spans his entire tenure with the Giants. Saleh is 0-6 in his career coaching against the Cowboys, his most recent game against them also coming in Arlington. Saleh was the head coach of the other New York franchise in 2023, when the Jets visited the Cowboys also in week two, and Dallas won 30-10. Before that, Saleh was the defensive coordinator for the 49ers in the last two games the Cowboys managed to win against San Francisco, in 2017 and 2020. Week 11 feels like a can’t win scenario for the Cowboys. The coaching matchup from a pure statistical history favors the Cowboys in such a big way, that any misstep the Cowboys make this week will be maximized – something evidenced already when Christian Parker was stripped of play-calling duties. The coaching matchup in a deeper sense would seem to give the Titans a path to victory, as they come in with loads of experience poised to run circles around a Cowboys staff that doesn’t know what it’s doing, and also nothing to lose. The Giants came into week one with a similar coaching structure, an experienced head coach with a former head coach as OC calling plays for a mobile QB, and really looked like the better team for all 60 minutes against the Cowboys. It’s scary to think what both former New York head coaches can do with this setup against the Cowboys for the Titans, with Cam Ward coming off his highest completion percentage of the season against a very good Jaguars defense. When the best thing the Cowboys have going for them coming into this matchup is they can’t be riding too high coming in since they didn’t win last week, that is not good. The Titans also come in off a 40-23 loss to the Jaguars, but the Cowboys should be exceptionally careful not to use this as any extra reason to downplay their opponent. The Titans never trailed by more than ten and were within seven very late in the fourth quarter. The Titans also have losses this season by four to the Eagles, five to the Giants, six to the Ravens, three to the Browns, and seven to the now red-hot Bengals (after leading 13-0). The Cowboys have lost to two of these teams and beat the Eagles without Jalen Hurts, who played when the Eagles were in Nashville in week two. Are the Cowboys closer to the 5-3-1 Giants, and capable of getting two wins in five days to prove this and make anything else this season matter, or closer to the 1-8 Titans and ready to join them in the ranks of having no hope for the playoffs after this Sunday? It all starts with beating the Titans at home for the first time since 2002, which ended up being Dave Campo’s last year as HC for the Cowboys. If Schottenheimer is unable to do so, it will be hard not to feel like a similar fate at season’s end isn’t inevitable. The Cowboys streak against the Titans even resembles a mirror image of how Schotty has led the Cowboys to mostly alternating wins and losses over two years. Since a Cowboys blowout win at the Titans in 2006, these sides have gone back and forth in each game in 2010, 2014, 2018, and most recently 2022 when the Cowboys won in week 17.

title: Cowboys news: Fallout from Christian Parker being stripped of play-calling duties
summary: Christian Parker will remain the defensive coordinator for the Dallas Cowboys, but the play-calling duties will now be in the hands of Mike Pettine. He’s had been around the NFL for a long time, and the experience he brings has a chance to make things for Cowboys’ defense look better going forward. With that said, […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Christian Parker will remain the defensive coordinator for the Dallas Cowboys, but the play-calling duties will now be in the hands of Mike Pettine. He’s had been around the NFL for a long time, and the experience he brings has a chance to make things for Cowboys’ defense look better going forward. With that said, head coach Brian Schottenheimer still feels like Parker is crucial part of what team will do going forward. Cowboys strip play-calling duties from defensive coordinator Christian Parker – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News 10 games in, the Dallas Cowboys have taken play-calling duties away from defensive coordinator Christian Parker. Mike Pettine will now takeover that role. The Dallas Cowboys have made a change at defensive play-caller. Senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine will take over for defensive coordinator Christian Parker and call plays starting Sunday against the Tennessee Titans, a person familiar with the move confirmed to The Dallas Morning News . Parker will retain the title of defensive coordinator. This is now the fifth defensive play-caller the Cowboys have had in four seasons. Brian Schottenheimer candid about Christian Parker’s future in Dallas – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com Despite being relieved of his role as the defensive play caller, Christian Parker still has the confidence of head coach Brian Schottenheimer. In Week 11, Parker was relieved of his play-calling duties after the team’s 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. He will remain on as defensive coordinator but, on game days, the real-time playcalling will revert to Pettine. As Schottenheimer explains, however, the plan remains for Parker to grow and develop in Dallas. “I want to clarify, right off the bat, that Christian Parker is still our defensive coordinator,” Schottenheimer said. “He’s a critical piece of what we’re trying to do as we search for answers and solutions, and I think he has an incredibly bright future, not just this year, but beyond it with us.” Cowboys’ handling of DC Christian Parker is bizarre, leaving Dallas with more questions than answers – Garrett Podell, CBS Sports Making a move when it comes to who makes the defensive calls in Dallas was undoubtedly needed. However, the way it was done was shaky. Instead of firing Parker on Wednesday, which the team perhaps seemed primed to do, head coach Brian Schottenheimer announced senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine will call the defensive plays for the rest of the 2026 season. However, he won’t become the team’s new defensive coordinator. Yes, Parker, who, at 34 years old, is the youngest defensive coordinator in Cowboys’ history, will remain the team’s defensive coordinator and lead team meetings, but he has been stripped of play-calling responsibilities. Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Who is Mike Pettine? Introducing the new Dallas Cowboys’ defensive play-caller – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram Mike Pettine brings a ton of experience to the table as the new play caller for the Cowboys’ defense. He is the only coach on staff with previous NFL head coaching experience, as he led the Cleveland Browns in 2014 and 2015. Prior to his two-year stint with the Browns, he was a defensive coordinator with the Buffalo Bills in 2013 and with the New York Jets from 2009 to 2012. He cut his teeth in the NFL with a seven-year stint with the Baltimore Ravens where he served multiple roles including outside linebackers coach. His defensive foundations include running a 3-4 scheme, similar to Christian Parker. 3 Dallas Cowboys DC Candidates Who Could Replace Christian Parker in 2027 – Josh Sanchez, Sports Illustrated There’s a good possibility that Christian Parker won’t be back in Dallas next year. Here’s a few ways things could go at defensive coordinator if he’s not. Jim Schwartz Schwartz fits the mold of what Jerry Jones has previously looked for in his defensive coordinators. Jones loves to hire assistants with previous head coaching experience, and Schwartz checks that box. After the failed Parker experiment, it would make sense for Jones to go back to his old ways. Schwartz most recently served as defensive coordinator of the Cleveland Browns, and watched Myles Garrett win back-to-back Defensive Player of the Year awards.

title: Brian Schottenheimer has been unable to conquer this team problem
summary: Penalties seem as old as time with the Dallas Cowboys. From 2020 to 2024, under Mike McCarthy, the Cowboys ranked first in the NFL with 570 penalties. It became a consistent talking point every Sunday with McCarthy at the helm and has continued under Brian Schottenheimer. Penalties aren’t always the defining trait that makes a […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images Penalties seem as old as time with the Dallas Cowboys. From 2020 to 2024, under Mike McCarthy, the Cowboys ranked first in the NFL with 570 penalties . It became a consistent talking point every Sunday with McCarthy at the helm and has continued under Brian Schottenheimer. The Dallas Cowboys have 212 accepted penalties over the last two seasons, the most by any team in the NFL. The gap between Dallas and the Houston Texans, who rank 2nd with 195 penalties, is the same as the gap between No. 2 and No. 16 on the list. (stats via @Stathead , @pfref ) pic.twitter.com/YiZvrq1UU7 — Brandon Loree (@Brandoniswrite) November 17, 2026 Penalties aren’t always the defining trait that makes a bad team. The Houston Texans are second with 195 penalties since 2025, and the Denver Broncos are tied for third with 193 . The combined record for both of those teams is 36-16. It’s the type of penalties the Cowboys have been getting—emblematic of what the last few years under Schottenheimer have felt like. On defense, it’s the holding calls or pass interference calls on a critical third-and-long that keep them on the field and the drive moving for the opposing offense. Dallas is tied with the Green Bay Packers for the NFL lead in automatic first downs (9) given via penalty on third down . The Cowboys also lead all teams with 22 penalties resulting in an automatic first down for opponents. The most defining penalty of the season—and maybe the culture of the entire organization—came versus the Indianapolis Colts, when DeMarvion Overshown ran out on the field as an inactive player. The Cowboys still led 20-17 at that point, but the 15-yard penalty set them back, and the offense ended up punting back to Indy, who tied the game on the next possession. Cowboys LB DeMarvion Overshown said he didn’t know going on the field last Sunday was a penalty. “I was just caught up in the moment. … I apologized to the team (after the game). It can’t happen again. It won’t happen again.” Overshown expects to play Sunday… — Jon Machota (@jonmachota) November 12, 2026 Then, late in the fourth quarter against the San Francisco 49ers, George Pickens got a taunting penalty as the offense is trying to score quickly and avoid wasting time off the clock. Instead of being at the 49ers’ 19-yard line, they got moved back to the 28. It took another six plays and a precious 42 seconds off the clock. Again, there are many reasons why the Cowboys sit at a 4-6 record. Penalties aren’t the only reason they are on the outside looking in as the playoff race starts to take shape. However, penalties signal an undisciplined team, and being the league leader over the last two seasons is starting to negatively define the culture Schottenheimer is building in Dallas.

title: From new hope to hopeless: Christian Parker’s journey with the Cowboys
summary: The Dallas Cowboys losing to the San Francisco 49ers wasn’t unexpected, but watching them give up 46 points and 584 yards in front of the home crowd was still a huge kick in the stomach. The defensive futility has taken fans to a dark place, but nobody feels grimmer than first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker. […]
full_text: Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys losing to the San Francisco 49ers wasn’t unexpected, but watching them give up 46 points and 584 yards in front of the home crowd was still a huge kick in the stomach. The defensive futility has taken fans to a dark place, but nobody feels grimmer than first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker. It’s reached a point where people have raised their hands in disbelief as we ponder just how much longer this ride is going to last. It’s very odd because it wasn’t that long ago that so many of us were singing a different tune. Fans felt vastly different in January when the Cowboys hired this 34-year-old coach, and Parker as the youngest coordinator in team history. He arrived with a glowing résumé, having helped the Philadelphia Eagles win Super Bowl LIX while turning young cornerbacks Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean into All-Pros. Before that, he molded Patrick Surtain II and Justin Simmons into stars in Denver. All signs pointed to the Cowboys scoring one of the sharpest young defensive minds in the game. The energy only got stronger in camp. Players who had previously been quiet were making noise, and defensive backs were making plays galore. Second-year corner Shavon Revel Jr. was so impressive that many were penciling him in for a breakout season. This new-look defense was going toe-to-toe with the team’s high-powered offense. Expectations were ginormous. Reality hit hard, and it hit hard fast. Right out of the gate, things were disastrous. Growing pains were expected, but did it have to hurt this bad? In the season opener against the New York Giants, Parker’s unit couldn’t get off the field. The Giants dominated time of possession, went 9/11 on third downs, and scored a touchdown every time they got into the red zone. A perfect four for four. A couple of weeks later, the Cowboys found themselves in a shootout in Rio where it looked like we were in for bonus football when an unforgivable soft coverage allowed the Baltimore Ravens to get into game-winning field goal range in a measly six seconds. Instead of promises of stealthy coverage and harassing quarterbacks, the defense made it easier than before. They couldn’t stop anyone. The learning curve was real, but when would it start to curve? Sadly, the bleeding didn’t stop. By Week 5, the Cowboys sat dead last in run defense, allowing 168.4 rushing yards per game while registering a pathetic five sacks, and they were the only defense in the league that didn’t have an interception. This wasn’t a risk-reward defense. There were never any rewards. It was just total punishment all of the time. Even when it looked like the defense would get a little reprieve by facing an undrafted rookie quarterback in Jalon Daniels, they made him look like a seasoned pro. Desperate for answers after the Tampa Bay upset, the Cowboys lured veteran coach Mike Pettine out of retirement to serve as a senior defensive assistant. Pettine brought over two decades of NFL wisdom and a personal history with Parker, having given him his first pro job in Green Bay back in 2019. The hope was that an experienced presence could stabilize the room, though bringing in a chaperone doesn’t exactly scream confidence in your young coach, but desperate times called for desperate measures. Unfortunately, Pettine’s arrival has done nothing to stop the hemorrhaging over the last month. The Cowboys dropped an overtime heartbreaker to the Arizona Cardinals where the defense allowed four-straight touchdowns in the final 16 minutes of regulation, getting shredded by backups Gardner Minshew and Tyler Allgeier. Sunday’s loss to the 49ers was just another example of how atrocious they can be as they allowed three touchdowns of 66 yards. Just when you think they can’t get any worse, they get worse. More change appeared to be coming after early in the week, owner Jerry Jones admitted on local radio that the team is actively discussing changes to Parker’s role before Sunday’s game. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer was equally noncommittal, refusing to offer a vote of confidence while promising to simplify the playbook. The lack of faith in Parker had reached upper management. On Wednesday, the Cowboys made it official. Pettine is taking over the defensive playcalling responsibilities . This hasn’t been an easy assignment for the first-year coordinator. The Cowboys have overhauled their defensive roster, switched to a 3-4 alignment, and have been without some of their new free agent safety acquisitions to shore up the back end. There have been a lot of changes, and it’s hard to create consistency with so much movement. At the same time, he’s had some decent pieces to work with. They have gotten strong play from some of their interior defensive line, and the addition of cornerback Joey Porter Jr. has been refreshing. Sadly, the sum of their parts has equaled a whole lot of nothing, and now the Cowboys are changing up the equation. The team is desperately trying to cling to whatever relevance they can, as they still have a shot at the playoffs thanks to playing in a weak division. Switching to Pettine is their last gasp. Is there any chance this will right the ship? If improvements happen, they will have to come from a modified scheme from Pettine’s influence, but it needs to be more than that. It will also mean the players have to tackle better and play with a physicality much different than what they’re doing right now. Christian Parker’s first 10 games have been a huge disappointment as all the luster from the once-hyped potential has faded. He arrived as a rising star brought in to transform the defense, yet he now finds himself fighting to survive his debut season. It will be interesting to see how the defense performs with this new change and what this means for his future going forward.

title: WR Ryan Flournoy continues showing up in clutch situations
summary: The Dallas Cowboys continue to disappoint at just about every turn. They’ve underperformed in all three phases of the game this season and show no signs of coming anywhere close to the team many believed could be Super Bowl contenders. Their latest loss to the San Francisco 49ers was yet another example of how far […]
full_text: Photo by Brian Rothmuller/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys continue to disappoint at just about every turn. They’ve underperformed in all three phases of the game this season and show no signs of coming anywhere close to the team many believed could be Super Bowl contenders. Their latest loss to the San Francisco 49ers was yet another example of how far this team has fallen. With everything that is happening in the Cowboys 2026 NFL season, it’s really difficult to appreciate some of the good things that have taken place thus far this year. But, that’s exactly what we want to do today by shining the spotlight on wide receiver Ryan Flournoy, who quietly having a career year. Now in Year 3 with the Cowboys, the former 2024 sixth-round pick has gone from someone trying to stick around on the roster to a reliable weapon in one of the most talented offensive units in the entire league. No. 19 is currently having himself a career year and has been absolutely clutching important situations here recently. To date, Flournoy has caught 38 passes for 466 receiving yards and three touchdowns. That already just about equals his 2025 totals of 40 receptions for 475 yards and four touchdowns. In just over the halfway point of the 2026 season, there’s no telling what his statistics will look like at the end of the season if he continues to produce. Flournoy’s success is a testament to his work ethic. He’s put in the work both on and off the field and earned the trust of his QB, Dak Prescott. It’s obvious Prescott trusts him in any given situation, even if the game is on the line, as evidenced by some clutch plays over the past couple of weeks. Two weeks ago against the Indianapolis Colts, he made arguably the most impactful play of the game. With 97 seconds left on the clock he made a one-handed catch with All-Pro CB Sauce Gardner draped all over him. That reception was pivotal in the Cowboys regaining the lead and ultimately winning the game. A clutch one-handed catch in a big moment from Ryan Flournoy 🤠 DALvsIND on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/zh2VfFSRkQ — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 Although the 49ers ultimately won, Flournoy once again made a couple of clutch plays to keep the Cowboys in the game last week. He ended the game with six catches for 71 yards and a touchdown, but made two key plays. First a big catch in the third quarter down the sideline to move the ball in the 49ers territory and later with his TD catch in the fourth. Ryan Flournoy with a catch-and-jump-and-run 😅 SFvsDAL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/gwB0ik4gyn — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 RYAN FLOURNOY ON 4TH DOWN SFvsDAL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/bEPXUSFH1P — NFL (@NFL) November 16, 2026 With players like CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens ahead of him on the depth chart, Flournoy is never going to be the go-to WR for the Cowboys. That seems to be okay though because he’s thriving as Dallas’ WR3 this year and most importantly is answering every time his number is called. It’s a little too early to start thinking about what his future may hold with the Cowboys next season, but it’s looking bright nonetheless. They were wise to lock him up for another year, especially with George Pickens future with the organization up in the air. It’s going to be really interesting to see how the remainder of the season plays out for Ryan Flournoy. If he continues to produce like he has recently he should finish the year with 60-70 receptions for around 800 receiving yards and a half a dozen touchdowns. Not bad numbers for WR who’s third on the Cowboys depth chart.
