title: Cowboys have the perfect chance to bounce back against Tennessee
summary: The Cowboys dropped to 4-6 after a wild 46-40 loss to San Francisco, but Sunday brings a much more favorable matchup. Tennessee comes to Dallas at 1-8, having lost its last three games and allowed 40-plus points in consecutive weeks. The defense struggled badly against San Francisco, forcing a desperate comeback that fell short. Dak […]
full_text: Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images | Getty Images The Cowboys dropped to 4-6 after a wild 46-40 loss to San Francisco, but Sunday brings a much more favorable matchup. Tennessee comes to Dallas at 1-8, having lost its last three games and allowed 40-plus points in consecutive weeks. The defense struggled badly against San Francisco, forcing a desperate comeback that fell short. Dak Prescott now has 2,724 yards and 21 touchdown passes this season. Tennessee has allowed 43 points to Cincinnati and 40 to Jacksonville in its last two games. This looks like another opportunity for Prescott and the offense to score heavily, especially after what George Pickens did against the 49ers. Pickens returned against San Francisco and immediately produced his best game of the season. He caught three touchdowns and finished with 145 receiving yards. Now Tennessee has to deal with Pickens alongside CeeDee Lamb, who already has 976 receiving yards and eight touchdowns. The Titans simply don’t have one receiver they can concentrate on stopping. The numbers between these two team’s offenses aren’t close. Dallas averages 28 points per game, fifth in the NFL. Tennessee averages only 18, ranking 28th. The Cowboys also average 368 yards per game compared with Tennessee’s 278. If Dallas gets into the high 20s or 30s again, Tennessee may struggle to keep pace. This is where having both Lamb and Pickens, along with players like Ryan Flournoy will come into play. Perhaps the most interesting statistic is time of possession. The Titans average only 25:12 with the football, worst in the NFL. That gives Dallas exactly what it needs after watching San Francisco control huge parts of Sunday’s game. Get Tennessee off the field and give Prescott, Lamb and Pickens as many possessions as possible. Tennessee has some serious injury issues and placed starting guard Peter Skoronski on injured reserve because of a hamstring injury. Linebackers Anthony Hill Jr. and Cody Barton are dealing with injury, and wide receiver Carnell Tate has a big question mark on whether he’ll suit up this Sunday. Wan’Dale Robinson is going on injured reserve. The offensive line injuries should interest a Dallas pass rush that finally produced some numbers against San Francisco. They recorded five sacks against Brock Purdy, including four in the first half. Cam Ward is a talented young quarterback, but Dallas needs to make him uncomfortable behind a weakened offensive line. Tennessee’s rookie quarterback can be pressured into mistakes Ward has shown improvement, but he is still learning. Through nine games he has thrown eight touchdowns and six interceptions with an 80.7 passer rating. He threw another interception against Jacksonville on Sunday. Then there’s the past between these two teams. The Cowboys won the last time these teams met when they travelled to Tennessee in December 2022, coming away with a 27-13 victory. Now the Titans have to travel to AT&T Stadium while carrying one of the worst records in football and knowing they’ve lost four out of the last six meetings between these two teams.
author: Mike Poland

title: Where does the Cowboys defense go from here?
summary: Coming into this season, the world had moderately low expectations for a Dallas Cowboys defense in the middle of a rebuild, paired with a first-time defensive coordinator. Given the offseason moves and what we saw in Oxnard, there was no reason things shouldn’t have at least been a little bit better than last season. If […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Coming into this season, the world had moderately low expectations for a Dallas Cowboys defense in the middle of a rebuild, paired with a first-time defensive coordinator. Given the offseason moves and what we saw in Oxnard, there was no reason things shouldn’t have at least been a little bit better than last season. If nothing else, it couldn’t possibly be worse for a defense that would have ranked 40th in 2025 if there were 40 NFL teams. Then 2026 hit us like a ton of bricks. The numbers The first-year Christian Parker defense ranks last in nearly every metric across the league. Dallas ranks last or near last in total yards allowed per game, rush yards per game, third-down conversion rate allowed, while also failing to contain explosive plays week after week. Despite possessing a top five scoring offense in the NFL, the Cowboys are just 4-6. While the offense isn’t without flaws of their own, the clearest reason for most losses comes down to a historically bad defensive performance. The Cowboys are once again on track to set all the wrong defensive records just one season after setting all the wrong defensive records. What’s going wrong This failure isn’t just a one year collapse. It’s the continuation of a multi-year slide that began after their peak during the Dan Quinn years where Dallas had a top five ranked defense in 2022 and 2023. Dallas has gone through defensive coordinators each year after the Quinn departure with Mike Zimmer, Matt Eberflus, and now Christian Parker. The front office spent the last year and a half spending draft capital, making big trades, and signing free agents to fix that side of the ball, yet the returns on investment are yet to be discovered. Parker, 34 and in his first defensive coordinator job is struggling to install a functional unit that won’t break down in tackling, communication, and scheme execution. While the pass rush has gotten significantly better since adding Mike Pettine to the staff, who is now taking over as the defensive play caller , the defense as a whole still suffers from an inability to execute the most basic functions of sound defense. The defensive line, including the edge group, plays undisciplined football. Setting the edge and staying disciplined seems to be something that the ends just simply aren’t interested in, as displayed by the Deebo Samuel reverse play against the 49ers. Quinnen Williams is the lone, consistent bright spot up front for the Cowboys. The secondary has been uneven with rookie Caleb Downs and Joey Porter Jr. playing the best amongst the group. Downs has hit some rookie bumps, as to be expected, but he’ll clearly be a good player in the NFL. Porter Jr. is a difference maker, consistently shutting down the short side of the field. But the gap between those two players and the rest of the secondary is too great to overcome. The floor of the players on the Cowboys defense appears to be too low and the first-year defensive coordinator has not done enough to raise it. They’ll play multiple quarters of, at worst, acceptable football. And then out of nowhere, the dam breaks thanks to a simple screen, blown coverage, or big run play. Dallas has simply been unable to put an end to this cycle week after week and it’s costing them games. Where it goes from here In the short term, there is no easy fix. The foundations have been laid and Dallas now turns the defensive play-calling duties to Mike Pettine in hopes of better gameday results. Dallas was heavily focused on improving the football intelligence and ability of the players on the defense, but are now looking to simplify the calls according to Brian Schottenheimer. With that in mind, there is still a more than small chance for the Cowboys to make the playoffs in 2026. The Giants schedule is hitting their tough stretch, while the Cowboys have a couple of easy games ahead. That may not mean much, however, as we’ve seen the Cowboys lose to bad teams like the Buccaneers and Cardinals, so they can lose to anybody. If the defense can clean up the most fundamental issues such as tackling and lane discipline, this team may stand a chance at winning the NFC East. If not, we’ll continue to witness struggles against even the worst teams in the league. For 2027 and beyond, the Cowboys find themselves in a tough situation to navigate. Salary cap restructures or cuts with DaRon Bland, Kenny Clark, Rashan Gary and others are looming. The biggest decision of the offseason may come down to Joey Porter Jr. versus George Pickens and who gets a new deal. Losing either player significantly hurts the ability on their respective side of the ball. Dallas will also have to make decisions on their coaching staff from the head coach down. The entire picture is muddy as the defensive rebuild continues, maybe even requiring another step back to properly build it out moving forward. Dallas spent significant resources in the middle of 2025 and in 2026 trying to remake the defense into a respectable unit this season. Unfortunately, the results have not matched the investment. With time running out of the season, the next several weeks will determine what happens with this coaching staff and how much rope the front office will allow them to course correct this year and beyond.
author: Dyllan Rivers

summary: The shoe has dropped. It goes without saying that this is a rather seismic decision. Parker is in his first season […]
full_text: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images | Getty Images The shoe has dropped. After speculation ran rampant on Monday afternoon in the aftermath of words from Brian Schottenheimer and Jerry Jones it is now official: The Dallas Cowboys are stripping defensive coordinator Christian Parker from play-calling duties. Christian Parker will remain as Cowboys defensive coordinator but Mike Pettine, the senior defensive assistant, will call the defense on gamedays, sources tell me and @ByKimberleyA — Todd Archer (@toddarcher) November 18, 2026 It goes without saying that this is a rather seismic decision. Parker is in his first season with the Cowboys, obviously his first as their defensive coordinator, and it is his first season ever calling plays in general. Revoking that puts his future in doubt for the Cowboys, but that is obviously a discussion for another day. ESPN’s Todd Archer noted in his report of the news that Mike Pettine, senior defensive assistant, is set to call plays moving forward. This makes sense in the vacuum of the moment, but considering that Pettine joined the Cowboys only a month ago (after the Buccaneers loss and before the Packers game) it isn’t exactly the most organized operation at the moment. What do you think? Was this the right decision? Was it the least awful one? Let us know in the comments below.

title: Cowboys Week 11 opponent: A look at the 2026 Tennessee Titans
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are coming off one of the ugliest defensive performances in franchise history, but they’ll have an opportunity to get back on track against a Tennessee Titans team that is still searching for answers. Tennessee enters Week 11 at 1-8, sitting at the bottom of the AFC South and holding the No. 1 […]
full_text: Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are coming off one of the ugliest defensive performances in franchise history, but they’ll have an opportunity to get back on track against a Tennessee Titans team that is still searching for answers. Tennessee enters Week 11 at 1-8, sitting at the bottom of the AFC South and holding the No. 1 spot in the projected 2027 NFL Draft order. The Titans are clearly in rebuilding mode under head coach Robert Saleh. They’ve struggled to put together consistent performances on either side of the ball, and their recent decision to trade defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons and safety Amani Hooker is another indication that the organization is looking toward the future. Still, this isn’t necessarily a game Dallas can sleepwalk through. Rookie quarterback Cam Ward has shown improvement, Tony Pollard remains a productive running back, and Tennessee’s defense has been surprisingly opportunistic when it comes to taking the football away. The Cowboys are 4-6 and desperately need a win, but after allowing 46 points to San Francisco, there are plenty of reasons to approach this matchup with caution. Cam Ward is showing signs of progress The Titans’ season hasn’t gone according to plan, but there are reasons for optimism surrounding rookie quarterback Cam Ward. The No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft has experienced the growing pains that come with playing quarterback for a rebuilding team, but he’s starting to show why Tennessee invested so heavily in him. Through nine games, Ward has completed 63.8% of his passes for 1,714 yards, eight touchdowns and six interceptions. His 80.7 passer rating isn’t impressive, but he’s shown flashes of the arm talent and athleticism that made him the top selection. Ward’s most recent performance against Jacksonville was encouraging despite the 40-23 loss. He completed 28 of 39 passes for 231 yards and two touchdowns, while also throwing an interception. He directed five scoring drives and connected with running back Tony Pollard for a touchdown that kept Tennessee within striking distance. Ward has also contributed 151 rushing yards and two touchdowns this season. His mobility gives the Titans another option when plays break down, and Dallas has struggled to contain mobile quarterbacks and prevent explosive plays. There is still plenty of room for improvement. Ward has been sacked 14 times, and his six interceptions demonstrate that he can be vulnerable when forced to make difficult throws. Against Jacksonville, he threw an interception on a pass across his body, a decision that immediately put his defense in a difficult position. The Cowboys need to make him uncomfortable without allowing him to escape the pocket. After giving Brock Purdy and the 49ers far too much room to operate, Dallas needs a much more disciplined performance from its pass rush and secondary. Easy pass from Cam Ward to Daniel Bellinger for six JAXvsTEN on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/W4Lw36MZeM — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 An offense searching for consistency, with contributions from multiple players Tennessee’s offense has struggled to find its identity this season. The Titans are averaging just 18.6 points and 278.6 total yards per game, ranking 28th and 29th in the NFL, respectively. Their inability to sustain drives has been a major reason for their struggles. However, there are a few players Dallas needs to account for. Tony Pollard remains the focal point of the rushing attack. The former Cowboy has rushed for 628 yards and six touchdowns on 142 carries, averaging 4.4 yards per attempt. He’s also contributed 136 receiving yards and a touchdown, giving Ward a reliable option out of the backfield. Tony Pollard slips tackles for a 32-yard score! JAXvsTEN on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/FPR0vlha2W — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 Pollard is coming off a relatively quiet rushing performance against Jacksonville, finishing with just 33 yards on nine carries. However, he made an impact as a receiver, catching eight passes for 66 yards and a touchdown. The receiving corps is a collection of players who have contributed in different ways. Rookie Carnell Tate leads Tennessee with 413 receiving yards on 34 receptions, while Elic Ayomanor has added 290 yards and is averaging 16.1 yards per catch. Wan’Dale Robinson has caught 38 passes for 272 yards and three touchdowns, but he is going on injured reserve. Chimere Dike has contributed 140 receiving yards and a touchdown, while tight end Gunnar Helm has added 183 yards on 21 receptions. The Titans aren’t particularly explosive as a team, but they spread the ball around and have enough players capable of making plays to punish a defense that loses track of its assignments. The Titans defense can create turnovers, but gives up plenty of yards Tennessee’s defense has been one of the more inconsistent units in the league. The Titans are allowing 26.6 points per game and have surrendered approximately 391 total yards per contest, making it difficult for the offense to overcome the defense’s struggles, like the Cowboys. Their secondary has struggled. Tennessee is allowing 266.9 passing yards per game, the most in the NFL. That’s an inviting matchup for Dak Prescott and a Dallas passing offense that has averaged 368.3 total yards per game. There is one major caveat, however: Tennessee knows how to take the football away. The Titans have recorded nine interceptions through nine games, tied for fifth in the league. They also have 21 sacks, putting them in the middle of the pack in that category. Defensive end Jacob Martin leads the team with 7.5 sacks, giving Tennessee a legitimate pass-rush threat. Linebacker Cedric Gray has also shown playmaking ability. With injuries affecting the Titans’ linebacker group, Gray stepped into a larger role against Jacksonville and recorded nine tackles and an interception. He has an opportunity to become an important part of the defense as the season progresses. Cedric Gray was the best player on the #Titans defense against the Jaguars, and he should play every defensive the rest of this season He's still an explosive downhill run fitter, high-end athlete with sideline-to-sideline range and sound in coverage. Communication shortcomings… pic.twitter.com/HtCazRJTlv — Drew Beatty (@IronCityFilm) November 16, 2026 The Titans’ recent performance against Jacksonville was a good example of the unit’s highs and lows. Tennessee intercepted Trevor Lawrence in the first quarter, but still surrendered 40 points and 459 yards. The Jaguars converted seven of 14 third-down opportunities, repeatedly extending drives and keeping the Titans’ defense on the field. For Dallas, the formula should be straightforward. Protect Prescott, take advantage of Tennessee’s vulnerable secondary and avoid giving the Titans opportunities to create turnovers. The Cowboys have the personnel to exploit this defense, but they cannot afford to become careless with the football. Can Dallas bounce back? On paper, this is a favorable matchup for the Cowboys. Tennessee is 1-8, ranks near the bottom of the league in both scoring and total offense, and has struggled to stop opposing passing attacks. Dallas, meanwhile, has one of the more productive offenses in the NFL, averaging 28.6 points and 368.3 yards per game. But the Cowboys have bigger problems than their opponent’s record can solve. The defense is coming off a game in which it surrendered 46 points, 584 yards and three touchdowns of at least 60 yards. Christian Parker’s unit has struggled to tackle, communicate and prevent explosive plays. Those problems won’t disappear simply because the opponent is Tennessee. Ward has shown enough improvement to take advantage if Dallas continues to make the same mistakes. Pollard is familiar with the Cowboys and can contribute as both a runner and receiver, while Tennessee has enough receiving options to test a secondary that desperately…
author: Jorge Guajardo

title: How the Denver Broncos can beat the Las Vegas Raiders
summary: The Denver Broncos return to the gridiron this Sunday. It’ll be an AFC West affair when the Broncos host their longtime rival the Las Vegas Raiders. At 7-2, the Denver is one of the top teams in the AFC. In order to have a shot at repeating as division champs, beating the Raiders is a […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - DECEMBER 07: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos calls a timeout against the Las Vegas Raiders during the fourth quarter at Allegiant Stadium on December 07, 2025 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos return to the gridiron this Sunday. It’ll be an AFC West affair when the Broncos host their longtime rival the Las Vegas Raiders. At 7-2, the Denver is one of the top teams in the AFC. In order to have a shot at repeating as division champs, beating the Raiders is a must. Here are three ways they can make that happen. The Broncos need to come out strong on offense after the bye This season, many fans across Broncos Country had optimism Denver’s offense was going to finally take flight. They added Jaylen Waddle in a blockbuster trade and drafted Jonah Coleman to set up third-year quarterback Bo Nix for the best season of his young career. Unfortunately, the Broncos’ offense struggled in the first half of the season. The good news? Nix and his teammates have fared much better in the second half slate of games. Head Coach Sean Payton hinted on Colin Cowherd’s show there could be some potential changes for the offense if things don’t improve—particularly at the offensive line. With an extra week of preparation under their belt, it’s time for the offense to start firing on all cylinders versus the Raiders. For the most part, Las Vegas has really struggled defensively. Despite making numerous big-named additions in free agency, they are performing worse than they did in 2025. The Raiders sport one of the NFL’s worst rushing defenses giving up over 150 yards per contest. With respect to pass defense, they are in the bottom 10 giving up over 250 yards per contest. To make matters worse, they just can’t seem to get off the field on third down. Opposing teams are moving the chains over 45-percent in that situation. From my perspective, this division rivalry matchup will be a big opportunity to see if the offense can finally get in sync. This is a game where I expect Denver to execute running the ball, throwing the ball, and producing a lot of points on the scoreboard. No more excuses—just take care of business. Throw everything and the kitchen sink at rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza Over the past few weeks, the Broncos have been banged up on the defensive side of the ball. For multiple contests, they’ve been without several key starters to their secondary. That has made things a bit tougher, but fortunately the unit has been clutch in big moments and are a big reason why the Broncos boast seven wins through the first nine games of the season. This Sunday, Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph and his players have an opportunity to come out of the bye week and make a statement. Why? They will be facing rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza, whose second career start will be against the Broncos. Last Sunday, Mendoza struggled against the Seattle Seahawks in his NFL debut. He completed just 17 of 29 passes for 143 yards. Prior to Mendoza being quarterback with Kirk Cousins under center, the Raiders had allowed just 11 sacks on the season. Against the Seahawks, Mendoza was often hurried and flustered and was sacked six times. Even though they have regressed compared to their historic sack rates in 2024 and 2025, the Broncos’ pass rush has been formidable. Having their defensive trenches play at a high level will be a big part of a winning recipe. I’m confident that Joseph and company will be able to dial up the heat and cause Mendoza a lot of trouble on Sunday. Go out there and win the turnover battle It’s a theme we could use every week for these. However, there is no doubt the turnover battle will be important for the Broncos to win on Sunday. This season, Denver’s defense has done quite well forcing turnovers. They have twelve takeaways alongside multiple stops on fourth down and several goal line stands. While the Raiders’ defense ranks lowly in many categories that I mentioned above, they’ve been opportunistic with turnovers. They had two against Seattle—both of them forced fumbles on Drew Lock. That brings their tally to sixteen on the season, which is one of the highest marks in the NFL. Being ahead in the turnover margin would go a long way towards the Broncos earning their eighth victory of the season. Going up against a rookie quarterback gives them a shot at making some big plays. Will Denver’s defense be able to rise to the occasion? I certainly believe they will.
author: Christopher Hart

title: NFL picks and predictions: Broncos vs. Raiders and the rest of Week 11
summary: Welcome back to the eleventh installment of Hart’s Picks for the 2026 NFL regular season. For Week 10, I did okay. I was 9-5 with my picks, with losses coming from choosing the Giants, Dolphins, Packers, Texans, and Ravens. With last week’s picks, I’m up to a 99-52 record on the season. This week there […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 08: Pat Bryant #13 of the Denver Broncos celebrates after scoring a touchdown with Bo Nix #10 during the fourth quarter against the Carolina Panthers at Bank of America Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Grant Halverson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome back to the eleventh installment of Hart’s Picks for the 2026 NFL regular season. For Week 10, I did okay. I was 9-5 with my picks, with losses coming from choosing the Giants, Dolphins, Packers, Texans, and Ravens. With last week’s picks, I’m up to a 99-52 record on the season. This week there are just 13 games with the Atlanta Falcons, Cleveland Browns, Green Bay Packers, Los Angeles Rams, New England Patriots, and Seattle Seahawks on their byes. Let’s see how I do this week. Indianapolis Colts at Houston Texans — Thursday Night Football This AFC South matchup isn’t as intriguing as I would have expected prior to the season. The Colts, despite coming off a win last week against the Dolphins are 3-7. Meanwhile, the Texans are down to 3-6 after dropping a close game to the Browns last weekend. Quite frankly, it’s a must-win game for the Texans. If they can’t win at home, and they haven’t all season, their playoff chances are likely over. I’m rolling the dice on them in primetime versus the Colts. Winner: Texans Arizona Cardinals at Kansas City Chiefs — Sunday (Early Game) The Cardinals are at the bottom of the NFC West with a 3-7 record and the worst point differential in the NFL. On the flip side, the Kansas City Chiefs are 7-2 and are at the top of the AFC West. I have no reservations taking the Chiefs at home. Winner: Chiefs Miami Dolphins at Buffalo Bills — Sunday (Early Game) The odds of a 1-8 Dolphins team heading on the road and beating an 8-1 Bills team seems incredibly low. Josh Allen and the Bills offense is one of the best in the league and should have no problems handling Miami at home. I’m taking Buffalo. Winner: Bills Baltimore Ravens at Carolina Panthers — Sunday (Early Game) The Panthers are the top team in the NFC South with a 4-5 record. The Ravens’ season is on life support after losing on Monday Night Football to the Los Angeles Chargers who were winless before beating them. I expect Carolina to win this one at home and get to .500 on the season. Winner: Panthers Tennessee Titans at Dallas Cowboys — Sunday (Early Game) The Cowboys have one of the highest scoring offenses in the NFL, but one of the worst scoring defenses. That’s why Christian Parker is no longer calling plays for them. They need this win if they want to keep their postseason chances alive. It’s a must-win game. Luckily for Dallas, the Titans are 1-8 and quite awful. Winner: Cowboys Pittsburgh Steelers at Philadelphia Eagles — Sunday (Early Game) I’ll just call this one the Gridiron Battle of Pennsylvania . If the Steelers can’t beat an Eagles team that has dropped seven games in a row, that would be a problem. Pittsburgh needs this win to keep up with the Cincinnati Bengals in the AFC North. I’ll take the Steelers. Winner: Steelers Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions — Sunday (Early Game) The Lions have won five in a row, but they will be without Aiden Hutchinson the rest of the year after he tore his knee celebrating a sack against Drake Maye that likely ended his season as well. Meanwhile, the Buccaneers may be without Baker Mayfield in this one due to a foot strain. The Lions have overcome a lot of adversity this year to be the top team in the NFC North. I expect them to win and remain the top team in that division. Winner: Lions New Orleans Saints at Chicago Bears — Sunday (Early Game) It would be quite the upset for the Saints to roll into Chicago and topple the Bears on Sunday. I just don’t think they have the talent on defense to slow down Caleb Williams and Chicago’s rising offense. I’ll be taking Chicago here. Winner: Packers New York Jets at Los Angeles Chargers — Sunday (Afternoon Game) This matchup is of little interest to me due to the fact that these teams have a combined three wins on the season. I’m going to go out on a limb and say lightning strikes twice for the Chargers, who somehow find a way to win their second victory in a row at home versus the Jets. Winner: Chargers Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos — Sunday (Afternoon Game) Fernando Mendoza had his first start last weekend against the Seattle Seahawks and he didn’t do to well. Unfortunately, he has to go up against a strong Broncos defense who does well getting after the quarterback. I’m confident that Denver will capitalize after their bye week and move to 8-2 on the season. I’ll be picking Denver at home. Winners: Broncos Jacksonville Jaguars at New York Giants — Sunday (Afternoon Game) It’s a battle of division leaders when the Jaguars head on the road to face the Giants. Though I don’t think there’s much argument here. Jacksonville is clearly the better team and will prove that on Sunday with a decisive victory. Winner: Rams Cincinnati Bengals at Washington Commanders — Sunday Night Football The Bengals are atop of the AFC North and their offense is firing on all cylinders. They look like a team who could go deep into the playoffs if they can get a bit better on the defensive side of the ball. The Commanders may have the homefield advantage, but that won’t be enough to take down a ferocious Bengals squad in primetime. Winner: Bengals Green Bay Packers at Los Angeles Rams — Monday Night Football Monday Night Football’s gridiron affair between the Packers and Rams may be the game of the week that has the most on the line. Both teams are 6-4 and need a victory to keep pace in the NFC’s tough playoff race. Right now, the Packers are the presumptive seventh seed and wildcard. If they drop this game, the Rams wille hold that spot for the time being. I like Los Angeles here. They’ve won four in a row and have the homefield advantage. That’s why I’m taking them. Winner: Rams

full_text: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 1: Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos looks on form the sidelines during the third quarter against the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field at Mile High on November 1, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. The Broncos defeated the Chiefs 28-24. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country. The Denver Broncos are back to the gridiron his weekend after a much-needed bye week. On Sunday, they will host the Las Vegas Raiders in an AFC West rivalry matchup. Sporting a 7-2 record, the Broncos are neck-and-neck with the Kansas City Chiefs atop the division. However, the pack of teams chasing a playoff spot in the AFC this week is extremely competitive. Every game from here on out matters, but it’s mission critical for Denver to take care of business versus the Raiders. Yesterday after practice, Head Coach Sean Payton talked about the status of the team and how he’d like to see the Broncos improve down the second half stretch. He also had high praise for the Raiders, in particular, Head Coach Klint Kubiak, who is in his first season leading their team. “I know his father. I know he was here. He’s one of the guys I spent a lot of time with. I have a ton of respect for their family and what he’s doing. There are a lot of ties just to that organization,” stated Payton discussing the Kubiak family and their ties to Denver. “I think already you can see it on tape what they’re wanting to build and the early success this year. You go through Kansas City, Seattle, Buffalo, these are all teams that are in the thick of it, and they played all those teams to one-score games.” Last year, the Raiders were dead last in points scored and total yards on offense. Virtually every part on that side of the ball is a complete mess. Though things have gotten much better with Kubiak calling the shots on offense. They’ve made a marginal leap up the boards in yards per game but come in at tenth best in the NFL in points per game. Over the course of the offseason, Las Vegas made a lot of big investments to their defense. Unfortunately for them, those free agency signings haven’t made much of a difference. They have taken a step back in most metrics and are allowing the second most points in the league. However, they have been one of the best defenses in the NFL at forcing turnovers with 16 on the season. The Raiders have fizzled to 4-6 on the season after starting out the year 3-0. Nevertheless, they aren’t a team the Broncos can afford to underestimate. Payton knows that divisional games can be tough and went on to talk about some of the things he has noticed they do well on tape. “They return kicks well. They punt it well. They force fumbles better than anyone in the league. They’re really good offensively, red zone. They’ll possess the ball if you allow them to. They do a really good job of the time of possession. The takeaways have been noticeable,” stated Paton. Throughout the season, the Broncos have had a lot of ups and downs. To be where they are at with seven wins given their issues on both sides of the ball, particularly on offense, is quite the accomplishment. With an extra week of preparation and recuperation, Denver has to come out of the gate quickly and find their rhythm on offense versus the Raiders. On defense, hey will also have to find a way to rattle and get after rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza. The 2026 NFL Draft’s top pick will be making his second career NFL start on Sunday. If the Broncos can accomplish those two things, they’ll have a good shot at earning their eighth victory of the season. Let’s hope Denver can dominate on Sunday and start the second half trek of the season on a high note. As always, thank you for reading. Here is today’s slate of articles for Horse Tracks .

title: Midseason focus for Broncos is run blocking and 3rd-and-long coverage
summary: The Broncos have run the gauntlet of their schedule by and large at this point. Now, it is time for them to hone their game and improve in order to make a postseason run. I’m not taking anyone lightly, by the way. Every game is going to be hard coming down the stretch. Heck, even […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL , CO - JUNE 4: Alex Palczewski (63) of the Denver Broncos works out with Kage Casey (78) during OTAs at the Broncos Park in Centennial, Colorado on Thursday, June 4, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images The Broncos have run the gauntlet of their schedule by and large at this point. Now, it is time for them to hone their game and improve in order to make a postseason run. I’m not taking anyone lightly, by the way. Every game is going to be hard coming down the stretch. Heck, even the Los Angeles Chargers have found a way to win a game against the Baltimore Ravens on Monday Night Football . For the Broncos, my hope is that they spent some quality time during their bye week digging deep into the team’s inefficiencies: executing zone coverage on 3rd and long and run blocking. 3rd and long troubles One of the few nagging issues on the defensive side of the ball has been the number of longer 3rd downs they have given up conversions on. I’m not sure anything other than health is going to greatly improve this one. Getting Talanoa Hufanga and Brandon Jones back will go quite a long way in this arena. The one thing that this issue points to in my mind is the lack of high-level talent behind our starters. No offense to any of the backup safeties or corners that have been playing. They have absolutely been giving it their all and doing an admirable job. That being said, the team has obviously been running a lot more zone schemes with the players playing off to minimize the damage down the field. The good thing about getting the depth players so many snaps is that it leads to teachable moments. They are going to be able to see in detail why they needed to move sooner, play closer, or react quicker. They will also get coached on how to read the routes being run to predict where they need to be at a higher level. Run blocking We’ve been pointing to their issues blocking all year long. It isn’t just one player, either. While we can all point to Ben Powers as the weakest link, the offense has had gaffes from every position group. If you want some excellent breakdowns on the woes of the run game, please check out Tyler Polumbus’ breakdowns . The first and most impactful change I think is possible is giving Alex Palczewski or Kage Casey (if he’s ready) the start at left guard. We need more steady blocking there, as it has been a weak point all season long, consistently. The next piece is just good old hard coaching about run blocking. I’ve seen wide receivers and tight ends blocking poorly. I’ve seen atrocious first steps from several linemen. It almost seems like the focus for the offense has largely been in the passing game. They need to up their game in getting their assignments blocked. The final piece to this is going to happen naturally when the team gets back Tyler Badie and RJ Harvey. Badie has been a phenomenal force as a blocker and has chipped in some good runs this season. Harvey returning adds a different challenge to defenses, especially the raw speed he brings to the table. I’m cautiously optimistic about the Broncos running game moving forward, if for no other reason than Sean Payton specifically mentioning it as a focus for improvement. Payton doesn’t spout nonsense about things like this. If he says it is a problem and a focus, it will be a focus until it improves. It is possible that it won’t improve without changes in players, but rest assured that will happen if that is what it takes. title: The Detroit Lions’ road to a Super Bowl will be paved with adversity
summary: The Detroit Lions’ Super Bowl aspirations took another painful hit, but coach Dan Campbell isn’t interested in letting adversity change how this team pursues a championship. Following the injuries to Jack Campbell and Aidan Hutchinson, Campbell was asked about the frustration of not having his full arsenal of players available. His response was about as […]
full_text: The Detroit Lions’ Super Bowl aspirations took another painful hit, but coach Dan Campbell isn’t interested in letting adversity change how this team pursues a championship. Following the injuries to Jack Campbell and Aidan Hutchinson, Campbell was asked about the frustration of not having his full arsenal of players available. His response was about as Dan Campbell as it gets . “If you’re not careful, you lay in bed at night and you start thinking about all the what ifs, and at some point, you just become a miserable piece of shit. And I’m not going to do it. We’re not doing it. I refuse to look at it that way.” Losing players like Jack and Aidan stings. Of course it does. “What has happened with Jack Campbell and with Hutch now will not be in vain. We can’t allow it to. They got us to this point. And so what are we going to do about it, man? Are we just going to let it go to waste, or are we going to do something and pick up the slack?” It’s a motivating response, but there’s something deeply familiar about this message. Almost six years ago, Campbell stood before the Detroit media for his introductory press conference and laid out the DNA of what he wanted this football team to become. “This team is going to take on the identity of this city. And this city’s been down, and it found a way to get up. It’s found a way to overcome adversity.” Then, the kneecaps. Instantly legendary. But the underlying message was laced with wisdom beyond the sound bites: Detroit is going to fight . And as this team continues to navigate the ups and downs of the Dan Campbell era, I’ve started to appreciate something about the journey that I don’t think I fully understood when it began. If the Detroit Lions eventually win a Super Bowl, I don’t think it will come through a perfect season or a series of fortunate circumstances. It will come through adversity. It will come through setbacks, difficult decisions, unexpected challenges, and moments of doubt. And deep down, I believe that’s the version of this story worth having. That’s the version tailor-made for this city. The light at the end of the tunnel For most of my life, believing in the Lions required a certain degree of delusion. I gaslit myself into believing some embarrassingly bad football decisions were winning decisions (I was all-in on the 2019 signing of free agent tight end Jesse James). Then coach Campbell arrived in Allen Park. The first year and a half was rough. I could spare you from revisiting the details. But I won’t. I want you to remember what it felt like. 3-13-1 in 2021, including Justin Tucker’s record-breaking 66-yard field goal as time expired at Ford Field, an excruciating 16-16 tie against the Pittsburgh Steelers, followed by a 1-6 start in 2022. The Lions had spent nearly two full seasons getting knocked down, but they kept getting back up. By the end of 2022, the Lions were 9-8 and had won eight of their final 10 games, including the greatest game the Lions have ever played at Lambeau Field , which sent Aaron Rodgers packing. Dan Miller’s impassioned speech spoke to the whole city, signifying a great shift in mindset. “Let’s get comfortable with being uncomfortable because you know what uncomfortable is? It means you’re good. It means you have expectations upon you–and now this team does.” Then came 2023. For the first time in generations, Lions fans had a legitimate reason to believe they were watching something special. Detroit exorcised demons by winning its first division title since 1993, beat Matthew Stafford and the Los Angeles Rams in the playoffs, and won a second playoff game at Ford Field, beating the Buccaneers to reach the NFC Championship Game. It was extraordinarily satisfying to watch Jared Goff beat Sean McVay and Stafford. There was something prideful about watching Ford Field become one of the most intimidating home-field environments in the NFL. The city was unhinged. OnePride was a factor. The team was on the verge of kicking the damn Super Bowl door down. And, for a moment, it was all right there for the taking. Detroit led the San Francisco 49ers 24-7 at halftime of the NFC Championship Game. Just 30 minutes away from the biggest game in franchise history. There it was. The light at the end of the tunnel. Except it wasn’t a light. It was a freight train. The Lions climbed all the way to the doorstep of the Super Bowl, only to get knocked down again. In hindsight, maybe my mistake was ever thinking that reaching that level of success—that light at the end of the tunnel—meant the hard part was finally over. After the game, Campbell spoke to a reality that, looking back on, I didn’t fully believe or couldn’t truly appreciate . “I told those guys, this may have been our only shot. Do I think that? No. Do I believe that? No. However, I know how hard it is to get here. I’m well aware. It’s going to be twice as hard to get back to this point next year than it was last year. That’s the reality.” When the Super Bowl becomes the expectation After unfamiliar success, I was convinced the 2024 season would be the year. Sure enough, the Lions got back up off the mat after the loss in San Francisco, went 15-2, and secured the NFC’s No. 1 seed. The offense was dominant, and the team had established itself as one of the NFL’s best. The gut punches, however, wouldn’t stop. The injuries kept coming. Hutchinson, Alim McNeill, Carlton Davis III, Derrick Barnes, and Malcolm Rodriguez all suffered season-ending injuries. Ultimately, the Washington Commanders ended Detroit’s season in the divisional round. But I also think something else happened during that period. For a fan base that had spent decades hoping to see a competitive Lions team, the Super Bowl had finally become the expectation. I know it happened to me. I believed in what Dan Campbell and Brad Holmes had built so much that I started expecting the Lions to win every single week. That was not necessarily a bad thing. This team had earned that confidence. Back to Dan Miller’s proclamation to get comfortable being uncomfortable: the uncomfortable feeling can’t fade away as the seasons go by. When Campbell spoke to the reality about the difficulty of repeating success in this league, I should have fully believed him. See, when you stop feeling that uncomfortable feeling, when the expectation is not complemented with appreciation for the moment and adversity, the edge becomes lost. The fire built up over years of starving for winning dies down. That uncomfortable feeling is essential. Back to the ground level Then came 2025. Ben Johnson left to become the head coach of the Chicago Bears. While many have called it a sign of betrayal, I think Ben’s deliberate choice to take the Bears job signified more. It suggests, perhaps subconsciously, his true belief: that he is better. That he would build a team better than Campbell and the Lions ever could without him. And in just one season, he started to make his case. The Lions struggled to recalibrate, injuries continued to take their toll, and the season ended with a 9-8 record and no playoff appearance. Meanwhile, Chicago won the NFC North. For a team that had spent the previous two seasons establishing itself as the division’s best, watching Ben Johnson instantly bring success to Chicago was humbling. Campbell’s immediate response at his end-of-season press conference, however, was notable. He said he wanted to get back to what the Lions were doing in 2022. “I want to get back to some of the things we were doing a couple of years ago. And what I mean by that is just getting back to a little bit of what we did at the ground level, just a little bit of the way we train, the way we go about things.” See, Dan speaks from his gut. He lets his experience and instincts be his compass. I think that quote is representative. His gut told him the team had lost something it once embodied. He recognized that some of the foundational elements that made them who they are as an organization needed…

title: Lions CB D.J. Reed won’t rush back after last year’s injury issues
summary: When Detroit Lions cornerback D.J. Reed went down with a hip injury in the team’s Week 8 game against the Minnesota Vikings, he couldn’t help but feel some frustrating déjà vu. Like last year, when a serious hamstring injury caused him to miss six games, he was again sidelined while at the top of his […]
full_text: Oct 4, 2026; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Detroit Lions cornerback D.J. Reed (4) looks on during warmups before the game against the Carolina Panthers at Bank of America Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect When Detroit Lions cornerback D.J. Reed went down with a hip injury in the team’s Week 8 game against the Minnesota Vikings, he couldn’t help but feel some frustrating déjà vu. Like last year, when a serious hamstring injury caused him to miss six games, he was again sidelined while at the top of his game. In an odd coincidence, in both games he was injured, he even tallied his first interceptions of the season. Instead of building on that progress, he now had to watch from the sidelines again. But this time around, he’s going through the process with a little more wisdom. In 2025, the hamstring injury was enough to land him on injured reserve—he estimates either a Grade 2 or 3—but he thankfully avoided surgery. In retrospect, though, he believes he rushed his way back onto the field. “When you get hurt, you obviously want to get back on the field as soon as possible. I kinda undermined the severity of a hamstring strain, especially a high-grade one, because I never hurt a hamstring that bad,” Reed said. “In hindsight, yes, I do feel like I came back (too) early.” When Reed returned to the field, he thought he was fine, but in the offseason, he noticed his clear lack of burst. His speed was gone, and it led to a tough stretch of football. PFF credited Reed with allowing 24 catches for 344 yards and a touchdown in the final seven games of the season. So this time around, he’s conscientious about returning too soon. The stakes are too high, and the defense is playing too well for him to jeopardize things by thrusting himself into the lineup before his body is ready. “I definitely want to make sure I come back and I feel like myself. I don’t want to rush it, especially because our defense is playing well,” Reed said. “So I don’t want to be a hindrance. So I just gotta be honest with myself, be honest with the trainers and my coaches to see if I’m ready to go, whenever that is.” Without Reed in the lineup, the Lions have allowed just 10 points against the Dolphins and 10 against the Patriots. Sure, that was against a poor Dolphins offense and a Patriots team without starting quarterback Drake Maye for most of the game, but Reed’s supporting cast of Rock Ya-Sin, Roger McCreary and a pair of solid safeties Brian Branch and Chuck Clark have undeniably been balling out. “I’m very proud of them,” Reed said. “Not just the DBs, but the whole defensive unit. Guys just continuing to step up. Like we always say, it’s a next-man-up business. Roger’s playing very well. Rock played amazing last game. Chuck is playing phenomenal. BB’s playing great, so we’ve just got to keep it up.” Reed wouldn’t offer too many details on the current hip injury, noting just that he thinks it’s a Grade 2 and he doesn’t think he’ll play this week against the Buccaneers. But he also made it clear he doesn’t think he’s going on injured reserve and he is getting better. “I’m progressing, I’m healing, I’m going to be fine. Just rehabbing and working it,” Reed said. On Wednesday, he took his first significant step toward coming back, being listed as a limited participant during Detroit’s walkthrough practice. But he won’t know for sure until he’s out there going full speed and can tell whether that explosiveness is truly back. “I think that’s the number one thing at my position is making sure I’ve got my burst, making sure that I could get the top-end speed, making sure that I can turn and flip the receivers like this and everything feels normal. I think that’s the most important thing.”

title: Lions, Bucs Week 11 injury report: D.J. Reed returns to practice
summary: The Detroit Lions (7-2) are back home in Week 11 and preparing to host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6). As the Lions work to reacclimate after returning from Germany earlier in the week, they elected to hold a walkthrough on Wednesday. A walkthrough practice means that all participation levels are estimates from the coaching staff […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 01: D.J. Reed #4 of the Detroit Lions is introduced ahead of a game against the Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field on November 01, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Mike Mulholland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions (7-2) are back home in Week 11 and preparing to host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6). As the Lions work to reacclimate after returning from Germany earlier in the week, they elected to hold a walkthrough on Wednesday. A walkthrough practice means that all participation levels are estimates from the coaching staff based on how the player would have participated in a traditional practice. So, with that in mind, let’s look at Wednesday’s injury report and get you up to date on what we know. Note: Any changes from the most recent injury report will be bolded . Injured list updates RB Isiah Pacheco (MCL/Back, IR) — expected to be out until December OL Giovanni Manu (undisclosed, NFI) — eligible to begin practicing at any time OL Ben Bartch (foot, IR) — eligible to begin practicing at any time EDGE Aidan Hutchinson (ACL, IR) — requires surgery; his season is over LB Devin White (forearm, IR) — eligible to begin practicing at any time LB Jack Campbell (neck, IR) — determined to play football again S Thomas Harper (ankle, IR) — eligible to begin practicing at any time Estimated n o practice C Cade Mays (low ankle sprain) Earlier in the week, Lions coach Dan Campbell said he wasn’t sure if Mays would be able to return to play this week, and while an estimated no practice to start the week is not ideal, he could still return to practice this week, even if the plan is not to play him. Estimated limited practice RB Sione Vaki (ankle) DL Tyler Lacy (shoulder) — New Injury LB Joe Bachie (knee) — New Injury CB D.J. Reed (hip) — UPGRADED from no practice last week CB Khalil Dorsey (ankle) — New Injury CB Ennis Rakestraw (shoulder) — New Injury Vaki missed two practices last week with an ankle injury, returned to practice on Friday in Germany, and played in the game. An estimated limited practice is a step in the right direction as he looks to stay on the field this weekend. Lacy did not appear to be limited by this injury in Germany, and Campbell has noted that the big end is in the plans to help replace Hutchinson, so an estimated limited practice is worth monitoring but with some optimism. Bachie didn’t play many defensive snaps last Sunday, but he’s been a consistent special teams contributor. Hopefully this injury won’t keep him sidelined. Reed’s status is still up in the air, as Campbell said he wasn’t sure whether the Lions’ top corner would be available against the Bucs. That being said, an estimated limited practice is a good sign that even if he can’t return this Sunday, he could be on track to return against the Bears on Thanksgiving. Dorsey was notably injured against the Patriots and required trainers’ assistance on the field in Germany. The Lions never assigned him an in-game injury designation, which suggests they were trying to see if he could return. Couple that with an estimated limited practice, and he’ll have a chance to play on Sunday. Rakestraw played only a limited number of snaps in Germany, though it’s not clear whether that was the plan ahead of time or whether this shoulder injury changed things. We’ll have to see how he progresses this week before we know his availability. title: Detroit Lions officially activate Kerby Joseph, place Aidan Hutchinson on IR
summary: On Wednesday, the Detroit Lions made two moves that were both expected, placing Aidan Hutchinson on injured reserve, while activating Kerby Joseph from the Physically Unable to Perform list to the 53-man roster. Joseph takes Hutchinson’s spot on the roster, keeping the roster at 53 players for now. Hutchinson’s placement on injured reserve is no […]
full_text: DETROIT, MI - SEPTEMBER 28: Detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph (31) takes the field prior to the Detroit Lions versus the Cleveland Browns game on Sunday September 28, 2025 at Ford Field in Detroit, MI. (Photo by Steven King/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images On Wednesday, the Detroit Lions made two moves that were both expected, placing Aidan Hutchinson on injured reserve, while activating Kerby Joseph from the Physically Unable to Perform list to the 53-man roster. Joseph takes Hutchinson’s spot on the roster, keeping the roster at 53 players for now. Hutchinson’s placement on injured reserve is no surprise, given that the team confirmed he tore his ACL while celebrating in Sunday’s win over the New England Patriots. While Hutchinson will miss the remainder of the season, coach Dan Campbell was optimistic he’d work his way back and be better than ever next year. “Knowing Hutch, he will attack this like he did the last time, and he will come back better than ever next year,” Campbell said. He also mentioned that the damage in his knee may go beyond just his ACL. “It sounds like there’s a little bit (more damage) in there. I don’t know how significant all of that is. And some of it you’re not going to know until you go in there and actually do the procedure,” Campbell said. As for Joseph, Campbell already notified media earlier in the week that the plan was to get the All-Pro safety involved this week. And while Joseph will be on a pitch count against the Buccaneers, Campbell doesn’t expect it to be too strict. “Is there a pitch count? Yeah, but not like what (Brian) Branch had his first game. So, I think we’re going to be able to get a little bit more out of Kerby here,” Campbell said on Tuesday. In addition to these moves, the Lions also re-signed cornerback Nick Whiteside to the practice squad, filling the vacancy left by Detroit’s cutting of defensive lineman Ben Stille earlier this week.
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: Detroit Lions planning to debut Ahmed Hassanein vs. Buccaneers
summary: The long wait is over. Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell noted on Wednesday that the current plan is to have defensive end—and fan favorite—Ahmed Hassanein make his NFL debut this Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Hassanein has been a healthy scratch all season, despite the fact that he was one of the more impressive […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - AUGUST 13: Detroit Lions defensive end Ahmed Hassanein (99) walks off the field at halftime during the preseason game between the Detroit Lions and the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The long wait is over. Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell noted on Wednesday that the current plan is to have defensive end—and fan favorite—Ahmed Hassanein make his NFL debut this Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Hassanein has been a healthy scratch all season, despite the fact that he was one of the more impressive defensive players during training camp and the preseason, albeit mostly working with the second and third teams. But after Aidan Hutchinson’s season-ending ACL injury last week, Campbell mentioned Hassanein among the players he has confidence in at the edge position moving forward. “We still feel pretty good about the edges that we have with (DJ) Wonnum and Derrick Moore and (Eric) O’Neill, and then we’ll probably get Ahmed going here a little bit,” Campbell said. Campbell was then asked how ready he thinks Hassanein will be to finally play in his first regular-season action. “How ready do you think he’s going to be?” Campbell said with a smirk, referencing Hassanein’s unmatchable intensity and drive. “He brings it every day in practice, just like you saw in camp,” Campbell said. “He’s out there and he tries do—everything you ask him to do in practice as far as he’s working his craft, what he’s being taught to by (DL coach) Kacey (Rodgers). And then when you get him on scout team, he wants to do exactly what the opponent does. […] He’s making himself better; he makes us better. So it’s going to be a great opportunity.” Hassanein was the Lions’ sixth-round pick in 2025, and lost most of his rookie season to a pectoral injury before rejoining the practice squad late. Due to his unique origin story—hailing from Egypt and learning the game of football late in high school—and intensity (telling Campbell “I will die for you” on his draft day phone call), Hassanein quickly became a fan favorite. And he flashed some of that football potential in the preseason, when he tallied 2.0 sacks, five quarterback hits, and one forced fumble in three games. With him—along with the versatility of players like Tyler Lacy, Skyler Gill-Howard, and Levi Onwuzurike—Campbell believes the team will be ready to bounce back from the Hutchinson injury, no matter what the situation calls for. “I feel like we’re equipped to kinda play the game any way we need to defensively with what we’ve got,” Campbell said.
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: Lions vs. Buccaneers thoughts after watching TB vs. Bears
summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are coming off a bye after a narrow loss to the Chicago Bears on “Sunday Night Football.” To get a sense of what the Detroit Lions could expect from the Buccaneers this week, I went back and re-watched that Buccaneers vs. Bears game and came out with six thoughts about this […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 08: Bucky Irving #7 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers carries the ball against the Chicago Bears during the third quarter at Soldier Field on November 08, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are coming off a bye after a narrow loss to the Chicago Bears on “Sunday Night Football.” To get a sense of what the Detroit Lions could expect from the Buccaneers this week, I went back and re-watched that Buccaneers vs. Bears game and came out with six thoughts about this upcoming matchup. Pass rush very effective… when blitzing The Buccaneers were an absolute terror for Caleb Williams, forcing him into four interceptions and just a 59.5 completion percentage. And while they only sacked him once, Williams faced a total of 25 pressures. But the Buccaneers also had to be super aggressive to create that pressure. Per NFL Pro, they blitzed 63.4% of the time, second only to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 9. Turns out for the season, they absolutely need to blitz to create pressure. For the season, the Bucs only have a 33.2% pressure rate (24th) and 5.0% sack rate (25th). But they may have found some answers with the blitz this past game. For the season, they still look like an ineffective blitzing team (28th in pressure rate when blitzing, 30th in sack rate), but with their highest blitz rate of the season vs. the Bears, they got home early and often. Bucky Irving is a dude Irving finished this game with 97 rushing yards, 4.9 yards per carry, and two touchdowns, but it was the manner in which he gained those yards that was particularly impressive. Per NFL Pro, he had 83 yards after contract. For the season, Irving ranks fifth in rushing yards after contact per game (65.9), 12th in yards after contract per rush (3.6), and leads the league with 16 broken tackles forced. He is a forced to be reckoned with, and the Lions will need to make sure they are tackling by committee on Sunday. The Bucs run game is inconsistent but strong No one runs the ball more than Tampa Bay, although that is admittedly skewed by Week 8, when Tampa ran the ball 56 times and threw it just three times in a monsoon. Still, I was mesmerized by just how versatile and diverse their run game was. They do under center, shotgun, zone, power, gap. They’ll try to run between the tackles, then hit you with a toss play. This graph is a pretty good indication of how they aren’t married to one kind of run, which speaks to the versatility of their decent offensive line ( top-10 per PFF ): Every team's run concept mix through Week 10: pic.twitter.com/5cK0tUTnge — SūmerSports (@SumerSports) November 17, 2026 But despite their strong running back and diverse scheme, the efficiency just isn’t what it should be. They’re ninth in rush EPA and ninth in success rate (43.9%). That’s certainly not bad, but it just seems like it should be better. Passing game has no identity Against the Bears, Baker Mayfield was just bad. He was inaccurate (-7.9% completion over expected) and he threw two interception. Aside from one deep ball connection with Tez Johnson, just about everything he completed was within 5 yards of the line of scrimmage. He hasn’t been helped by a weak receiving corps. While Emeka Egbuka still has WR1 potential, the Buccaneers were victimized by a pair of critical drops from second-year receiver Johnson. In short, it just looked like there was no chemistry between Mayfield and his receivers. For the season, the Buccaneers are just 30th in dropback EPA and 31st in dropback success rate. They could play Jalon Daniels this week, but he’s averaging just 5.1 yard sper attempt and has a 63.3 passer rating on the season. Interior offensive line could be a weakness With Jeffery Simmons aboard, the Bears were able to create a ton of havoc up the middle vs. Tampa, in both the run and in terms of pass rush. While at times it seems like Tampa is getting a ton of push up the middle, all three starting interior offensive linemen rank in the bottom half of the league in run blocking grade. Pass protection seemed like a bigger issue against the Bears, though. All three posted PFF pass blocking grades lower than 60, with left guard Ben Bredeson ceding pressure, center Graham Barton responsible for one sack, and right guard Cody Mauch posting a 52.1 pass blocking grade. While Detroit may be overmatched at the tackle positions—with Tristan Wirfs and Jake Goedeke at the top of their games, and Aidan Hutchinson out—Alim McNeill, Skyler Gill-Howard, and Tyleik Williams could be in line for big days. That secondary is balling While they were helped by a reinvigorated pass rush against the Bears, the secondary made everything difficult for Caleb Williams on Sunday night. Jacob Parrish is perhaps the most surprising of breakout players, as he is currently PFF’s No.4 graded cornerback in just his second year in the NFL. Opposite him, Zyon McCollum has 11 pass breakups (t-third in NFL) and four interceptions (t-third). And Tampa’s safeties Antoine Winfield Jr. and Tykee Smith are both ballers, as well.

title: Detroit Lions’ playoff odds: Postseason, division, Super Bowl probabilities
summary: The Detroit Lions are in a pretty darn good position through 10 weeks, sitting at 7-2 overall while currently holding the NFC’s No. 2 seed. They’re at the top of a competitive NFC North via tiebreakers, and you can see the full NFC playoff picture laid out here. But despite that 7-2 record, the Lions’ […]
full_text: Munich, Germany - November 15: Jared Goff of Detroit Lions gestures during the NFL match between New England Patriots and Detroit Lions at Allianz Arena on November 15, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Mario Hommes/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images) | DeFodi Images via Getty Images The Detroit Lions are in a pretty darn good position through 10 weeks, sitting at 7-2 overall while currently holding the NFC’s No. 2 seed. They’re at the top of a competitive NFC North via tiebreakers, and you can see the full NFC playoff picture laid out here. But despite that 7-2 record, the Lions’ path to the playoffs will not be a cakewalk in the final eight weeks of the season. Not only do they have four remaining divisional games, but the entire NFC conference is pretty competitive among the top-nine teams. For example, the ninth-ranked team in the conference—the Los Angeles Rams—are just two games behind Detroit at 6-4, and LA has won four in a row. The 6-4 Seattle Seahawks (eighth in NFC) have won three of their last four. So let’s take our first look at the Lions’ playoff odds—including their chances to win the NFC North, secure the conference’s top seed, and reach the Super Bowl—according to several analytical models. Postseason odds: NYT simulator: 79% RBSDM: 78% DVOA: 77.7% ESPN (FPI): 89.4% To hold a 7-2 record and have less than a four-in-five probability to make the playoffs shows just how competitive this division is. However, you’ll notice a pattern here: ESPN is curiously very high on the Lions compared to the rest of the models. I’m not exactly clear why, but I imagine it has something to do with having just the 16th-hardest remaining schedule, per their model. That’s among the easiest compared to the rest of the NFC contenders (49ers: 9th, Rams: 1st, Bears: 6th, Seahawks: 2nd, Vikings: 22nd, Packers: 5th). NFC North title odds NYT simulator: 24% (Behind Vikings, Bears) RBSDM: 26% (Behind Vikings, Bears) DVOA: 19.4% (Behind Vikings, Bears) ESPN (FPI): 33.1% (Behind Vikings) For all four models, the Vikings have the best odds to win the division, despite Detroit currently holding the top spot. Perhaps that’s because of their schedule. Perhaps that’s because they’ve already tallied an impressive 3-1 record in the division. The Bears are generally favored over Detroit as the stronger of the two teams, but they’ll have to overcome a brutal schedule ahead—and an o-2 record in the division. Meanwhile, every model has the Packers’ NFC North title odds below 3 percent, because they’re both two games back and have a 1-3 divisional record. NFC’s No. 1 seed NYT simulator: 10% RBSDM: 12% DVOA: 6.9% ESPN : 9% Though Detroit is just a single game behind the NFC West-leading 49ers—and San Francisco has a brutal schedule—Detroit has somewhere around just a 10 percent chance of earning a first round bye. But given the bye didn’t help the Lions at all in 2024, I doubt Detroit fans care much. Super Bowl appearance odds ESPN (FPI): 10.4% DVOA: 5.9% Yes, it’s weird to me, too, that ESPN gives the Lions a better shot to make it to the Super Bowl than to win the NFC’s top regular season seed. But I’ll take a 10.4% chance at this point in the season. DVOA is much more down on Detroit, seeing as they have the Lions ranked as the 13th best team overall .

title: Detroit Lions scouting report: Tampa Bay’s defense is dangerous
summary: After a trip overseas to Germany, the Detroit Lions return home to Ford Field to face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Detroit comes in at 7-2, on a five-game winning streak with no signs of slowing down, and has become the top team in the NFC North. Both sides of the ball are humming, despite being […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 8: Alex Anzalone #34 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers reacts during the third quarter against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on November 8, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a trip overseas to Germany, the Detroit Lions return home to Ford Field to face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Detroit comes in at 7-2, on a five-game winning streak with no signs of slowing down, and has become the top team in the NFC North. Both sides of the ball are humming, despite being down star EDGE Aidan Hutchinson for the season with a torn ACL . Tampa Bay, meanwhile, is coming off a much-needed bye week after winning two of its last three games to improve to 3-6. While the record isn’t pretty, this team is better than it shows. They were without starting quarterback Baker Mayfield for three weeks, and the team went 1-2 in his absence. Since he’s been back, the offense has improved, and the defense continues to play strong. Like Detroit, the Bucs still have a chance to win their division despite their record, as the NFC South continues to appear as the worst division in the NFL. Let’s take a deep look at the Bucs and how their 2026 season has been so far. Tampa Bay Buccaneers 2026 season thus far (3-6) Week 1: Lost to Cincinnati Bengals 33-27 Week 2: Lost to Cleveland Browns 23-19 Week 3: Lost to Minnesota Vikings 23-16 Week 4: Lost to Green Bay Packers 17-14 Week 5: Defeated Dallas Cowboys 24-16 Week 6: Lost to Pittsburgh Steelers 26-19 OT Week 7: Defeated Carolina Panthers 43-13 Week 8: Defeated Atlanta Falcons 16-0 Week 9: Lost to Chicago Bears 27-24 Week 10: BYE Offensive stats: As I mentioned earlier, Mayfield has missed time due to injury, and he hasn’t been as solid as he was last year, throwing for 922 yards, a 60.6 completion percentage, three touchdowns, and four interceptions. This follows a contract extension he signed with the Bucs for three years at $165 million. In his absence, backup rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels took over and was a mixed bag, throwing for 501 yards, a 61.2 completion percentage, three touchdowns, and five interceptions in the four games he played for Mayfield. While the passing game has had its woes, the running back spot has seen solid play from its starter, Bucky Irving. Irving has been having a solid season, rushing for 825 yards (fifth in the NFL), averaging 4.9 yards per carry and seven touchdowns. When the team needed to lean on him, he’s answered the call as the passing game has taken a step back. The wide receiver room seemed to have found its next star in Emeka Egbuka last year, but now that their other former star, Mike Evans, is gone, it’s been a rough go for the group. Egbuka is the leader with 31 catches for 278 yards and two touchdowns, but for the leader to be that low at Week 11 is shocking. Chris Godwin just doesn’t look like the same player he was before the injuries piled up, with 29 catches for 259 yards. The team has a young core outside of Godwin, and life without Evans has been rougher than expected. Tampa Bay just can’t seem to move the ball through the air, as they are in the bottom tier of multiple passing statistics. Part of the issue has been the quarterback play, but also the receivers struggling to get open. According to PFF, Tampa Bay’s receivers grade out to 59.2, ranked 31st, ahead of only the Los Angeles Chargers. The offensive line is ranked sixth in pass-blocking (73.7), so the blame can’t be put on them. Defensive stats: On defense, they’re one of the best units in the NFL, arguably better than the Minnesota Vikings. The pass rush isn’t as dominant, but it’s still a respectable front seven that teams can’t ignore. Linebacker David Walker leads the team with four sacks, with YaYa Diaby behind him at three. The former Lion trio of defenders—Al-Quadin Muhammad, Alex Anzalone, and A’Shawn Robinson—has four sacks combined. You also can’t ignore the beast at nose tackle, Vita Vea, who hasn’t had a big season, but is still a problem teams need to prepare for. Meanwhile, the secondary has played solid defense this year. Cornerback Zyon McCollum is tied with Anzalone with four interceptions and seems to be becoming a lockdown corner for this team. Second-year cornerback Jacob Parrish has been involved too, leading the team in pass deflections with 14 and has two interceptions of his own. This defense has dominated the turnover battle, with 21 takeaways, leading the NFL. They’ve gotten 16 interceptions and five fumbles. The entire defense picking off quarterbacks. It doesn’t matter where you throw the ball; anybody at any level can create a turnover through the air. You also have to respect the Bucs’ run defense. They’ve allowed the fewest rushing yards (712) and the third-lowest yards per carry (3.5), while only allowing three rushing touchdowns, the fewest in the NFL. They’ve contained the big plays, allowing only four 20+ yard runs, with the longest being for 31. Injury notes Key players ruled out : None Key players to monitor : QB Baker Mayfield (foot), WR Jalen McMillan (IR), WR Emeka Egbuka (foot), LB Yaya Diaby (knee) Wide receiver Jalen McMillan is on IR and can return, but odds are, with no practices in him yet, he will not play this week. Egbuka was questionable in Week 9 but played with a foot injury, so with the week off, we can see if there has been any improvement. Diaby didn’t play in Week 9 due to a knee injury, so like Egbuka, if the week off helps, Diaby could return on Sunday. The biggest story came up on Sunday: Mayfield suffered a foot injury against the Chicago Bears in Week 9, and his status this week is unknown. The Bucs signed quarterback Cooper Rush to their practice squad and elevated Easton Stick to their 53-man roster on Monday, which could be insurance if Mayfield can’t see the field on Sunday. Mayfield will be the biggest name to watch this week, and this team has played without him already this season, so it wouldn’t be something they haven’t dealt with before. The #Lions are up big in Germany right now then head back to Detroit to face the #Buccaneers . Right now, it’s unclear whether they’ll see Baker Mayfield, as sources say he’s dealing with a lower-leg injury suffered against the #Bears https://t.co/PJvIgW0idw — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) November 15, 2026 Biggest strength: Turnovers You’d think with the amount of turnovers the Bucs defense has generated this year, their record would be better than what it is. Unfortunately, even if you lead the NFL in turnovers, it doesn’t always guarantee success. Either way, what the Bucs are doing right now is impressive, and even more impressive is how versatile they are in generating these interceptions. Interceptions by position Cornerbacks – 6 Linebackers – 6 Safeties – 2 Defensive lineman – 2 View Link For a defensive lineman like Robinson to have as many interceptions as safety Tykee Smith is impressive. The Bucs are averaging 1.7 interceptions a game this season, and if they keep that pace up, they will finish with 30 interceptions. The last team to get 30 interceptions was the 2009 Green Bay Packers. While it isn’t close to the NFL record (hello 1961 San Diego Chargers with 49!), it’s still tough, and teams have to watch it when throwing the football. Biggest weakness: Wide receivers It’s a bit surprising to list this position as the team’s biggest weakness, but the evidence speaks for itself. The loss of Evans is bigger than the team expected, and while Egbuka is a good player to take on that WR1 role, he isn’t the same player as Evans. Egbuka had almost 1,000 yards last year as the number two option, but now that all eyes are on him, he isn’t getting that same kind of production. He certainly took advantage of having someone like Evans on the roster, but with most of the pressure on him, Egbuka seems to be struggling a little bit. Then you have Godwin, who’s taken a big step back due to all the injuries that have piled up over the past few…
