summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Jaguars fans and fans across the country. With a 7-2 record about halfway through the 2026 NFL season, the Jacksonville Jaguars are tied for third in win percentage (.778) and rank top three […]
full_text: Oct 6, 2025; Jacksonville, Florida, USA; Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington (11) celebrates with wide receiver Travis Hunter (12) after a touchdown during the first half against the Kansas City Chiefs at EverBank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Morgan Tencza-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Jaguars fans and fans across the country. With a 7-2 record about halfway through the 2026 NFL season, the Jacksonville Jaguars are tied for third in win percentage (.778) and rank top three in FPI and DVOA efficiency metrics. They lead the league in point differential (+125). The Jags are elite, and we all know their coaching staff plays a major part. But it’s always been players over plays. Trevor Lawrence has been Jacksonville’s best player this season. He’s on pace for 4,314 passing yards and 40 passing touchdowns — if the season ended today, it’d be the best in franchise history in terms of yards per attempt (8.8), passer rating (112.8), EPA per dropback (0.281), and dropback success rate (53.4%). It’s not a conversation. pic.twitter.com/UIOI94XVIo — Gus Logue (@gus_logue) November 18, 2026 Lawrence is the main catalyst of this team. Outside of the quarterback position, though, it’s a toss-up between a few guys for Midseason MVP. Two of this year’s stars had big cleats to fill. Ventrell Miller replaced All-Pro linebacker Devin Lloyd and currently leads his position in PFF grade; Bhayshul Tuten filled in for 1,000-yard rusher Travis Etienne and is on pace to score 15 touchdowns. DaVon Hamilton probably deserved to be an option for this survey. Walker Little deserves a shoutout for filling in more than admirably at left tackle. And Cam Little has been automatic. But this probably comes down to Parker Washington or Travis Hunter. Who do you think has been the Jaguars’ best non-quarterback so far this season? Who has been Jacksonville’s best player? Are you confident in the Jaguars? Sign up here to participate in the weekly emailed surveys: Let us know your thoughts in the comments below!

(Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars have received injury news on starting center and captain Robert Hainsey Wednesday morning. Jaguars starting center Robert Hainsey is considered week-to-week with a knee sprain, per sources. Very well could miss time but not season-ending. pic.twitter.com/8d6cqd5uxT — Jeremy Fowler (@JFowlerESPN) November 18, 2026 For the overall depth of the Jaguars, Hainsey not being ruled out for the season is a huge boon. title: Expect Travis Kelce to continue playing through his ankle injury
summary: Most observers expect 2026 to be the final season for Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce — who will likely then be a first-ballot Pro Football Hall of Fame selection. Unfortunately, our possible final months of watching the star appear are impacted by a recurring ankle injury first suffered in Week 6 against the […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Most observers expect 2026 to be the final season for Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce — who will likely then be a first-ballot Pro Football Hall of Fame selection. Unfortunately, our possible final months of watching the star appear are impacted by a recurring ankle injury first suffered in Week 6 against the Los Angeles Chargers . After seeing the ankle repeatedly taped since — and covering Kelce on every published injury report — he seemed to aggravate it badly in the first quarter of Sunday’s win over the Atlanta Falcons . Although he went to the locker room and was listed as questionable to return, Kelce made it back into the game and even recorded another catch. In the team’s first practice before Week 11’s game against the Arizona Cardinals, Kelce was listed as a full participant with the ankle injury. Speaking before practice, head coach Andy Reid said Kelce was ready to fight the coaches to reenter. “He wants to play,” remarked Reid. “He wants to practice every play. He wants to play every play. I want to make sure that thing doesn’t get worse. Unfortunately, that play — the whole action of twisting probably wasn’t really good for it.” Still, how Kelce looked limping off the field in Atlanta should not be confused with how he must be feeling as the Chiefs start another practice week. The coach also noted that Kelce’s particular ankle injury lends itself to quick recovery, even when it is aggravated. “He’s doing well now,” Reid explained. “He’s out running around. With high ankle sprains, he’s had this before. They get tweaked, literally, and then they recover fairly quick from there. That’s what this was. It just happened early in the game. So, I kind of held back on him. He was very mad. He wanted to play. That’s all part of it.” Many have suggested limiting Kelce’s practice reps, or even sitting him against the lowly Cardinals, with a Thanksgiving road contest against the Buffalo Bills four days later looming. Reid showed no desire to fight with Kelce to limit his work, even as he plays through obvious pain. “That doesn’t work,” Reid declared. “He thinks he’s still 20.” In this week’s episode of the New Heights podcast, hosted with his brother Jason, Kelce left no doubt about his intentions for Sunday. “I’m ready to rock and roll this week,” he said. “It’s one of those things where once you turn it in at the beginning of the year, you’ve just got to deal with the high-ankle sprain and the process it takes to heal. When you’re battling through week to week trying to get it to 100%, it’s going to be a lot slower than just taking time off. But I love playing this game, and if I’m out there on a good ankle or a bad ankle, it doesn’t f–king matter to me. I’m out there because I love this game. I signed up for this thing to be out there putting my heart on the line and my body on the line for my teammates.”

full_text: (Photo by Amy Kontras/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs have a lot of history with their home venue since 1972: Arrowhead Stadium. It has seen heartbreak and triumph over the years, and many loyal fans in Chiefs Kingdom have sat in the crowd over 100 times. However, only three Chiefs players have ever played in 100 regular-season games at Arrowhead — and tight end Travis Kelce is slated to be the fourth this Sunday. Chat live throughout the game Browse with fewer ads Easily jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Download the SB Nation app on your mobile device! For Apple devices, click here . For Android devices, click here . The latest Kansas City Chiefs news Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce’s top moments at Arrowhead Stadium | ESPN “You come through the facility, and you just see Arrowhead [Stadium] pop up out of nowhere,” Kelce said recently. “That’s the best feeling for me.” Few players in the Chiefs’ 67-year history have entered Arrowhead to put on the team’s red jersey, helmet and cleats as many times as Kelce. On Sunday, against the Arizona Cardinals (1 p.m. ET, CBS), Kelce will become only the fourth player in franchise history — joining Hall of Fame right guard Will Shields, kicker Nick Lowery and punter Dustin Colquitt — to play 100 regular-season games at Arrowhead, a venue that opened in 1972. Kelce considers Arrowhead a revered place, even before the venue was the site where his relationship with Taylor Swift, his wife, became public. Kansas City Chiefs share updated renderings of new stadium | KMBC 9 In another rendering, the interior of the stadium is shown, with, of course, a sea of red, and a domed roof. One rendering shows what the stadium could look like if Kansas City is selected to host the NCAA Final Four. In that rendering, a basketball court is shown in the middle of the stadium with fans covering the floor and the stands. The final design shows a first look at the possible entertainment district, with a paved walking area surrounded by restaurants and a Chiefs shop. Kansas City Chiefs vs. Arizona Cardinals Fantasy Football Matchup Breakdown For Week 11 | The Fantasy Life And oh yeah … start the Chiefs’ running back, whoever it may be. Backup Emmett Johnson did such an excellent job in relief (22-101-0; 6-70-2) that Andy Reid’s now granted the freedom to get Kenneth Walker as much time as he needs to heal up 100% for a deep playoff run. Crazy that Johnson’s logged a single start and still ranks as fantasy’s RB23 in total points — he’ll continue to rank as fantasy’s top backup with standalone value in games with double-digit spreads like this one, even if Walker suits up. Why Chiefs’ Emmett Johnson continues to tune out the noise despite recent success | The Kansas City Star Before his junior season at Nebraska, Johnson said he was hearing “a lot of outside noise about what kind of year I would have and what I was capable of. My brother reminded me to ‘Tune Out the Noise.’” The quote comes courtesy of a clothing brand website started by the brothers — “Tune Out the Noise” — and explains the origin. TONT offers sweats, hoodies, T-shirts and hats emblazoned with an inspirational message about focusing on the task at hand. Chiefs terminate veteran LB, two-time Super Bowl champion in Week 11 | Chiefs Wire The Kansas City Chiefs terminated the practice squad contract of veteran linebacker Cole Christiansen on November 18. Christiansen started his career as an undrafted free agent with the Los Angeles Chargers in 2020 and signed with Kansas City in 2022. A member of the Chiefs’ Super Bowl LVII and LVIII rosters, Christiansen exclusively saw action as a special-teamer for Kansas City and Los Angeles, logging a total of 399 NFL snaps without a single defensive down played. Around the NF L Diego Pavia, Heisman finalist and former Vanderbilt star, picked No. 1 in UFL draft | The Athletic The Columbus Aviators picked the 24-year-old Pavia after his brief offseason stint in the NFL. Pavia went undrafted in April but later signed a three-year deal with the Baltimore Ravens. The Ravens, who have played four quarterbacks this season, waived Pavia in July to make room for center Ethan Pocic. At Vanderbilt, Pavia led the Commodores to their first 10-win season in 2025 and became the school’s first Heisman Trophy finalist. He finished second in voting to Indiana’s Fernando Mendoza, the eventual No. 1 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. Cowboys’ Mike Pettine to take over defensive play-calling duties from DC Christian Parker | NFL.com Pettine has been a coordinator with the New York Jets, Buffalo Bills and Green Bay Packers. He also served as head coach of the Cleveland Browns from 2014 to 2015. The Cowboys will keep the 34-year-old Parker in the defensive coordinator role, but hope putting play-calling in the hands of the more experienced Pettine will help turn around a defense that has been torched in 2026. Parker is “a critical piece of what we’re trying to do as we search for answers and solutions,” Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said Wednesday, confirming the decision. “I think he has an incredibly bright future not just this year but beyond with us. Cam Skattebo says he is retiring his backflip celebration after what happened to Aidan Hutchinson | Yahoo! Sports “It’s hard to see,” Skattebo told a couple of reporters after Monday’s practice. “I’m saying yeah (no more). Mentally, I’m like, ‘I’m not doing that.’ That ain’t going to happen to me.” Skattebo has become known for his backflip celebration. Even after dislocating his ankle and fracturing his tibia last year, he was seen still sporting his backflip celebration at a Fanatics Fest event over the summer that sent social media into a frenzy. While head coach John Harbaugh and general manager Joe Schoen spoke with him after that event, Skattebo said this decision to retire his backflip is his alone. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Andy Reid and Chiefs will be cautious with Kenneth Walker this week It would feel shortsighted for the Chiefs to put Walker on the field against the (3-7) Arizona Cardinals in a game where Kansas City is favored by 15.5 points, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . Four days after that matchup, the Chiefs will be on the road to play their AFC rivals, the (8-1) Buffalo Bills, in a pivotal Thanksgiving night game. Reid acknowledged that the quick turnaround could factor into Walker’s availability this weekend. “That goes into the equation,” Reid said about the coming short week. “I’m not saying that’s the answer, but that goes into [it]. You look at the distance between games, you look at what the symptoms are and where he’s at.” “If he’s not going to further injure it, then he’ll go play,” Reid stated. “If he can, if it looks like he’s on the edge there, then he doesn’t play. title: Chiefs-Cardinals Week 11 Wednesday injury report: 3 Chiefs starters miss practice
summary: Each practice day this season, the Kansas City Chiefs release an official injury report ahead of the next game. In Week 11, the Chiefs play the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday afternoon. Here is the Chiefs’ first official injury report of the week, courtesy of the team’s official website: Chiefs Cardinals Many Arizona players rested on Wednesday, […]
full_text: (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Each practice day this season, the Kansas City Chiefs release an official injury report ahead of the next game. In Week 11, the Chiefs play the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday afternoon. Here is the Chiefs’ first official injury report of the week, courtesy of the team’s official website : Chiefs Starting right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) did not participate in practice and hasn’t since leaving the Week 9 game against the New York Jets in the third quarter with an ankle injury. During his Wednesday press conference, head coach Andy Reid said Moore “is making progress, but still sore.” Right guard Trey Smith (concussion) did not participate in practice after entering concussion protocol during the first quarter of last week’s game against the Atlanta Falcons . Running back Kenneth Walker (groin) did not participate in practice again after missing Sunday’s game and last Friday’s practice. Head coach Andy Reid will be cautious with Walker’s availability this week . Rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods (neck) was a full participant in practice for the first time since exiting the Week 8 game against the Denver Broncos with a neck injury. Second-year defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) was a limited participant in practice again. He was activated from the Reserve/Physically-Unable-to-Perform list on Wednesday. Tight end Jared Wiley is not listed after reportedly fracturing his ankle in the win in Atlanta. Wiley was placed on the Reserve/Injured list to make room for Norman-Lott on the active roster. Wiley’s season is likely over. Linebacker Nick Bolton (shin) was surprisingly a limited participant in practice. Cardinals Many Arizona players rested on Wednesday, a sign of where the (3-7) Cardinals are after trading away Week 1 starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett weeks ago.

title: Numbers Never Lie: 3 Chiefs stats to know at midseason
summary: Numbers never lie, right? There are so many statistics to parse during the NFL season that some can be misleading. After each game, it’s a good exercise to review NFL “Next Gen Stats” and “Premium Stats” from Pro Football Focus and find the numbers that paint a picture not only of the game, but of […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Numbers never lie, right? There are so many statistics to parse during the NFL season that some can be misleading. After each game, it’s a good exercise to review NFL “Next Gen Stats” and “Premium Stats” from Pro Football Focus and find the numbers that paint a picture not only of the game, but of what to expect from the Kansas City Chiefs moving forward. Here are X statistics through nine games and what they mean moving forward: 1. Chiefs have an average point differential of 9 points The Chiefs have the fifth-best point differential in the NFL. Jacksonville Jaguars (+128) Buffalo Bills (+88) San Francisco 49ers (+85) Cincinnati Bengals (+85) Chiefs (+81) That brings their average point differential to 9 points, the highest it has been in a season since 2018, the first season quarterback Patrick Mahomes started for the Chiefs. It’s quite a change from the past few seasons, when Kansas City found itself in one-score games constantly, averaging only 2 points of difference in 2025 and 3.5 in 2024 — despite going 15-2 that season. The Chiefs are finishing games with authority more often, a testament to a running game that wasn’t as effective before the arrival of running back Kenneth Walker (and rookie Emmett Johnson). Regardless of opponent, Kansas City made blowouts like the last two weeks rare in recent years. It’s also as simple as scoring more points: Kansas City has scored 30 or more points in five games this year. That is more than 2025 (3), 2024 (2), or 2023 (3) already. 2. Chiefs turn the ball over at the second-lowest rate in the NFL Only the Houston Texans (5%) turn the ball over on a smaller percentage of their drives than Kansas City does, although the Chiefs are tied with the Denver Broncos (6.1%) for second. The team has been locked in on ball security this season. The Chiefs have seven giveaways; four of them came in comfortable victories against the Los Angeles Chargers and New York Jets . Kansas City didn’t turn it over in either of the divisional road games it has played this year. Mahomes has the fifth-lowest interception rate in the NFL (1.3%). According to P ro Football Focus , he is tied for the seventh-fewest turnover-worthy plays among quarterbacks with at least 200 dropbacks this year. Running the ball certainly helps keep the ball out of harm’s way, but the Chiefs’ signal caller seems to have sharpened things further since his red-zone interception against the Chargers in Week 6. This will only become more important as the team plays in pivotal games against the Bills, Bengals and others soon. 3. The Chiefs’ defense has allowed only 7 passing touchdowns this year Only the Minnesota Vikings (6) have allowed fewer passing touchdowns this season than the Chiefs; Kansas City has allowed two fewer than the Seattle Seahawks and three fewer than the Jacksonville Jaguars . Only three of the seven scores were from further than one yard out. This statistic reflects defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo’s bend-don’t-break style, which has ultimately led to the third-fewest points per game (17.3) and eighth-fewest total yards per game (315) this year. Obviously, the quarterbacks are about to get a lot more challenging, but it’s notable that the Vikings have 20 more sacks than the Chiefs (and the Seahawks have 10 more). Kansas City’s coverage is exceptional despite its lack of pass-rush productivity compared to other top defenses in the league.
author: Ron Kopp Jr.

title: ‘Which?’ Wednesday: Who is getting the No. 1 seed in the AFC?
summary: Past the halfway point of the 2026 NFL regular season, the Kansas City Chiefs are one of five AFC teams with two or fewer losses: The ultimate question is: who will earn the conference’s No. 1 seed at the end of the schedule, earn a postseason bye and have homefield advantage over the rest of […]
full_text: (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images Past the halfway point of the 2026 NFL regular season, the Kansas City Chiefs are one of five AFC teams with two or fewer losses: Buffalo Bills (8-1) Jacksonville Jaguars (7-2) Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) Denver Broncos (7-2) Chiefs (7-2) The ultimate question is: who will earn the conference’s No. 1 seed at the end of the schedule, earn a postseason bye and have homefield advantage over the rest of the AFC? Chiefs Kingdom knows a matchup with the Bills awaits on Thanksgiving night, which is a pivotal matchup in this discussion. Buffalo still has to play the Broncos and the (6-4) Green Bay Packers on the road, and host the (7-2) Chicago Bears . Jacksonville has already lost to Denver and the Houston Texans ; the Bears and (6-3) Pittsburgh Steelers still await. The Bengals have won five games in a row and should be favored to win the next three games before welcoming the Chiefs for a Week 14 battle. Kansas City and the Cleveland Browns (twice) are the only two opponents with winning records left on Cincinnati’s schedule. Denver — also riding a five-game win streak — is coming out of the bye in Week 11 with games against the Las Vegas Raiders and Steelers. Pittsburgh and the Bills are the only two opponents with winning records left on the Broncos’ schedule. Who do you think earns the AFC’s No. 1 seed by the time it’s all said and done? Let us know in the comments.

title: Andy Reid and Chiefs will be cautious with Kenneth Walker this week
summary: To open his Wednesday press conference, Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid addressed the groin injury starting running back Kenneth Walker suffered Thursday last week, which forced him to miss the game against the Atlanta Falcons. Reid said Walker “won’t work” during Wednesday’s practice before being asked whether the injury was any more serious than he […]
full_text: (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images To open his Wednesday press conference, Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid addressed the groin injury starting running back Kenneth Walker suffered Thursday last week, which forced him to miss the game against the Atlanta Falcons . Reid said Walker “won’t work” during Wednesday’s practice before being asked whether the injury was any more serious than he imagined initially. “He had a sore groin, so it’s getting better, but with that, you don’t want to do something stupid,” Reid admitted. “[Like] put him out there, and it’s still bugging him a little bit. But he’s feeling a lot better than he was.” “We’ll just see,” Reid finished. “It’s a day-to-day thing, so we’ll just see how it goes.” It would feel shortsighted for the Chiefs to put Walker on the field against the (3-7) Arizona Cardinals in a game where Kansas City is favored by 15.5 points, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . Four days after that matchup, the Chiefs will be on the road to play their AFC rivals, the (8-1) Buffalo Bills , in a pivotal Thanksgiving night game. Reid acknowledged that the quick turnaround could factor into Walker’s availability this weekend. “That goes into the equation,” Reid said about the coming short week. “I’m not saying that’s the answer, but that goes into [it]. You look at the distance between games, you look at what the symptoms are and where he’s at.” “If he’s not going to further injure it, then he’ll go play,” Reid stated. “If he can, if it looks like he’s on the edge there, then he doesn’t play. Keep it simple.” Walker is still less than a week removed from the injury, so he could still improve before the weekend, but all signs point to rookie running back Emmett Johnson leading the run game again. It will be worth watching the status of right guard Trey Smith (concussion) and right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) as the week progresses; neither player will practice on Wednesday, but unlike the backfield, the offensive line doesn’t work as easily with understudies in.
author: Ron Kopp Jr.

title: Patrick Mahomes found his deep ball again in Chiefs’ latest win
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs defeated the Atlanta Falcons 35-13 on Sunday to improve to 7-2 and tie the Denver Broncos for first place in the AFC West. The Chiefs offense suffered multiple big blows from injuries before and during the game, but they made up for it with their passing attack. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes had […]
full_text: (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs defeated the Atlanta Falcons 35-13 on Sunday to improve to 7-2 and tie the Denver Broncos for first place in the AFC West. The Chiefs offense suffered multiple big blows from injuries before and during the game, but they made up for it with their passing attack. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes had a massive day, throwing for 348 yards on 22 completions, a 135.4 quarterback rating, and a whopping five touchdowns, the most he has thrown in a game since his most recent MVP season in 2022. Patrick Mahomes recorded his 50th career game with 3+ passing touchdowns on Sunday, and his seventh career outing with 5+ passing scores. Both are the most in the NFL for any player since 2018, and Mahomes' seven five-touchdown games are the fourth-most in league history. — Matt McMullen (@KCChiefs_Matt) November 16, 2026 Mahomes’ monster day came from an onslaught of deep balls, multiple new weapons in the offense and well-timed protection sets from the offensive line. A week after Chiefs fans held their breath when he exited the field with a visible elbow injury, Mahomes played his best game of the season and instilled a reinvented attack. Connecting with Downs Josh Downs played only eight snaps on passing downs, but he made the most of them, and Mahomes made sure to find him. They call that efficiency pic.twitter.com/JWz2Fskepv — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) November 16, 2026 On four catches in five targets, he put up 53 yards and a touchdown, showing the route-tree diversity the Chiefs coveted when they acquired him. With a play-action look and an expanded pocket for Mahomes, Caliendo pulls, the middle of the field opens up for Downs, and Mahomes finds him for a 20+ yard gain. This look is as easy a layup as there is for Mahomes, and it was a great way to get Downs involved in a play that helped the offense move the chains. Later in the first half, Mahomes would find Downs for the pair’s first touchdown connection. The Chiefs sought a man-beating wideout before the deadline, and that is what they got in Downs. Out of a tight bunch, the Chiefs go with a post-wheel concept, with Downs releasing all the way from the inside. The deep safety follows Xavier Worthy on the post; meanwhile, Downs already has a space advantage on the corner due to his delayed release behind Worthy and Cyrus Allen. The corner squares up Downs, who slow plays it initially, but once he recognizes the safety go to the post, he plants and gets upfield in a hurry. Mahomes maneuvers the pocket and delivers a perfect back shoulder throw. Post wheel action with Worthy pulling the safety. Downs with the double move to win the outside. 15 with a dart. pic.twitter.com/XMkfs2JKK8 — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) November 15, 2026 The pocket isn’t perfect, but with the front line walled off and the edge rushers running past him, he has time to step up and fire a bullet. Downs’ role will only grow in the coming weeks. Shots for Armstrong and Allen Downs wasn’t the only Chiefs wideout to find the endzone on Sunday. Mahomes connected with two of his newer wide receivers on big shots to the end zone, the first to Cyrus Allen. This play is a simple concept being run to a high level, and Allen runs a fantastic route to find the endzone. Only three Chiefs run routes on the play, but the stop-and-start move from Allen, Mahomes holds the safety to the middle with his eyes before firing it deep. With seven in protection, Mahomes has plenty of time to drop back and fires a dart to Allen, who easily took it in for six. Not every concept needs to be a complex equation; sometimes the best course is to let good players win snaps. Later in the game, Mahomes found Armstrong deep on a third down. On third down and one, the Chiefs run a roll-out look with receivers flooding one side of the field. Mahomes has time to throw shorter routes and convert the needed yard, but Armstrong has his man beat deep, and Mahomes knows it. With a little pump fake of his own, Mahomes holds the defensive end in place and buys time to roll and throw the ball deep. With a big rip, Mahomes fires the pass, and Armstrong locates it in the air and comes back to it. Mahomes lets it fly, and Armstrong is there to haul it in, likely securing himself more snaps and more targets moving forward. Finding Rice Rashee Rice didn’t find the end zone, but he led the Chiefs with 82 receiving yards on five receptions. Early in the game, Mahomes and Rice connected on their usual underneath looks, with Mahomes doing a great job to extend the pocket. These underneath throws have been the bread and butter for the Mahomes and Rice connection, but later in the game, Mahomes would finally give Rice a chance to show off his ball-tracking ability. Rice and Allen line up out of a stacked look, and on the snap both run vertical routes, with Allen going up the middle and Rice staying outside. The deep safeties go after Allen, but with leverage inside, Rice continues upfield vertically. In the pocket, Mahomes has to deal with pressure and can’t even fully step into the pass, and it doesn’t matter. With a flick of the wrist, Mahomes throws a bomb, and Rice does a phenomenal job tracking the ball and hauling it in for a big catch. Most of Mahomes and Rice’s big plays have come underneath and with YAC attached, so it will be interesting to see if the deep ball connections continue. The bottom line Mahomes must have heard the ADOT (Average Depth of Target) crowd this week, and he made it his mission to attack the Falcons vertically. This performance also came as he missed his starting right tackle and starting running back; right guard Trey Smith left the game with a concussion, and center Creed Humphrey missed snaps after being gouged in the eye. Mahomes is as good as ever, and while it is still to be seen if the deep ball can become a consistent threat in the Chiefs’ offense, the building blocks are now in place, and the chemistry between Mahomes and his receivers is coming into its own.
author: Caleb James

title: The Good and the Bad from the Chiefs’ win over the Falcons
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs won their seventh game of the season, 35-13, over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 10. Let’s look at two things that went well and something that didn’t from the game: The Good Chris Jones against the run It’s been an up-and-down year for Chris Jones, particularly as a pass rusher. But […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs won their seventh game of the season, 35-13, over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 10. Let’s look at two things that went well and something that didn’t from the game: The Good Chris Jones against the run It’s been an up-and-down year for Chris Jones, particularly as a pass rusher. But one thing about Jones is undeniable: he’s still a beast against the run. Jones still has enough juice to split an open gap, and he does it here, immediately forcing the running back to slow down and let pursue defenders come free to tackle Robinson. The longer Jones has played, the better he is at using his length to keep guys off his chest in the run game. He destroys Pro Bowl guard Chris Lindstrom by getting inside his chest with his length and not letting Lindstrom get any movement. Jones has shown more juice as a pass rusher the past couple of weeks, which is big. I still need to see Jones dominate against a more mobile quarterback before I believe he’s fully back, but the run defense and occasional moments of pass rush brilliance make Jones a critical part of the defense. The Good Everything about Emmett Johnson Emmett Johnson is an awesome rotational running back. In a game where the Chiefs didn’t have Kenneth Walker, it was up to Johnson to be the lead back. He responded with 22 carries for 101 yards and six catches for 70 yards and two receiving touchdowns. Johnson isn’t the most explosive in the run game because he lacks the high-end speed to get past the defense before they can tackle him. Johnson makes up that lack of explosiveness in the run game by being an explosive pass catcher. Johnson is too good at breaking tackles to stick linebackers on him in man coverage, and he is great in the screen game where he can get his legs moving in free space. Johnson is a really strong player for someone who is only 202 lbs. If you try to arm tackle him, he will run through the first tackle. He can even run through defensive linemen, as he does on this play. Johnson gives the Chiefs the ability to run more power runs, as they do here. It’s not that Walker can’t run these runs, but he’s so good on outside zone runs, and those runs give Walker more chances to get into open space and create big runs. Johnson isn’t going to do that as much, but he can run power runs and get 4-6 yards. Johnson is so good at hitting the brakes and cutting it back that he can access any gap created in the power scheme. Johnson might not be explosive in the 20+ yard range, but in the 0-10 yard range, he’s dynamite. It takes real juice to hit this jump cut inside and then bounce off a tackle to get 10+ yards. At Nebraska, Johnson did this fly-by move all the time. Johnson hits the brakes so well that guys consistently fall off of him or trip over themselves. He has an uncanny ability to stay on his feet on first contact. Johnson emerging as a real piece of the offense gives the Chiefs offense a very high floor. Walker has a chance to take any run to the house, and Johnson gives them another punch with his high-efficiency style. With Josh Downs in the picture as well, the Chiefs offense feels like it has enough to score with anyone. The Bad Chiefs giving up interior pressure The only thing I didn’t really like in this game was the Chiefs’ pass protection. They had some rough moments, but some of that was due to injuries. Trey Smith went out early, leaving two backup linemen on the right side. Mike Caliendo is bad in pass protection and not strong enough to keep Gervon Dexter from getting upfield. Joshua Ezedau is not great in space and gives up the corner here. Everyone kinda lost on this play. Suamataia gets pushed back, Caliendo and Ezedau lose the corner and Benson gives up space. Rough rep. Johnson played great in this game, but he did whiff on this pass-protection rep and let the linebacker get a free run at Mahomes. When Trey Smith gets back, the Chiefs’ pass protection will be better. We’ve seen three games with Caliendo playing for Smith or Suamataia, and all three haven’t gone well. The interior offensive line has to be healthy for the Chiefs to go on a run. They already have to compensate for their tackles in pass protection. They need their interior to be firm, and Caliendo can’t do that. The health of Suamataia and Smith is uber important down the stretch.
author: Nate Christensen

title: Week 11 AP NFL Power Rankings: A new team vaults to the top
summary: The contenders are beginning to separate themselves from the pretenders. It was an odd but interesting week of NFL action. Half of the games were decided by two scores or more. Several of these lopsided contests were divisional games, signaling the disparity between team quality within divisions. With over half the season in the books, […]
full_text: (Photo by Brian Rothmuller/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The contenders are beginning to separate themselves from the pretenders. It was an odd but interesting week of NFL action. Half of the games were decided by two scores or more. Several of these lopsided contests were divisional games, signaling the disparity between team quality within divisions. With over half the season in the books, it seems like two divisions are already effectively decided. In the AFC, the Bills and Jaguars have firm control over the East and South, respectively. In the West, it’s between the Chiefs and Broncos, while the Bengals appear to be the cream of the crop of the North. When looking at the standings, depending on who you ask, it looks like anywhere from nine to twelve teams have a realistic shot at hoisting the Lombardi in February. The rest of the league could win or lose on any given week, which is exactly what the league desires. Let’s take a look at how the Arrowhead Pride staff sees the league, one week away from Turkey Day. Biggest riser: Kansas City Chiefs +5 Biggest faller: Pittsburgh Steelers – 4 This week, along with myself, staff voters were: Maurice Elston, Ron Kopp Jr., Rocky Magana, Jared Sapp, and Matt Stagner . 1. San Francisco 49ers (2nd) The average age of the 49ers’ wide receiver corps is approximately 75 years old, but head coach Kyle Shanahan continues to put all his offensive weapons in position to succeed. 2. Buffalo Bills (1st) Why does the AFC East always feel so one-sided? For decades, the Patriots dominated the division with no credible threat. Now, it’s the Bills. I know the Pats won the division last year, but that now seems like a fluke. 3. Jacksonville Jaguars (3rd) The Jaguars have a complete stranglehold on the AFC South. 4. Cincinnati Bengals (6th) This team looks very dangerous. Quarterback Joe Burrow is currently in line for his first MVP award. 5. Chicago Bears (4th) The Bears face the Saints off their bye week, one of only two “gimmes” (if there is such a thing in the NFL) left on their remaining schedule. We’ll find out if they deserve to be ranked this high. 6. Kansas City Chiefs (11th) It was so fun to see that swagger back in Patrick Mahomes. His best performance in several years? 7. Minnesota Vikings (7th) What a feel-good story. Kirk Cousins made his first start at quarterback for the Vikings, at Lambeau, where he last played for them and tore his Achilles three years ago. The Vikings have a Super Bowl-caliber defense and have a legitimate shot at the Super Bowl with competent quarterback play. 8. Denver Broncos (5th) They possess the easiest remaining schedule of any team in the NFL. 9. Detroit Lions (9th) Some of the worst luck in the NFL. To have your defensive leader and captain of the team tear his ACL when celebrating a sack is just brutal. 10. Seattle Seahawks (8th) The defending Super Bowl champions wouldn’t be in the playoffs if the season ended today. 11. Los Angeles Rams (13th) Complete domination without wide receivers Davante Adams and Puka Nacua simply comes down to excellent coaching. 12. Green Bay Packers (10th) Jordan Love was sacked eight times on Sunday. A quarterback has not been sacked that many times at Lambeau since the Ice Bowl. 13. Cleveland Browns (16th) One of the big surprises of the 2026 season. And a great rookie class with a promising future. 14. New York Giants (14th) Quarterback JJ McCarthy has shown enough to warrant another chance in the league—somewhere. 15. Houston Texans (17th) They screwed around at the beginning of the season and are now reaping the reward. 16. Pittsburgh Steelers (12th) The Steelers have been the exact same football team for what feels like eight seasons. I feel they are appropriately ranked right in the middle of the NFL. Mid. 17. New England Patriots (15th) The season is effectively over in New England. The defending AFC champions are likely missing the postseason. 18. Carolina Panthers (18th) Currently leading the NFC South, with a losing record. The winner of this division is going to cause a postseason realignment, aren’t they? 19. Las Vegas Raiders (19th) A respectable first start for quarterback Fernando Mendoza. And a really cool gesture for the fans to stay seated for his first career touchdown, in honor of Mendoza’s mother, who is wheelchair-bound due to multiple sclerosis. Respect. 20. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (21st) We’ll see if their passing attack looks any less anemic coming off their bye week. 21. Dallas Cowboys (22nd) The Cowboys donning a red, white, and blue stripe on their helmet might be the most pompous thing in all of sports. Get over yourselves and figure out your defense. 22. Atlanta Falcons (20th) The Falcons have a major quarterback problem. It doesn’t matter if you have a top wide receiver or running back when the quarterback position is underperforming. 23. Washington Commanders (25th) They saved their season on Thursday night. And because they play in the NFC East, they still have a chance. 24. New Orleans Saints (24th) Welcome to the NFL, Jordyn Tyson. 25. Baltimore Ravens (23rd) Pretty embarrassing to lose at home to the 0-8 Chargers. 26. New York Jets (26th) Geno Smith was injured on Sunday. Somehow this Jets’ season got even more depressing. 27. Arizona Cardinals (27th) The Chiefs have to take care of business this Sunday against another team they should beat. 28. Philadelphia Eagles (29th) There haven’t been any updates about quarterback Jalen Hurts in a while. If the Eagles continue to lose football games, it will be fascinating to see what they do at the quarterback position in the offseason. 29. Tennessee Titans (28th) They have to move on from Cam Ward in 2027, right? 30. Indianapolis Colts (30th) Colts fans resorted to the paper bag on Sunday. Given Daniel Jones’s performance—can’t say I blame them. 31. Los Angeles Chargers (32nd) “Who’s got it better than us? Almost everyone! “ 32. Miami Dolphins (31st) Despite the losses, it seems like the Dolphins have a credible head coach for the future. This doesn’t keep them from dropping to last in the rankings, however.

title: Chargers Week 10 PFF Grades: Del’Shawn Phillips lead spirited effort vs. Ravens rushing attack
summary: The Chargers beat the Ravens to move to 1-8 on the season. The 0-17 jokes and hypotheticals can all finally stop. Justin Herbert and the offense took a step forward with zero turnovers and a dominating performance on the ground with 160 yards, spurred by Omarion Hampton’s 105-yard night. Herbert also added 51 yards and […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 16: Del'Shawn Phillips #53 of the Los Angeles Chargers runs with the ball against the Baltimore Ravens during an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on November 16, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chargers beat the Ravens to move to 1-8 on the season. The 0-17 jokes and hypotheticals can all finally stop. Justin Herbert and the offense took a step forward with zero turnovers and a dominating performance on the ground with 160 yards, spurred by Omarion Hampton’s 105-yard night. Herbert also added 51 yards and a rushing score, as well. Speaking of ground games, the Chargers held the Ravens to almost nothing on the ground. All-Pro back Derrick Henry was limited to just 10 yards on 10 carries. The zero yards on the ground for Baltimore during the first half was a historic low for the franchise. You can’t be much more dominant than that. Let’s go ahead and check out the grades from Monday night. Offense Best TE Charlie Kolar – 74.8 OG Logan Taylor – 74.4 QB Justin Herbert – 73.0 WR Tre’ Harris – 72.0 FB Scott Matlock – 70.2 It was poetic for Kolar — the former Baltimore Raven — to catch the first-down pass that helped seal the win over his former team. He was also dyamite in the run game, posting the second-high run block grade with a 74.6. His 76.4 pass block grade was also fourth best on the night. Monday was Taylor’s best performance as a pro, finishing with zero pressures or sacks allowed on 27 dropbacks. His 81.1 pass block grade was tops on the team while his 68.9 in run blocking was fourth best. For the first time all season, Herbert did not throw an interception and it led to his highest game grade of 2026. Harris caught five passes for 86 yards all in the first half. Unfortunately he caught zero passes in the final 30 minutes of game time, but his yardage still gave him a new season and career high. During the broadcast, it was shown that, at one point, the Chargers were averaging 5.1 yards per carry with Matlock on the field and 3.8 when he was not. He’s done an excellent job as the team’s starting fullback and I believe the switch from a zone-heavy run scheme to a gap scheme has benefitted both him and Hampton. Worst OT Travis Burke – 39.5 WR Quentin Johnston – 52.4 OG Cole Strange – 53.4 WR Derius Davis – 53.6 WR Theo Wease Jr. – 54.1 Unfortunately the team’s first win of the year was also one of Burke’s worst performances of the season. He allowed a team-high five pressures and had an abysmal 27.9 pass block grade to go with a penalty. The next worse grade among the offensive line was Strange with an above-average 64.0. Johnston finished with one catch on one target for six yards. His season may be one of the biggest failures for Mike McDaniel in a season packed to the brim with them. The aforementioned Strange allowed four pressures and was also called for a penalty. His 57.3 in run block was below average but still better than Joe Alt’s 53.2. Defense Best LB Del’Shawn Phillips – 90.6 DT Teair Tart – 82.8 CB Donte Jackson – 77.4 EDGE Tuli Tuipulotu – 73.7 EDGE Khalil Mack – 73.0 What a night for Phillips, and also what a season it’s turning into for the first-year NFL starter. Phillips was a menace against the run on Monday night, helping the Chargers hold Derrick Henry to just 10 yards on 10 carries. He also snagged the team’s only interception off Jacoby Brissett when he sprinted under a deflected by Cam Hart. All night long, his high effort was apparent. Tart had his highest-graded game of the season overall to go with his season-high 81.7 pass rush grade. He tied a season-high of three pressures, as well. Jackson rebounded after a rough performance against the Texans to allow just one catch for six yards in three targets his way. Mack and Tuli combined for 15 pressures on Brissett with the latter recording a nine by himself. His previous season high was six in Week Three. Worst S R.J. Mickens – 25.1 CB Deane Leonard – 28.5 S Elijah Molden – 40.9 LB Daiyan Henley – 51.7 DT Jamaree Caldwell – 53.9 Mickens luckily knocked down the Hail Mary attempt by the Ravens to seal the team’s first win of the season, but it was otherwise a bad night for the second-year safety. His overall game grade was his worst of the year by far and his 26.6 coverage grade was very much the same. Mickens was also called for his third penalty of the season. Molden was credited with allowing five receptions on six targets towards him for 65 yards, including 53 after the catch. Henley also was dinged a bunch in coverage. PFF has him credited with a whopping nine receptions allowed on 11 targets in his area.

full_text: BLOOMINGTON, IN - OCTOBER 31: Indiana Hoosiers wide receiver Charlie Becker (80) warms up prior to the start of a college football game between the Minnesota Golden Gophers vs the Indiana Hoosiers on October 31, 2026 at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington, IN. (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Chargers have given away the first overall pick after winning their first game of the season on Monday night. However, as current owners of the second overall pick, they’re still in a position to come out with amazing value on day one. In a new 2027 mock draft by ESPN’s Jordan Reid, the Chargers end up trading out of the second slot with the Jets, which allows them to pick up an additional first-rounder. With the first of their two picks (No. 4), the Bolts still land a top receiver in Indiana’s Charlie Becker. Here’s what Reid had to say about the pairing: “The Chargers have been extremely disappointing this season, and their one-win start has exposed the need for more talent everywhere. That and the fact they already have a QB in Justin Herbert are why I had them trade out of No. 2 and add another pick. And we’ll use this first pick to get Herbert some help .” “ Becker is an excellent vertical threat who has 10 touchdowns this season (sixth in the FBS) and can also execute the short to intermediate levels of the route tree. He is tall (6-foot-4) and sure-handed (zero drops on 85 targets this season) with excellent body control and elite hand-eye coordination, allowing him to win in the air on long and contested catch opportunities. Becker would immediately become Herbert’s WR1. ” As for the 13th overall pick, Reid has the Chargers grabbing one of the best and most versatile offensive linemen in the class with Iowa’s Trevor Lauck, who can play both tackle and guard at the next level. “ After acquiring a pass catcher with their initial first-rounder, it’s time for the Chargers to give Justin Herbert some blocking help. Between the erratic health of tackles Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt and the constant issues with the interior line, the Bolts have struggled to keep Herbert upright in the pocket. Lauck is a steady blocker who doesn’t have much flash but simply gets the job done, allowing just five pressures and zero sacks in 10 games this season. Scouts are mixed on where they see Lauck playing in the NFL, but that shouldn’t matter for a Los Angeles team that needs help across the entire line. ” What do you think of this potential draft haul for the Chargers? summary: The article below lists a few NFC teams to root for as the Los Angeles Rams sit this Sunday out for their bye week. full_text: The article below lists a few NFC teams to root for as the Los Angeles Rams sit this Sunday out for their bye week. Among those teams to root for include the New Orleans Saints, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Minnesota Vikings. The Saints, Bucs and Vikings play the Chicago Bears, the Detroit Lions and the San Francisco 49ers respectively. In theory, and in reality, as we enter Week 11 the Bears, Lions and 49ers are a threat to the Rams and their chances to make the playoffs. Of course, it’s still early enough in that season that nothing is certain, yet. If the Rams can gain some ground by others losing on their week off then that is great, but the Rams mostly need to worry about winning. The fan can scoreboard watch, while the Rams need to win, baby, win. Rams Week 11 rooting guide: Which games can help LA during the bye? (ramswire) “The Los Angeles Rams won’t be in action this week, but it won’t be long before they take the field again on Thanksgiving Eve next Wednesday . During their brief bye, it’ll be hard for them to gain much ground on a playoff berth . The Green Bay Packers and Seattle Seahawks , with whom the Rams are tied at 6-4, are both on their bye, as well. The San Francisco 49ers are playing, but they’re going up against the Minnesota Vikings – a team the Rams could be battling for a playoff spot come January. Still, there are a couple of games that can help the Rams’ playoff odds if they go in Los Angeles’ favor. According to The Athletic , the Rams currently have a 47% chance to make the playoffs. Using The Athletic’s playoff predictor, we can get a better idea of which games can help L.A. this weekend.“ Rams rumors: ESPN insider opens door to shocking Puka Nacua free agency gambit (sports.yahoo) “The Rams are currently set to have $75.27 million in cap space during the 2027 offseason. That could be enough to extend Nacua and still fill out the roster. However, it could mean letting another talented player walk in free agency. Graziano also cited Nacua’s injury history as another reason for concern. Puka is on IR with a knee injury and has dealt with nagging injuries throughout his career. It is fair to question if longevity will be a long-term concern for the superstar receiver. “He’s 25 years old and a brilliant player, but his play style makes you wonder about his longevity,” Graziano argued. “All of that is to say: I could at least imagine a scenario in which the Rams let him hit free agency, or franchise him and listen to offers.” Rams Game-by-Game Predictions: Will Los Angeles Survive a Brutal Final Stretch? (si.com) “At the end of the day, 11-6 should be enough to get the Rams into the playoffs. If they beat the Packers out of the bye week, they’ll hold the head-to-head tiebreaker over Green Bay and will have two opportunities to earn it against Seattle. The Rams may have the most difficult schedule in the NFL going forward, but at 6-4 and on a four-game win streak, they are in a good spot to make a playoff push in December.” Rams’ roster math suggests Davante Adams, Kobie Turner may both be back in Week 12 (ramblinfan) “Let’s break it all down to show why fans may be correct in anticipating some healthy players returning to the fray: Center Dylan McMahon to IR – Frees up a roster spot Wide receiver Brennan Presley waived – Frees up a roster spot Nose tackle Jalen Hunt contract terminated – Frees up a practice squad roster spot Signed wide receiver Brennan Presley – Takes up a practice squad roster spot By the numbers, LA’s active roster has freed up two spots. And the team is confident enough at receiver and defensive tackle to shrink its options going forward. With an extended period until LA resumes competition, the time to activate players from injured reserve is now. “ Rams’ Kyren Williams, Blake Corum keep team afloat during rough waters (sports.yahoo) “Among running backs who recorded at least 100 carries and averaged eight attempts per game in 2025, Corum ranked fifth in yards per carry and second in rushing success rate, trailing only Williams. Corum also is top 10 in missed tackles, gains of 15 yards or more, and is one of the NFL’s most efficient running backs . Oh, and he’s only fumbled twice in two years. Think about that. Two running backs sharing the same backfield finished first and second in a category measuring how consistently they keep an offense moving down the field. And somehow, they’re still being overlooked.“ NFL broke 24-year scheduling trend with Rams’ shortened bye week (ramswire) “The Rams-Packers game isn’t just the first game ever on Thanksgiving Eve. It’ll be the first time in NFL history that teams will play on a Wednesday after a bye. In fact, no team has even played a Thursday game after a bye since the 2001 season, according to Stathead . From 1990 to 2001, there were 28 games played on a Thursday after a bye. But since 2002, there hasn’t been a single one. Since 2002, the quickest turnaround was when the Colts played the Vikings on a Saturday in Week 15 of the 2022 season, and when Indianapolis faced the Patriots on Saturday in 2021. Other than that, every team has played a Sunday or Monday game following a bye since 2002.“ NFL QB rankings, Week 11: Kirk Cousins climbs; Josh Allen slips from top three (nfl.com) “ Matthew Stafford has every reason to disintegrate at this point in the season. He’s lost Puka Nacua and Davante Adams , yet he’s still making it work (albeit at a much lower rate of production) with the remaining cast. If anyone is capable of adjusting and following a new game plan, it’s Stafford; just don’t expect another MVP season from him. Next Gen Stats insights (via NFL Pro): Kirk Cousins completed 9-of-12 passes on third down for 110 yards with a touchdown and an interception against the Packers. Cousins’ average time to throw on third down was 2.20 seconds. Cousins threw both of his TD passes over the middle third of the field, matching the Vikings’ season-total TD passes allowed in that area in Weeks 1-9.“ Seattle Seahawks may have an Aaron Donald problem (again) (12thmanrising) “So, what if he’s back-back? Like, what if he’s slowly ramping up to return to his Defensive Player of the Year form? The Rams always knew they didn’t need Aaron Donald in October or even November. Hell, they might not even need him in December. But if Donald keeps trending up, finding his footing, and getting his legs back under him, the Rams might be playing meaningful games in early 2027, and that spells trouble for the defending champions.“ Mike’s Mid-Week Chat: How do the Packers fix what went wrong? (packers.com) “ The shorter bye gives less time to ponder the Vikings game, but also less time for players who need to get healthy to heal up. Getting another break after next Wednesday’s game should prove beneficial for the stretch run. Hi Mike. would it be a terrible thing if we got the 7th seed again while finishing last in the North? We get a last place schedule next year, we still have a chance to advance this year and…….it moves Dallas back a ways in the draft. I couldn’t care less about the Dallas draft pick or what seed the Packers might get. Just do what it takes to get in and let the chips fall. Do the struggles of he rest of the team, particularly the O-Line allow the team to give a bit more freedom to let Trey Smack to work through his issues? Meaning if these loses were coming down to kicking would his job be in danger?“ Comment of the day: Feed post of the day:

title: Who will the Rams designate to return from injured reserve?
summary: The Los Angeles Rams have already used half of their available injured reserve return designations during the 2026 NFL season, making roster flexibility an increasingly important storyline heading into the second half of the year. Through Week 10, Los Angeles has designated four players to return from injured reserve: offensive tackle Keagen Trost, tight end […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - JANUARY 10: Puka Nacua #12 of the Los Angeles Rams celebrates with Davante Adams #17 after scoring a touchdown during the second quarter of an NFL wild card playoff game against the Carolina Panthers at Bank of America Stadium on January 10, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams have already used half of their available injured reserve return designations during the 2026 NFL season, making roster flexibility an increasingly important storyline heading into the second half of the year. Through Week 10, Los Angeles has designated four players to return from injured reserve: offensive tackle Keagen Trost, tight end Terrance Ferguson, defensive end Myles Garrett and running back Ronnie Rivers. That leaves them with just four activations left despite a bunch of injuries across the roster. How will they use those designations? Here’s a look… Activated / Designated to Return Keagan Trost, OL The Rams designated the offensive tackle to return on October 15. He was activated two days later, providing some much-needed offensive line depth. Terrance Ferguson, TE The rookie tight end was designated to return on November 4 after suffering an ankle injury. However, he subsequently dealt with a hamstring injury, complicating his return. Myles Garrett, EDGE The All-Pro defensive end was designated to return on November 4 and activated on November 7. His return provides a significant boost to the Rams’ pass rush. Garrett has appeared in 3 games in 2026: Week 1 against San Francisco, Week 9 at Washington, and Week 10 at Arizona. Ronnie Rivers, RB The running back was also designated on November 4 and activated on November 7, giving the backfield another option behind Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. Currently on IR Davante Adams, WR Adams ruptured his hamstring in Week 6 against the Arizona Cardinals. He had surgery to clean out the tendon area. It is reported that Adams could make his return for the game against the Green Bay Packers. Adams was expected to be sidelined for 6-10 weeks. He has already missed the four game minimum. The bye week provides an extra week of recovery. Week 12 against Green Bay would get Adams to about 5 1/2 weeks of recovery. Puka Nacua, WR Puka Nacua was injured at the end of Week 9 against the Washington Commanders. He injured his MCL, PCL, and is dealing with turf toe. The earliest Nacua can return is Week 15 against the Dallas Cowboys. Kobie Turner, DL Turner suffered a grade 2 groin strain in Week 6. Turner was given a 6-8 week timeline. He has missed the four game minimum already and could be activated for Week 12 against the Packers. My expectation is that Turner will miss the Green Bay game and would be available for the Kansas City Chiefs game in Week 13. Dean Connors, RB Dean Connors broke his hand in Week 8 against the Los Angeles Chargers. Dylan McMahon, OL McMahon entered the game last week against the Cardinals after Coleman Shelton went down with an injury. A few players later McMahon suffered a partial patella tear Jordan Whittington, WR Whittington had been battling a back issue for quite some time and the Rams placed him on IR on November 10th. Justin Dedich, OL Justin Dedich was placed on IR back in late August due to hand injury he suffered in July. Jaylen Watson, CB Jaylen Watson could not work through his shoulder injury and required surgery. He is not expected to return to the team even if LA makes the playoffs. Blake Grupe, K Grupe tore his ACL in Week 6 and will not return this season. Poona Ford, DL Ford tore his triceps in the Week 6 loss. That injury carries a 5-6 month recovery effectively ending Ford’s season. Injured (not on IR) Coleman Shelton, OL Shelton was injured in Week 10 when he went down with a hamstring. He has not been placed on Injured Reserve despite expecting to be sidelined for 4-6 weeks. Joe Cardona, LS Cardona likely won’t be placed on IR despite missing multiple games. Steve Avila, OL Avila suffered a hamstring injury in Week 9. He is expected to miss multiple weeks. IR Activation Predictions The Rams have used 4 of their 8 IR returns. Ferguson hasn’t officially returned yet but the Rams have to make a decision soon within his activation window. Adams, Nacua, and Turner are near locks to be designated to return, leaving one spot remaining. Since Coleman Shelton and Steve Avila are not on IR, it seems likely that Justin Dedich could receive the final designation. However, the Rams may be cautious and leave that final spot open until they get closer to the end of the season. If the Rams make the playoffs, they will get an additional two IR designations.

title: Does Davante Adams have a better Hall of Fame case than Torry Holt?
summary: The Los Angeles Rams are hoping to get back Davante Adams when they return from their bye week to play against his former team, the Green Bay Packers, next Wednesday. Adams will have an opportunity to produce at a high level for the rest of the year, as the Rams wait for the return of […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams are hoping to get back Davante Adams when they return from their bye week to play against his former team, the Green Bay Packers, next Wednesday. Adams will have an opportunity to produce at a high level for the rest of the year, as the Rams wait for the return of Puka Nacua from his own set of injuries. The last time Adams played without Nacua, he had 195 yards and two touchdowns. With a handful of games as Matthew Stafford’s number one receiver, imagine how much more Adams could add to his Hall of Fame resume. Nothing would make him feel more at ease than adding a Super Bowl championship — or even just an appearance — to his resume at this stage of his career. Unfortunately, the Rams know what it’s like to watch an elite receiver go year after year without induction to the Pro Football Hall of Fame. Torry Holt has been denied entry to the Hall of Fame 12 times, including seven times as a finalist. Imagine being that close every year and not getting in. Will Adams face a similar wall? The Case for Holt: 19th all-time in receiving yards (13,382) 27th all-time in catches (920) 7 Pro Bowls 1 first team All-Pro Super Bowl winner Led NFL in yards twice and catches once The Case for Adams: 22nd all-time in yards (13,113) 14th all-time in catches (1,047) 6th all-time in touchdown catches (121) 6 Pro Bowls 3 first team All-Pro Led NFL in touchdowns three times If you had to pick one — and I know many of you don’t want to pick one — but if you HAD to pick one…who has the better case? After all, that’s how the Hall of Fame works. You don’t pick all. You have a limited number of selections every year, which is why Holt has never gotten in. Who has the better case right now?
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Puka Nacua’s last season with the Rams? ESPN thinks maybe
summary: The Los Angeles Rams have had a decision to make with Puka Nacua since the beginning of the 2026 offseason, and the longer they hold off on his next contract, the more likely it becomes that the fourth-year receiver won’t get one from Les Snead and Sean McVay. Nacua is set to become a 2027 […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams have had a decision to make with Puka Nacua since the beginning of the 2026 offseason, and the longer they hold off on his next contract, the more likely it becomes that the fourth-year receiver won’t get one from Les Snead and Sean McVay. Nacua is set to become a 2027 free agent and ESPN’s Dan Graziano speculated on Wednesday that the Rams could be too concerned with his off-field issues and/or his injury to commit to him like other teams have committed to number one receivers. Nacua didn’t get the big contract extension that Jaxon Smith-Njigba got last offseason, even though he was eligible. And the Rams don’t hold a fifth-year option on him for next year because he wasn’t a first-round pick. Nacua also made bad headlines with his off-field behavior in the offseason and could still face league discipline under the personal conduct policy. Plus, he’s banged up again. He missed two games earlier this season with hip and groin injuries, and he’s currently on IR with a knee injury that will cost him at least four more games (counting the one he missed Sunday) and possibly more than that. Nacua played all 17 games in his rookie season but hasn’t managed to do that since. He’s 25 years old and a brilliant player, but his play style makes you wonder about his longevity. All of that is to say: I could at least imagine a scenario in which the Rams let him hit free agency, or franchise him and listen to offers. Graziano didn’t get into the weeds of what a franchise tag would look like and how challenging that would be for the Rams given their slate of free agents in 2027. Graziano: Rams hope to get Puka Nacua (knee, toe) back around Week 14 – Week 15. — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) November 11, 2026 What does a WR tag cost? OvertheCap.com is projecting a $30.9 million franchise tag for wide receivers in 2027. What that Means: The Rams would have to pay Nacua a fully-guaranteed $30.9 million salary in 2027 The Rams would have a deadline to either extend Nacua, pay him the tag, or rescind the tag The non-exclusive tag means Nacua could negotiate with other teams and if he signs with a team and the Rams don’t match the offer, the Rams would get two first-round picks from that team The exclusive tag means Nacua can’t negotiate with other teams The Rams could still trade Nacua to another team on the exclusive tag The Rams could still extend Nacua before the deadline, this would just buy them some time Paying Nacua a $30.9 million salary in 2027 seems exceptionally challenging for L.A.. The Rams only have one starting offensive lineman under contract — AJ Jackson — and only one recent draft pick who might be a contender to start — Keagen Trost — meaning that at best L.A. only has three starting offensive line positions to fill. They will have a hard time replacing anyone in the draft because the Rams don’t have a first-round pick and they’re not keen on starting rookies anyway. The Rams also have to make a decision on WR2, as Davante Adams is a free agent. There are plenty of other free agents, including Kobie Turner, Byron Young, and Ethan Evans. In fact, the Rams also need to pick a kicker and potentially invest more money in special teams next year. An extension for Nacua could carry a 2027 cap hit of roughly $10-$15 million. That makes a tag 2-3 times more expensive next year at a time when the Rams have to sign almost half of their important starters. A tag would be very difficult for the Rams to pull off. Rams placed WR Puka Nacua on injured reserve due to his MCL injury. HC Sean McVay has said he expects Nacua to miss “extended time.” pic.twitter.com/XAR4rutM0Q — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 13, 2026 Will Nacua be a free agent? I highly doubt it. The Rams would only get a third-round comp pick in 2028 if Nacua leaves in free agency. That’s not enough compensation for one of the NFL’s best players who is only going to be 26. It would be a mistake of absurd proportions. The Rams will figure something out with Nacua, most likely. Free agency is highly unlikely. But the longer the Rams make us speculate, the more speculation that will occur.

title: Next Rams game is the biggest one of the season
summary: The Los Angeles Rams face a massive game against the Green Bay Packers in Week 12. The winner of that game may end up making the playoffs while the loser will still have a chance, but it could all be for nought if the winner of Week 12 keeps winning. Both teams have so much […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams face a massive game against the Green Bay Packers in Week 12. The winner of that game may end up making the playoffs while the loser will still have a chance, but it could all be for nought if the winner of Week 12 keeps winning. Both teams have so much at stake, and both will be coming off of their bye weeks. Throw in that this game will be the first ever Thanksgiving Eve Game, and this could be one of the more memorable games of the year. There will be plenty to talk leading up to the game such as if the Packers high scoring offense shows up, or if the Rams defense gets after the offensive line for Green Bay. Will the Rams offense show up? Will Davante Adams play? Will Sean McVay beat Matt LaFleur for the first time? Plenty of storylines. Enjoy Week 11 and L.A.’s bye week. Week 12 is coming, and all that comes with it. What are the Rams’ playoff odds with 7 games remaining? (ramswire) “At the Week 11 bye, here’s a look at the Rams’ playoff odds across various outlets. The Athletic and ESPN give them below a 50% chance to make the postseason, while Next Gen Stats puts the Rams’ odds at 52%. Sportsbooks such as DraftKings and FanDuel still give the Rams a better than 50% chance to make it based on the latest betting lines. FanDuel: -116 (54%) The Athletic : 47% Next Gen Stats : 52% ESPN : 46% DraftKings: -144 (59%)“ Russell Wilson sends warning to rest of NFL about Rams’ playoff threat (sports.yahoo) “During Tuesday’s broadcast of “Set Hut,” with former NFL offensive lineman Kyle Long, Wilson claimed that the Rams are the last team opponents want to see make the playoffs in the NFC. With the club in the middle of a four-game win streak going into the bye, Wilson believes Los Angeles has a chance to make some noise in the second half of the regular season. “If you’re a team across the NFC, or the AFC, you don’t want to see the Rams sneak into the playoffs,” Wilson said… “So, this schedule here. title: Fernando Mendoza struggled to throw downfield
summary: Raider Nation got its first chance to watch the number one pick in the draft. The Las Vegas Raiders rookie quarterback, Fernando Mendoza, got his first action on Sunday with a loss to the Seattle Seahawks, 21-13. Mendoza had a hot start, going 11/13 in the first half for 90 yards and a rushing touchdown. […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Raider Nation got its first chance to watch the number one pick in the draft. The Las Vegas Raiders rookie quarterback, Fernando Mendoza, got his first action on Sunday with a loss to the Seattle Seahawks, 21-13. Mendoza had a hot start, going 11/13 in the first half for 90 yards and a rushing touchdown. It fell apart in the second half, as he went 6/16 for 43 yards. Mike McDonald turned up the heat by blitzing every third down in the second half, leading to four sacks. One area Mendoza needs to improve is throwing downfield. When throwing 10-plus yards last Sunday, he struggled to find completions. He finished the game 1/8 for 22 yards on throws over 10 plus yards. Mendoza is known for his accuracy, but he threw plenty of errant passes throughout the game. He needs to tighten up his mechanics when throwing downfield. He also needs to get on the same page with his new receiving corps. Plenty of miscommunication led to inaccurate throws, especially on third down. Fans should expect Mendoza to fix this issue going forward. To succeed in the NFL, the team needs explosive plays. Hitting throws in the intermediate and deep parts of the field will accomplish that. If this becomes a recurring issue, the Raiders offense will have a long second half.
author: Marcus Johnson

title: Thoughts Fernando Mendoza’s first game
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders finally unleashed Fernando Mendoza, the 2026 No. 1 overall pick, against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. A game that the Raiders would lose 21-13. Without rushing to any judgment, good, bad, or indifferent, lots of good information on Mendoza was gathered. Let’s break it down. The eye test For […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders finally unleashed Fernando Mendoza, the 2026 No. 1 overall pick, against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. A game that the Raiders would lose 21-13. Without rushing to any judgment, good, bad, or indifferent, lots of good information on Mendoza was gathered. Let’s break it down. The eye test For as long as football has been football, the most important test a player has got to pass is the eye test. Mendoza passed the eye test in the first half of the game when he was 11/13 for 98 yards and scored his first touchdown by running a quarterback sneak 10 yards to pay dirt. A simplistic overview, but let’s get more in-depth. Raiders really drew up the National Championship winning play for Fernando Mendoza's first career NFL TD 🤌 pic.twitter.com/NQlAkxCXdZ — NFL Memes (@NFLMemes) November 15, 2026 Against the champs, Mendoza came out swinging; from the outset, it was clear the moment was not too big for him. He was never rattled and did not make any egregious rookie mistakes. The hits weren’t too much for him to handle and the speed of the game did not overwhelm him. Throughout the game, he played with poise and confidence. Mendoza stayed within himself; once Brock Bowers went down, he remained playing as though he were 1/11 of the offense. Ball security Throughout his collegiate career, particularly at Indiana University, Mendoza always took care of the football. Through the process of getting sacked, tucking and running and taking hits from free rushers, he always secured the football. By his own account, when running the scout team in practice, Mendoza refused to practice putting the ball in harm’s way. Meaning he didn’t even want to practice placing the ball in positions where it could be intercepted. Fast forward to Sunday’s game and it showed. The only pass he threw that was moderately questionably placed was when his receiver was assisted in falling down out of his break. Accuracy, ball placement and decision-making were all traits Mendoza was exceptional at in college and so far it appears to have translated to the NFL. What stood out Mendoza’s ability to tuck it and run provided a wrinkle the Seattle Seahawks had trouble defending. Using his legs to get what was available on the ground was a missing element from Klint Kubiak’s offense. On more than one occasion, it kept the chains moving and both the crowd and offense engaged. Being able to execute bootlegs and move the launching point allowed Mendoza to have early success. Fernando Mendoza ➡️ Cody White for the first down! SEAvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/KmbkHKSAKr — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 Moving around in the pocket and evading the rush was clearly upgraded by inserting Mendoza into the lineup. Not just sliding in the pocket, but being able to muscle out of a collapsed pocket and still be able to keep his eyes downfield. He made one play, spinning out of trouble, rolling out and then hitting Cody White on a nice sideline pass to keep the chains moving Mendoza’s best trait in the passing game was going through his progressions and getting to his checkdowns quickly. We have seen veteran and even playoff quarterbacks be one-to-two read quarterbacks, then play hero ball. Mendoza wasn’t one of them. All week long, the message was that he was 1/11th of the offense and that’s what they stuck to. He hit his checkdowns after establishing that his other reads were covered in an efficient manner. Never committing the cardinal sin of staring down receivers or leading defenders to the ball. Another of the many quality things done was no hospital balls thrown against a head-hunting defense. Things to improve on The Seahawks defense finished the day with six sacks and got to the quarterback in completely inexcusable ways. Seahawks cornerback Devon Witherspoon, known for his slot/nickel blitzes, tallied three sacks on the day. It wasn’t just that he got the sacks; no offensive member laid a finger on him; he came free and clear. Fernando Mendoza told @MikeSilver that this Devon Witherspoon sack was his "In a Blender" moment from his first NFL start. Seattle shows overload blitz to the weak side, so Mendoza checks the protection to slide that way. But the look was Mike Macdonald preying on his… https://t.co/EAidYAbHgF pic.twitter.com/pnauK0PyDC — Sam Warren (@samwarren83) November 16, 2026 Mendoza, moving forward, is going to need to be more cognizant of his own pass protection. The entire line was struggling mightily, and the overloads/unaccounted for rushers are most certainly something he’s going to see repeatedly. Which is something he acknowledged he needed to get better at speaking to the media after the game. Without Bowers, the offense was brought to a halt. Having four of six second-half drives end in negative yards and 27 yards of total offense in the second half isn’t going to cut it. Now, to be fair, blame isn’t being placed on Mendoza. While he most certainly has his part to play, the atrocious blocking, running and route running did him no favors either. Final thoughts An impressive early showing gave way to positive signs for the future. No one should have expected a rookie making his first start to topple the defending champions by himself. The least impressive yet most effective thing was Mendoza not digging a deeper and deeper hole trying to do too much. There were plenty of wow plays; not many went for huge gains or points. But they were impactful and kept the chains moving in situations where the offense needed a spark. Getting this experience against one of the best defenses the NFL has to offer should be priceless to a film junkie such as Mendoza. Following it up with a couple more tough defenses in Denver and Cleveland will make him better, as long as it doesn’t break him. Raider Nation, be patient. Mendoza is the future and with a properly built team around him, the future is bright.
