title: Brock Bowers not at open of practice Wednesday
summary: It appears Las Vegas Raiders superstar tight end Brock Bowers will continue to be “day-to-day” moving forward as the team prepares to play at the Denver Broncos on Sunday. Kickoff is set at 1:25 p.m. PT. According to The Athletic, Bowers was not seen during the practice window that was open to the media Wednesday […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images It appears Las Vegas Raiders superstar tight end Brock Bowers will continue to be “day-to-day” moving forward as the team prepares to play at the Denver Broncos on Sunday. Kickoff is set at 1:25 p.m. PT. According to The Athletic, Bowers was not seen during the practice window that was open to the media Wednesday morning. It’s not a major surprise. Bowers injured his ankle Sunday in a home loss to the Seattle Seahawks. He left the game twice and for good in the second quarter. Monday, Las Vegas coach Klint Kubiak labeled Bowers’ injury status as “day-to-day.” Thus, he still could have a chance to play in Denver if he gets on the practice field by Friday. In addition to his ankle, Bowers is also listed with a quad issue. After practice Wednesday, Kubiak said Bowers could play Sunday even if he doesn’t practice this week. Also, defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway wasn’t at practice Wednesday, either. He was hurt late n third quarter, but did return. He has a stinger. Kicker Matt Gay was limited with a hip issue.

full_text: (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raider recently signed quarterback Brett Rypien to the practice squad recently. Let’s take a closer look at Rypien: Size: 6-2, 212 pounds. NFL experience: The Raiders are the 12 program (He was with the Minnesota Vikings twice) he has been part of since entering the NFL in 2019. He was with Denver from 2019-22. He last threw a pass in a regular-season game in 2023 while with the Los Angeles Rams. He was released from Tampa Bay’s practice squad last month. Draft status: Rypien went undrafted in 2019. College: He went to Boise State. Raiders ties: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak was Denver’s passing game coordinator and quarterbacks coach in 2022 when Rypien played four games. Famous family: His uncle is Mark Rypien a Super Bowl MVP quarterback. How he will fit in with Raiders: Rypien is the third quarterback in the Raiders’ program behind starter Fernando Mendoza and backup Aidan O’Connell. Las Vegas needed to add to the quarterback room because they traded Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings last week. Rypien’s history with Kubiak made this an easy choice.

title: Jack Bech not making impact after return
summary: Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2025 draft class fared in a home 21-13 loss to the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at the Denver Broncos. Ashton Jeanty: The No. 6 overall draft pick played 71 percent of the snaps, his most since Week 7. Still, […]
full_text: . (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2025 draft class fared in a home 21-13 loss to the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at the Denver Broncos. Ashton Jeanty: The No. 6 overall draft pick played 71 percent of the snaps, his most since Week 7. Still, his production was clacking. He has had nine carries for 18 yards. He has averaged 2.9 or less yards per carry for the sixth time this season. He did have four catches on four targets for 46 yards. Jack Bech: The second-round pick played 56 percent of the snaps after playing 34 percent in Week 9. Bech has not produced since returning in Week 8 from a broken forearm. He has three catches for 19 yards on nine targets in those three games. He’s just not making an impact. Darien Porter: The third-round pick was replaced by Zeke Masses as the starter, but he did play 53 percent of the snaps. So, he’s still in the mix. Caleb Rogers: The benched starter played just three special teams snaps. Charles Grant: The offensive lineman, taken in the third round, played three special teams snaps. Dont’e Thornton: The wide receiver, taken in the fourth round, has been on the 53-man roster for three games and he was inactive for all three games. Tonka Hemingway: The fourth-round pick played 61 percent of the snaps, the most of any Raiders’ defensive tackle. JJ Pegues: The defensive tackle, taken in the sixth round, was active for the fifth time this season. He played 12 defensive snaps, which is his range. Cody Lindenberg: The seventh-round pick played 22 snaps on special teams, which is his norm. He has played just three defensive snaps this season.

As the preparations for the Bills game continue, the Dolphins are also supporting the release of Grand Theft Auto VI, perhaps the most anticipated video game ever. summary: Following this past Sunday’s loss to the Indianapolis Colts by our Miami Dolphins, I asked the following question: What are your overall takeaways from this afternoon’s ninth game of the season (Week 10) between the Miami Dolphins and the Indianapolis Colts? What are the positive and negative takeaways from this afternoon’s game, as they apply […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 15: Grover Stewart #90 of the Indianapolis Colts knocks down a pass from Kyle McCord #14 of the Miami Dolphins during the fourth quarter at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images Following this past Sunday’s loss to the Indianapolis Colts by our Miami Dolphins, I asked the following question: What are your overall takeaways from this afternoon’s ninth game of the season (Week 10) between the Miami Dolphins and the Indianapolis Colts? What are the positive and negative takeaways from this afternoon’s game, as they apply to the team overall and to individual units and/or players? Below are some of your thoughts on Sunday’s game- DolfaninME got the news they were hoping not to get. How is Biggers? Dolfanjoe seems pleased with what they saw from McCord’s first outing. Playing the Colts after a fire sale. Yes we very well could have won that game. McCord played dam well for a first timer ! Too many knocked down at the line of scrimmage, a few risky throws. But over all a good showing. No Seiler in the middle showed on some run plays, but we were going against Taylor and his running mate. Still making them a formidable running team. Bills come into town next week with the odds against us. Just need to see them give it hell like this game. We are going to get better and more experienced over the next two years. Talent will be added, there will come a time when suddenly we are that better team and should win ! Phoenix6 cares about kickers even if you don’t! Kickers are important! Cutie0716 is happy with how the team is being built from the ground up. I looked at the roster and counted 15 rookies on the 53. Not including the ones on the Injured list and the PS. These rookies are playing the way I had wished our rookies of yesterday would have played. Let them play. Let them make mistakes. These guys are really developing a nucleus. I HONESTLY don’t care about wins and losses. Every game I read about, I read how tough the D is getting. How they are fighting until the end. These guys are hungry. This is going to be a big deal with our 2027 draft picks. It’s one thing to be on a losing team, but when MORE THAN HALF of the whole team are rookies, it makes a statement. They are playing hard and meaningfully. I give the Coach and GM credit for picking their own guys. Proctor will be, if he’s not already there, a beast by next year. A rookie that our team depended on. It’s wonderful. No one thought that Proctor would be our pick. I knew months ago that we wouldn’t win much. Some were predicting five wins. If we win 2-3, BUT ESTABLISHING building blocks, we have done a great job. The building of a cohesive team is all that we need right now. I know that most of you, if not all, strongly disagree with my opinion, and that’s fine. You have your own opinion. No problem. I gave you mine. I love to see the replays on NFLN because I see HOW HARD these guys play. I CHEER THEM FOR THAT. And so should you. Respectfully StanleyDoyle1 is happy with the rookies’ contributions so far. My takeway: I cannot remember a season when more rookies had a meaningful impact on the team. This season, Rodriguez, Proctor, Johnson, Douglas, Taafe have all shown real talent and made a meaningful difference in games. Kacmarek, Bell and Coleman have shown promise. That’s eight rookies. 2020 had 7 contributors. 2012 had 6. 2007 had 5. 1997 had 6. To find something comparable to this season, you have to go back to 1982 when they had 12 rounds to find as many contributors from the draft. This bodes well for next year’s draft. Luvs2drnk took a different stance from StanleyDoyle1. In reply to StanleyDoyle1 If we were winning more games, I’d be inclined to agree with you. But the main reason we have so many rookies playing meaningful snaps is due to the gutting of the roster. So while they are getting meaningful snaps on our team, not so sure they would do the same on a competitive team. I’d give you Rod, Proc, Johnson, and Douglas although the first 3 would be the only ones who would likely be starting on any other team. Taafe has shown some potential, need to see more consistancy. Kac likely becomes a blocking TE with little to no impact as a receiving TE, which is disappointing for a 3rd rounder. Bell could still develop, but won’t likely have any impact till next year hopefully. Coleman could eventually replace Washington or fade into obscurity if more talented receiving options are added. The fact we got 4-5 potential long term starters out of this class is a feat in itself, and that definitely bodes well for next year’s draft. Let’s just hope they have better luck in the FA department next year. I’ll give this year a pass due to cap restrictions. Well, it was a bit slow, but I guess the fans’ overall enthusiasm is down because of the losing, and those fans choosing something else to do right now are missing out on seeing these rookies ball out. Anway, thank you to each of you who took the time to join in and answer our Phinsider Question Of The Day.

title: Third time’s a charm; Dolphins sign new kicker to replace Zane Gonzalez
summary: Last week, the Miami Dolphins worked out two kickers amidst Zane Gonzalez’s struggles regarding the conversion of field goal attempts — a pretty important task for kickers in the National Football League. Despite impressive days from Ben Sauls and Daniel Carlson, Miami decided to roll with Gonzalez last Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts. That decision […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 18: Daniel Carlson #10 of the New Orleans Saints looks on during the third quarter against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium on October 18, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last week, the Miami Dolphins worked out two kickers amidst Zane Gonzalez’s struggles regarding the conversion of field goal attempts — a pretty important task for kickers in the National Football League. Despite impressive days from Ben Sauls and Daniel Carlson, Miami decided to roll with Gonzalez last Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts. That decision came back to bite them in the tuchus … big time. In a game in which the Dolphins lost by just two points, Gonzalez missed two field goals and an extra point try. Those gaffes cost the team the game, and the kicker his job in Miami, leaving general manager, Jon-Eric Sullivan, to go searching for his third player at the position during the 2026 NFL season. On Tuesday, the Dolphins signed Carlson to their practice squad — giving the team roster flexibility while being able to call up the kicker to their active roster on game days three times before being required to sign him to their 53-man squad. Carlson — a 9-year veteran — has played for a number of teams in his career. His most recent stint was with the New Orleans Saints. However, Carlson was released earlier this season after going just 8 for 12 on field goal tries in 7 games played. For his entire career, Carlson has made 233 tries on 271 attempts — good for an 86% average. For the sake of comparison, Gonzalez has a career field-goal conversion rate of 79.6%. Our first opportunity to find out if Sullivan has finally found his kicker will take place when the Dolphins travel to Highmark Stadium this Sunday to take on the Buffalo Bills.

title: The Hits Keep On Coming: Dolphins’ Jordan Phillips Suffers Season-Ending Injury
summary: The Miami Dolphins’ defensive line suffered another major blow Tuesday, with defensive tackle Jordan Phillips becoming the third member of the unit to suffer a season-ending injury in the span of two weeks. ESPN’s Marcel Louis-Jacques reported that Phillips suffered a torn biceps during Sunday’s loss to the Indianapolis Colts and will miss the remainder […]
full_text: The Miami Dolphins’ defensive line suffered another major blow Tuesday, with defensive tackle Jordan Phillips becoming the third member of the unit to suffer a season-ending injury in the span of two weeks. ESPN’s Marcel Louis-Jacques reported that Phillips suffered a torn biceps during Sunday’s loss to the Indianapolis Colts and will miss the remainder of the 2026 season. The Dolphins subsequently placed Phillips on injured reserve. The Dolphins lost veteran defensive tackle Zach Sieler to a ruptured biceps in their Week 9 loss to the Detroit Lions. Zeek Biggers suffered a knee injury against Indianapolis and will undergo season-ending surgery to repair the lateral meniscus in his right knee. With Sieler, Phillips, Biggers and Grant leading the way, the Dolphins have climbed to 10th in the NFL in total defense and 10th in rushing yards allowed per carry. Those rankings could take a significant hit with three of the four players now sidelined for the remainder of the season. Phillips, a fifth-round selection in the 2025 NFL Draft, had emerged as an important piece of Miami’s defensive line. The 22-year-old appeared in all nine games this season, recording 28 tackles and a tackle for loss while playing approximately 60 percent of the team’s defensive snaps. His importance to the defense went beyond the statistics. Phillips had become a reliable run defender, occupying blockers and allowing Miami’s linebackers to make plays. He was expected to take on an even larger role following Sieler’s injury, with head coach Jeff Hafley previously identifying him as someone who needed to step up and provide leadership to the defensive line. Instead, Miami will have to move forward without all three of its most heavily used defensive tackles. With Phillips and Biggers joining Sieler on injured reserve, the Dolphins are left with Kenneth Grant and Keith Cooper Jr. as their primary defensive tackles. Miami promoted Jordan Jefferson from the practice squad to the active roster Tuesday and also signed former Dolphins defensive tackle Matthew Butler and Chris Smith to the practice squad. The timing of these injuries couldn’t be much worse. Miami travels to Buffalo in Week 11 to face a Bills offense averaging more than 150 rushing yards per game, with James Cook among the league’s leading rushers. The Dolphins will need their remaining defensive linemen to find a way to replace the production of three players who had become central to their defensive success.

title: The Phinsider turns 20
summary: Today marks the 20th birthday for The Phinsider. This site, started by Matt Infante on November 18, 2006, has become a huge community of Miami Dolphins fans as we all ride the roller coaster that is this team. The site has been here through the eras of Nick Saban, Cam Cameron, Tony Sparano, Todd Bowles, […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - DECEMBER 29: A closeup view of the Miami Dolphins logo on a sweatshirt prior to a game against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on December 29, 2024 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images Today marks the 20th birthday for The Phinsider. This site, started by Matt Infante on November 18, 2006, has become a huge community of Miami Dolphins fans as we all ride the roller coaster that is this team. The site has been here through the eras of Nick Saban, Cam Cameron, Tony Sparano, Todd Bowles, Joe Philbin, Dan Campbell, Adam Gase, Brian Flores, Mike McDaniel, and now Jeff Hafley. It has seen Daunte Culpepper, Joey Harrington, Cleo Lemon, Trent Green, John Beck, Chad Pennington, Chad Henne, Tyler Thigpen, Matt Moore, Ryan Tannehill, Jay Cutler, Brock Osweiler, Ryan Fitzpatrick, Josh Rosen, Tua Tagovailoa, Jacoby Brissett, Teddy Bridgewater, Skylar Thompson, Tyler Huntley, Quinn Ewers, Malik Willis, and Kyle McCord start at quarterback. (Yes, there have been 22 different starting quarterbacks in The Phinsider’s 20 years.) The Dolphins are 150-184 over the 20 years of the site. The site launched during Nick Saban’s final year, immediately weathered the 1–15 nightmare of 2007 (saved only by Greg Camarillo), and then celebrated the 2008 Wildcat revolution and AFC East title under Tony Sparano and Chad Pennington. We lived through Cameron Wake’s walk-off safety on Halloween night in 2013, the “bullygate” scandal, Jay Ajayi’s back-to-back 200-yard rushing games in 2016, and, of course, Kenyan Drake’s touchdown in the Miami Miracle in December 2018. We debated “Tank for Tua”, cheered the 2022–2023 offensive track meets featuring Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle, marveled at dropping 70 points against the Denver Broncos in September 2023, and now navigate the rebuild under Jeff Hafley in 2026. We have been through a lot together over the last 20 years. Infante, in 2011, took a look back at his goals when he founded the site. He wrote: I essentially planned on using this platform as my outlet, my escape, from grad school work. Hell, we all know that this football team drives us friggin’ mad most of the time. So I figured writing about the week to week and year to year disappointments of the Dolphins would be very good therapy. Living up in New Jersey, there obviously aren’t many Dolphins fans to vent with. So I thought that the platform SBN was providing me would also help me cope with the annual frustration that we all have come to expect out of this team by interacting with a few Dolphins fans. Never in my wildest dreams did I think that “a few Dolphins fans” would turn into the community that we’ve all built here. We’re now talking about a Miami Dolphins community that has just under 7,000 members now. The way this community came together was something I never expected. I took over the management of the site in July 2011. I originally thought I would be a temporary placeholder, getting the site through that season before handing it over to someone else as a permanent replacement for Infante. I am not a writer and never thought I would do something like this. Now, 15 years later, I am still here because of you, and I’m so thankful for your support of the site and the community we have built, and the opportunities that have come with it. From Infante founding the site in 2006 to the powerhouse it is today, we have seen the platform evolve over the years, with changes to the site’s look and new ways for you to interact. We have explored videos and podcasts. We have added polls, daily live chats, and more. And we have grown through all of it because of the sheer staying power of the community. Generations of Phinsider readers have bonded over traditions that often felt bigger than the regular season itself: NFL Draft live threads, debate-heavy mock draft seasons, free agency trackers, 53-man roster cutdown threads, and the legendary game-day live threads where hundreds of comments fly per quarter. As The Phinsider turns 20, I truly want to thank you for being the best Dolphins community on the internet. Thank you for reading, commenting, sharing, and discussing. Thank you for the FanPosts, FanShots, and Feed posts over the last 20 years. Thank you for caring about the site, for moderating yourselves, and for looking out for your fellow Dolphins fans. Thank you to all of the fans of other teams who have come to The Phinsider and become members of the community, adding insights about other teams, and maybe some fun-filled trash talking. And, a huge thank you to everyone who is and has been part of the author team on the site. I can never fully express how appreciative I am of each of you. Thank you to everyone just for being here. What brought you to The Phinsider? What made you stay? And what is your favorite memory from the site’s first 20 years? Here’s to the next 20!

title: A New Era: Kirk Cousins’ Redemption Arc
summary: Terry Bradshaw said it best during the halftime show of last week’s Vikings vs. Packers game when he said, “Minnesota seems to OWN Green Bay.” Yes, Terry, that is correct. The Vikings have now won five of the last six games against the vomit and urine team. Kirk Cousins’ return/revenge game went about as well […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WI - NOVEMBER 15, 2026: Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins (8) threw a pass in the second half at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisc., on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. (Photo by Jerry Holt/The Minnesota Star Tribune via Getty Images) Terry Bradshaw said it best during the halftime show of last week’s Vikings vs. Packers game when he said, “Minnesota seems to OWN Green Bay.” Yes, Terry, that is correct. The Vikings have now won five of the last six games against the vomit and urine team. Kirk Cousins’ return/revenge game went about as well as it could have. Things weren’t perfect, but the offense moved the ball, converted on big third downs, and SCORED TOUCHDOWNS! This was Cousins’ eighth game this season throwing for multiple touchdowns, which ties him for the league lead with the quarterback on the other sideline, Jordan Love. All other Vikings quarterbacks combined for only eight such games since the beginning of the 2025 season. That is not a surprising statistic, but it is representative of how much we have suffered watching this offense since the departure of Sam Darnold. We’re here now; that’s all that matters I could talk about how the Vikings had multiple opportunities to keep Cousins on the roster and argue that these struggles are of their own doing, but I’m not going to focus on that aspect. Conventional wisdom at the time of Cousins’ departure was that the Falcons egregiously overpaid for the veteran quarterback. I was in agreement back then, as there were many questions about whether or not he could recover from his torn Achilles tendon and still be the same player. That version of Kirk Cousins was not going to deliver us to the promised land. That version of Kirk Cousins still needed to recover and work his way back to proper form. If you saw Cousins’ post-game interview after the game against the Packers last week, you couldn’t help but get a sense that Kirk was incredibly grateful to be back on the Minnesota Vikings. He spoke to how difficult the journey has been: leaving the franchise that was nearest to his heart, signing with a team that turned around and drafted Michael Penix, underperforming with the Falcons, and then moving to Las Vegas, playing in front of their eventual franchise quarterback. He was a bridge quarterback for both of those teams, buying time for rookie quarterbacks. Now, he is THE GUY (at least for this season). Growth comes from adversity The time he spent away from Minnesota changed him as a person and a player. Something is different about this version of Kirk Cousins. There has been a shift in his persona where the lovable caricature, Kirko Chainz: the Kohl’s Cash-spending, Great Clips-using iteration of the player, is gone. What remains is someone who is determined to cement his legacy. What remains is a player with a huge chip on his shoulder. What remains is Kirk’s best version of himself. He endured turmoil, uncertainty, and failure, just like we have as fans of the Minnesota Vikings. A narrative that has picked up traction in the last week is that the Vikings were incompetent for even letting him walk in the first place. I disagree. What we are seeing transcends logic and the forces of man. Kirk Cousins’ return is part of a bigger picture; it’s destiny. Morpheus said it best in The Matrix: Reloaded when he said: “What happened, happened, and couldn’t have happened any other way.” Moving forward, this is a team that will garner respect from players, pundits, and fans around the league. Just a few weeks ago, we were touted as the worst 6-0 team in NFL history. I have drunk so much of the Purple Kool-Aid that I was fighting against that narrative and believing that Kyler Murray could improve and lead this team to the playoffs. Thank goodness I don’t have to defend that take anymore. Cousins, for all of his flaws, is a capable veteran quarterback in the NFL. He has been playing for a long time and provides a calming presence. He has always been a great leader, and he’s currently on the best roster he has ever been a part of. The holistic approach. We finally saw a complete game from the Vikings. I will play devil’s advocate and not anoint us as Super Bowl favorites. I think the Packers are incredibly overrated this season. Yes, they were the hottest offense coming into last Sunday, but we saw that they can’t protect their quarterback, and they are abysmal running the ball. Yes, they were missing Josh Jacobs on offense and Micah Parsons on defense, but I think this was a game the Vikings should win handily, and they did. I could see the Packers going on a downward spiral and missing the playoffs altogether. Although it was incredibly gratifying to see a dominant performance against the worst team in the NFC North, it’s not a game to hang our hats on. This team did what should be expected of them. Going into Mexico City, the Vikings’ number one defense is going up against the 49ers’ number one offense. It is a strength-on-strength matchup in a high-altitude environment with even higher stakes. It would be an incredible statement win for Minnesota if they can pull it off. We know this defense is great and that this offense can now complement the best unit in the NFL. People’s perception is that Kirk Cousins is still the lovable version of himself from three years ago, but perception here does not match reality. Cousins is on a mission to prove his detractors wrong, to show that he is a great NFL quarterback, that he can win in primetime, and that he can lead our (and his) favorite team to the promised land. I will leave you with something different. A contribution from my brother, Kollin. A short poem of sorts: I believe in SKOL, the Father Almighty, creator of hope and heartbreak; I believe in Kirk Cousins, our only hope this year, our Captain, Who was conceived of the GM Spielman, born of a guaranteed contract; Suffered under Zimmer; Was pressured, sacked, and was injured, he descended into Atlanta; On the third year away he rose again;and ascended to the Vikings He is seated at the right hand of the Jettas; and he shall come again to judge the Packers and the Bears I believe in the Holy Skol, The Holy Minnesota Vikings, The communion of the Purple, The forgiveness of the picks, The resurrection of the offense, and the Super Bowl Everlasting. YOU LIKE THAT. AMEN Until next skol.

title: Jordan Addison to Avoid IR; Vikings Make Several Other Moves
summary: The Minnesota Vikings made a handful of roster moves on Wednesday, and also got some very positive news about one of their best wide receivers. Jordan Addison had surgery to correct the thumb injury we mentioned on Monday, and it turns out that he will not be going on short-term injured reserve after all. That […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 01: Jordan Addison #3 of the Minnesota Vikings plays against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on November 01, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings made a handful of roster moves on Wednesday, and also got some very positive news about one of their best wide receivers. Jordan Addison had surgery to correct the thumb injury we mentioned on Monday, and it turns out that he will not be going on short-term injured reserve after all. That means the team expects him to miss less time than the four games mandated by a stint on IR. We’ll see how many games Addison misses, but the team’s decision not to put him on injured reserve should be seen as a positive sign for him. Unfortunately, outside linebacker Bo Richter was not so fortunate, as the team placed him on IR on Wednesday. Richter suffered a foot injury in Sunday’s win at Green Bay, but the team is hopeful that he can return at some point later in the season. A third-year player from the Air Force Academy, Richter has played almost exclusively on special teams for the Vikings this year. The Vikings have also signed wide receiver Jeshaun Jones to the active roster from the practice squad. Jones has been with the Vikings for a couple of seasons, primarily on the practice squad, and recorded the first catch of his NFL career against New Orleans in Week 5. In one last move for the day, the Vikings signed former Seattle Seahawks and Miami Dolphins wide receiver D’Wayne Eskridge to the practice squad. Eskridge, who was selected by the Seahawks in the second round of the 2021 NFL Draft, worked out for the Vikings back in October during the same workout that saw the Vikings bring in veteran JuJu Smith-Schuster. So, to give everyone a full update, the Vikings’ practice squad now looks like this, as the team also lost safety Tavierre Thomas to the New York Giants on Tuesday. title: Week 10 Observations: I Like That!
summary: The Vikings began the unexpected second act of their 2026 season with a resounding 30-10 road victory over the rival Green Bay Packers. Between Kirk Cousins’ emotional return and the defense’s historic season, it’s hard to imagine a more memorable and satisfying result. How could you not be moved by this? The Daily Norseman crew […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 15: Kirk Cousins #8 and Christian Darrisaw #71 of the Minnesota Vikings celebrate a touchdown against the Green Bay Packers during the fourth quarter at Lambeau Field on November 15, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Vikings began the unexpected second act of their 2026 season with a resounding 30-10 road victory over the rival Green Bay Packers. Between Kirk Cousins’ emotional return and the defense’s historic season, it’s hard to imagine a more memorable and satisfying result. How could you not be moved by this? An emotional Kirk Cousins, in his return to the Vikings at Lambeau Field: “I tore my Achilles here and it’s been a tough three years…” pic.twitter.com/8PhbEVs7Oq — Lindsey Thiry (@LindseyThiry) November 15, 2026 The Daily Norseman crew did their usual stellar job recapping the rewarding victory here , here , and here . Aside from the obvious candidates (e.g., Turner, Van Ginkel, Redmond, Smith, Wilson, Van Noy, Price), I was particularly encouraged by contributions from Caleb Banks, Elijah Williams, Gavin Bartholomew, Tai Felton, and Jakobe Thomas. Maybe we do have some depth, huh? Topline Takeaways Like He Never Left. Kirk Cousins parachuted into Vikings practice on Wednesday and started on Sunday. As unheard of as that is, given the chaos that’s defined the past two seasons at quarterback, seeing him run out to the huddle for the opening series felt totally normal, as if time stood still. I was eagerly soaking it all in. Even with a few days of prep and a playbook that had changed since 2023, Cousins’ familiarity with the scheme and system was evident from the get-go. While the numbers weren’t overwhelming – 21 for 31, 207 yards, 2 TDs, and an interception – the eye test was passed with flying colors. Of course, not all passes and not all yards gained on them are created equal. How and when matter. That’s where Cousins immediately changed things. EPA per play improved (+0.04), and the Vikings offense converted 8-of-16 third downs. This included a 3rd-and-23 TD to Myles Price and a critical 3rd-and-12 conversion to Justin Jefferson, who also saw a season-high number of targets. Coincidence? I think not. This was a notable improvement over the 3-for-10 third-down conversion rate in the loss to the Lions and the 3-for-11 in the ugly win against the Colts. The Bills game? Let’s not go there. Drew Brees liked what he saw. Drew Brees with high praise for @KirkCousins8 in his first game back with the Vikings. @drewbrees 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/0hhdxTezwx — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) November 15, 2026 It’s also no fluke that Sunday’s game saw the Vikings’ offensive time of possession jump to over 35 minutes. This was a marked improvement over the abysmal 17 minutes against the Bills and 24 minutes against the Lions, respectively, in the team’s two losses. It was also much better than the 28 minutes in the ugly home win over the hapless Colts. It’s almost as if the mere threat of an effective passing game suddenly makes running the ball easier. Weird. It’s just one week, and time will tell, but based on interviews and body language, this seems like a different Kirk Cousins to me. One who is not only more confident and comfortable but also grateful for the opportunity to change the narrative of his career forever – something that seemed out of reach just days earlier. All made easier by what’s shaping up to be a historic defense by his side. I basically said it all last week: Cousins realizes the feel-good, storybook ending is within reach. Reports say the Raiders left the trade decision in his hands. He knows. This is his last, best chance. A Kirk Cousins with a Super Bowl ring would not only have a legitimate Hall of Fame resume (the statistics will be there), but he’d also have a statue outside U.S. Stadium to immortalize his role in ending the long-suffering anguish of a tortured fan base. I’ve Seen Enough. This Defense is Generational. After another impressive performance against a top-flight offense, it’s time to discuss the 2026 Minnesota Vikings’ defense in historic terms. While national media talking heads usually write narrative checks on the Packers that they inevitably can’t cash, it was worse coming into Sunday’s game because the Packers had won five of their last six, including a dominant win over a fraudulent Patriots team living off last season’s rep the week prior. Instead, they got another kind of check: a reality check. The eight sacks and four turnovers didn’t do justice to the torture Brian Flores inflicted on Matt LaFleur, Jordan Love, and the entire Packers offense throughout the afternoon. It was yet another piece of the puzzle that, when complete, could look record-breaking. oh OK, wow pic.twitter.com/iXMWXwyekv — Krauser (@Krauserrific) November 16, 2026 Points allowed through 9 games. 2026 Vikings: 126 1985 Bears: 124 — PowerTrip Bets (@PowerTripBets) November 16, 2026 The comparison to the 1985 Bears is impressive enough, especially given the changes made to benefit offenses over the past 20 years. Enjoy the rest of the ride, folks. Soak it all in, because this isn’t normal. It’s thrilling, but it’s not guaranteed to last beyond this season. Brian Flores will get another head-coaching opportunity someday, and key players such as Blake Cashman, Andrew Van Ginkel, Isaiah Rodgers, and Kyle Van Noy will be free agents. Meanwhile, Jalen Redmond is a restricted free agent, and it’s almost certainly Harrison Smith’s last hurrah. Third Time a Charm? Since 1990, the Vikings have made the playoffs 17 times, tying for 7th in that span. Not too shabby. Each year, the purple neurons in my brain lit up, distorting reality into something that justified the belief that they could not only make the Super Bowl but win it. My intuition has proven far more reliable. It’s equipped with the right defenses to filter out most delusions and purify it all. It shocks me back into reality, takes off the blinders so I can see clearly, and acknowledges the issues you know deep down will inevitably dash the dream. They truly aligned only twice: 1998 and 2009. Not 2000. Not 2017. My gut didn’t trust the defense in 2000 or the offense in 2017. In the end, both sides of the ball were an issue, but that doesn’t matter now. What matters is… things are close to aligning with this team again after 17 years. The convergence of multiple elements (i.e., the defense and Cousins’ return) for a magical season appears to be in place. There are still eight games left, so that could change before the playoffs, and that very well could happen. But I’ve never been as close to the long-awaited third instance as I was after this impressive win in Green Bay. A win, or even a razor-thin loss, to the 8-1 49ers next week will put it within arm’s reach. If so, let’s hope the third time is the charm and that the season ends with a third act, one that culminates in a Lombardi Trophy triumphantly lifted in the air.

West- IR DT Knee FP Mykel Williams DE Hand, Ankle FP Trent Williams* LT NIR-Rest DNP Injury Report Terms and Glossary FP = Full participant in practice. LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. NIR = Not injury related. PUP = Physically unable to participate list. IR = Injured reserve. Note: only starters on IR are listed. Player Name* = Starter. Injury designation definitions: Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. Notes on Injured Players For the Vikings, it looks like just Jordan Addison and Kyler Murray will be out for Sunday’s game. Addison just had thumb surgery and won’t play on Sunday while Murray won’t be active either with his hamstring injury. Cashman, Ingram-Dawkins, Hockenson, and Jauan Jennings are all on track to practice and play on Sunday. Van Ginkel and the rest look like they have some minor injuries they are playing through. For the 49ers, beyond the IR players both Mike Evans and Dre Greenlaw didn’t practice today (although Evans was seen doing a few very limited things on a side field). 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said he hoped Evans would practice later this week and hoped he could go on Sunday. For now he looks more doubtful but we’ll see how he progresses during the week. Getting him back would be big for the 49ers offense. Brock Purdy’s EPA/dropback has been roughly twice as high with Evans in the lineup than without. Evans has missed the last three Niners’ games with Achilles tendonitis. Renardo Green is also one to keep an eye on as a starting cornerback. He has been dealing with a back injury for a couple weeks now and had to leave the Cowboys game on Sunday because of it. We’ll see how it goes with him and Stout- another cornerback limited to start the week. My guess is that Green will be questionable on Sunday and if he plays he won’t be 100%. Stout has been dealing with an AC joint issue for several weeks now. The neck issue is new. C.J. West has his window open to return from IR. The others look to be dealing with minor injuries they can play through or aren’t starters so less impact one way or another. We’ll have updates tomorrow and Friday with injury designations. Follow me on X/Bluesky @wludford

title: What Are the Chances of the Vikings Getting “Flexed” the Rest of This Season?
summary: Now that we’re into the second half of the 2026 NFL season, the potential for games to get “flexed” into different time slots has increased. Yesterday, as there were rumors that the Week 12 matchup between the Minnesota Vikings and the Atlanta Falcons at U.S. Bank Stadium might get flexed to Sunday Night Football that […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - SEPTEMBER 13: A general exterior view of U.S. Bank Stadium on September 13, 2025 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Aaron M. Sprecher/Getty Images) | Getty Images Now that we’re into the second half of the 2026 NFL season, the potential for games to get “flexed” into different time slots has increased. Yesterday, as there were rumors that the Week 12 matchup between the Minnesota Vikings and the Atlanta Falcons at U.S. Bank Stadium might get flexed to Sunday Night Football that week, the league decided to move the game between the Las Vegas Raiders and Cleveland Browns to that spot instead. You read that correctly. . .the league moved a game between Cleveland and Las Vegas into a prime time spot, moving a game between the Los Angeles Chargers and New England Patriots out of that spot. So, with Week 12 no longer a possibility, do the Vikings have any other potential chances of being moved into a prime time slot for the rest of the season? Let’s take a look. To briefly review the flex scheduling rules, games can be flexed to Sunday Night Football with 12 days notice between Weeks 11-13 and with 6 days notice between Weeks 14-17, to Monday Night Football with 12 days notice between Weeks 12-17, and to Thursday Night Football with 21 days notice between Weeks 13-17. Basically, time is running short for the league to move games around, particularly if they want to move them to Thursday night. With that, here we go. Week 13: Panthers at Vikings, currently scheduled for 3:25 PM Central on CBS Sunday Night Football : Texans at Steelers Monday Night Football : Cowboys at Seahawks If the league is going to move this matchup into one of those two prime time spots, we’re going to know by this time next week, as it’s the last week that requires 12 days notice before moving a game into either of those spots. (The Sunday night requirement drops to 6 days starting in Week 14, as outlined above.) On top of that, the league has a couple of other matchups they’d likely find more attractive than Panthers/Vikings, such as Jaguars/Bears and Bengals/Browns, depending on which matchups the networks are protecting. Week 14: Vikings at Patriots, currently scheduled for Thursday Night Football Sunday Night Football : Bills at Packers Monday Night Football : Steelers at Jaguars The league would have to make the decision by tomorrow if they wanted to move Vikings/Patriots off of Thursday Night Football because of the 21-day notice requirement. The issue there is that two of the most potentially attractive matchups are already in prime time slots for that week. Chiefs/Bengals and Rams/49ers are both set for the late window on FOX in Week 14, and I don’t know if FOX can protect both of those games or not. If they can’t, one of those could be a possibility. Again, if it’s going to happen, we’ll know by tomorrow. Week 15: Lions at Vikings, currently scheduled for Sunday Night Football Yeah, the league isn’t moving this one. Week 16: Commanders at Vikings, date and time currently TBD Thursday Night Football : Texans at Eagles Sunday Night Football : Jaguars at Cowboys Monday Night Football : Giants at Lions Week 16 could get a little tricky. Vikings/Commanders is one of four games (along with Buccaneers/Falcons, Bengals/Colts, and Panthers/Steelers) that is currently set to, potentially, be a part of a Saturday doubleheader on the NFL Network. The two games from that group that aren’t selected for that Saturday, according to the footnote on the NFL’s schedule page for Week 16 , are eligible to be played on Thursday night. . . or on Sunday afternoon. . . or on Sunday night. . . or on Monday night. It’s Thunderdome out there in Week 16, kids. If both the Texans and Eagles continue to struggle, that Thursday night matchup might be one the league is looking to move off of for a prime time spot. But whether or not they move that Vikings/Patriots game out of the Week 14 spot could play a role in that, too. Lot of ins, lot of outs. . .lot of strands to keep in the dude’s head. The Week 16 matchups are supposed to be determined “immediately after Week 14,” so we’ll see how that works out. Week 17: Vikings at Jets, currently scheduled for noon Central on CBS Thursday Night Football : Ravens at Bengals Sunday Night Football : Eagles at Niners Monday Night Football : Texans at Packers I’m not going to spend a whole lot of time on this one. I just don’t think the league is going to put Vikings/Jets into a prime time spot for any reason, honestly. Week 18: Bears at Vikings, TBD As the league has done for the last few years, the schedule for Week 18 won’t be known until Week 17 is pretty much completely in the books and we know which matchups are going to carry the greatest playoff implications/drama going into the final week of the season. So, should we worry about the Vikings potentially getting their schedule changed over the second half of the season? It doesn’t look like it, honestly, but the league could give us a surprise. The biggest surprise would be moving the New England game off of Thursday Night, but if that’s going to happen, we’ll know about it by tomorrow because of the timing requirements.

title: Vikes Views: Which WR will Step Up in Jordan Addison’s Absence?
summary: Minnesota Vikings WR 2 Jordan Addison is expected to be out for the next several weeks. It hasn’t been the most productive season for Addison, but he has played a lot of snaps. Those snaps, along with new QB Kirk Cousins, will provide a big opportunity for someone to step up in Addison’s absence. Who […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 15: Myles Price #4 of the Minnesota Vikings celebrates with teammates after scoring a touchdown against the Green Bay Packers during the first quarter at Lambeau Field on November 15, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images Minnesota Vikings WR 2 Jordan Addison is expected to be out for the next several weeks . It hasn’t been the most productive season for Addison, but he has played a lot of snaps. Those snaps, along with new QB Kirk Cousins, will provide a big opportunity for someone to step up in Addison’s absence. Who do you think is most likely to take advantage of the opportunity? title: Vikings Debriefing: Daily Norseman Week 10 Postgame Roundtable (A 30-10 win over the Packers)
summary: Hello everyone, and welcome to the Week 10 Minnesota Vikings postgame roundtable here at Daily Norseman. The Vikes are coming off easily their most complete effort of the season — a 30-10 dismantling of the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. So be honest….DO YOU LIKE THAT? Let’s talk to it: Question 1: Let’s freestyle […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 04: T.J. Hockenson #87 of the Minnesota Vikings celebrates against the Miami Dolphins in the fourth quarter at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. The Vikings defeated the Dolphins 15-10. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello everyone, and welcome to the Week 10 Minnesota Vikings postgame roundtable here at Daily Norseman. The Vikes are coming off easily their most complete effort of the season — a 30-10 dismantling of the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. So be honest….DO YOU LIKE THAT? Let’s talk to it: Question 1: Let’s freestyle for a minute — get your initial thoughts out about the Vikings beating the Packers in Week 10, 30-10. Brandon Warne : The Vikings went out and had a ‘belt-to-ass’ performance against their biggest rival, completing a sweep with — for my money — their two most impressive/intriguing games of the season. If the Vikings can average 20 points per game with Cousins the rest of the way — they scored 20-plus just three times entering last weekend, and just twice since the opener — this is a damn scary squad. Christopher Gates : Few things in Vikings fandom are more satisfying than watching our favorite team slap the Packers around for sixty solid minutes. There really wasn’t a point in this one where it didn’t feel like the Vikings were fully in control, which was surprising given the trajectory that these two teams came in on. The Packers came off of a 45-point performance against New England the previous week, while the Vikings were coming off of the Monday Night disaster against Buffalo. But after the Packers fumbled on their first possession, it seemed like the Vikings grabbed on to this one and weren’t going to let go. Kirk Cousins provided the sort of quarterback play this team hasn’t had all season, and it let the defense catch a breather after a couple of weeks of being overworked. Warren Ludford : I was a bit surprised by the extent of the blowout. I wasn’t confident before the game when I saw the inactive list. But as the game went on, I realized again how bad the Packers OL is and how that completely compromises their deep ball game, which is what they do. I was pleasantly surprised that Cousins could move the offense and convert 3rd-and-longs. Craig Williams : My initial feeling is excitement. I don’t think the team has looked this much like a legitimate contender since the NFC Championship Game season. Cousins isn’t a top-tier quarterback, but he’s more than good enough to get this offense moving. For the first time all year, it feels like the Vikings have all three phases working in the same direction. I can’t wait to see what the offense looks like once T.J. Hockenson and Jordan Addison are back in the lineup. Shawn C. : Ecstatic. Given the unique circumstances of Kirk Cousins returning midweek, midseason, to the very place where his first tenure with the Vikings ended, this was the most satisfying regular-season win I can remember. The fact that it was against the Packers was the icing on the cake. Sam Buegler : Man, that was so much better than I hoped – the first half especially. I got nervous during the second half, but the defense held strong, and we got just what we needed out of Kirk to wind down the clock and seal the deal. ————— Question 2: Who was your Vikings MVP? BW : I have the benefit of seeing everyone else’s answers, so I’m going to zig when everyone else zags and say Dallas Turner. He was literally unblockable — not that it seemed like Green Bay put up much resistance — and is making a lot of those Jared Verse conversations look pretty silly right about now. Let’s get this guy signed up long term, please and thank you. CG : Even with the incredible defensive performance the Vikings put on…it has to be Cousins, doesn’t it? After eight games of watching Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz do…whatever, exactly, it was that Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz were doing…seeing Cousins do the little things on offense and move the chains consistently was exactly what this team needed. Throw in the fact that he did it with one full practice and with no Jordan Addison, no T.J. Hockenson, and no Jauan Jennings available, and it gets even more impressive. He was hitting guys like Myles Price, Tai Felton, Gavin Bartholomew, whoever the Vikings were making available to him. As the Vikings get those weapons back and Cousins gets more reacclimated to the offense, things should only get better. WL : Kirk Cousins has to be the MVP despite the defensive dominance. He made the offense work again. CW : Everybody is going to pick Kirk Cousins, and rightfully so. I’m going with Eric Wilson. He was asked to wear the green dot and fill Blake Cashman’s role against a division rival in a big game. That’s not an easy assignment. Wilson stepped up, led the defense, and was all over the field. That’s exactly what good teams need from their depth players. SC : Cousins is the easy answer, given the palpable excitement and enthusiasm for his return. But I definitely want to give a shoutout to Levi Drake Rodriguez, who recorded 8 pressures and 2 sacks. With all the playmakers showing up on defense this season, LDR often gets lost in the shuffle. He was front and center on Sunday. SB : I am going with Myles Price, since I assume someone else will choose Kirk. 4/4, 49 yards, a TD, and averaging 12 yards per catch is exactly what we needed with JA and TJ out. It was fun to watch him start to thrive with Cousins, and I am hoping to see more of him moving forward. ————— Question 3: Who was your Vikings LVP? BW : Outside of a couple of boneheaded penalties early, it’s really hard to isolate anyone who played poorly. Christian Darrisaw doesn’t seem to have the same juice as last year and PFF, for what it’s worth, didn’t particularly enjoy the work of the team’s safety trio of Josh Metellus, Harrison Smith and Theo Jackson. But trying to find an LVP feels like a real stretch here — in a good way. CG : Man, it’s really hard to find a least valuable player after a performance like this. I guess Jay Ward had a dumb penalty on the kickoff that followed the Vikings’ first field goal that gave the Packers good field position. Honestly, that’s probably about the best I can do there. I just can’t remember any other plays from the game where I shook my head and said, “Wow, that was really bad.” I can’t remember who got beat in coverage on the Packers’ one touchdown, but it wasn’t egregious enough for me to single anyone out, I don’t think. WL : Hard to pick a LVP, but I’ll go with Jay Ward for his personal foul early in the game on special teams that gave the Packers good field position near midfield. You can’t give up cheap yards like that with extracurricular activity on special teams. Especially on the road. CW : Surprise pick: Christian Darrisaw. He just hasn’t looked like himself this season. After allowing six sacks entering the game, he gave up two more against Green Bay. That’s eight sacks allowed already, which is a career high. The Vikings won comfortably, so it gets overlooked, but they’ll need better play from one of their highest-paid offensive linemen moving forward. SC : No one really stood out. But if I’m forced to pick someone, I guess it’s CB James Pierre, who probably had the weakest game in an otherwise exceptional season so far. Not worried at all. SB : LVP is a hard category to give out on a week when we crush the Packers. I am not going to single out a particular player, but I will say that the team needs to clean it up when it comes to flags. The reffing crew was calling them tightly, but 7 penalties for 75 yards needs to be fixed. It felt like that was what kept the Packers alive at points, so if we can get rid of those and still perform like we did yesterday, we will be in fantastic shape. ————— Question 4: How much has the Kirk Cousins acquisition changed your outlook for this team? How many wins did you expect them to finish the season with…

title: Tackle issues high up on Patriots’ post-bye to-do list
summary: Another week, another underwhelming performance for the New England Patriots defense. What was once a highly-touted unit surrendered 35 more points on Sunday against the Detroit Lions, and at an average of 24.2 points given up per game is now only ranked 18th in the NFL. There are a multitude of factors contributing to this, […]
full_text: Another week, another underwhelming performance for the New England Patriots defense. What was once a highly-touted unit surrendered 35 more points on Sunday against the Detroit Lions, and at an average of 24.2 points given up per game is now only ranked 18th in the NFL. There are a multitude of factors contributing to this, but tackling is high up on the list. The loss against Detroit was a clear example of that: the Patriots missed 11 tackles, including in some key situations. The most prominent of those came in the first quarter, after the Patriots had taken a 3-0 lead. Forcing the Lions into a 3rd-and-9 on their own side of the field, they surrendered a 56-yard catch-and-run touchdown that saw various players — in succession: Christian Gonzalez, Craig Woodson, Kevin Byard and Marcus Jones — all fail to bring wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown down on his way to the end zone. That play was exemplary for the Patriots’ failures on Sunday. Through 10 games, they have missed 73 total tackles for a rate of 12.6%. While that number means they are still the 10th-best tackling team in the NFL on the season as a whole, the discrepancy between wins and losses is stark: in their five victories, the Patriots missed 8.8% of tackle attempts; in their five losses, that number jumped to 16.2%. “It comes down to fundamentals,” said cornerback Christian Gonzalez on Sunday. “Just have to make those tackles in space. People are going to make catches in the NFL. Receivers are going to make catches. Running backs are going to break through. That’s going to happen. It’s the NFL. But at the same time, we have to be able to make the tackle and not let something short turn into a big play.” Gonzalez, who was the first player with a shot at St. Brown on the aforementioned touchdown, pointed to himself as the starting point for improvement. On the year, his four missed tackles are ranked eighth-worst among all Patriots defenders. So, how can they improve? For linebacker Christian Elliss, responsible for eight misses on the year, technique and effort are the key. “Just coming to balance, making sure you’re not falling off the diving board,” he said. “Make sure you’re wrapping up. At the end of the day when you have your brothers come to the ball with you, even if you’re about to lose grip or whatever, he should be getting smoke. So, I think it’s effort from the whole defense.” Whatever the solution is, the Patriots defense needs to find it quick. With quarterback Drake Maye possibly out for the year , the unit will be under pressure to carry the team over the final seven weeks of the season. It’s recent performance particularly in the tackling department, however, is worrisome.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: A.J. Brown injury update: New report adds information to Patriots WR’s status
summary: While Drake Maye’s ankle injury dominated the headlines coming out of the New England Patriots’ Week 10 game against the Detroit Lions, the star quarterback was not the only member unable to finish the game. Wide receiver A.J. Brown also left the contest prematurely, even though there has been far less coverage of his injury. […]
full_text: While Drake Maye’s ankle injury dominated the headlines coming out of the New England Patriots’ Week 10 game against the Detroit Lions, the star quarterback was not the only member unable to finish the game. Wide receiver A.J. Brown also left the contest prematurely, even though there has been far less coverage of his injury. However, according to a report by Jeremy Fowler of ESPN, the hamstring ailment “most likely puts him out for a little while.” While the information shared is admittedly vague and leaves room for interpretation, it is a first hint that he, like his QB, also is slated to miss at least some time. For Brown, 29, this is the latest chapter in what has been a disappointing season. Acquired in April in a trade with the Philadelphia Eagles, he looked good in training camp before suffering a high ankle sprain in the third quarter of New England’s season opener in Seattle. The injury sidelined him for the next four weeks, with his comeback being short-lived: Brown appeared in just two games before a knee ailment forced him out of the subsequent two contests. He did make the Patriots’ trip to Germany for the game against the Lions, but once again ran into injury problems . In the third quarter, after a 21-yard catch and run, he exited with the aforementioned hamstring issue and was unable to return to the eventual 35-10 loss. Unlike Drake Maye, Brown did travel back to the United States with the rest of the team. With the Patriots on their bye and not slated to return until Monday, it remains to be seen how long his absence will ultimately last. In four games this season, Brown has amassed 160 total snaps as well as 11 catches for 128 yards.

title: Drake Maye injury: Everything we know about the Patriots QB’s status
summary: Their Week 10 game against the Detroit Lions was the worst-case scenario for the New England Patriots. Not only were they blown out with a final score of 35-10 to drop to 5-5 on the season, they also lost their starting quarterback to an injury: Drake Maye exited the game in the first quarter due […]
full_text: Their Week 10 game against the Detroit Lions was the worst-case scenario for the New England Patriots. Not only were they blown out with a final score of 35-10 to drop to 5-5 on the season, they also lost their starting quarterback to an injury: Drake Maye exited the game in the first quarter due to what was later announced as an ankle injury. Shortly after the game, information was scarce but the first bits and pieces have started to come in. Based on everything we know, here is what we can say about Maye and his injury situation. What happened? The Patriots started Sunday’s game against the Lions with the ball, and actually moved down the field relatively well; it took them only eight plays to get from their own 25-yard line to the Detroit 3. Once there, however, things started to fall apart. Two penalties bookending an incomplete pass set up a 3rd-and-goal from the 13-yard line, and that play turned into a disaster for the Patriots. Aidan Hutchinson easily got around left tackle Christian Elliss, and dragged Maye down from behind and he was climbing an increasingly collapsing pocket. Along the way, the two-time Pro Bowl edge came down on Maye’s right ankle. He did get up under his own power, but Maye showed a noticeable limp while making his way toward the sideline. Once there, he received attention from the team’s medical staff and afterwards headed into the blue medical tent. When he emerged, still clearly hobbled, backup quarterback Tommy DeVito was already getting ready to enter the game. Maye slowly walked back to the locker room shortly thereafter, and initially labeled questionable to return by the team. Midway through the second quarter, he was downgraded to out. What do we know about the injury? Neither head coach Mike Vrabel nor any of his teammates were able to provide an update on Maye’s status during their post-game media availability. “Obviously, he wasn’t able to finish the game, so we’ll have to get some more tests run and we’ll see when we come back what it ends up being and the severity of whatever injury he has,” Vrabel said at the podium. “I know that it was a low leg injury. I don’t know the exact details of it but I know he couldn’t go back in. … He couldn’t function. Couldn’t play. Couldn’t run. Couldn’t do whatever he needed to do to play quarterback, to protect himself, to execute, or function at that level.” Left tackle Will Campbell, who briefly occupied the blue medical tent before Maye went in, gave some more information in the postgame locker room. “I talked to him,” Campbell told MassLive’s Mark Daniels. “He’s in good spirits and just waiting to hear more information about what it is, and just told him I love him and praying for him and he’s going to be fine. He’s a fighter. Whatever comes his way, he’s going to attack it full head of steam and come back better.” The Patriots will fly back to the United States on Sunday, with some follow-up testing expected to take place after the team’s arrival on Monday. [UPDATE 11/16/2026] Initial reports suggest that Maye suffered a “significant lower leg injury” that might keep him out for the remainder of the season. For the Patriots, this is very much the worst-case scenario. [UPDATE 11/16/2026] The Patriots are concerned that Maye suffered a fractured ankle against the Lions. [UPDATE 11/16/2026] Drake Maye did not travel back to the United States with the rest of the Patriots, per head coach Mike Vrabel. “He’ll be traveling back here shortly. Just wanted to make sure that everything was good for him to travel back and safely. The things that go around injuries and just wanted to make sure everything was in line for him to travel, and it seems like he is. He’ll be returning here, I think, shortly.” [UPDATE 11/16/2026] If indeed diagnosed as a fractured ankle, Drake Maye would “almost certainly” be out for the rest of the season, according to a report by Ian Rapoport. [UPDATE 11/17/2026] Appearing on local radio, Patriots safety Kevin Byard said that Maye was “probably out for the season.” What does it mean for the Patriots? “Any time your starting quarterback goes out and is not able to return, there are questions,” safety Kevin Byard told the media after the game. The questions mentioned by Byard are manifold in the direct aftermath of both the injury and the contest as a whole. Information about severity or a potential recovery timeline is limited, which in turn also limits the avenues the Patriots might have to explore in the immediate or long-term future. What we do know is that for however long Maye is sidelined, Tommy DeVito will be the top quarterback on the depth chart with third-stringer Behren Morton backing him up. DeVito completed 12 of 24 pass attempts for 81 yards with one touchdown and interception each after entering the Lions game midway through the first period. DeVito described his and the offense’s performance after he took over for Maye as “not good enough.” The next chance to improve upon it will come after the Patriots’ upcoming bye, with a Sunday Night game versus the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 12. New England will not start its on-field preparation for that game until a few days beforehand; the team will return to its usual in-game schedule following the bye. [UPDATE 11/16/2026] If the injury is indeed as significant as believed, here is a rundown of how it would impact the Patriots moving forward.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

full_text: If you were holding out hope that Drake Maye would still return this season, it might be time to adjust your expectations. For the first time since the New England Patriots starting quarterback suffered an ankle injury on Sunday against the Detroit Lions, one of his teammates has commented on the severity of the ailment. While not asked directly about the injury or any recovery timelines, Kevin Byard did drop a hint about how long Maye might be out. “Our quarterback’s out, and he’s probably going to be out for the rest of the season,” Byard told WEEI’s Rich & Ken on Tuesday. Byard’s statement echoes earlier reporting about the injury . Maye is believed to have suffered a fractured ankle on the opening drive against the Lions, an injury that necessitated him undergoing additional treatment in Germany and flying back to the United States later than the rest of the team. While no official statement has been released by the team on his status, head coach Mike Vrabel mentioned on Monday that Maye being available coming out of the Patriots’ upcoming bye was not expected. That statement plus Byard’s and the reports available start painting a clear picture: anything but the 24-year-old missing the remainder of the 2026 season would be a positive surprise. If that is indeed the case, Tommy DeVito is expected to take over as New England’s starting quarterback. For Byard, the backup quarterback will not be the only one in the spotlight, though. “The reality of the situation is that we have to get behind ‘Tommy Two Chains’ at the end of the day,” he pointed out. “We’re all going to have to do more, myself included. Everybody has to play better around our quarterback. This is honestly before Drake was injured, but we have to play better around our quarterback. We have two choices: we can rally behind this guy or we can pack it up. This is just where we are right now in the season.” Coming off back-to-back blowout losses, the Patriots are entering their Week 11 bye with a 5-5 record and on the outside looking into the AFC playoff picture .

title: Patriots vs. Lions snap counts from Week 10

full_text: Halfway through the 2026 season, the New England Patriots’ trade for wide receiver A.J. Brown is not looking good. The 29-year-old has appeared in only four games so far, catching just 11 passes for 128 yards. Injuries have been the main reason for his lack of production, with ankle and knee issues seemingly derailing any momentum he had built during training camp. On Sunday against the Detroit Lions, he picked up another ailment: Brown left the game in the late third quarter because of a hamstring injury and did not return. On the day, he therefore played only 28 of 59 snaps (47%) and registered two receptions for 27 combined yards. It was the latest in a string of disappointing outings for a player acquired from the Philadelphia Eagles for two draft picks, including a first-round selection in 2028. “I thought he had a good week of practice. He was into it. I think he had a drop and then came back and made a big catch for us there, and unfortunately wasn’t able to finish the game,” said head coach Mike Vrabel about Brown on WEEI’s The Greg Hill Show on Monday. “A.J. had a good week of practice, was excited about trying to help us win. We knew that he was going to be on a limited basis, wasn’t going to take 95% of the reps. I thought we were headed in the right direction there, but unfortunately we’ll have to see how he comes out here in the next couple days.” Here is our full snap count report from the Patriots’ 35-10 loss . Offense Total snaps: 59 | Time on the field: 25:30 | * denotes starter LG/C Greg Van Roten* (59; 100%), RG Matt Pryor* (59; 100%), WR Mack Hollins* (54; 92%), C Jared Wilson* (53; 90%), LT Will Campbell* (53; 90%), QB Tommy DeVito (49; 83%), RT Morgan Moses* (45; 76%), WR DeMario Douglas (38; 64%), TE Eli Raridon* (37; 63%), TE Hunter Henry* (33; 56%), WR A.J. Brown* (28; 47%), RB Rhamondre Stevenson* (26; 44%), RB Corey Kiner (25; 42%), WR Kyle Williams (23; 39%), RT/FB Caleb Lomu (15; 25%), FB Reggie Gilliam (13; 22%), QB Drake Maye* (10; 17%), RB Lan Larison (8; 14%), WR Efton Chism III (8; 14%), LT Marcus Bryant (6; 10%), LG Andrew Rupcich (6; 10%), TE Cameron Latu (1; 2%) The Patriots offense saw the entire game and season changed after one drive. Starting quarterback Drake Maye hurt his ankle on a third-down sack, with initial reports indicating a fracture that likely would end up sidelining him for the rest of the season. On Sunday, this meant Tommy DeVito entering the game in his place and trying to build on the success the offense has had on its opening series. He couldn’t: the Patriots ended up scoring only once in 10 competitive drives with him at the helm, while Detroit pulled away further and further. The time on the field is a reflection of New England’s offensive ineptitude, and it ultimately led to the team mixing and matching its personnel. Backups such as Lan Larison, Marcus Bryant and Andrew Rupcich saw increased opportunities with the score getting out of hand. That said, there are still a few notable takeaways from the game. The Patriots opted to insert Greg Van Roten at left guard in his first game back from a stint on injured reserve, despite him having played only one in-game snap at the position in the previous six seasons. Van Roten also served as the backup center, snapping to DeVito during warmups and moving there when the O-line rotation started. Rhamondre Stevenson, who had suffered a knee injury the previous week versus the Packers, played 26 snaps in a clearly reduced role. The game script likely also contributed to his usage, same with tight end Hunter Henry. However, he might as well have been: one week after playing a season-low 39% of snaps, he was on the field for only 31% against the Lions. Five other interior lineman surpassed his snap total of 22. Even considering how the game went and the fact that the Patriots are using him as a package player first and foremost, that number is surprisingly low. At this point in time, it appears that Milton Williams and Cory Durden are the clear 1-2 at the position. That said, Sunday’s game showed that the group as a whole needs improvements at the position: Detroit ran over New England at will, in large part because of its ability to reset the line of scrimmage. Speaking of low snap totals, Robert Spillane finished with a 68% playing time share. The team captain, who typically plays close to 100% of snaps any given week was banged up late in the first half and later exited the contest due to an illness. In his place, Darius Muasau took over as the top off-ball linebacker and on-field signal caller wearing the green dot on his helmet. His 23 snaps (32%) are a new season-high. As was the case on offense, the Patriots also managed to give their lesser-used personnel some opportunities on Sunday. Karon Prunty and Channing Canada replaced Christian Gonzalez and Marcus Jones late in the game, while Mike Brown entered the field in place of Kevin Byard. title: Our Offense vs. Their Defense: Chicago Bears
summary: The New Orleans Saints take their offense and all of its issues on the road this week to play against one of the best defenses in the league in the Chicago Bears. This is an opportunity for the Saints to show signs of improvement, as the history of this current staff, the offensive pitfalls, and […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - NOVEMBER 15: Jordyn Tyson #0 of the New Orleans Saints runs after a catch against the Carolina Panthers during the first half of a game at Caesars Superdome on November 15, 2026, in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New Orleans Saints take their offense and all of its issues on the road this week to play against one of the best defenses in the league in the Chicago Bears. This is an opportunity for the Saints to show signs of improvement, as the history of this current staff, the offensive pitfalls, and roster mismanagement are now telling a story of what can be expected when the Saints’ offensive unit takes the field. This team is starting to become a team that has to be something it is not. The goodwill and grace that were given to this team by so many are all but lost at this point in the 2026 campaign. This Saints offense is now what it is, and it is bad. The play designs, play-calling, and personnel usage all deserve to be questioned, so it is understandable that the Saints are 10-point road underdogs. The Bears’ defense held the Saints to only 14 points last year in what was former Saints head coach Dennis Allen’s first season as the Bears’ defensive coordinator. This year, he will be leading a top-10 defense in the NFL, as the Bears are currently ranked 7th in total defense, allowing only 310.9 yards per game. They are also allowing only 91.1 yards per game on the ground and 219.8 yards per game through the air, ranking 7th and 11th, respectively. They can affect the passer in multiple ways, as the Bears are currently tied for 11th in interceptions with 7 and tied for 9th in sacks with 26. Their 13 takeaways on the season have them ranked 10th in the league. They lead the league in third-down defense, allowing opponents to convert only 22.8% of their attempts, and they allow touchdowns on only 53.8% of red-zone trips, which ranks 12th. The Bears’ defensive front is a monster. It features Montez Sweat, Austin Booker, Dayo Odeyingbo, and the recently acquired Jeffery Simmons, who is probably the best interior defensive lineman in the league right now. Simmons has 6 sacks so far this season, and he’s now playing alongside a pass rush that features three different rushers with at least 3 sacks. The linebacker group is very talented as well, especially with Devin Bush leading the way. He currently has 53 tackles and 2 sacks on the season. The secondary is not one to play around with, either. Jaylon Johnson, Kyler Gordon, and rookie safety Dillon Thieneman are playing at very high levels right now. Gordon is playing that nickel/slot corner role that Dennis Allen loves to utilize so much, and he’s playing it at an elite level. Gordon has recorded 4 sacks in 4 games, as well as 5 TFLs, so the Saints can expect pressure off the edge. This matchup will present a very difficult challenge for this Saints offense. Morale is a little low around this team, and they just don’t seem to have any answers. In this game, the Saints will have to become something they have not been in quite some time, and that is an actual functioning offense that can play complementary football. The Saints should be more aggressive in the intermediate passing game. The Bears are allowing 8.2 yards per attempt and 13.2 yards per completion. The Saints are currently averaging 6.3 yards per attempt and 9.5 yards per completion. The Saints will have to continue playing well on third downs because, as previously mentioned, the Bears are the best in the league at getting teams off the field on third downs. Finally, the Saints will have to find a way to score in the first quarter. The Bears are a team that plays a time-of-possession style of football. When they get the ball, they like to keep it, so that means the Saints have to capitalize on every possession, especially in the first quarter. Force an offense that wants to play slowly out of its comfort zone. The Bears are averaging 34:31 in time of possession, which leads the league. That plays back into the defense’s ability to get off the field on third downs. In this game, the Saints should not play into the Bears’ hands offensively by playing their style of football. The issue with that, however, is that it’s the only way this Saints offense knows how to play right now. The Bears can be beaten, but the Saints will have to find their groove and be balanced on offense to do it. What are your thoughts on this Saints offense going up against this Bears defense and do you think the Saints can score in the first quarter? .
