title: Nick Bosa concedes he’s been struggling to execute his calling card
summary: Throughout his career, Nick Bosa has enjoyed huge success rushing the passer in a very obvious and relatively simplistic fashion. But, after going another game without a sack in the 49ers’ shootout win over the Dallas Cowboys last Sunday, Bosa conceded he has been struggling to execute parts of his game that have been his […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - NOVEMBER 15: Nick Bosa #97 of the San Francisco 49ers rushes the passer during an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Throughout his career, Nick Bosa has enjoyed huge success rushing the passer in a very obvious and relatively simplistic fashion. But, after going another game without a sack in the 49ers’ shootout win over the Dallas Cowboys last Sunday, Bosa conceded he has been struggling to execute parts of his game that have been his calling cards in previous years. Bosa has long since been known as one of the game’s premier power rushers, with the former Defensive Player of the Year winning primarily by translating his speed off the ball into sheer brute force. But the devastation he can often cause has been largely conspicuous by its absence since he returned from a calf injury in Week 9, with Bosa still without sack in four games this season. And, speaking to the media on Wednesday, Bosa acknowledged that issues with his get-off have played a part in his failure to bring down opposing quarterbacks so far this season. Bosa said of his adjustment to Raheem Morris’ defense: “I think there’s a learning curve and … a lot of guys haven’t had many reps in the scheme so far. I’m trying to break it down to the basics and just kind of get back. I missed a year and then missed camp. I kind of took for granted some of the things that I did automatically, and I thought I could just kind of coast and continue to do those things automatically and focus on other things. But I need to, especially with a newer defense, really hone in on the things that made me the player that I am.” Asked what he took for granted, Bosa replied: “Just getting down, getting my feet set, and getting off the ball. “It takes time. I’m not going to make excuses because nobody really cares. And but I’m going to get better. And I’m pretty confident in that physically and how I’m playing.” To his credit, Bosa delivered a reminder of what can happen when he gets it right as a pass rusher against Dallas when a superb bull rush against Terence Steele forced a rushed throw from Dak Prescott that should have been intercepted by Dre Greenlaw. The 49ers need those kind of impactful rushes on a more consistent basis from their best pass rusher, though the level of attention he draws in terms of double teams and chips has played a role in negating his influence. Bosa, though, is used to that kind of treatment and will need to find a way to overcome it if the 49er pass rush is to improve down the stretch. There may be external concern surrounding Bosa’s lack of production, but nobody can doubt he is in the right mindset as he looks to reprise the form that made him one of the NFL’s most feared pass rushers.

title: 49ers News: The team seems to have a good attitude about attitude
summary: Elevation gain? 49ers hope for an edge vs. Vikings in Mexico City by getting expletives out early (paywall)“After arriving in Colorado Springs on Sunday night, the 49ers will spend a week in a high-elevation environment, which Fibel said is when the “partial benefits” of altitude acclimatization can start to be realized. Before kickoff, the 49ers […]
full_text: MEXICO CITY, MEXICO - NOVEMBER 21: George Kittle #85 of the San Francisco 49ers reacts after scoring a touchdown during the second half of a game against the Arizona Cardinals at Estadio Azteca on November 21, 2022 in Mexico City, Mexico. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images Elevation gain? 49ers hope for an edge vs. Vikings in Mexico City by getting expletives out early (paywall) “After arriving in Colorado Springs on Sunday night, the 49ers will spend a week in a high-elevation environment, which Fibel said is when the “partial benefits” of altitude acclimatization can start to be realized. Before kickoff, the 49ers will get through a rough stretch that often occurs during days 2 to 4 after arriving at a high altitude in which sleep is disrupted and fatigue and dehydration risk are common. “By game time they will have had a chance to partly acclimate where they’re not going to have as much as those deficits,” said Fibel, who works at Cedars-Sinai Orthopaedics and Sports Medicine in Los Angeles. “Their sleep is more regulated and they’re more adjusted to the decreased oxygen that’s available as they’re competing.” The Vikings will arrive Saturday — avoiding the negative delayed effects — after their extended elevation-room work at the team facility. Fibel noted elevation sessions can start to increase the body’s ability to produce red blood cells, which can help transport oxygen. “That can take several weeks to start happening,” Fibel said. “So their approach gives them some of the benefits of the exposure to high altitude.” Fibel declined to say which approach he’d choose if he was running an NFL team, terming it a “challenging question” due to a variety of factors. For example, the Vikings will maintain their weekly routine by staying home while the 49ers are displaced during a nine-day trip that began Saturday in Dallas. However, the 49ers’ weeklong exposure to high elevation could be more beneficial than the Vikings’ multi-week elevation-room sessions.” Where the 49ers’ biggest defensive concern is heading into the second half “The Raiders were 6-for-10 on late downs. They converted five in a row before the final two opportunities. The defense forced Dallas into an absurd number of late-down attempts —21, to be specific. You’d like to think that forcing 21 late-down attempts means you’re doing something right defensively. However, only six of those were six yards and longer. The Niners allowed a 3-for-6 conversion rate on those, but one of those was converted on 4th & 1. It’s difficult to generate a pass rush in shorter yardage situations, since the quarterback can throw the ball quickly. You’re putting more pressure on your coverage units. And, as we know, that is not a strong suit for the Niners….Morris had his work cut out for him heading into 2026. So far, he’s done a good job of limiting the damage. The Niners have traded field goals for touchdowns. With their offense, it’s a prudent approach. They’re 11th in red zone scoring. But as the schedule stiffens and offenses improve, we’re starting to see cracks in the defense, enough that it’s a concern as we head into the second half. It seems like the root of it all is failing to get off the field on late downs.” Kyle Shanahan shares 49ers injury updates and previews Vikings matchup “They’ve been good. We haven’t been around the players much. They were away from us Monday and Tuesday after we reviewed the game from Dallas on Monday. Coaches, we’ve kind of just been in our hotel rooms and our offices just working, but I definitely am out of breath a little bit right now walking over here. Everyone does feel it just like you always do when you come to Colorado, but it’ll be good to get out on the field today, get in the sun and get to work.” Kawakami Mailbag: Warriors emergency! Answers that might get fans mad! (Paywall) “Sacks sometimes happen in random and mysterious ways and right now none of them are happening for Bosa, who still is sitting on zero sacks this season (in four games) and went offside twice on Sunday. I think it’s fair to say that the 49ers need more from him, especially if they’re not getting much from anybody rushing from the opposite side. But Bosa had four quarterback pressures on Sunday; sacks are likely coming. He also is coming off of the third ACL surgery of his career. Who knows what physical percentage Bosa’s playing at now? Maybe he won’t come close to winning another Defensive Player of the Year or even get to double-digit sacks again, but I learned long ago that you can’t measure a pass rusher by a handful of games against offenses that are concentrating on making sure he doesn’t wreck things.”

title: 3 things to watch on Sunday: The Vikings’ defense can be beaten on the ground
summary: The San Francisco 49ers and Minnesota Vikings will do battle on Sunday Night Football in Mexico City, with both teams fighting for the number one seed in the NFC. The 49ers are looking to snap their dry spell against the Vikings and Brian Flores-led defenses. The marquee matchup is Kyle Shanahan against Flores. Mike Evans […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers and Minnesota Vikings will do battle on Sunday Night Football in Mexico City, with both teams fighting for the number one seed in the NFC. The 49ers are looking to snap their dry spell against the Vikings and Brian Flores-led defenses. The marquee matchup is Kyle Shanahan against Flores. Mike Evans could return on Sunday, and the addition of Keenan Allen helps the offense and Brock Purdy, who will have to contend with Flores’ aggressive and complex defensive plans. Here are three things to watch for on Sunday: The Vikings’ run defense Minnesota’s defense is number one in many metrics. However, Buffalo may have laid out a blueprint for wearing the defense down. Yes, it is true that the defense was on the field too much with their sputtering offense, and Kirk Cousins was brought back to fix that issue, but the 49ers’ defense could be the key to getting the Vikings’ defense into vulnerable spots. The Vikings are 18th in the NFL and tied with the New England Patriots and Philadelphia Eagles with 27 ten-plus-yard runs allowed. While the defense has only allowed five rushing touchdowns, the key for the 49ers will be running the football and keeping the defense honest. A heavy dose of Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black should be the plan. The 49ers run defense On the flip side, forcing the Vikings to become one-dimensional on offense stands to benefit Raheem Morris and the 49ers’ defense. The 49ers have allowed four rushing touchdowns and FIVE ten-plus-yard runs. Being tied for first in the NFL with Jacksonville and Tampa Bay with an EPA/rush allowed of -0.14, is extremely impressive. Cousins is an obvious upgrade over Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz, but forcing him to throw the football more will lead to opportunities to take the football away. If the 49ers have their hands full against Flores and the defense, turnovers can tip the scales back to San Francisco. Deciphering Flores’ coverages While the Vikings blitz at nearly 70% of snaps, the coverages behind them aren’t man looks. The 49ers will likely not have Purdy turn his back to the defense because of the disguises and how quickly the looks change. Minnesota plays zone on 84.4% of snaps and two-high safeties on 68.2% of snaps. This is where the experience of Evans and Allen is important. Both veterans will know where to sit their routes down for Purdy. It’s fair to expect a ton of straight dropbacks for Purdy, and from under center, the 49ers are under center at the third-highest rate of 52.6%,
author: Jason Aponte

title: Where the 49ers’ biggest defensive concern is heading into the second half
summary: The San Francisco 49ers have been surprisingly effective on defense this season. They’ve gone out of their way to take away the big play through the air and stop the run. That formula has made them ninth in EPA per play and second in rushing EPA. On early downs, Raheem Morris’s unit has been excellent […]
full_text: (Photo by Brian Rothmuller/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers have been surprisingly effective on defense this season. They’ve gone out of their way to take away the big play through the air and stop the run. That formula has made them ninth in EPA per play and second in rushing EPA. On early downs, Raheem Morris’s unit has been excellent during the past three games. They’re fifth in EPA per play and 10th in rushing success rate. But they have not gotten off the field on late downs. The Niners are 31st — only the Raiders are worse — in EPA per play and success rate on late downs. Their struggles through the air are concerning: they rank 30th in dropback EPA and 29th in dropback success rate. The pass isn’t the only issue. The 49ers rank 30th in rushing EPA and dead last in rushing success rate on late downs, allowing 80% of the runs they face to succeed. The Raiders were 6-for-10 on late downs. They converted five in a row before the final two opportunities. The defense forced Dallas into an absurd number of late-down attempts —21, to be specific. You’d like to think that forcing 21 late-down attempts means you’re doing something right defensively. However, only six of those were six yards and longer. The Niners allowed a 3-for-6 conversion rate on those, but one of those was converted on 4th & 1. It’s difficult to generate a pass rush in shorter yardage situations, since the quarterback can throw the ball quickly. You’re putting more pressure on your coverage units. And, as we know, that is not a strong suit for the Niners. The 49ers are facing 13.22 third-down attempts per game, good for 21st in the league. The defense faces only 10.7 drives per game, the third-lowest in the league. This season, they benefited from not being on the field. But there’s noise in the numbers. The 49ers are 23rd in points per drive. Opposing offenses score on 41.5% of their drives, which ranks 24th. Morris had his work cut out for him heading into 2026. So far, he’s done a good job of limiting the damage. The Niners have traded field goals for touchdowns. With their offense, it’s a prudent approach. They’re 11th in red zone scoring. But as the schedule stiffens and offenses improve, we’re starting to see cracks in the defense, enough that it’s a concern as we head into the second half. It seems like the root of it all is failing to get off the field on late downs.

Kyle Shanahan said, “I’m definitely out of breath a little walking over here. Everybody feels it when you come to Colorado.” It’s a windy day. But Shanahan said “hopefully” both can practice on Thursday. Mike Evans sighting in Colorado…. pic.twitter.com/yj5KrAiwba — Matt Barrows (@mattbarrows) November 18, 2026 Evans last suited up on October 19. He’s still in the NFL’s top five in EPA per target. Evans was one of the league’s most valuable wideouts. If Evans returns, another receiver will be inactive. Last week, it was Brandin Cooks, with Keenan Allen in the fold. Shanahan said, “I expect Keenan to be a part of our plan every week.” It could be Jacob Cowing this week, although the Niners would need another punt returner. Cowing has had his fair share of adventures returning this year. Shanahan said he remains confident in Cowing: “I’m confident in Jake, especially in his return abilities. I don’t think we’ve got a ton of good looks. Haven’t got a lot of returns. I know our numbers are very bad in that area. But Jake has the ability to be a very good punt returner. I hope he keeps getting more confident and consistent at catching the ball. And I hope we get better at blocking and get so more opportunities, because Jake can make plays. Hasn’t gotten that on a punt return yet. But it’s something that I know he can do.” Evans, Allen, Watkins, and Robinson could make up the receiver room, but if the Niners have the bodies elsewhere, they’ll have a sixth receiver active in Cowing. These players will be limited Wednesday: CB Upton Stout (shoulder/neck) DE Khalid Kareem (ankle) S Siran Neal (knee/foot) S Ji’Ayir Brown (ankle) We’ll see if an injury to Brown impacts the safety rotation.

title: The Matador and the Magic King: How the 49ers can beat the most aggressive defense football has ever seen
summary: México City is home to the world’s largest bullring. On Jan. 7, 2007, Plaza México booked a 54-year-old baker’s son, Rodolfo Rodríguez, as a favor. They called it his farewell. “El Pana” showed up in a horse-drawn carriage, a cigar in his teeth, and a pink suit of lights that had seen better decades. His […]
full_text: (Photo by Adam Bettcher/Getty Images) México City is home to the world’s largest bullring. On Jan. 7, 2007, Plaza México booked a 54-year-old baker’s son, Rodolfo Rodríguez, as a favor. They called it his farewell. “El Pana” showed up in a horse-drawn carriage, a cigar in his teeth, and a pink suit of lights that had seen better decades. His bull was named Rey Mago—the Magic King. Rey Mago did what every fighting bull does. It erupted into the ring, head low, hooves digging, bred for one thing and never once asked to be gentle. And that’s exactly why it lost. Because a matador doesn’t fight the bull; he follows three words as old as the ring itself: parar, Templar mandar . Stand still. Match the charge. Command it. Hold your ground while the horns come. Slow the charge to your rhythm with the cape. Then send it exactly where you want it to go. Every whiff drains a little more of the fury. The bull never notices. The crowd does. And most importantly, the matador does. El Pana never beat Rey Mago with the sword. He beat it with the cape. By nightfall, México City wasn’t calling it a farewell. They called it his Resurrection Sunday. Sunday night, the 49ers walk into that same city to face a new Magic King. Brian Flores’ bull is real. Minnesota’s front five weigh 1,391 pounds combined, about what a full-grown fighting bull weighs. And no defense in football has ever charged like this one: 72.5% of the time, per Next Gen Stats. Before this season, the record was 51.5%. But like any good magic trick, it’s built on getting you to watch the wrong hand. The big fellas inside aren’t the ones getting home. Minnesota’s interior linemen have combined to create pressure on just 6.4% of their rushes this season, per Sports Info Solutions, below the league average for a defensive tackle. Their best, Jalen Redmond, has 19 pressures on 257 rushes. Blake Cashman, a linebacker, has 24 on 88. That’s the trick. The danger is in the horns: Dallas Turner off the edge and Cashman walking up over the guards. And most of the time it’s five rushers, not six, with zone coverage sitting behind them. The Magic King doesn’t need everybody to come. He needs you to think everybody’s coming. The bull is young. The matador is not. The 49ers came into the year with one of the oldest rosters in the league, and Trent Williams, at 38, will spend Sunday night staring at a 23-year-old pass rusher. So the old matador goes back to the three words. Parar: Stand Still The young matador’s instinct is to drift back when the horns come. The old ones plant their feet. Offensive linemen have their own version of that. It’s called a jump set: instead of backing up and waiting for the rush, you meet the defender at the line, get your hands on him first and take away the runway before the charge ever builds. A blitzer who gets punched in the chest at the line of scrimmage can’t get where he’s going. This group has shown it can stand its ground. In Melbourne, Trent saw Myles Garrett one-on-one 11 times and gave up one pressure. And Brock Purdy doesn’t flinch either. When he’s been blitzed this year, he’s averaging 12.1 yards a throw with 12 touchdowns and two picks. Charging Brock Purdy has been an expensive habit. The horns are still real, and they’ll go looking for the youngest feet. Connor Colby has had his rough days, but almost all of them came against elite interior guys like Dallas’ Quinnen Williams, a technician you just can’t jump. Minnesota’s tackles aren’t that. Let Colby meet them at the line. The real question is whether Flores sends Blake Cashman right at him. If he does, Jake Brendel has to be the one sliding over to help, with Trent left alone on Turner. And if Cashman still gets through, the 49ers have a running back who ran into Quinnen Williams so hard on a bootleg that Williams left the game. An old matador can’t stand still for the young ones. But he can teach them where to plant their feet. Templar: Match The Charge Templar is the art of the cape, slowing the bull down to your rhythm until the charge belongs to you. For the 49ers, that’s the run game, and it’s where this whole line gets to go forward. Dominick Puni has the fewest blown run blocks of any 49ers lineman this season. Colton McKivitz is right behind him. Even Colby, a better run blocker than pass blocker, gets to go downhill and be himself. And it shows up every week. The 49ers are averaging 4.9 yards a carry this season against defenses that normally give up about 4.3. They’ve run better than a defense usually allows in six of nine games, including against the two best run defenses on the schedule, Seattle and the Rams. The other half of Templaris patience. In Dallas, the 49ers spent the first half dropping back and getting hit, five sacks on the night and a little bit of everything breaking down, and went into the locker room barely ahead. Shanahan didn’t panic. He stuck with the cape. In the second half, they ran it right at the Cowboys for 169 yards and scored 29 points. Minnesota’s bull charges upfield, and Turner rushes the passer on almost every passing down. Let him. Let him spend his fury on air while the ball goes through the space he just left. Teams that have shown that patience have made this defense sweat. Jonathan Taylor ran for 95 on them. Miami’s Ollie Gordon ripped off 86 yards on seven carries before the Dolphins apparently forgot he was on the roster. And when opponents run it 30 or more times, the Vikings are 2-2 and score 11.5 points a game. When they don’t, Minnesota is 5-0 and scores 26. Now, those were the old Vikings. Kirk Cousins is back, and he threw two touchdowns in his first game back. But Cousins doesn’t play defense. He doesn’t play running back, either. Minnesota has run for four touchdowns all season. He didn’t change the bull the 49ers have to face, only what’s at stake if they don’t tame it. Before, running the ball was how you beat this defense. Now it’s also how you keep Cousins and Justin Jefferson sitting on a bench in México City. Every carry drains a little more. The bull never notices. The crowd does. And the old matador knows exactly how many passes he has left. Mandar: Command It Mandar is what makes a matador a legend. Once the bull is held and slowed, he stops reacting and starts sending the charge exactly where he wants it. A bull charges what moves, and no offense in the NFL moves more before the snap than the 49ers. Motion is the flick of the cape. It makes the Magic King show his hand early. And when Purdy lines up under center, where Minnesota blitzes almost 90% of the time, the 49ers know exactly where the charge is headed. So send it somewhere, and go where it isn’t. When the rushers leave, they leave a hole in the zone behind them. That’s Christian McCaffrey’s grass. When Flores sends six or more, half of the big completions against him this year have gone to tight ends, and I don’t have to tell you who the 49ers’ tight end is. And then there’s Keenan Allen, 34, who has spent a career sitting down in the exact spot the blitzer just left and turning around to wave. A veteran who knows exactly where the bull just was? That’s the most matador thing on this roster. Minnesota’s corners are a different story. They haven’t allowed a touchdown all year. You don’t wave the cape in front of those horns. Unless Mike Evans is back, he hasn’t played since Oct. 19, and Kyle Shanahan is only “hoping” to get him on the practice field this week. But if he makes the trip, he’s the one guy you can throw to while the horns are still coming, and every safety Flores keeps back for him is one less body in the charge. The Bull’s Safe Spot Every bull has a querencia , the place in the ring where it feels strongest. Minnesota’s is third-and-long. Get there against a six-man rush, and you’re basically punting with extra steps. The matador’s job is to never let the bull get home: stay on schedule, keep it in the middle of the ring, and make it chase. They say a bull is never fought twice,…

title: Is this Kyle Shanahan’s best offense with the 49ers?
summary: Following a 46-point performance against the Dallas Cowboys, the San Francisco 49ers are 8-1 with the best record in the NFC halfway through the season. On Sunday, they weathered a rough defensive performance, responding every time with their offense to win a crucial game, as Brock Purdy had 389 yards and three touchdowns. San Francisco’s […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 15: George Kittle #85 of the San Francisco 49ers walks off the field after the game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images Following a 46-point performance against the Dallas Cowboys, the San Francisco 49ers are 8-1 with the best record in the NFC halfway through the season. On Sunday, they weathered a rough defensive performance, responding every time with their offense to win a crucial game, as Brock Purdy had 389 yards and three touchdowns. San Francisco’s offense has become hyper-efficient this year, as Purdy has enjoyed an MVP-caliber season, while the run game ranks in the top five in success rate and EPA per rush. This is the best quarterback play that Kyle Shanahan has had with the 49ers. He also might have his best true receiver since Julio Jones with Mike Evans (although 2021 Deebo Samuel and 2023 Brandon Aiyuk are both strong contenders). And the 49ers run game has returned to being efficient after an up-and-down 2025 season. Currently, the 49ers rank first in the NFL in yards per game and second in points per game. They’re balanced. They’re elite in the red zone. They’re first in the NFL in third-down conversion rate. Whatever the metric is, the 49ers offense seems to be near the top of the NFL this season. So, it’s a fair question to ask: is this Kyle Shanahan’s best offense with the 49ers? San Francisco just added another piece to the fold this past week, as Keenan Allen posted five catches for 61 yards in his 49ers debut. Now, on paper, the skill position group may not be as elite as the Brandon Aiyuk, Deebo Samuel, Jauan Jennings, George Kittle, and Christian McCaffrey group. But the 49ers have an elite WR1 in Mike Evans, quality complementary options with Deebo Samuel, Keenan Allen, and (eventually) De’Zhaun Stribling, and Kittle and McCaffrey still in the fold. Their banged-up group still posted nearly 500 yards of offense on Sunday against the Dallas Cowboys, and Kittle has high hopes for the rest of the season. “When you add Mike Evans to [our current offense], I’ve actually never been more confident in an offense,” the star tight end said on Sunday. And it’s a fair assessment. The 49ers have a go-to receiver. They have strong yards-after-the-catch weapons with Samuel, Kittle, and McCaffrey. They just added a very good separator with Keenan Allen. And they have a quality offensive line that has been a good unit in both pass protection and run blocking. Now, the one true knock is age. All of the 49ers top weapons are 30+ years old, and we’ve already seen the injury bug hit this season. But fully healthy? This very well could be Kyle Shanahan’s best offense as the 49ers head coach. The last moving part is Shanahan himself. He’s put himself firmly in the Coach of the Year mix and just continues to elevate as a playcaller and play designer. The biggest test of the season comes next weekend against the formidable Minnesota Vikings defense. If San Francisco is able to even thwart Brian Flores’s elite group, then there’s no doubt this is an offense to be reckoned with this season.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

title: How ‘backyard football’ play style has contributed to Brock Purdy’s MVP like campaign
summary: It’s no secret that San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy is enjoying the best season of his career this year, as he’s been considered in the MVP conversation once again amongst several elite quarterbacks in the NFL. Thus far, Purdy has thrown for 2,369 yards, 20 touchdowns, and five interceptions, while completing a career-high 70.1 […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 15: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers looks to pass during the second half against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s no secret that San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy is enjoying the best season of his career this year, as he’s been considered in the MVP conversation once again amongst several elite quarterbacks in the NFL. Thus far, Purdy has thrown for 2,369 yards, 20 touchdowns, and five interceptions, while completing a career-high 70.1 percent of his passes. The yards per attempt (9.0) remains high, while his QBR (81.3) ranks second in the NFL. Purdy had one of his best games of the season in San Francisco’s thriller victory this past weekend, completing 22 of 28 passes for 389 yards and three touchdowns. It was a big improvisational day, as Purdy was able to extend plays and make key throws on his feet, with the most impressive being one of Christian McCaffrey’s long catch-and-run touchdowns after Purdy created time rolling to his right. “I’m always trying to keep my eyes down the field when I’m scrambling and stuff, and seeing if guys can feel me and see me, and try to get to space,” Purdy said of the play. “But then there’s a point where it’s like, ‘All right, I think I can try to go use my legs now in this moment.’ And I was going to do that, and then all of a sudden, I just felt Christian pop. So I stopped and gave him the ball, and I was probably right at the line of scrimmage, so it was pretty close.” Well, McCaffrey attributed it to ‘backyard football’, which kind of feels exactly how Purdy has played at several times this year. “It really is backyard football at that point,” the star running back added said. “I think we’ve all played it as kids at recess when you’re drawing up plays on your hand and then it never happens. You ever tell a five-year-old to run like a post route, and he just runs a corner or something else, but he’s open? That was kind of what that was. And again, I think those little decisions that you make in games for Brock to not scramble, not to just surrender the play, but to keep it alive, that’s a big deal. So there’s no planning that goes into that. It’s just him doing a great job playing ball.” Purdy has made a number of impressive improvisational plays that show off both his IQ and playmaking ability, adding yet another layer to a 49ers offense that has already been clicking on all cylinders. It’s not just that Purdy is making these ‘backyard football’ type of throws; he’s doing so consistently while keeping the ball out of harm’s way and playing with a changing set of pass-catchers. It feels like the final piece of the puzzle, making him a truly complete quarterback, which has now shown up on film all year long. We’ve seen other MVP candidates like Josh Allen, Patrick Mahomes, and even Joe Burrow at times make the backyard football-like plays to extend drives for their teams. Purdy has started to ascend into that group this year with a variety of plays that should keep him in the MVP discussion if he keeps up his current style of play.

title: Buccaneers at Lions: Initial injury report for Week 11
summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers returned from their bye week and began preparations for their Week 11 matchup against the Detroit Lions on Wednesday, with much of the attention surrounding the health of quarterback Baker Mayfield. Tampa Bay listed six players on its initial injury report, including two who did not participate in practice. Mayfield (foot/right thumb) […]
full_text: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers returned from their bye week and began preparations for their Week 11 matchup against the Detroit Lions on Wednesday, with much of the attention surrounding the health of quarterback Baker Mayfield. Tampa Bay listed six players on its initial injury report , including two who did not participate in practice. Mayfield (foot/right thumb) was held out of Wednesday’s session after suffering an injury to his foot and ankle area during the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Chicago Bears. The veteran quarterback had reportedly been wearing a walking boot periodically throughout the bye week but was seen without one Wednesday while observing practice in street clothes. Head coach Todd Bowles offered somewhat encouraging news regarding Mayfield’s recovery, saying the quarterback has made progress and is doing considerably better than he was a week ago. However, as reported by Buccaneers senior writer Scott Smith , the team will wait until Friday to make a determination on his availability against Detroit. Rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels took first-team reps Wednesday and would once again be called upon should Mayfield be unable to play. The Buccaneers also promoted quarterback Easton Stick to the active roster earlier this week and signed veteran Cooper Rush to their practice squad. Aside from Mayfield, safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (ankle) was the only other Buccaneer held out of practice Wednesday. Outside linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee), who missed Tampa Bay’s game against Chicago, was a limited participant. Cornerback Josh Hayes (knee), tight end Cade Otton (thumb) and left tackle Tristan Wirfs (toe) participated fully. Hayes returned to practice Wednesday, opening his 21-day activation window from injured reserve. For Detroit, center Cade Mays (ankle) was the only player listed as a non-participant. Cornerbacks D.J. Reed (hip) and Ennis Rakestraw Jr. (shoulder) were among six players listed as limited, while safety Kerby Joseph (knee) was listed as a full participant. The Lions conducted a walkthrough Wednesday, meaning their participation designations were estimates. All eyes will remain on Mayfield throughout the remainder of the week as the Buccaneers look to avoid playing without their starting quarterback for the fourth time this season. The Buccaneers and Lions are scheduled to kick off Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET on CBS.

title: The Titans need more from 3 defenders vs. Cowboys in Week 11
summary: The Tennessee Titans defense has fallen apart since trading Jeffery Simmons and Amani Hooker. Over the previous three losses to the Browns, Bengals, and Jaguars, they’ve allowed an average of 36.6 points and 486.6 yards per game. Robert Saleh’s unit doesn’t have enough talent, and has also struggled to acclimate to his scheme. The Dallas […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - NOVEMBER 15: Jakobi Meyers #3 of the Jacksonville Jaguars is tackled by Alontae Taylor #24 and Isaiah Oliver #28 of the Tennessee Titans during the first half of the game at Nissan Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tennessee Titans defense has fallen apart since trading Jeffery Simmons and Amani Hooker. Over the previous three losses to the Browns, Bengals, and Jaguars, they’ve allowed an average of 36.6 points and 486.6 yards per game. Robert Saleh’s unit doesn’t have enough talent, and has also struggled to acclimate to his scheme. The Dallas Cowboys represent a terrific challenge in Week 11 . They are averaging an explosive 32.3 points per game across that same Titans sample size. We’ve identified three Titans defenders who need to play significantly better versus the Cowboys. CB Alontae Taylor We’re not convinced Alontae Taylor shouldn’t be benched versus the Cowboys. If he plays nickelback over Marcus Harris again, he needs to be significantly better than he was against the Jaguars. PFF credited Taylor with allowing seven receptions (via seven targets) in coverage for 143 yards. He was a total turnstile in coverage. The Cowboys’ high-octane passing attack will target him if Coach Saleh leaves him in the lineup. DT John Franklin-Myers The Jeffery Simmons trade placed an even bigger spotlight on John Franklin-Myers, who Coach Saleh reiterates is playing through a difficult back injury. The Titans signed JFM to a $63 million contract in the offseason and they need more production than they’ve gotten. He’s been credited with 17 pressures and two sacks this season. Making Cowboys QB Dak Prescott uncomfortable in the pocket will be critical. S Kevin Winston Jr. There was a generous amount of offseason hype surrounding safety Kevin Winston Jr. Thus far, he’s performing like a league-average starter. That doesn’t make the former Penn State standout a Mike Borgonzi bust, but we all assumed he’d show more playmaking ability. That hasn’t been the case. Winston hasn’t registered a single interception or pass breakup, nor has he recorded a sack. There’s a bigger spotlight on No. 23 following the Amani Hooker trade.

title: Carnell Tate injury update: Titans rookie WR will practice today
summary: Carnell Tate has missed the Tennessee Titans’ last two games with a shoulder injury he suffered in the loss to the Cleveland Browns. Robert Saleh said today that the rookie wide receiver will practice today. It sounds like he has a good chance to be back for the game against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday. […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - OCTOBER 04: Carnell Tate #14 of the Tennessee Titans reacts after a first down in the third quarter of the game against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images Carnell Tate has missed the Tennessee Titans’ last two games with a shoulder injury he suffered in the loss to the Cleveland Browns. Robert Saleh said today that the rookie wide receiver will practice today. It sounds like he has a good chance to be back for the game against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday. Tate has been really good this season with 34 catches for 413 yards and a touchdown through 7 games. Saleh also said that Anthony Hill and Cody Barton will return to practice today. It will be interesting to see what that means for Cedric Gray. For reasons that aren’t exactly clear, Gray spent most of his time on the sideline when both Hill and Barton were healthy. Gray, who might be the best defender left with Jeffery Simmons and Amani Hooker both gone, was really good last week against the Jacksonville Jaguars. In addition to getting those guys back on the practice field, Fernando Carmona will get his first practice in since he injured his ankle against the New York Giants. Saleh also said that Wan’Dale Robinson will miss the rest of the season. The team placed him on IR yesterday .

title: Titans designate Fernando Carmona to return from IR
summary: The Tennessee Titans have opened the practice window for rookie guard Fernando Carmona to return from injured reserve. Carmona was injured in the Titans’ 12-7 loss to the New York Giants in Week 3. He started the first three games of the season at right guard. The Titans will now have 21 days to activate […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 13: Fernando Carmona Jr. #66 of the Tennessee Titans lines up before the snap during an NFL football game against the New York Jets at Nissan Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tennessee Titans have opened the practice window for rookie guard Fernando Carmona to return from injured reserve. Carmona was injured in the Titans’ 12-7 loss to the New York Giants in Week 3. He started the first three games of the season at right guard. The Titans will now have 21 days to activate Carmona. Carmona, a 5th-round pick out of Arkansas in the 2026 NFL Draft, was one of the biggest stories of training camp. He came in and won the starting job with a great camp. Jackson Slater, Carmona’s backup, was also injured in that game. The offensive line has done a remarkable job with both of those guys out of the lineup. A lot of credit goes to offensive line coach Carmen Bricillo. He has done a great job getting the next guy up ready to play each week. It cannot be overstated how important having a good offensive line coach is. It will allow the Titans to not have to invest high picks in interior offensive linemen.

title: How the Titans should align at WR vs. Cowboys in Week 11
summary: The Tennessee Titans will have some decisions to make at wide receiver versus the Dallas Cowboys this week. Rookie stud Carnell Tate is returning to practice and is expected to be in the lineup. We’ve examined how Brian Daboll should utilize his receivers against the Cowboys in Week 11. Carnell Tate It goes without saying […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 20: Carnell Tate #14 of the Tennessee Titans warms up prior to the game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Nissan Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tennessee Titans will have some decisions to make at wide receiver versus the Dallas Cowboys this week . Rookie stud Carnell Tate is returning to practice and is expected to be in the lineup. We’ve examined how Brian Daboll should utilize his receivers against the Cowboys in Week 11. Carnell Tate It goes without saying that Tate should reclaim his spot as WR1 in the lineup. His two-game absence means he’s only played one game alongside Cam Ward since the Titans made the philosophical shift to a more aggressive no-huddle offense . Ward has caught fire, and having Tate back at his disposal should be a terrific development for a passing game starting to find its footing. Elic Ayomanor Elic Ayomanor had a frustrating and inconsistent day versus the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 10, but he still registered five receptions for a team-high 79 yards. That included an explosive 50-yard pass from Ward. Ayomanor is currently the Titans’ 2nd-most consistent receiver. He can move around the offensive formation, but is best suited to play on the outside. Chimere Dike Wan’Dale Robinson was placed on IR with an ankle injury . The Titans seemingly benched Calvin Ridley, who was limited to seven snaps versus the Jaguars. With Robinson sidelined, Xavier Restrepo was promoted to the roster. Chimere Dike deserves to be receiving opportunities in the slot, with Restrepo and Ridley mixing in. Dike had 71 receiving yards and a touchdown versus the Bengals two weeks ago, and should be getting extended looks at receiver with the two veteran options struggling. He’s capable of playing more snaps.

(Photo by Dylan Buell/Getty Images) | Getty Images Commanders: Bengals isn’t a ‘must win’, but it would be good to get one The Daily Slop – 19 November 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. WEAR BLACK. pic.twitter.com/EWKbLh1KzK — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) November 18, 2026 Articles Metro Sports Page Still strapped in, still believing While Jayden was doing his thing on offense, another great story of our season continued Thursday night: Sonny Styles is making an increasingly legitimate run at Defensive Rookie of the Year. His top competition will likely come from his college teammate and fellow NFC East linebacker, Arvell Reese. (Picking at the top of the draft last year had me falling in love with the idea of Reese, Styles or Caleb Downs coming to town. Now they all will, as members of the NFC East, which kind of blows.) Styles edged Reese on the stat sheet with an extra solo tackle and a tackle for loss that Arvell wasn’t able to get. What stands out more than the stats, though, is the tape of that tackle for loss. After positioning his entire team for the play he seemed to know was coming, Styles beat every member of the Giants offense to the spot and brought down J.J. McCarthy for arguably the biggest stop of the game. It led to a 12-yard punt that set up the game-winning drive. Styles continues to impress, displaying the speed, intelligence and tackling ability we sorely need in the middle of our defense. There is still a lot of football to be played, but I believe he is the front-runner for DROY, having put just a sliver of daylight between himself and Reese after Thursday’s game. [W]hat does this all mean in terms of taking care of our business? The margin for error has shrunk to almost nothing, but we do still have some room to work. At 3-5-1, we still have a chance to get to 5-6-1, which is the saddest aspiration I have voiced out loud as a fan in quite some time. That would mean going 2-1 against Cincy, Arizona and Tennessee. That is not an unreasonable expectation, as we should be favored in the last two. The game against Cincinnati is not a “must-win” because we can still navigate our way to a playoff berth with a loss. But at some point, this Commanders team will need to win a game folks might not expect it to win. That opportunity comes this week. Shutting down Joe Burrow would be great, but we have another path: a Jayden gem on offense and, when we need it most, a Sonny Styles impact play. That is the recipe for success in Week 11. title: Washington Commanders vs. Bengals MNF Week 11: Inside the Matchup
summary: From John Portis: The 3-5-1 Washington Commanders return home for another primetime matchup after securing a must-have win versus the Giants on Thursday Night Football. Also, the Dallas Cowboys lost to the 49ers on Sunday, further tightening the race for first place in the NFC East. The Commanders look to secure consecutive wins for the […]
full_text: From John Portis: The 3-5-1 Washington Commanders return home for another primetime matchup after securing a must-have win versus the Giants on Thursday Night Football. Also, the Dallas Cowboys lost to the 49ers on Sunday, further tightening the race for first place in the NFC East. The Commanders look to secure consecutive wins for the first time this season but could find it tough going against the Cincinnati Bengals ( 7-2 ), who are coming off an impressive win over the Steelers in their own primetime game last Sunday. While the Commanders secondary has improved with the return of cornerback Trey Amos, safety Nick Cross, and, on the coaching staff, the addition of defensive advisor Steve Wilks, they will now be facing MVP candidate Joe Burrow along with top wide receivers Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. They form one of the most productive QB/WR trios of the last two decades. Most productive QB/WR trios through Week 10 since 2006 The Bengals trio of Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins is on a historic pace this season. pic.twitter.com/6G1uJEMwFc — Gridiron Grading (@GridironGrading) November 17, 2026 Their work is supported up front by one of the better offensive lines in the NFL. The Bengals’ line ranks second behind only the L.A. Rams in pressure rate allowed, with only 16 sacks given up so far this season. Right tackle Amarius Mims, who was selected with the 18th overall pick in the 2024 NFL draft, has been a key piece of their success. On 381 pass-blocking snaps he’s only given up six pressures (per PFF). Even when pressure does get home, Burrow is changing how he faces it, notching a career-best 14.8% pressure-to-sack ratio this season (13th-best in the NFL). The Bengals allowed just a 15.9% pressure rate in Week 10, the 2nd best performance by any pass protection unit this season, per @SumerSports Here is every single Bengals dropback with particular appreciation for right tackle Amarius Mims and left tackle Orlando Brown Jr. pic.twitter.com/CaEiwKIUNC — Shawn Syed (@SyedSchemes) November 16, 2026 Naturally, the Bengals’ offense leans heavily on the passing game, utilizing a 62.6% to 37.4% split between Cincinnati’s No. 1 ranked passing offense and 30th ranked rushing attack. Running backs Chase Brown and Samaje Perine are primarily utilized in the receiving game, with Brown reeling in two touchdown receptions this past Sunday, his first since Week 1. Their true value, however, lies in pass protection. As Commanders defensive coordinator Daronte Jones schemes ways to attack Burrow, the blitz matchup between linebacker Sonny Styles and Chase Brown will be one to watch. As Bill-in-Bangkok pointed out this summer, the Bengals defense was one of the worst in the league last season, but was overhauled with the additions of edge Boye Mafe, safety Bryan Cook and defensive tackles Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen. Lawrence has been a game-changer for the Bengals, and Washington’s former defensive captain, Allen, is having a good year in Cincinnati. Mafe has also been particularly effective in improving the Bengals’ pass rush. Yeah real terrible huh Jonathan Allen has 4.0 sacks, a 17% pass rush win rate (per ESPN), and a 75% double-team rate (per ESPN; 60.9% per Pro Football Focus) in 9 games https://t.co/sSmxsUCKUR pic.twitter.com/4LpUDUBWs1 — Divine_thoughts (@Devine_thought) November 18, 2026 Boye Mafe vs. Pittsburgh Steelers Mafe led the Bengals in pressures with 7 on SNF. He is 7th overall in the NFL for an edge rusher this season with 43. pic.twitter.com/LV84DcR5K8 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 17, 2026 The net result has been a return to respectability, and the Bengals rank 10th in team defense after their impressive showing against the Steelers on Sunday night. The one area in which they have been susceptible is rushing defense, where Cincinnati ranks 20th in the league and 31st in yards allowed per rushing attempt (5.0 YPC). Offensive coordinator David Blough and the Washington Commanders should look to establish their rushing game early, which could be bolstered by the return of running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt, who saw his 21-day practice window opened earlier this week. The Commanders’ chances for victory may seem low, but the Bengals entered the season with the second-easiest strength of schedule and this matchup has all the makings of a trap game for Cincinnati. Washington fans will be anxious to see if Jayden Daniels and the Commanders can recreate the magic of their 2024 Monday night matchup . Betting Lines Oddsmakers have established the visitors as the favorite for this matchup. Point Spread : Bengals -5.5 Game Total (Over/Under) : 53.5 points A -5.5 point spread represents the belief in the Bengals ability to win as visitors vs the Burgundy & Gold, something they’ve managed only twice since 1970. The point total is set at 53.5 reflecting expectations of substantial offensive output from both sides — not surprising given the result the last time these two teams met on Monday Night Football . From Bill-in-Bangkok – originally published July 9, 2026 Week 11 Preview: Cincinnati Bengals at Washington Commanders Date: November 23, 2026, 8:15 p.m. ET (Monday Night Football) Location: Northwest Stadium in Landover Maryland The Bengals ended with a disappointing 6-11 record in 2025, finishing 3rd in the AFC North and missing the playoffs for a 3rd consecutive year. The season was quickly derailed when franchise quarterback Joe Burrow suffered a turf toe injury in Week 2, forcing him onto injured reserve and leading to a brutal 1–8 stretch without him. Compounding Burrow’s absence, star pass rusher Trey Hendrickson was limited to just seven games, with the defense giving up 28.9 points per game and ranking dead last in rush defense. To solve these glaring issues ahead of 2026, the front office revamped the defensive interior by trading their 2026 1st-round pick for 3-time Pro Bowl DT Dexter Lawrence, while also restructuring Burrow’s contract to free up cap space. Looking ahead, a healthy roster paired with a dominant defensive anchor gives Cincinnati bounce-back potential, and the Bengals are favored in 15 of their 17 games, including this prime time matchup against the Commanders in Landover. The All-Time Series Numbers Washington and Cincinnati have a very limited history, having played just 12 times since the Bengals joined the NFL as an expansion team in 1967, with the first game between the two being a 20-0 shutout by the Redskins in the then newly-renamed RFK Stadium. The overall series stands at 6-5-1 in favor of Washington. The Bengals won 3 straight contests from 2004 to 2012, but the Redskins won 4 out of 6 games played before 2000, and Washington is 2-0-1 in games played in the past decade. London Washington’s first-ever international game was played against Cincinnati in October 2016, ending in a 27-27 tie. Washington forced overtime late in the fourth quarter when quarterback Kirk Cousins engineered a 10-play drive, capped by a 23-yard touchdown pass to Jordan Reed and a game-tying extra point with just over two minutes remaining. In the extra period, the Redskins had a prime opportunity to win, but kicker Dustin Hopkins missed a potential game-winning 34-yard field goal wide left with 2:13 left on the clock. Cincinnati’s final desperation drive then stalled out when DT Chris “Swaggy” Baker forced an Andy Dalton fumble near midfield. On 4 subsequent passes, Kirk Cousins was unable to move the offense, cementing what was the first tie game in NFL international series history. In a display of poised execution, neither team punted or turned the ball over for the entire sixty minutes, a statistical anomaly that hadn’t previously happened in a regular-season game since World War II . title: Former Commanders DL Jonathan Allen on ‘emotional’ return to Washington
summary: Jonathan Allen played his first eight NFL seasons in Washington. The 2017 first-round NFL draft pick went to two Pro Bowls. He was a Walter Payton Man of the Year nominee. He was a solid interior pass rusher and run defender, and that got him paid to the tune of $72 million over the four […]
full_text: Jonathan Allen played his first eight NFL seasons in Washington. The 2017 first-round NFL draft pick went to two Pro Bowls . He was a Walter Payton Man of the Year nominee. He was a solid interior pass rusher and run defender, and that got him paid to the tune of $72 million over the four years following the expiration of his rookie contract. Even the good professional relationships between team and player eventually come to an end, and Washington cut Allen before the 2025 campaign . It was time, and both sides have moved on. He played the Commanders as a Viking in Minnesota last season, but Monday night marks his first return to Washington after all those years here. “It was of those things where you try not to make too much of it before the game plays,” Allen said during a Wednesday appearance on the Up and Adams Show with Kay Adams . “Obviously, it’s going to be emotional come game time. I’m excited to see a lot of guys I was with the first eight years of my career and guys who helped me become the player I am today. “But, that was in the past. I’ve moved on to a new chapter. And I love those guys and I wouldn’t change (the experience) for the world but I’m excited to be where I’m at. For me, it’s just trying to keep everything the same, not be too high to low, just be consistent and go out there and play a great game from the first quarter through the fourth.” Adams followed up with guys he’s looking forward to seeing on game day. He included strength coach Chad Engelhart, who arrived in Washington in 2017, the same as Allen. The Alabama product would spend winters in Washington and they would spend tons of time together. “We’ve all got those one or two guys that we’re super close with,” Allen said, “and he’s definitely that one for me.” Note: Allen talks about his Washington experience at the tail end of the interview. full_text: Editor’s note: It’s Scott Bair here. Shogun submitted this story to run early this week and I let it slip through the cracks. Argh. That’s completely on me. Apologies for that. Please vote in the poll below and enjoy reliving that dramatic Commanders win over the Giants. Another Washington victory means it is officially time to hand out the hardware and crown this week’s Boss Hog of the week. It has already been a tightly contested race this season. Marcus Mariota claimed the crown back in Week 3, and the front seven took home the honors after the Week 8 win over Philly—even if Sam Cosmi technically won the people’s vote in the comments! Now, coming off Thursday night’s win against the New York Giants, it is time to see where the pendulum swings. As a quick refresher on how this works: • Weekly Standalone Votes: Every victory brings a fresh slate, and each week’s poll stands on its own. • The Season Crown: Once the regular season wraps up, I will tally all the weekly winners to crown the official, definitive Boss Hog of the Season. • Make Your Voice Heard: Every vote counts toward the end-of-year hardware, so make sure to drop your pick and state your case in the replies. Without further ado, let’s break down the standout performers who made the difference on the field: WR Stefon Diggs Stat Line: 6 catches, 83 Yards, 1 TD Diggs delivered his finest performance of the season this week, punctuated by a 32-yard touchdown catch that helped him eclipse his previous season high in receiving yards. He currently leads the team in touchdowns and is officially on pace to crack double digits by the end of the year. With Terry McLaurin sidelined for the remainder of the season , Diggs has stepped up as an absolute rock in the passing game. At this rate, he is making a very strong case for Washington to keep him around for another year. LB Sonny Styles Stat Line: 13 Tackles, 1 Tackle for Loss I have never been happier to be completely wrong about a draft prospect than I have been with Sonny Styles. Granted, we are still in his rookie campaign, but he looks every bit like a star in the making— visibly progressing from week to week. There are still a few minor things to clean up in his game, as expected for a rookie, yet there is no denying he has been flat-out balling. His critical tackle for loss on third down was the exact play that saved the game for Washington. If he keeps up this trajectory, this rookie linebacker group could end up rivaling the 1998, 2005 and 2007 draft classes. We will hold off on comparing them to the legendary 1996 and 2012 groups just yet— but the foundation is officially there. QB Jayden Daniels Stat Line: 23-for-33 passing, 249 Yards, 3 TDs, 2 INTs Resilience is the best word to describe Jayden Daniels’ performance in this game . He threw two baffling interceptions that easily could have cost Washington the victory, yet when he was given a third chance to seal the deal, he made sure to capitalize on it. He needed this win badly. You can visibly tell he is getting more comfortable in the offense with each passing week. While there have certainly been some hiccups this season—many of which have been out of his control — he stood tall and delivered a clutch final drive right when the team needed him most. LB Frankie Luvu Stat Line: 6 Tackles, 1 Forced Fumble Luvu has been enjoying a tremendous bounce-back season so far. While his limitations in coverage are well-documented, he consistently proves that he knows how to make an impact play right when the defense needs one most. His forced fumble on Malik Nabers was a massive momentum swing that tilted the game in Washington’s favor early on. If Luvu keeps playing at this high level, do not be surprised to see a contract extension coming his way soon. TE Ben Sinnott Stat Line: 4 Catches, 44 Yards, 1TD Call it a banner night for Ben Sinnott. While the final stat line might look pedestrian on paper, it was a huge positive to finally see him break out of the funk he has been in since getting drafted. He has always had the tools to develop into a solid starting tight end, yet he simply never received the consistent touches needed to show what he could become. He set a great tone early in the matchup, and hopefully this performance is a sign of many more targets to come. Note: Chris Paul, Sam Cosmi, and Nick Allegretti deserve plenty of love here too. Cosmi continues to play at an elite level, looking more and more like a top-five player at his position with each passing week. Paul finally put together a consistent game and Allegretti was rock-solid alongside them in the trenches. Hopefully, the trio can build on this momentum and string together a strong stretch of games moving forward. Washington suddenly finds itself right back in the thick of the race, and the focus now shifts to stacking wins moving forward. Up next, the Cincinnati Bengals present a tough Monday night matchup, though they can certainly be beaten if Washington plays clean, sound football on both sides of the ball. Here is hoping we get plenty more victory polls like this over the coming weeks—and maybe even see our first repeat winner of the season along the way. Now it is your turn to decide. Drop your pick in the poll below and let us know who deserves to take home this Boss Hog crown!

summary: The Daily Slop – 18 November 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. full_text: The Daily Slop – 18 November 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Bullock’s Film Room Commanders Film Review: Ben Sinnott vs Giants It’s fair to say Commanders tight end Ben Sinnott has yet to live up to the lofty expectations of being a second round pick back in 2024. Sinnott has quietly developed into a strong blocker that can line up as a tight end or move around into fullback positions, so he still provides some value to the team, but his receiving numbers have been almost nonexistent. Prior to the Giants game on Thursday night, Sinnott had a total of 17 catches for 148 yards and two touchdowns through the first two and a half years of his career. Obviously, much more production is expected from a second round pick. But against the Giants, Sinnott had the best game of his career to date. When starting tight end Chig Okonkwo left the game with an injury, Sinnott stepped up and caught four passes for 42 yards and a touchdown. Again, those aren’t staggering numbers, but they were career high numbers for a player that has lacked opportunities and production in the passing game. So let’s dive into Sinnott’s career day and see what might be sustainable going forward. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE SI.com Can the Commanders Keep Pace With Joe Burrow Without Terry McLaurin? A month after tying the Giants, the Washington Commanders beat them 24–21 Thursday night and kept their season alive. Monday brings a familiar quarterback in Joe Burrow. Jayden Daniels beat him and the Bengals 38–33 in 2024. Now Washington faces the prospect of keeping pace with Burrow without Terry McLaurin. What Changed Since the 2024 Shootout Daniels, in just his third career game, began his iconic rookie-year scoring reel in Cincinnati, at a time when the Bengals were still respected as one of the NFL’s feared contenders. His 27-yard pass to lead wideout Terry McLaurin was one of the most electrifying instances of the stars’ immediate chemistry, as well as one of the first indicators of the potentially special underdog roster that Washington’s executives had compiled. McLaurin caught four passes for 100 yards against Cincinnati in 2024. He’s out for the season after tearing his patellar tendon. Stefon Diggs caught the winning 32-yard touchdown against the Giants last week, and Antonio Williams scored from 31 yards out. If Monday requires the same kind of scoring from Daniels, those are plays Washington needs from its current receivers. Cincinnati’s defensive front looks different from the one Daniels faced in 2024. After Trey Hendrickson’s departure, Boye Mafe became a primary edge rusher, while Dexter Lawrence and former Commander Jonathan Allen added strength inside. Cincinnati’s defense gave up 36 points to Tennessee on November 1, so Daniels should have chances. The Bengals have since beaten Atlanta and Pittsburgh, holding the Steelers to 18 points Sunday while Burrow threw for 409 yards and four touchdowns . Cincinnati is 7–2 and has won five straight. Washington may need far more than it scored against the Giants to keep up Monday. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Download the SB Nation app Commanders fans, take command of game day! Follow the action and share every cheer, question and instant reaction with fellow fans on the SB Nation app. Chat live during every game Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly move between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Commanders.com ‘Baby Kobe’: Jayden Daniels was clutch when Commanders needed him most Jayden Daniels, who was the only starting quarterback not to throw an interception heading into the Washington Commanders’ second matchup with the New York Giants, opened his postgame press conference with a joke. “Yes, I threw two picks,” Daniels said. “Yeah, got that out of my system. So, we can move forward about that.” Daniels delivered a clutch performance — his first fourth-quarter comeback in almost two seasons — against the Giants, finding Stefon Diggs for a 32-yard touchdown to give the Commanders a 24-21 victory. However, what he did on the previous two drives played a role in making the moment necessary, as he threw two interceptions in a span of five plays. Each moment felt like a death knell for the Commanders, who needed a win in Week 10 to keep their playoff hopes — and their season — alive. But if the interceptions were proof that Daniels is still a young quarterback with plenty to learn, the plays he made with the game on the line were the latest examples of why he’s viewed as the future of the franchise. “I was proud of him [Daniels] for coming back to respond and ripping it,” head coach Dan Quinn said after the game. Daniels had put together a solid game through the first three quarters. He looked comfortable in the pocket as he led the offense to 17 points, throwing his ninth and 10th touchdowns of the season to Ben Sinnott and Antonio Williams, respectively. There were some bumps along the way, like taking a sack for a 14-yard loss and failing to capitalize on a forced fumble from the defense, but Daniels looked mostly like himself, completing 16 of his 21 pass attempts for 180 yards in the first 45 minutes. The Commanders’ next three drives ended in frustration at best and disaster at worst. They stalled on fourth-and-1 at the Giants’ 30-yard line, setting up a 66-yard touchdown from Isaiah Likely that gave New York a four-point lead three plays later. The Commanders got into Giants’ territory again, but Daniels’s pass to Chig Okonkwo was underthrown and thrown inside, which made it easy for safety Javon Holland to intercept it at the Giants’ 2-yard line. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Riggo’s Rag Laremy Tunsil’s next step leaves Commanders facing more than a medical call Head coach Dan Quinn confirmed that left tackle Laremy Tunsil has moved on to the next stage of his rehabilitation from a torn triceps after a recent doctor’s visit. It’s the strength part of the process, but the Washington Commanders still don’t know if he will feature again in 2026. It’s a precarious situation, but the Commanders shouldn’t rush things. And Tunsil’s return may even be predicated on how the Commanders fare heading into their stretch run. Laremy Tunsil’s recovery takes the next step, but Commanders should be cautious Losing the five-time Pro Bowl blindside enforcer during training camp was a body blow. Tunsil is one of the few elite players Washington has, arguably the team’s best overall player. And his presence has been sorely missed. Brandon Coleman is trying to fill the void , but his skills look best suited to the interior. There isn’t really anybody else who can man the left tackle spot, aside from Esa Pole on the practice squad. That speaks to a lack of depth and the wrong offseason recruitment approach, but it shouldn’t impact Washington’s plan with Tunsil. Tunsil’s been out for months. He may be making good progress, but until his strength returns, the Commanders’ hands are tied. And if they are out of contention in the coming weeks, one has to wonder what the point of Tunsil’s return would be. Obviously, Tunsil is a supreme competitor. Even in his absence, the Ole Miss product has stayed engaged, helping the likes of Coleman and right tackle Josh Conerly Jr. with their technique, overall approach, and week-to-week preparation. That’s a sign of his exceptional leadership , but he will no doubt be itching to get back onto the field. title: NFL Power Rankings Week 11: Everything’s better after a Commanders win
summary: The Washington Commanders are 3-5-1 and coming off a big win over the division-leading New York Giants. That win was seen as a make-or-break game for the Commanders season, and we might have been reading some mock drafts instead of power rankings if Washington hadn’t been able to secure the victory in New Jersey. Now […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NJ - NOVEMBER 12: Jayden Daniels #5 of the Washington Commanders drops back to pass during an NFL football game against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium on November 12, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Washington Commanders are 3-5-1 and coming off a big win over the division-leading New York Giants. That win was seen as a make-or-break game for the Commanders season, and we might have been reading some mock drafts instead of power rankings if Washington hadn’t been able to secure the victory in New Jersey. Now we get a few more weeks for the Commanders to show us if they have the heart, talent, and luck to push through the remaining 8 games on the schedule and take the NFC East, where they are two-games back in Week 11. They have a tough task immediately ahead in Week 11 as they host Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals on Monday Night Football. The power rankers liked what they saw on Thursday Night Football, and Washington’s average jumped up accordingly. The Commanders’ highest ranking is all the way up to 14, while the low still sits at 24. Washington climbed an average of 4 spots, but, while they’re sitting right outside the top 20, they still have a lot of work to do to erase some of the more embarrassing moments from earlier in the season. A win over the Bengals on Monday night would shoot them up the rankings, while a loss can still get washed away by facing an offensive juggernaut led by the MVP-favorite this season. Let’s just get the win and keep moving towards the top of the division! High: 14 Low: 24 Average: 20.6 #14 Real GM Last week: 18 #16 Sports Illustrated (Orr) I don’t know what to do with any of these teams. I think that Washington has a higher ceiling than a majority of the NFC South, hence its positioning here. The same goes for the quarterback. I’m not sure there’s a run that Dan Quinn can put together to save his gig but compared to the rest of the NFL, this collection of players is not that god-awful. Last week: 28 Full Press Coverage (Glendon) Jayden Daniels overcame two interceptions to hit Stefon Diggs for a 32-yard touchdown with 57 seconds remaining against the Giants. The 24-21 win keeps the Commanders relevant in a tight NFC East. Two wins in three weeks represent progress despite the still-unfavorable overall record. Last week: 22 Walter Football The Redskins are +410 to win the division on FanDuel. That doesn’t seem like a bad bet, considering that Washington is the most balanced team in the division. The Redskins have a better quarterback than the Giants do and a better defense than the Cowboys. They’re not great anywhere, but they’re at least not incompetent on either side of the ball. Last week: 18 #17 Big Blue View (Falato) The Commanders responded to Wilson’s aggressive approach and found a way to earn a pivotal road victory against the Giants 24-21. Jayden Daniels threw three third-down touchdowns against New York, and Washington’s defense stiffened against a flaccid final two drives by the Giants’ offense. Last week: 25 #20 NFL.com (Shook) Washington enjoyed some vengeance Thursday night by finishing off a comeback win over the Giants , a team the Commanders should have defeated in their first meeting if not for their own disorganization. This is a minor victory in a season in which they’re still alive by virtue of existing in a terrible division, but it’s also a year when firings seem to be following them like a shadow. Last week: 26 Yahoo Sports (Schwab) Linebacker Sonny Styles is going to make a case for Defensive Rookie of the Year. Against the Giants, the seventh overall pick of the draft had 13 tackles. His biggest tackle came on a third-and-3 right after the two-minute warning when he shot through for a tackle for loss on a J.J. McCarthy designed quarterback run. Styles read that play because the Giants had run it in Week 5, which is high-level awareness from a rookie. "I had an idea it was QB run." @sonnystyles_ had flashbacks to a week 5 play, predicted right and made a game-saving tackle 🧠 @Commanders pic.twitter.com/pMP7KtWjEa — NFL Films (@NFLFilms) November 13, 2026 That tackle allowed Washington to get the ball back, and Jayden Daniels led a game-winning drive that kept the Commanders’ season alive. Styles is up to 80 tackles on the season and he is used often as a blitzer. He has one interception and one sack. He is looking like a great first-round pick. Last week: 24 USA Today (Davis) QB Sam Hartman has gone next level in his pursuit of a ring. Last week: 24 Sporting News (Iyer) The Commanders are right back in the race for the weak NFC East as they hold the tiebreaker over the Giants with a 1-0-1 mark in the season series. Dan Quinn and Jayden Daniels can still get some redemption. Washington gets Cincinnati next, but it also has Arizona, Tennessee, Houston and Atlanta in four of the next five games. Last week: 26 Team Rankings Last week: 21 #21 ESPN Non-QB MVP at midseason: LB Sonny Styles The seventh pick in April has made an instant impact with his speed and smarts. Styles leads Washington with 80 tackles — nobody else has more than 55. He has recorded one sack, forced a fumble and intercepted a pass. His speed has helped stop big plays, and his pre-snap diagnosis even led to a crucial tackle for a loss in Week 10. Styles is still learning and has certainly made mistakes, but he has provided Washington a defensive player to build around. — John Keim Last week: 24 NBC Sports (Wirth) Jayden Daniels almost gave the game away with a couple late picks, but delivered in the end to stay alive in the division race. Last week: 26 Pro Football Talk When the dust settles on the season, they could be the NFC East champions. Last week: 26 Sharp Football Analysis (Summerlin) The Commanders exorcised some late-game demons on Thursday night, scoring a late touchdown to take the lead before the defense sealed the game with an interception. Of course, the fourth-quarter drives before the touchdown ended in a turnover on downs and two interceptions, but Jayden Daniels got it done when it mattered most. I still don’t think the Commanders are good, but no one else in their division is either. Last week: 26 Pro Football Network (Infante) Offense Rank: 16 Defense Rank: 23 Playoff Odds: 14.10% Don’t count out the Washington Commanders just yet. With a 3-5-1 record, they still have a lot of work ahead of them to catch up to first place in the NFC East. But their 24-21 victory over the Giants on Thursday night got them right back in the mix, picking up a key divisional victory while dealing a blow to the first-place team. The consistency has been lacking for the Commanders this season, but the highs have been high. They defeated the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks in Week 3, and they closed out in the clutch against New York in Week 10. As rocky as things have been week over week, they’re still not out of the NFC East race. Last week: 24 Bleacher Report Something important is happening with the Washington Commanders, because Jayden Daniels is starting to find his rhythm again. Granted, Daniels threw two poor four-quarter interceptions. No one will deny those mistakes. However, the 2024 NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year still led the game-winning drive directly after those poor decisions, which says a lot about where he’s at in his development. Furthermore, the quarterback is helping to elevate the play of those around him. Rookie wide receiver Antonio Williams and tight end Ben Sinnott were critical contributors during Washington’s latest victory. The Commanders may still own a losing record and earlier concerns have not gone away entirely, but this team is starting to show signs of life, which portends good things for the future.
