title: NFL Week 11 uniforms: Texans debut 'Rivalries' look, Commanders rock 'Hail Raiser'
summary: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 11, led by Houston debuting its "Rivalries" combination.
full_text:
A primetime game can be a perfect opportunity for a team to send a message with its play. It also helps when it is looking its finest on the gridiron. The Houston Texans and Washington Commanders enter Week 10 with one part of that down with the debut of their respective uniforms.

 

 It's the Texans' turn first, as they will wear their "Rivalries" threads against the Indianapolis Colts on "Thursday Night Football." The look is primarily white, but includes H-Town blue and battle red with details that pay homage to Houston's streets. The city's signature blue street tiles appear on the uniform's helmet, name plate, sleeve, collar and pant stripes in a two-tone battle red and blue finish. Houston's "be someone" bridge is the inspiration for the blue jersey numbers.

 For the first time, the Texans will wear a liberty white helmet, paying tribute to the white prototype founder Robert C. McNair revealed in 1999 before shifting to a deep steel blue lid. The white helmet's face mask includes a chrome H-town blue finish, a nod to Houston's car culture. 

 As part of the Commanders' redesign of their uniform closet last offseason , they unveiled the all-black "Hail Raiser" alternates, which debut against the Cincinnati Bengals on "Monday Night Football." It features a black helmet with a "Spear W" logo on both sides, as the spear and "W" are interwoven at their center. Burgundy and gold stripes appear on the sleeve and pants, while the lid includes a three-stripe look on top of similar colors. Solid burgundy block numbers are outlined by gold. 

 The Buffalo Bills are also rocking a "Rivalries" look against the Miami Dolphins . Buffalo debuted its all-white "Cold Front" combination last season, but it returns with icy details throughout. The shoulder sleeve features a chrome charging buffalo, the first time a Bills uniform incorporates this element. The white helmet similarly includes a frosty metallic-filled charging buffalo logo, while the shoulder and pant leg patters boast a cracked-ice texture with a pattern that resembles snowfall on a bison's fur. 

 It's an alternate week for the Detroit Lions as well. Detroit is going all-black against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Complete with a Honolulu blue matte helmet, the "Motor City Muscle" threads were first unveiled in 2024. The lid also includes a leaping lion logo in silver with a black stripe down the middle. The Lions wore these threads in Week 7 against the Green Bay Packers .

title: Midseason reports on every NFL team's offensive coordinator, playcaller
summary: Here's the good and the bad for each offensive coordinator or playcaller through Week 10, plus keys to their success the rest of the way.
full_text:
We've seen the good and bad of offensive coordinators and playcallers across the league throughout the first half of the 2026 NFL season.

 With Dan Pitcher coordinating the offense and coach Zac Taylor calling plays, Joe Burrow has the Cincinnati Bengals ' offense humming. The same goes for Trevor Lawrence and the Jacksonville Jaguars , with Grant Udinski as OC and coach Liam Coen the playcaller. Both QBs are in the MVP conversation.

 On the other side of things, the Los Angeles Chargers ' offense under OC/playcaller Mike McDaniel has been a disaster. The Minnesota Vikings had struggled to put points on the board until they acquired QB Kirk Cousins , which had an immediate impact on coach Kevin O'Connell's playcalling in Sunday's win over the Green Bay Packers .

 There are eight weeks left this season, and the pressure will continue to build for coordinators and playcallers looking for winning formulas, while those who shine might be in position to become head coaches in 2027.

 With that in mind, here is what has gone right, what has gone wrong and the key to the second half for every offense in the NFL.

 
 Jump to: 
 ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN 
 CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND 
 JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN 
 NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF 
 SEA | TB | TEN | WSH 

 
 

 

 

 AFC EAST 
 

 Buffalo Bills 
 Offensive coordinator: Pete Carmichael

 Playcaller: Joe Brady

 What has gone right? Just about everything. The Bills lead the NFL in scoring and are doing so with a varied attack that features RB James Cook III handling a career-high workload and QB Josh Allen leading his most explosive passing attack since arriving in Buffalo. Most encouragingly, this offense has proved just as capable of winning in slow-paced ball-control games as in up-tempo shootouts.

 What has gone wrong? Pre-snap sloppiness is a recurring problem. Between false starts, illegal shifts, delays of game, offsides and too many men in the huddle calls, the Bills are averaging close to three pre-snap offensive penalties per game, and that's not to mention the 132 yards the Bills have had nullified by holding penalties.

 Key to second half: Allen has always benefited from the abnormal consistency, continuity and health in front of him on the offensive line. In recent weeks, tackles Dion Dawkins and Spencer Brown and guard Alec Anderson have dealt with injury concerns. Keeping the line together, especially with cold weather coming and how the Bills are already leaning on Cook, is paramount.  -- Nick Suss 

 

 

 
 

 Miami Dolphins 
 Offensive coordinator: Bobby Slowik

 Playcaller: Bobby Slowik

 What has gone right? The Dolphins entered this season vowing to run the ball and they've done so successfully -- remarkably, even without starter De'Von Achane , who tore his left ACL in September. Second-year back Ollie Gordon II  has filled in nicely for Achane, at one point scoring a rushing touchdown in four straight games. Miami's offensive line has been physical at the line of scrimmage and leads the league in average rushing yards before first contact per rush attempt.

 What has gone wrong? Miami has largely struggled to move the ball consistently through the air, averaging the third-fewest passing yards per game in the NFL this season. Third-round rookie Caleb Douglas looks like a definite starting receiver, but the Dolphins are still looking for consistent production from the rest of the room. Some of that also falls on quarterback Malik Willis , who will be on injured reserve until at least Week 14 with a groin/core injury.

 Key to second half: Continue to get receivers Douglas, Chris Bell and Kevin Coleman Jr . involved in the passing game. Their development will be worth keeping an eye on with Willis sidelined and second-year quarterback Kyle McCord starting in his place. With the playoffs out of the picture, the Dolphins' focal point should center on their three rookie receivers and continuing to sharpen their run game.  -- Marcel Louis-Jacques 

 

 
 

 New England Patriots 
 Offensive coordinator: Josh McDaniels

 Playcaller: Josh McDaniels

 What has gone right? Explosive plays. They are among the league leaders in passing plays of 20 yards or more, and running plays of 20 yards or more. They've also received solid contributions from a young core of players who project to be a big part of their future -- OTs Will Campbell and Caleb Lomu , C Jared Wilson and TE Eli Raridon 

 What has gone wrong? Too many injuries. WR A.J. Brown sustained a high right ankle sprain in the third quarter of the season opener, which foreshadowed what was to come -- a run of injuries across the offense that has challenged finding continuity and consistency, and now includes Drake Maye . The Patriots are expected to use all eight of their return-from-IR designations and Maye might be done for the season.

 Key to second half: Supporting QB  Tommy DeVito . He is being thrust into the starting role and that means everyone else needs to raise their level of play to lift him up. The return of starting left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker and No. 2 receiver Romeo Doubs should also help.  -- Mike Reiss 

 

 
 

 New York Jets 
 Offensive coordinator: Frank Reich

 Playcaller: Frank Reich

 What has gone right? The veteran Reich, in Year 1 with the Jets, has done a nice job of helping QB Geno Smith curb his turnovers. Smith, who had more interceptions (52) than any quarterback from 2022 to 2025, has reduced his picks to three. Smith is having the best statistical season of any Jets QB since Ryan Fitzpatrick in 2015. Reich, himself a former QB, deserves some credit for that.

 What has gone wrong? Reich has above-average talent, including gifted skill players in WR Garrett Wilson and RB Breece Hall , and yet the Jets are only 24th in points per game (19.4). The main reasons: poor red zone efficiency (31st), vanilla game plans, questionable halftime adjustments and inconsistency in getting the ball into the hands of their top players.

 Key to second half: The Jets can start off by scoring a touchdown; they've gone nine straight quarters without one, tied for the second-longest drought in the league this season. Reich needs to create an identity for the offense. They want to be physical and run-oriented, but they stray from that during games. Another key: Get Kenyon Sadiq more involved. The talented rookie tight end has been a nonfactor over the past seven games. -- Rich Cimini 

 

 

 AFC NORTH 
 

 Baltimore Ravens 
 Offensive coordinator: Declan Doyle

 Playcaller: Declan Doyle

 What has gone right? Getting RB  Derrick Henry in the end zone. The Ravens have failed to consistently run and throw the ball this season, but Henry continues to pile up touchdowns. By midseason, he recorded his ninth season of 10 or more touchdowns, which ties LaDainian Tomlinson for the most in NFL history.

 

 What has gone wrong? Injuries at quarterback. It's gotten so bad that the Ravens became the third team since 1950 to start four different quarterbacks in four weeks (excluding the 1987 strike season), according to the Elias Sports Bureau. Lamar Jackson is out until at least mid-to-late December after having surgery on his right thumb and Tyler Huntley is out for the season with turf toe. After one start with undrafted Joe Fagnano , Baltimore was in desperation mode when it traded for Jacoby Brissett .

 Key to second half: Getting the offense on track with Brissett. Entering Monday night's game, the Ravens had gone four straight games without scoring more than 14 points for the first time in team history. The Ravens have praised Brissett for his ability to drive the ball downfield. Since the start of the 2025 season, Brissett has thrown 33 touchdown passes, which is more than Justin Herbert (32), Baker Mayfield (29) and Jackson (27).  -- Jamison Hensley 

 

 
 

 Cincinnati Bengals 
 Offensive coordinator: Dan Pitcher

 Playcaller: Zac Taylor

title: 2027 NFL mock draft: Reid's midseason first-round predictions for all 32 picks
summary: Which NFL team could land Drew Mestemaker? Who needs Chris Cole, Ashton Hampton or Jamari Johnson? Jordan Reid projected first-round picks for 2027 -- and a trade.
full_text:
Now that the NFL trade deadline has passed and we're in the second half of the 2026 season , it's a great time to look ahead to the 2027 NFL draft .

 Some teams whose playoff hopes are mostly dashed are already fully into the process of evaluating prospects for the draft, which will take place in April in Washington. So why not take our own look at how that draft might turn out?

 This latest mock draft factors in a combination of what NFL teams need, my evaluation of production and tape from the 2026 college football season , and conversations I've had with trusted scouts and evaluators. Of course, things will change between now and April -- players will move up and down the board or exit the class entirely by returning to school -- but this is how I see things currently.

 The draft order obviously is far from set, so I based this 1-32 on what the order would look like if the season ended today. There have already been six trades in Round 1, and I actually pitched a seventh that could make sense.

 How many quarterbacks will make Round 1? Here are my full projections for all 32 first-round picks.

 Note: Underclassmen are marked with an asterisk. 

 

 

 1. Tennessee Titans  (1-8) 
 Jeremiah Smith , WR, Ohio State* 

 Smith is  the best player in this draft, and as the first wide receiver to go No. 1 since 1996 (Keyshawn Johnson), he would allow the Titans to continue to build around quarterback  Cam Ward , the No. 1 pick of the 2025 draft. How  special  is Smith? He has drawn comparisons to some of the best wideouts of the past quarter century -- including Calvin Johnson, Larry Fitzgerald and Julio Jones -- by NFL scouts.

 Smith's 131.7 receiving yards per game ranks second in the FBS, and he continues to thrive despite Ohio State's quarterback issues . Speaking of the Buckeyes, the Titans could reunite Smith with fellow wide receiver  Carnell Tate , Tennessee's first pick in 2026. Smith's rare combination of size (6-foot-4 and 225 pounds), speed and power gives him early All-Pro potential and makes him the type of player Ward and the Titans need to further improve their offense.

 
 

 Projected trade: Jets package two first-rounders to move up 
 The Jets have three first-round picks, so I have them sending Nos. 4 and 13, along with a 2028 third-rounder, to the Chargers for the No. 2 selection. New York originally acquired the No. 13 pick in a trade with the Cowboys for defensive tackle  Quinnen Williams .

 Could this move finally allow the Jets to select their quarterback of the future?

 
 

 2. New York Jets  (via projected trade with 1-8 LAC ) 
 Drew Mestemaker , QB, Oklahoma State* 

 Mestemaker has progressed from a walk-on who didn't start in high school to my top QB in this class. The Jets have used the past three drafts to establish an offensive base, selecting bookend tackles ( Olu Fashanu and Armand Membou ), wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr.  and tight end Kenyon Sadiq in Round 1. Along with star wideout  Garrett Wilson , they make New York an ideal landing spot for a rookie signal-caller.

 Mestemaker excels at pushing the ball down the field, with his 21 completions of 20 or more yards this season ranking eighth in the FBS. His decision-making is inconsistent at times, but Mestemaker is young (he's in his first season as a Power 4 starter) and has the tools to transform the Jets.

 

 
 

 3. Miami Dolphins  (1-8) 
 Colin Simmons , Edge, Texas* 

 After drafting 13 players last year, the Dolphins have a foundation of young talent on their roster. Now, Miami needs a star, which Simmons could be on defense. He is arguably the top pass rusher in this class and one of the best in the FBS at generating pressure off the edge. His 10.5 sacks are third most in the country despite him missing two games because of injury . His 20.5% pressure rate ranks fifth in the FBS, and Simmons' powerful hands let him set a violent edge in run defense.

 Pairing Simmons with 2024 first-rounder  Chop Robinson  would give the Dolphins an explosive pass-rush duo for defensive-minded coach Jeff Hafley.

 
 

 4. Los Angeles Chargers  (via projected trade with 2-8 NYJ ) 
 Charlie Becker , WR, Indiana* 

 The Chargers have been extremely disappointing this season, and their 1-8 start has exposed the need for more talent everywhere. That and the fact that they already have a QB in  Justin Herbert  are why I had them trade out of No. 2 and add another pick. And we'll use this first pick to get Herbert some help.

 Becker is an excellent vertical threat who has 10 touchdowns this season (sixth in the FBS) and can also execute the short to intermediate levels of the route tree. He is tall (6-foot-4) and sure-handed (zero drops on 85 targets this season) with excellent body control and elite hand-eye coordination, allowing him to win in the air on long and contested catch opportunities. Becker would immediately become Herbert's WR1.

 
 

 5. Philadelphia Eagles  (2-7) 
 Dylan Stewart , Edge, South Carolina* 

 This season has been a disaster for Philadelphia, but it allows the Eagles to get an elite edge-rushing talent. Stewart is a toolsy and explosive player who has the unique ability to bend around the corner and wreak havoc in the backfield. The 6-foot-5, 250-pounder hasn't had consistent production in college, but his tools and flashes of potential are tantalizing and reminiscent of  Brian Burns  coming out of Florida State . Stewart will have to answer questions during the predraft process about his production and an in-season suspension , but he's an ideal talent for the Eagles to draft and develop behind  Jonathan Greenard , Nolan Smith Jr.  and Jalyx Hunt .

 
 

 6. New York Jets  (via 3-7 IND ) 
 Leonard Moore , CB, Notre Dame* 

 Now that the Jets have traded up to take their quarterback of the future, they could select my No. 1 defensive prospect in this year's class here. Moore's 8.6% target rate is the lowest among all FBS corners this season, and he has allowed only seven completions in eight games. Moore is one of the most consistent cover guys in the country and has the length (6-foot-2, 197 pounds) and ball skills to be a shutdown corner in the NFL. He could start right away at outside corner for New York.

 
 

 

 7. Arizona Cardinals  (3-6) 
 Jordan Seaton , OT, LSU* 

 The Cardinals desperately need to add help in the trenches, and Seaton is an upper-tier athlete who is very polished in pass protection. He has allowed only one sack and four pressures this season on 344 pass-blocking snaps. He is more than capable of mirroring and matching edge rushers, though he needs to get stronger and improve his anchor and drive strength. But Seaton would be a plug-and-play starting option at either tackle spot opposite  Paris Johnson Jr. , who will be on his fifth-year option in 2027.

 
 

 8. Atlanta Falcons  (3-6) 
 CJ Carr , QB, Notre Dame* 

 With  Michael Penix Jr.  struggling to find consistency in Year 3, the Falcons could once again be convinced to use the No. 8 pick on a QB -- like they did three years ago with Penix , especially since the Falcons' front office and coach have changed since making that selection. Atlanta has plenty of skill-position talent (RB  Bijan Robinson , WR Drake London , TE Kyle Pitts Sr. ) that could enable a young QB to thrive immediately.

 Carr is an instinctive passer who consistently has answers and has already been given considerable autonomy in Notre Dame's offense. He doesn't have the high-end traits of some passers in the class (picture a more mobile Kirk Cousins ), but he is polished in many of the skills that are essential to playing the position.

 
 

 9. Houston Texans  (3-6) 
 Zereoue Williams , OT, Utah 

 "I could see him making a rise similar to  Kolton Miller " is a text that a scout sent me after watching Williams earlier this season. Miller was drafted No. 15 in 2018 by the Raiders, and Williams could be taken even higher. He is already 24 years old, which is part of why he is receiving some…

title: NFL Week 11 latest intel, buzz questions, news, fantasy tips: What we're hearing
summary: What are people around the league saying about Fernando Mendoza? Could changes be coming in Dallas? And what now for New England? Here's the latest intel.
full_text:
Week 11 of the  2026 NFL season  is here, and insiders Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano have been calling sources around the league for the latest news and notable buzz.

 First, what are people saying about last weekend's much-anticipated first start for Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza ? What did he show against the Seahawks and what does it tell us about the rest of his season? Then, what are we hearing on the Cowboys' struggling defense and any potential changes on the horizon? What about the Patriots and their sudden downturn in the aftermath of Drake Maye 's injury? And finally, who are the most interesting 2027 free agents and what is the early intel on them?

 It's all here, as Jeremy and Dan answer big questions, hand out useful fantasy football nuggets and empty their reporting notebooks heading into Week 11.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Mendoza's debut | Cowboys' defense 
 Patriots' concern | 2027 free agents 
 Fantasy advice  | More notes, intel 

 
 

 What are people around the league saying about Fernando Mendoza 's debut? 
 Graziano: They are saying he looked the part and that the moment didn't look too big for him. And that is really what you're looking for if you're starting a rookie No. 1 pick in Week 10 against the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks' defense .

 Mendoza obviously has work to do on pre-snap diagnosis and other aspects of the job at this level, but he's not the first quarterback to not see Devon Witherspoon coming on a blitz, and he won't be the last. He clearly offers something with his legs that Kirk Cousins does not at this point, and he made throws outside the numbers that people view as a sign the offense can evolve with him at the helm.

 Fowler: People I spoke with saw flashes. Playing Seattle is an arduous task. But Mendoza used his legs to escape congestion, completed passes to 10 different receivers and navigated an offense that was without star tight end  Brock Bowers for much of the game. The Seahawks eventually overwhelmed him. He missed a few blitzes and took six sacks. He missed some throws, particularly to the left side of the field. But as one personnel evaluator noted, the game didn't look too big for him and he kept his eyes downfield, whether in the pocket or on the move. The arm strength and mobility are obvious, and those can be assets to the Raiders' offense in the coming weeks and into 2027.

 

 While Cousins probably would have started another week had he stayed, Mendoza was making enough progress behind the scenes that he was going to play soon enough. And he did enough to at least validate that promise.

 Graziano: He did, and it will get better. This is quite similar to the situation Eli Manning had as a rookie with the Giants in 2004, when veteran Kurt Warner started the first half of the season and Manning took over midway through. One key difference is that Warner remained on that Giants team for the rest of the season, whereas Cousins is no longer there to be a sounding board for Mendoza. So that's something to watch. But the Raiders have been extremely deliberate about Mendoza's development program, and while yes, his first start came a few weeks earlier than they had planned, they believe he's ready enough. And Sunday's debut didn't cause any fresh concern that I can detect in that building.

 It doesn't get a lot easier, with Denver and Cleveland in the next two weeks ahead of the Raiders' bye, but Mendoza has something, and people are excited to see more. It's no coincidence that the NFL flexed that Week 12 Raiders-Browns game into primetime on Tuesday.

 Fowler:  This is a challenging three-game stretch for a young quarterback. In order for him to survive it, the Raiders must find a way to run the ball more efficiently. How a Klint Kubiak-run offense ranks last in yards per rush at 2.9 is shocking to me, even with the transitional state of the offensive line. The Raiders' backs have a combined two rushing performances of more than 60 yards --  Ashton Jeanty  (102) in Week 1 and  Mike Washington Jr . (83) in Week 8. That's it. Running the ball well is a staple of the Kubiak system, and if the Raiders are to properly support Mendoza, they must find a way to manufacture explosive plays on the ground.

 The rest should come into focus. "Mendoza is a good fit for Klint [Kubiak's] offense," an NFC offensive coach said. "I thought he did well when facing live bullets."

 

 
 What's next for the Cowboys and their major problems on defense? Could they shake things up? 
 (Update: On Wednesday morning, the Cowboys made a playcalling change , and the below text has been updated to reflect that.)

 Fowler: The big shake-up would be changing coaching personnel on defense and based on public comments coming from the Dallas brass this week, it feels like everything is on the table when it comes to defensive coordinator Christian Parker's status. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer and owner Jerry Jones have been noncommittal about Parker. On Wednesday morning, the Cowboys did make a change and gave playcalling duties to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine. Parker was formerly a Pettine understudy in Green Bay.

 In talking to people in Dallas, they believe firing coaches wouldn't solve much. Parker is a good young coach. It just hasn't worked out thus far. The personnel on defense, though improved on paper from a year ago, still isn't great and is clearly a year away. Yes, it looks bad --  Christian McCaffrey running untouched upfield twice is a hard image to shake -- but the Cowboys have already tweaked the defensive lineup earlier in the season. Plus, it's tough to make wholesale changes, in part because Dallas is very much alive in a weak NFC East.

 Graziano: Agreed. And I believe that's the way the Cowboys see it, too. Jones made some comments on the radio Tuesday  hinting about possibly changing defensive playcallers, and Dallas ultimately went that route. But this is very much not an ownership group that likes to make in-season coaching changes, so they would consider it a drastic step to move on totally from Parker now. Also, if Schottenheimer is concerned about his own job security at the end of this season, throwing a second defensive coordinator overboard in two years might not be the best way to project that he has everything under control.

 

 Fowler: The Titans and Eagles are on the schedule over the next two weeks. That could be a stretch for Dallas to get things right, though Cam Ward is improving in Tennessee and that game is hardly a gimme. Playoffs or not, the Cowboys will have serious work to do in the offseason to replenish the defense ... again. Defensive tackle  Quinnen Williams is worth building around. He's having a strong season as one of the lone bright spots on that side of the ball. But the Cowboys will need help at all three levels. There are not enough standouts. And they have just four picks in April's draft to change that.

 Situating the futures of corner Joey Porter Jr . and wide receiver George Pickens is critical. Franchise-tagging one of them could risk losing the other, and cornerback is a major need for the team, even with Porter in the lineup. Dallas was brimming with confidence defensively coming out of camp, and the good feelings dissipated early in the season. This is going on two years of bad defensive football.

 Graziano: It makes you wonder if the organization needs to take a broader look at the way it scouts, acquires and develops defensive talent. The Cowboys seem to need a more coherent overall plan, which admittedly is tough when you change defensive coordinators every year. Since Dan Quinn left to coach the Commanders, they have cycled through Mike Zimmer, Matt Eberflus and now potentially Parker. The criticism of Eberflus last season was that he didn't coach to the specific abilities of his players enough and wasn't flexible in making scheme changes to reflect the players' strengths and weaknesses. But things are worse on that side of the…

title: Falcons seek change, but keep ending up in the same spot
summary: Mediocre record, questions at quarterback, rinse, repeat. Maybe next year the Falcons can start making progress.
full_text:
Bijan Robinson was visibly frustrated. He was in the locker room addressing the media after another Atlanta Falcons loss. The star running back referenced the team's bye this week and how it was time to put up or shut up.

 "We have to come together this week and just tell ourselves, is this how we want to end this season and is this how we want to go about the rest of the season with this product or are we going to change and are we going to strain for each other?" Robinson said after a 35-13 home loss to the Kansas City Chiefs last Sunday. "Are we going to go out there and play for each other no matter the situation and just be dominant on the field, man?"

 It is an all-too-familiar feeling for Robinson, who has yet to play for a winning team in his four seasons in the NFL.

 The Falcons have lost five of their last six games to fall to 3-7. That was their exact record through 10 games last season. Over the previous five seasons, Atlanta has gone 7-10 three times and 8-9 twice. The franchise has not made the playoffs since the 2017 season, the second-longest drought in the NFL after the New York Jets .

 The Falcons have been like the football version of Bill Murray's Groundhog Day. There has been a certain sameness to it all across three different coaching staffs and two different front offices.

 Head coach Kevin Stefanski, general manager Ian Cunningham and president of football Matt Ryan -- the last Falcons' franchise quarterback from 2008-21 -- took over last offseason. The story, though, remains on repeat: a team good enough to knock off top teams (the Philadelphia Eagles in 2024, the Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Rams in 2025 and the San Francisco 49ers this season) yet one inconsistent enough to suffer seemingly annual blowout losses to the middling Carolina Panthers .

 

 The Falcons offense was supposed to get a facelift this season, a new system led by Stefanski, an offensive guru, and young offensive coordinator and playcaller Tommy Rees. They have gotten some things right, like making quarterback Michael Penix Jr . into a primarily under-center passer with more play-action looks. But the results have been maddeningly similar to where the Falcons were at this time in 2025.

 Through 10 games this season, the Falcons have scored 20.1 points per game and have accumulated 327.4 yards per game. Atlanta has an offensive success rate of 40.8% and its EPA per play is -0.16. That latter mark is tied for fifth-worst in the league.

 Last season, through 10 games, the Falcons had scored 19.5 points per game and had racked up 332.5 yards per game. The 2025 team had a 43.4% success rate with a -0.07 EPA per play. Eerily similar numbers.

 Even if you remove the first two games of this season started by third-string quarterback Cooper Rush , the Falcons stats are only marginally better: 23.1 points per game, 343.8 yards per game, a 41.7% success rate and a -0.08 EPA per play.

 There are some positives. Unlike last season when the Falcons were already mathematically eliminated from the playoffs at 3-7, they are still in the division race this season. The entire NFC South is only separated by two games in the loss column. Atlanta closes its season with three straight games against its division rivals.

 Also, if you want to look ahead, the Falcons will have more than $140 million in salary-cap space this offseason, the most in the NFL. That will allow Cunningham, Ryan and Stefanski to build the kind of roster they want moving forward. Atlanta could be looking at a top-10 draft pick, as well. The Falcons are currently projected to pick No. 8, a familiar spot, of course, for a franchise that is stuck in a loop. That's where they selected wide receiver Drake London , Robinson and Penix in consecutive years.

 

 Stefanski is not thinking about that right now. Despite trading away starters Jessie Bates III and Ryan Neuzil at the deadline, the Falcons would still love to turn things around and end that eight-year playoff drought. Atlanta heads to face the Minnesota Vikings on the road after the bye.

 "With the amount of time that you have [during the bye] and you're not game-planning for the next week, you can really put a fresh set of eyes on it, if you will, and look at areas that we can do better because the truth is we have to do better in multiple areas," Stefanski said. "And then the first part of that is identifying those areas."

 Robinson's advice to teammates? Just play more freely. Maybe that's the only way for the Falcons to get out of this rut.

 "I told some of the guys, 'Act like it's like street ball out there,'" Robinson said. "You're just free flowing, you know your assignment and just make it happen.

 "So that used to be our mentality is just to not worry about anything external, just worry about what we have going on and try to make it better for ourselves and for everybody watching."

title: Ravens' Humphrey apologizes for quip that Baltimore 'best at making criminals'
summary: Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey apologized Wednesday for the derogatory comment he recently made about Baltimore on his podcast.
full_text:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- Outspoken Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey apologized for the derogatory comment he made about the city of Baltimore on his recent podcast.
On an episode of "The Marlon Humphrey Show" released Wednesday, Humphrey took a swipe at the city when asked what Baltimore was best at making.
After first mentioning "The Star-Spangled Banner" and National Bohemian beer, Humphrey quipped, "They're best at making criminals."
After Wednesday's practice, Humphrey said he regretted those remarks.
"I would like to apologize for some comments on my podcast I had to the city of Baltimore," Humphrey said. "As you guys know, I've been here my whole career. Spent lots of offseasons here. Welcomed a son here and I'm an investor in the city. And obviously, I do know the effect that words have and just like to apologize for those comments."
Humphrey received heavy fan backlash on social media Wednesday afternoon. The podcast episode featuring Humphrey's "criminals" comment has since been deleted from his YouTube page.
Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott acknowledged Humphrey's apology in a statement posted to social media , but noted, "a verbal apology is not enough. Baltimore is a city full of young Black boys who look to the Ravens as a beacon of light in their lives and to have someone that looks like them who wears a Baltimore Ravens jersey relegate them to becoming criminals cuts deeper.
"I wonder how he would feel if prominent Baltimoreans used their platforms to imply that Baltimore once produced great defensive backs but we have recently lost our way."
Scott then added, "They wouldn't do that because our team and city are supposed to be united as one. Baltimore versus the world."
Scott concluded his post by inviting Humphrey to sit down with him and some Baltimore citizens "who have re-entered into our community and are now preventing others from making the mistakes they made."
A post shared by Mayor Brandon M. Scott (@mayorbmscott)
Humphrey, 30, is in his 10th season with Baltimore and is the longest-tenured defensive player on the Ravens. The No. 16 selection in the 2017 draft by Baltimore, Humphrey has been to four Pro Bowls, which are the most by a Ravens cornerback.
In recent years, Humphrey has struggled and has drawn the ire of fans. This season, he has given up an NFL-worst 313 yards in coverage in the fourth quarter.
Asked if he understood why fans would be upset with this comment even if he was joking, Humphrey replied, "Yeah, I just apologized ... and that won't really happen again."
Humphrey is in the final year of a five-year, $97.5 million extension. His $26.276 million salary cap hit is the largest for any cornerback in 2026.
Humphrey's slight at Baltimore comes at a time when the franchise is dealing with one of its worst stretches in its history. The Ravens (4-6) have lost five straight, including a 23-20 loss to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers on Monday. Baltimore has also lost seven of its past eight games at home.
Ravens coach Jesse Minter said he would keep any conversations with Humphrey about this matter private.
"Just speaking for myself, I love this city," Minter said. "I know what this city means to me and my family. I take a lot of pride in being here. It's a great city with a bunch of great people. We desperately want to represent this city the right way by how we play most importantly."
This isn't the first time that Humphrey has caused a stir with his podcast. One month ago, Humphrey said safety Kyle Hamilton "knew" he was going to make a game-sealing interception of Atlanta Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa once he replaced injured starter Michael Penix Jr . in overtime. Hamilton later shot down that characterization, describing Humphrey's account as "pretty hyperbolic."
"I think Marlon is very unapologetically himself," Hamilton said Wednesday. "He can be slightly abrasive at times, but that's just him. And talking to his family has always been like that. But we all love Marlon and we appreciate everything he's done for us [and] will do for us. And he's one of us."
Humphrey has been a target of fan criticism over the past two seasons. He has been frequently booed during home games at M&T Bank Stadium.
During the "Monday Night Football" broadcast two days ago, when the Ravens were losing to the winless Chargers, fans could be heard shouting "F--- Marlon Humphrey" as they exited the stadium.
"I love the city. I think I've expressed this many times," Humphrey said. "I want to win in front of the fans just because it's not cheap to be in those seats."
Has the fans' negativity toward him affected his view of them?
"To answer your question," Humphrey replied, "nothing has changed how I feel."

title: Ravens' Flowers 'super frustrated' by latest late-game fumble
summary: Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers said he was "super frustrated" after having the ball ripped away around midfield in the final two minutes of a loss to the Chargers on Monday night.
full_text:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- In his first comments since his critical fourth quarter fumble Monday night, Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers was terse in explaining what he needs to do to stop his costly late-game turnovers.
"Protect the ball," Flowers said Wednesday.
This marked the first time Flowers spoke since he had the ball ripped away around midfield in the final two minutes of a 23-20 loss to the Los Angeles Chargers . Flowers did not talk to reporters after the game.
Flowers' turnover led to the Chargers' first win of the season and the Ravens' fifth straight loss.
Flowers, who was curt throughout his 2½-minute media session, said he is "super frustrated."
"Because that's the drive we got to go in the game on," Flowers said. "We were supposed to go get the win, at least to get a tie out of that."
Flowers has four fourth-quarter fumbles since 2023, the most among all NFL wide receivers over that span. All four of Flowers' fourth-quarter fumbles led to losses, including Baltimore's 17-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in the 2023 AFC championship game.
On Monday night, he had the ball pulled away when he was trying to cut back and gain more yards.
Asked if he feels pressure to make plays with the Ravens' offense struggling, Flowers replied, "Playmakers make plays. So, every opportunity you get to touch the ball, you want to make a play. So, I wouldn't say it's pressure; I'd just say it's just playing football."
The Ravens (4-6), who currently have the NFL's second-longest losing streak, had their wide receivers work on a ball security drill at Wednesday's practice. Flowers, who leads Baltimore in receptions (49), receiving yards (688) and touchdown catches (3), has produced 54% of his receiving yards after the catch.
"You want the ball in his hands, but you also want to understand the situation [and] understand what they're going to be trying to do," Ravens coach Jesse Minter said after the game. "[It's important to] know when the journey's over and know when you're fighting for extra yards."

title: The NFL's current worst team? Lamar-less Ravens making that case
summary: The Ravens have gone 38 days without a win. It has been 24 days since they've had a lead.
full_text:
BALTIMORE -- In the final seconds of Monday night's 23-20 loss to the winless Los Angeles Chargers , Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry voiced his displeasure on the sideline while looking up at the scoreboard. 
 
 "This is horrible," Henry said. 
 
 In a matter of weeks, the Ravens have gone from being a Super Bowl contender to a team facing a once unthinkable question: Is Baltimore currently the NFL's worst team? The Lamar Jackson -less Ravens have certainly looked like it. 
 
 Over the last four weeks, Baltimore has a minus-74 point differential -- 21 points worse than any other NFL team. During this stretch, in which Jackson has been limited to one snap because of ankle and right thumb injuries, the Ravens offense ranks 30th in scoring (13.3 points) and their defense is 28th (31.8). 
 
 As far as where the Ravens' frustration ranks, let's just say it's off the charts. 
 
 Asked about the level of urgency on the team, Henry snapped back, "How many have we lost in a row? OK, so the urgency should tell you right there. I don't mean to be rude, but you all are asking questions I think you all know the answer to." 
 
 The Ravens have gone 38 days without a win. It's been 24 days since they've had a lead. 
 
 Baltimore has not led at any point in its past three games. The Ravens haven't had a stretch like this in 19 years. 
 
 
 
 The message from Ravens coach Jesse Minter to his players: There's no more margin for error. 
 
 "Honestly, we have a two-game stretch before our bye to stay alive," Minter said. "That's really where it's at." 
 
 After a 4-1 start, Baltimore has seen its season fall apart. The Ravens (4-6) now have a better chance at a top-five pick in the 2027 draft (8.6%) than a playoff spot (4.1%), according to ESPN Analytics. 
 
 ESPN's Football Power Index is projecting Baltimore to win one of its final seven games (Week 16 against the Cleveland Browns ). After playing on Monday night, the Ravens have a quick turnaround before playing at the Carolina Panthers (4-5) on Sunday (1 p.m. ET, Fox) and at the Houston Texans (3-6) the following week. 
 
 "It's going to be about getting up off the mat and coming back to work," Minter said. "And I think we have the guys to do that, but we have to do it. We keep talking about things, and [we need] more action." 
 
 The Ravens' problems range from self-inflicted mistakes to missed assignments on defense to the inability to run the ball. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 BALTIMORE'S ISSUE ON offense has been getting out of its own way. The Ravens have been flagged for a league-worst 55 offensive penalties. 
 
 On Monday night, Baltimore hurt itself with a turnover. On a potential comeback drive, wide receiver Zay Flowers had the ball ripped out of his grasp around midfield with two minutes remaining. 
 
 Flowers left the locker room as soon as reporters entered, leaving others to explain his critical mistake. 
 
 
 
 "I mean, he should have held onto the ball," Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton said. "There are plays that everybody has given up, that I've given up. That's my teammate, and he has made countless plays but he's human, too. The Ravens aren't the Ravens without him, and we believe in him. We love him." 
 
 This was Flowers' fourth fumble in the fourth quarter since 2023 (including playoffs), the most among wide receivers during this span. He also made a costly mistake in the 2023 AFC Championship Game, when he fumbled near the goal line in the fourth quarter of a 17-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs . Flowers did not talk after that game, too. 
 
 "He has made plays time and time again, and he's helped this team win a lot of games," tight end Mark Andrews said. "He's a guy who's going to learn from his mistakes and get better from this. I think that at the end of the day, we have to have each other's backs and be on one accord. We talk about that and just [to] stay together, and I for sure have his back." 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 JESSE MINTER LANDED  the Ravens head coach job, in part, because of his defensive expertise. So far, Baltimore is on pace to give up the second-most points in team history. 
 
 The Ravens were no match for the top three quarterbacks in the AFC. Joe Burrow put up 35 points on them. Josh Allen totaled 36 points. Trevor Lawrence racked up 33 points. 
 
 Then, on Monday night, it wasn't about the quarterback. It was the collapse of the Baltimore run defense. 
 
 The common denominator in all those games: There is a disconnect on defense. 
 
 "I think the particular reason is everyone wasn't doing their job play in and play out," Ravens middle linebacker Roquan Smith said. "We can all put a hand in it. So, we have to get better. It just comes down to the details. Each and every player has to hone in on their details at the end of the day and be able to come out and play the game the way we want to play." 
 
 The Ravens are on pace to allow 440 points, which would fall one point shy of the franchise record (441 in the inaugural season 1996). Trey Hendrickson , the prized free agent addition, has two sacks and seven quarterback hits in eight games. Marlon Humphrey , the team's most experienced cornerback, has allowed the fifth-most passing yards in coverage (425) this season, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. 
 
 Minter believes accountability goes beyond showing up to meetings and practice on time. It's about attention to details. 
 
 "Accountability means a lot of different things," Minter said, "but to me, it's really what happens on the field when it matters." 
 
 Still, the long-standing identity of this franchise has been to stop the run and establish the run. Can the Ravens do both at a high level? 
 
 "I think we have guys that can," Minter said, "but talk is cheap." 
 
 
 
 
 THE RAVENS SET a team record on Monday night that they would rather forget. Baltimore managed no yards rushing in the first half. 
 
 "Unacceptable," Minter said before adding, "It's embarrassing." 
 
 The Ravens offensive line continually got pushed back, and Henry struggled to break tackles. Henry was hit at the line or behind it on eight of 10 carries, which resulted in 10 total rushing yards. 
 
 Baltimore finished with 16 yards rushing, which is the third fewest in Ravens history. 
 
 "We're just not doing a good enough job to be efficient in the run game," Henry said. "Sixteen total yards is a clear explanation." 
 
 What's also clear is how the Ravens perform with and without Jackson, who is expected to miss six to 10 weeks after having right thumb surgery in early November. Baltimore acquired quarterback Jacoby Brissett to try to keep the season alive in case Jackson can return, but the playoff chances are quickly dwindling without the two-time NFL Most Valuable Player. 
 
 With Jackson as their starting quarterback, the Ravens are 82-38 (.683) and average 27.6 points per game. Without Jackson as its starter since 2019, Baltimore is 7-16 (.304) and average 17.4 points per game. 
 
 "Lamar is a big part of what we do, but it's a grown-man's league," Henry said. "It hasn't been good enough, and I think losing five in a row shows that. So, of course having [No.] 8 will help, but at the end of the day, we have to go out there and do our jobs."

title: Fantasy buzz: Kirk Cousins, Stefon Diggs bring reliability to fantasy lineups
summary: Every lineup needs consistent, week-to-week performers and Tristan has three players to start down the stretch.
full_text:
As an avid fan of -- and our primary ranker for -- our new Knockout fantasy football game this season, I'm all about the consistency kings.

 (On an aside, it's a great week to join a new Knockout league , being that you need only eight managers to play!)

 Sure, those win-your-matchup-all-by-himself scores from  George Pickens , Jordan Love or Tee Higgins  the past three weeks are plenty of fun. But bolstering your lineup with the "old reliables" is important, too, and that's especially so in a game where avoiding a low statistical floor is paramount.

 That's why last week's trade which sent veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders to the Minnesota Vikings piqued my interest. Cousins is tied for the fourth-most games as a top-10 fantasy quarterback this season (five), but he has also been the most consistent player at his position. Aside from his five top-10 weeks, Cousins' other games saw him finish 11th, 17th, 18th, 19th and 21st, and in only three of those was his score more than five points beneath the No. 10 score.

 Best yet, you can surely get Cousins for a song in trade, being that he has exceeded the one-third (33.3%) start rate in ESPN leagues only once all season (in Week 6), and sits at only 65.1% rostered today. He fits, almost perfectly, the mold of the old-reliable backup/weekly superflex quarterback. To that end, in a freshly drafting Knockout league of mine Tuesday night, my No. 1 quarterback target was Trevor Lawrence -- more on that in a moment -- but my backup was Cousins. It's a pairing that will bring much comfort at a discounted price from many of the other name brands.

 

 Cousins' reliability also benefits his receivers, who warrant trade inquiries as well. Justin Jefferson 's best seasons came with Cousins under center, and Jordan Addison 's thumb surgery, which is expected to cost him multiple weeks, locks Jefferson into the alpha role in Minnesota. Jefferson had a season-high 13 targets and 16.4 fantasy points in Cousins' return, which bolstered Jefferson's fantasy WR1 status. Tight end T.J. Hockenson   should also benefit from Cousins' installation and Addison's absence.

 To put a bow on it, the Vikings have the second-most-favorable remaining schedule for quarterbacks, and the fifth-most favorable for wide receivers.

 Cousins and his Vikings teammates, aren't the only ones on my consistency-oriented trade target list. Here are two others:

 Bhayshul Tuten , RB, Jacksonville Jaguars : I'm all-in on the Jaguars in fantasy, as they're on an unreal run over the past year, and they match up brilliantly, schedule-wise , down the stretch. It's the reason for my Lawrence interest in Tuesday's draft, but when examining an offense likely to remain on a roll, the running back is certainly someone you want. Tuten's 56% rushing share is 13th at the position, and only 14 running backs have delivered a top-25 "start worthy" score more often. In a season of injury-driven fantasy lineup volatility, he's a "set it and forget it" weekly RB2.

 Stefon Diggs , WR, Washington Commanders : He's a ho-hum type, started in greater than 40% of ESPN leagues only three times all season, but someone has to catch passes in Washington. Diggs has a 20% target rate for the season, and he's tied for 11th among wide receivers in top-25 fantasy weeks. Antonio Williams might be the exciting, high-ceiling receiver in the Commanders' offense, but there's Diggs week after week, delivering his 10-15 points to his fantasy managers. Also be aware that the Commanders have the position's fourth-most-favorable remaining schedule .

 - Tristan H. Cockcroft 

 

 Nov. 17: Henry has confusing night, Hampton breaks through 

 Derrick Henry had an interesting game on Monday night. I mean, it's hard to say he had a bad game when he scored 19 fantasy points. However, it was one of those games where you're happy with the result, but worried about what it means moving forward. Henry was quite inefficient as he turned his 15 touches into just 20 total yards. His 10 rushing yards are the second fewest he has had in any game with double-digit touches in his career. It was his also fifth consecutive game running for less than 60 yards.

 

 While Henry's struggles on the ground are worrisome, there's some good news. He was targeted much more frequently with Jacoby Brissett   under center for the  Baltimore Ravens .  His five catches tied for the second-highest total of his career. More targets could help make up for the lack of ground production. Henry has a potential rebound opportunity next week against the  Carolina Panthers  who rank top-two in both rushing touchdowns and fantasy PPG allowed to RBs.

 Other takeaways from Monday's game 

 
 The Ravens were not afraid to let Brissett air it out in his first start for the team. He threw 49 times, finishing with 340 passing yards and 11.8 fantasy points. Yes, the fact both Baltimore touchdowns came on the ground hurt his fantasy total, but the volume should not be ignored. With all the QB injuries, plus six teams taking their bye in Week 11, Brissett is in play as a streaming option against the Panthers. 
 Zay Flowers finished with six catches for 74 yards on seven targets. He has surpassed 11 fantasy points in every game -- except the two with QB  Joe Fagnano . That safe floor, paired with his upside, means he should be started every week. 
 Mark Andrews had his best game of the season, turning eight targets into eight catches for 82 yards. He finished with 16.2 fantasy points, all of which were season highs. I believe a resurgence has arrived for the star tight end, due to the team's QB change. Brissett has always targeted tight ends at a high rate. Fantasy managers in need of TE help should try to get Andrews on their roster this week -- whether it be adding off the waiver wire or trading for him. 
 Omarion Hampton had the best night for the no-longer winless  Los Angeles Chargers . He turned 22 carries into 105 yards and a touchdown. It was his second game of the season playing on over 60% of snaps and he reached 100 yards and scored a touchdown in both. Hopefully, the Chargers will continue to feature him. He has a favorable matchup coming up against the  New York Jets , who allow the second-most rushing yards before contact per carry. Consider him to be a low-end RB2 during the upcomng Bye-mageddon. 
 Justin Herbert had his best game of the season, scoring 16.26 fantasy points. He threw for only 129 yards with no touchdowns. However, the bulk of his fantasy points came via his legs, as he ran for 51 yards and a score. I'm reluctant to jump back on his bandwagon, though, due to the lack of passing results. 
 Tre' Harris finished with 86 receiving yards, which is even more impressive considering how few yards Herbert actually threw for in this one. Harris benefitted from  Ladd McConkey 's absence and is worth adding in deeper 12-team leagues. That said, I would be reluctant to trust any piece of this team's passing attack right now. 
 
 -- Michael F. Florio 

 
 Nov. 16: Who got the ball in Week 10? 
 

 The box score doesn't tell you everything. Here are the roles and usage trends from Sunday that stood out.

 New England Patriots vs. Detroit Lions 
 Rhamondre Stevenson  tried to play through his knee injury, but finished with just seven touches and 1.5 fantasy points. He narrowly outsnapped Corey Kiner , who had more rushing attempts (10-6) and ran more routes (14-12). Stevenson handled most of the backfield work early in the game but didn't play in the fourth quarter with the game out of reach. The upcoming bye week gives Stevenson more time to recover and, with TreVeyon Henderson on IR, he should remain the team's lead back. New England has upcoming favorable matchups against the Chargers and Bills, but much will depend on Drake Maye 's health .

title: NFL survivor power rankings: Why this is the week to use the Bills or the Texans
summary: ESPN NFL survivor pool strategy, predictions and ranking the top six options for Week 11.
full_text:
Each of the first eight weeks saw an underdog of a touchdown or more pull off the upset, but since then, the last two weeks have been dominated by favorites. Closing line favorites of at least four points are 16-1 outright over the last two weeks, with the only loss coming by the Houston Texans last week against the Cleveland Browns .

 Week 11 is shaping up to be another great week for favorites. As of Wednesday morning, the average point spread is 8.1, which would be the highest prior to the final two weeks of the season since 1987.

 Five teams are double-digit favorites, including the two biggest favorites all season -- the Buffalo Bills and the Kansas City Chiefs . There are also two more favorites of at least a touchdown, and the 1-8 Los Angeles Chargers are also laying more than a field goal.

 

 With so many strong options, the biggest decisions involve looking at selection rate, future value and your path to Week 18. Every one of the double-digit favorites has multiple additional weeks where they will likely be similar-sized favorites down the road.

 Out of the five double-digit favorites, the one with the least future value is the Chicago Bears . However, they are currently tracking to be the most-selected team on ESPN.

 The Bills will likely be the chalk pick in most contests, though not on ESPN, where they are 30% available. The Chiefs are the other massive favorite, but they are 13% available on ESPN, and even lower in some other contests. If you somehow have them available, they are a fine pick, but you can also save them for later when they will be even less owned with potentially fewer other elite options.

 The Texans are the third-biggest favorites according to the betting market, but with so many other options, the 3-6 team playing on Thursday could slip through the cracks and be a great contrarian pick.

 

 The Denver Broncos are the last double-digit favorite, and they are also widely available. They have five future weeks with at least a 75% chance to win, blending models from ESPN Analytics and Mike Clay, tied for most of any team. This could be one of the last times to get them as a big favorite at relatively light selection, but you are giving up immediate win equity and the chance to use them down the road.

 As for the rest of the board, the Dallas Cowboys are the only other team that combines strong win probability with lack of future value, especially if you can cover next week when they host the Philadelphia Eagles . However, Dallas is currently 21% selected, so you aren't getting an edge there at all.

 In double-pick pools, the Carolina Panthers , Pittsburgh Steelers and Chargers are strong plays with Carolina being the preferred option if available.

 Note: Odds by DraftKings and subject to change. Future value based on Mike Clay's cheat sheet .  

 

 1. Buffalo Bills (vs. Miami Dolphins ) 
 

 The Bills likely only have two more non-Week 18 games after this week where they will be huge favorites. One is in Week 13 against the New England Patriots , when the Denver Broncos will likely be heavy chalk against the Dolphins. The other is in Week 17 where most of the other biggest projected favorites are widely unavailable ( San Francisco 49ers , Jacksonville Jaguars , Cincinnati Bengals , Kansas City Chiefs and Minnesota Vikings ). Just keep in mind that the Bills are much more widely available in non-ESPN contests, and if that's the case in your contest, then I would likely pivot to another option, as their ownership should be a lot higher than it will be on ESPN.

 
 Chance to win: 95% (ESPN Analytics), 96% (Mike Clay) 
 Spread: Bills -16.5 (-1450 moneyline) 
 Notable games: at Patriots (Week 13), at Dolphins (Week 17), vs. Jets (Week 18) 
 Availability: 30% 
 ESPN Selection: 14% 
 

 2. Houston Texans (vs. Indianapolis Colts ) 
 

 The Texans are the best combination of lack of team quality and current win equity. The two weeks down the road to watch are next week (vs. Ravens) and Week 16 (at Eagles), though Week 18 could be more relevant with the Texans than most teams, since they are unlikely to rest starters. If you are concerned about them playing on Thursday, note that double-digit home favorites are 29-2 on Thursdays since the NFL instituted "Thursday Night Football" in 2006.

 
 Chance to win: 74% (ESPN Analytics), 87% (Mike Clay) 
 Spread: Texans -12.5 (-750 moneyline) 
 Notable games: vs. Ravens (Week 12), at Eagles (Week 16), vs. Titans (Week 18) 
 Availability: 68% 
 ESPN Selection: 7% 
 

 3. Chicago Bears (vs. New Orleans Saints ) 

 The Bears will be a popular pick this week, as they are widely available in most contests. On ESPN, they are 70% available and currently 29% selected. Unlike the other favorites, the Bears have only one more great opportunity to use them (Week 14), so you give up the least future value using them now. The trade-off is that you are eating a lot more chalk this week, while getting slightly lower win equity than the other big favorites.

 
 Chance to win: 79% (ESPN Analytics), 89% (Mike Clay) 
 Spread: Bears -11.5 (-700 moneyline) 
 Notable games: at Dolphins (Week 14) 
 Availability: 70% 
 ESPN Selection: 29% 
 

 4. Denver Broncos (vs. Las Vegas Raiders ) 
 

 According to ESPN Analytics, the Broncos have played the second-toughest schedule in the NFL thus far behind only the Arizona Cardinals , but they have the easiest remaining slate. That means that Denver is both widely available and the holder of plenty of future value. Week 13 is the most appealing game of that group when they host the Dolphins, though they should be extremely popular. Both ESPN Analytics and Mike Clay's models also have the Broncos as bigger favorites than the betting market, which could make them undervalued this week.

 
 Chance to win: 86% (ESPN Analytics), 92% (Mike Clay) 
 Spread: Broncos -10 (-575 moneyline) 
 Notable games: vs. Dolphins (Week 13), at Jets (Week 14), at Raiders (Week 15), at Patriots (Week 17), vs. Chargers (Week 18) 
 Availability: 60% 
 ESPN Selection: 7% 
 

 5. Kansas City Chiefs (vs. Arizona Cardinals ) 
 

 The Chiefs look like an amazing choice, with 92% win probability combined with extremely low selection. However, that low selection is largely due to them being the least-available team in Survivor (13%). As a result, if you have other options this week, I would save them for later when they will be even lower-picked and there might not be as many huge favorites to choose from.

 
 Chance to win: 88% (ESPN Analytics), 96% (Mike Clay) 
 Spread: Chiefs -16.5 (-1450 moneyline) 
 Notable games: vs. Patriots (Week 15), at Chargers (Week 17), vs. Raiders (Week 18) 
 Availability: 13% 
 ESPN Selection: 6% 
 

 6. Dallas Cowboys (vs. Tennessee Titans ) 
 The Cowboys are similar favorites to the Bears and Texans, according to ESPN Analytics and Mike Clay, and the only other time to use them would be next week against the Eagles. That would make them a strong pick, except they are currently 21% selected on ESPN. That rate would make them very difficult to justify this week, but I expect that number to be lower in most groups, especially where the Bills are widely available. And the less they are picked this week, the more they will be picked next week against the Eagles.

 
 Chance to win: 80% (ESPN Analytics), 83% (Mike Clay) 
 Spread: Cowboys -8.5 (-380 moneyline) 
 Notable games: vs. Eagles (Week 12) 
 Availability: 80% 
 ESPN Selection: 21%

title: Monroe Freeling, Lee Hunter top Panthers' rookie report at Week 11
summary: Will this year's draft class have a major impact on Carolina's second half of the season and potential postseason?
full_text:
The NFC South-leading Carolina Panthers (4-5) will look to get back to .500 in Week 11 when they host the Baltimore Ravens (4-6) on Sunday ( 1 p.m. ET, Fox ).

 The Panthers will rely on a slew of young players, including several members of the 2026 NFL draft class . That group of rookies, like the Panthers as a team, has had its share of ups and downs over the past 10 weeks. And if the class, as a whole, can avoid the dreaded rookie wall, Carolina should be set up for success over the next eight games.

 Last year's draft class -- headlined by wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan , outside linebackers Nic Scourton and Princely Umanmielen and safety Lathan Ransom  -- was instrumental in helping the Panthers clinch their first division title since 2015.

 Will this year's group have a similar impact down the season's second-half stretch? Let's check in on the rookies, beginning with the Panthers' top pick:

 

 Monroe Freeling , OT, Georgia 
 

 Draft: No. 19, 1st round 
 Stats to know: Eight games (seven starts) at right tackle; six sacks and 27 total pressures allowed on 305 pass sets, according to NFL Next Gen Stats

 Freeling, at 22, is the second-youngest player on the team (behind linebacker Nic Scourton ). He was drafted to be a foundational offensive lineman, but it was clear the Carolina brass saw him as a developmental prospect with excellent traits heading into his rookie offseason.

 

 However, after longtime right tackle Taylor Moton was diagnosed with blood clots this past summer, Freeling -- who primarily played left tackle at Georgia -- was thrust into a starting role at a somewhat unfamiliar position.

 Freeling has had predictable growing pains with a steep learning curve. He has gone up against some notable pass rushers and been the victim of quite a few tough moments in protection.

 But in Week 10's win against the New Orleans Saints , Freeling -- the presumed starting right tackle for the remainder of the season with Moton recovering from ankle surgery -- had his most encouraging performance yet. He allowed one QB pressure in 34 pass sets in the road win, per NFL Next Gen Stats.

 

 Lee Hunter , DT, Texas Tech 
 

 Draft: No. 49, Second round 
 Stats to know: Nine games (five starts); 21 tackles (two for loss) and two QB hits

 Hunter has played 34% of the Panthers' defensive snaps. He is working in a rotation that features Derrick Brown , Bobby Brown III and Turk Wharton at the top. And while he is already working with the second playcaller of his pro career -- interim defensive coordinator Todd Wash took over for Ejiro Evero in Week 9 -- Hunter has shown major flashes in limited playing time, particularly against the run.

 Hunter has played just 28 snaps over the past two games under Wash, but his impact has been noticeable, producing five total tackles (two for loss) and a QB hit.

 

 Chris Brazzell II , WR, Tennessee 
 

 Draft: No. 83, third round 
 Stats to know: N/A (on injured reserve since training camp)

 Brazzell injured his left knee during training camp in July. The team decided the receiver should undergo MCL surgery, and he has been sidelined on season-ending IR since .

 John Metchie III , Brycen Tremayne and Xavier Legette have filled out the wide receiver rotation behind McMillan and Jalen Coker .

 

 Will Lee III , CB, Texas A&M 
 

 Draft: No. 129, fourth round 
 Stats to know: Seven games (four starts); 33 tackles, seven pass breakups, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery; allowed 25 catches for 317 yards and a touchdown on 45 targets, per NFL Next Gen Stats

 Lee has missed the past two games because of a left hamstring injury. However, he has made the most of his opportunities when healthy, including serving as the No. 1 cornerback in the lineup with Mike Jackson (groin) and Jaycee Horn (quad) sidelined.

 A natural press-man coverage cornerback, Lee stands to benefit from Wash's more aggressive defense when he returns to action.

 

 Sam Hecht , C, Kansas State 
 

 Draft: No. 144, fifth round 
 Stats to know: Seven games (11 snaps on offense).

 Hecht fell to the fifth round despite considerable draft hype in the spring. He has yet to play a meaningful snap on offense, as Luke Fortner has remained the starting center all season. Corey Bullock , claimed off waivers in August, has seemingly succeeded Hecht as Fortner's backup entering Week 11.

 

 Zakee Wheatley , S, Penn State 
 

 Draft: No. 151, fifth round 
 Stats to know: Eight games (five starts); 33 tackles, four pass breakups, an interception and a forced fumble

 Wheatley has been the steal of the Panthers' draft class so far. Despite being a Week 1 inactive, he has produced two turnovers and become a staple of the secondary this season.

 Against the Saints, Wheatley surpassed veteran Nick Scott in the lineup, playing all 61 snaps. He didn't surrender a catch in New Orleans.

 

 Jackson Kuwatch , LB, Miami (Ohio) 
 

 Draft: No. 227, seventh round 
 Stats to know: Nine games; 197 special teams snaps (80% of total special teams plays); 11 tackles and a forced fumble

 Kuwatch was a one-year wonder in college. He was drafted as a flier with upside in the seventh round, and so far, he has been stellar on special teams. He has received the occasional snap on defense (28 total), so he's getting eased into action in that phase.

 

 Aaron Hall , DT, Duke 
 

 Draft: Undrafted 
 Stats to know: Nine games (one start); 19 tackles (one for loss) and two QB hits.

 The Durham, North Carolina, native has made the most of his familiar surroundings. Hall has played 30% of the defensive snaps this season, despite being in a heavy rotation, and he has made those snaps count. He has also logged 47 snaps on special teams.

title: Panthers secondary set for boost with return of CB Mike Jackson
summary: Panthers starting cornerback Mike Jackson, who has been sidelined since injuring his groin in Week 3, plans to be in the lineup Sunday against the Ravens.
full_text:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- Carolina Panthers starting cornerback Mike Jackson (groin) plans to be in the lineup Sunday against the Baltimore Ravens at Bank of America Stadium.
"I'm game ready, so I'll be out there on Sunday," Jackson said after Wednesday's practice.
Jackson had his 21-day practice window opened last week, but he didn't play in Carolina's 20-17 win over the New Orleans Saints .
The 29-year-old cornerback was a full participant in the first workout of Week 11, and coach Dave Canales noted that Jackson and running back Jonathon Brooks (groin) were on the cusp of returning from injured reserve.
"I think they're ready," Canales said. "We do have to work through all the different things with the roster ... so that's the part that [general manager] Dan [Morgan] and I have to talk about, but these guys are hungry to get back out there and so we're going to try to find a way for them to help us."
Brooks underwent core muscle surgery after leaving the Panthers' Week 2 win over the Falcons with a groin injury. Brooks has played in just five of 43 regular season-games since being selected with the 46th pick in the 2024 NFL draft. During his two games this season, Brooks collected 30 rushing yards and 43 receiving yards on 11 total touches. He's yet to score his first NFL touchdown in his limited action.
Jackson injured his groin in a Week 3 loss to the Cleveland Browns and underwent surgery the following week. Jackson and fellow starting cornerback Jaycee Horn (quad), who was also injured against the Browns, have missed the Panthers' past six games.
Rookie Will Lee III , Chau Smith-Wade and practice squad call-ups Marco Wilson and Corey Thornton have played in place of the injured starting cornerbacks as the Panthers have gone 3-3 in their absence. Lee, who has missed the past two weeks with a left hamstring injury, was a full participant Wednesday and Canales said he expected the rookie to play in Week 11 as well.
And while Lee has flashed during his rookie season, Jackson's return should provide a proven boost to the secondary. Jackson led the NFL with 19 pass breakups last season. He has also produced six interceptions during his 37 games with the Panthers.
"On Sundays, knowing that you have a guy like that out there, it's huge," quarterback Bryce Young said.
The Panthers are also weighing the status of versatile offensive lineman Brady Christensen .
The 2021 third-round pick had his 21-day practice window opened in Week 9 and the Panthers have until Tuesday of next week to activate him onto the 53-man roster.
If Carolina does not activate Christensen before the deadline, he will revert back to season-ending injured reserve.
"Brady is ready to go, too," Canales said. "And again, it's just a matter of timing, space on the roster and all those things, and we're up against it now with Brady, with his window being open."
While Jackson, Brooks, Lee and Christensen were all full participants Wednesday, tight ends Tommy Tremble (knee) and Darren Waller (knee) were sidelined. Canales said the Panthers will monitor their injuries, and if one or both were to miss time, 2024 fourth-round pick Ja'Tavion Sanders could be asked to play Sunday. Sanders has played in only one game this season.
Linebacker Bobby Okereke (foot), running back Chuba Hubbard (rest) and special teams ace/linebacker Isaiah Simmons (knee) were also held out of the workout. Outside linebacker Trevis Gipson (ankle) was listed as limited.
Young (foot) also appeared on the injury report. However, Canales and Young both said the QB -- who was a full participant -- had no restrictions during the workout.

title: NFL flexes Raiders-Browns to replace Pats-Chargers in SNF slot for Week 12
summary: The NFL has flexed the Raiders-Browns Week 12 game into NBC's "Sunday Night Football" slot.
full_text:
The NFL has flexed the Las Vegas Raiders - Cleveland Browns Week 12 game into NBC's "Sunday Night Football" slot, the league announced Tuesday.
The Nov. 29 matchup will replace the previously scheduled New England Patriots - Los Angeles Chargers game, which will move to the 4:05 p.m. ET slot.
Instead, Cleveland will host Las Vegas in a primetime game that will have huge implications in the AFC playoff race.
The Browns (6-4) currently are the AFC's seventh seed, holding the third and final wild card spot in the conference. Cleveland is 4-0 at home for the first time since 1963.
The Raiders (4-6) are two games behind Cleveland in the standings. Las Vegas lost to the Seattle Seahawks in Week 10 in first overall pick Fernando Mendoza 's first career start. The Raiders will face the Denver Broncos on the road in Week 11.
The New England-Los Angeles rematch from last season's AFC wild card round game has been diminished with the Chargers' 1-8 start and Patriots quarterback Drake Maye being sidelined with a right ankle injury. New England (5-5) has dropped two straight and three of its last four.
