title: Pettine to take over defensive playcalling for Cowboys; Parker still DC
summary: Christian Parker will remain as the Cowboys' defensive coordinator, but Mike Pettine will call the defense on game day, coach Brian Schottenhiemer said.
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas -- Despite Christian Parker losing playcalling duties after just 10 games, Dallas Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said he believes in his defensive coordinator's future, but he is concerned about the present with his team 4-6 and fighting for contention in the NFC East.
While Parker will retain his title as defensive coordinator, senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine will call the defense for the rest of the season.
"He's still running meetings. He's still leading walk-throughs. He's still doing all of those things," Schottenheimer said. "The only thing that's different is he's not calling the plays on game day."
The Cowboys have turned to Mike Pettine to take over playcalling for a defense that ranks 30th or worse in several key categories this season.
A day after Parker's defense allowed 584 yards, the most given up in a home game in team history, in the 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers , Schottenheimer and Parker had their first discussions about a change in roles. By mid-morning Tuesday, Schottenheimer had made the decision to make Pettine the defensive playcaller for the rest of the season.
"Watching over the past few weeks, looking back at some things, I think that the different perspective was good for us," Schottenheimer said.
Through 10 games, the Cowboys are last in total yards (393.8), last in run defense (154.1) and last in third-down defense (48.8%).
Pettine last called defenses in 2020 as the Green Bay Packers ' defensive coordinator. He served as the coordinator of the New York Jets , with Schottenheimer on that staff, and the Buffalo Bills . In 2014-15, he was head coach of the Cleveland Browns .
He joined the Cowboys before Week 5.
Schottenheimer informed the players of the move at Wednesday's team meeting.
"I was upfront and honest with them. And again, Christian Parker is a huge part of what we're trying to build here and that he is our defensive coordinator," Schottenheimer said. "He is our leader. He is not changing any of those things, but that I do feel that in the best interest of winning that Pett's calling the game is going to help us get to where we want to get to."
Parker became the youngest defensive coordinator in team history when he was hired in January after a two-season run as the Philadelphia Eagles ' defensive passing game coordinator.
He earned the job after an exhaustive search of nine candidates to replace Matt Eberflus after the Cowboys finished the 2025 season as the 30th-ranked defense and gave up 511 points.
There was praise for the hire considering Parker's history with cornerbacks Patrick Surtain II in Denver and Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean in Philadelphia.
Parker changed the Cowboys to a 3-4 front with principles from Vic Fangio's zone-based scheme Parker learned with the Broncos and Eagles.
The Cowboys made a number of moves on defense, including signing safety Jalen Thompson to the biggest free agent deal in more than a decade (three years, $33 million), trading for linebacker Rashan Gary in the offseason and cornerback Joey Porter Jr . in season, and drafting safety Caleb Downs and linebacker Malachi Lawrence in the first round.
There were promising signs in training camp and in joint practices against the Los Angeles Rams and New Orleans Saints , but the Cowboys have allowed more than 20 points in every game, a streak that has now reached 17 games over the past two seasons.
But it has not translated to regular-season success.
In the past three games, the Cowboys have given up six plays of at least 50 yards, including scoring plays of 74, 70 and 66 yards to the 49ers. The Cowboys have given up an NFL-high nine plays of 50 yards or more.
"I think Christian is an incredibly strong and committed man who wants to get it right," Schottenheimer said. "I love the fact that he and I could have the real conversations and honest conversations and we talked through a number of different things. But at the end of the day, this decision was made because again, I do think it gives us the best chance to win. And CP understands that the decision has been made and he wants to help us beat the Titans."
Schottenheimer said the Cowboys' next two games against less-than-stellar offensive teams in Tennessee and the Eagles had nothing to do with the timing.
It was done with an eye toward saving a season.
"If we don't make the playoffs, it's a failure. The season's a failure," Schottenheimer said. "That's what we play for. We play to win and we play to make the playoffs, and we've got seven games left and again, we need to put together a run of success."
The defensive players who spoke Wednesday supported Parker. Defensive tackle Kenny Clark said he was "bummed" for Parker. Downs said the news "hurt his heart."
Downs and Parker have been joined at the hip in meetings and the practice field since the Cowboys selected Downs in the first round. Downs said Parker remained the same energetic coach he was before the move.
"He's still somebody that we're playing for in the building and somebody that we love," Downs said. "He's still in the building, still in the meetings, still talk to him every day ... still one of the people that we're looking to have around. It's like looking to play for one of our sources of motivation."
Clark was with Pettine in Green Bay.
"Coach Pettine, he's a great coach," Clark said. "We're going to be running, doing the same things that we've been doing. It's not a completely new defense. As players, we've got to still be intentional about what we're doing, prepare the right way. It's no magic playcall or nothing that Pett is going to be able to give us. So it's our job to go out there and execute the game plan, whatever it is."
Said defensive tackle Quinnen Williams , "Everything is on us [as players]. We're on the field. No matter what play gets called, no matter who call it, we've got to execute the play. And that's going to be around the NFL, that's going to be youth football, college football, NFL, man. Once the play gets called, no matter who call it, the players on the field got to execute it. And that's what we haven't been doing. We got to do it going forward."

title: Why Packers can't protect Jordan Love or rush successfully
summary: The two-year demise of the Packers' offensive line began on March 10, 2025, and has no end in sight.
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- The beginning of the downfall of the Green Bay Packers ' offensive line can be traced to a specific day: March 10, 2025.

 That was when general manager Brian Gutekunst signed then- San Francisco 49ers guard Aaron Banks to a four-year, $77 million free agent deal. Not only have the Packers not gotten their money's worth out of Banks due to injuries and poor performance, but his signing set in a motion a game of musical chairs at just about every position on the line.

 The result was what the Packers put on display in their most recent showing, the obliteration of their pass protection by the Minnesota Vikings in Sunday's 30-10 loss at Lambeau Field. In between that March 2025 day and Sunday has been 20 months of trying to get the offensive line settled.

 Combine that with a position coach, Luke Butkus, and an offensive coordinator, Adam Stenavich, who have come under fire, and there's plenty of blame to go around for nearly two seasons' worth of offensive line issues.

 "I think it's easy to pinpoint and point the finger and everybody wants to pinpoint blame, but the blame can go to everybody," coach Matt LaFleur said this week. "It's all of us in this together. Certainly it starts with myself and then it goes to everybody else. It's coaches and players collectively."

 

 Don't forget about Gutekunst.

 He started all this by signing Banks, who had played all but six of his 2,464 snaps for the 49ers at left guard. The problem was the Packers already had a left guard. A two-time Pro Bowl left guard in Elgton Jenkins . To accommodate Banks, the Packers moved Jenkins to center for the 2025 season. From a business perspective, Jenkins wasn't thrilled with it and sat out part of the offseason program in the hope that the team would adjust his contract. Jenkins eventually returned without a new deal, fractured his lower leg halfway through last season and was released in March.

 In theory, Jenkins could have still been the Packers' left guard for this season had they never signed Banks because Jenkins had one year left on his contract when he was cut.

 This season, the Packers have started four different left guards -- Banks, Donovan Jennings , Jager Burton and Laken Tomlinson . In all, they've started seven different guards, counting the three at right guard ( Jacob Monk , Travis Glover and Tomlinson). It would have been eight had Kevin Zeitler not sustained a triceps injury in practice late last week. The in-season addition was set to start at right guard with Tomlinson back at left guard. Instead, the Packers went back to Glover at right guard.

 That means Banks, who took home $29 million last season and will make $18 million this season, not only wasn't viewed as the best option at his natural left guard spot but couldn't beat out Glover, a 2024 sixth-round pick who missed all of last season because of a shoulder injury.

 "We were going to shuffle up the O-line a little bit," LaFleur said after the Vikings' game. "I think Laken's been doing a pretty good job and we put him back to his natural position, and we were going to let Banks compete at the right guard, and he doesn't have a ton of time on task at that position, so we went the way we did tonight."

 

 To make matters worse, the Packers probably can't move on from Banks after the season. They converted his $9.5 million roster bonus in March into a signing bonus for immediate salary cap help, but it means the Packers would have to count $26.288 million in dead money on next year's cap if they release him in the offseason. The only tenable way to cut him would be as a post-June 1 cut next year, but that wouldn't erase the dead money.

 Meanwhile, the franchise left tackle they thought they picked in the first round of the 2024 draft, Jordan Morgan , didn't get his crack at the job until this season. Instead, they made Morgan play guard for two seasons, mostly as a backup or fill-in starter, for two years while they stuck with Rasheed Walker at left tackle. Walker finished on such a downer with a poor performance in the playoff loss at the Bears last season that the best he could do in free agency was a one-year, $4 million deal with the Panthers.

 In the 2025 draft, Gutekunst used a second-round pick on Anthony Belton , who also has bounced between guard and right tackle. He has played the latter ever since Zach Bako-Bewele , their best lineman, went down with a season-ending knee injury for the second straight season in Week 2.

 Gutekunst tried to fix the line in midstream earlier this season when he signed a trio of former first-round picks in Tomlinson, Zeitler and Mekhi Becton within the span of a week in late September.

 Tomlinson seemed to settle the line, and then the Packers lost center Sean Rhyan to an ankle injury in Week 7 against Detroit. John Williams , who had never taken a regular-season snap before, held up for a while in Rhyan's place until the Vikings game, where he sailed a shotgun snap wide left of quarterback Jordan Love , allowing the Vikings to recover the fumble.

 In all, Love was sacked eight times on Sunday. In two games against the blitz-happy Vikings, Love has been sacked 12 times and hit 27 times.

 "I hope it's just a Vikings thing," LaFleur said. "But you're as good as your last game and unfortunately, it wasn't good enough."

 There's reason to think it's more than just "a Vikings thing."

 Not only have they been unable to open up holes in a running game that ranks last in the NFL in rushing yards per game, but the Packers have a seasonlong pass block win rate of 31%, which is on track to be the worst by any team since ESPN first introduced the metric in 2017.

 

 It has affected Love even when the pressure hasn't gotten home -- such as the potential touchdown he missed to Christian Watson in the third quarter on Sunday when Love appeared to rush the throw even though he actually had time for a change.

 "Yeah, that affects a quarterback," Stenavich said. "Jordan will take ownership of it. He'll say, 'I've got to make that play,' obviously, because that's the kind of guy he is. But it's on everybody to make sure the quarterback feels comfortable in the pocket. Coaches, we've got to do a better job of making sure that happens, and the players on the field, definitely do too. So, again, it's on everybody."

 It may not get any easier the next time out. After this week's bye, the Packers play at the Rams, who feature two of the best pass rushers in the game in Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett .

 "I'm very confident in this team still," Love said. "It's a frustrating loss. We've talked about it. We've been here before this season. We've had some frustrating losses. We've had some good wins. So it's all about just getting back to work, cleaning it up.

 "Still a lot of season out in front of us. We get a little bit of a break to be able to get some guys back, get some bodies back. But yeah, we've just got to find ways to overcome and be better."

title: How Houston has banded together through backbreaking losses and adversity
summary: Houston enters "Thursday Night Football" against the Indianapolis Colts with a 32.4% chance of making the playoffs.
full_text:
HOUSTON -- A despondent Kamari Lassiter lumbered into a borderline vacant Houston Texans locker room following a Week 1 loss to the Buffalo Bills .

 An hour prior, Bills quarterback Josh Allen floated a 30-yard pass into the end zone with 1:48 remaining in the season opener -- a balloon pass that hit the hands of a falling Lassiter.

 The cornerback bobbled it, and the ball slipped out of his grasp and dribbled into the end zone. Laying side by side with the ball, Lassiter clutched it in disbelief.

 On the next play, Bills wideout Joshua Palmer spun Lassiter around and Allen zipped a touchdown pass to Palmer to go up 36-31 with 1:36 remaining. Quarterback C.J. Stroud & Co. tried to respond -- marching down the field with the game on the line -- but on third-and-goal, Stroud was sacked and fumbled, dropping Houston to 0-1.

 

 As Lassiter was slouched in front of his locker stall, still sporting his game worn white pants, he took notable pauses in response to questions. He noted that "a lot of the plays that happened" weren't up to the team's standard and his play just wasn't him.

 "Yeah, it was really bad for me," Lassiter said. "Man, I just feel like it was just not me. It was just not the best day at all."

 How did Lassiter handle a day where he allowed 95 yards in coverage, the game-winning score and a penalty in the second quarter that positioned the Bills on the 1-yard line, resulting in a touchdown? He went nearby to his mom's house and invited safety Calen Bullock and linebacker Jamal Hill over as he paced around in frustration.

 He was seeking the kind of brotherhood and unity that has kept a team with Super Bowl hype coming into the season mentally afloat through a disappointing 3-6 start. They have banded together, finding ways off the field to uplift one another.

 "Our team is really close," Bullock told ESPN. "Everybody is always kicking it with each other, even outside the building. We all go to dinner. We stay close even when times are hard. We still got each other back, and we bring each other up."

 Houston's defense allowed the second-fewest points last season (17.4 per game), but it has allowed 24.3 (18th) in the first half of this season. And most inexcusably, the unit has blown four leads in the waning minutes of fourth quarters and also allowed a game-winning score in overtime against the New York Giants .

 Coming off a backbreaking 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns , in which they squandered a 17-0 lead, the Texans are looking to rebound once again -- as they are set to host the Indianapolis Colts (3-7) on "Thursday Night Football" (8:15 p.m. ET, Amazon Prime).

 Despite ESPN's Football Power Index giving Houston a 32.4% chance to make the playoffs -- considering the struggles of the AFC compared to the NFC -- coach DeMeco Ryans isn't "discouraged" by the rough start and Stroud believes his team can find a way. With a win, Houston's playoff chances rise to 37%, but with a loss, they drops to 15%.

 Not playing meaningful football is an unfamiliar place to these Texans -- three straight winning seasons and postseasons that started with Stroud and Ryans' arrival in 2023. 

 "What else are we going to do?" Stroud said. "Cry about it and hold our heads down? Woe is us, woe is this team? I don't believe in that. It sucks, yeah, I'm not the happiest camper.

 "A motivated Texans is a scary team. It's up to us. We don't need anybody else. That's my message to the guys."

 

 A good bye 

 Offensive guard Ed Ingram shot a text to his teammates. He had an idea for a team bonding activity during their bye week: A halloween party.

 It was something he and his wife experienced when he was with the Minnesota Vikings , and they wanted to bring that tradition to Houston. They rented out a local restaurant called "King Steak" and had a clown theme night. The costumes were creative, but a highlight for multiple players was offensive guard Wyatt Teller doing the "South Dallas Swag" dance.

 

 "It was a goofy version," Ingram told ESPN with a laugh. "That was probably one of my favorite moments. When you have camaraderie outside the facility, it shows you that it's more than just a job. We're more than coworkers, we're a brotherhood.

 "If you can build that environment around here, you can go far -- because when you're on the field, you're not just playing for money, you're playing for the person next to you. We are ready to go out there and die for each other."

 Eight players also attended the Ohio State versus USC game during the bye -- with friendly bets on the line. The losers had to wear the opposing school's clothing. That meant Stroud, an OSU alum, had to don the cardinal and gold after the Trojans defeated the Buckeyes 30-18.

 "We put belts on the boys," said Bullock, a USC alum. "[Stroud] was on that side, we was on this side. After every touchdown, we celebrated looking at C.J., talking trash to him. They get a first down, he's talking trash to us.

 "It got to a point of the game where he disappeared though. It's just stuff like that outside the building, and you see how close we are."

 Coming out of the bye week, Houston was able to pick up its third win of the season -- an impressive 44-22 win over the Los Angeles Chargers . That week featured five touchdown passes from Stroud along with eight sacks from the defense and two takeaways. But the biggest highlight of the day was wideout Tank Dell , who scored a 63-yard touchdown in his second game back since a gruesome knee injury in December of 2024 that sidelined him.

 When he crossed the end zone, a sea of Texans waited for Dell to reach the sideline to congratulate him.

 "You could see the energy shift. Everybody is happy to be here," Dell told ESPN. "Happy to see where we are going and the work that we are putting in. Just creating that relationship, man, that helps tremendously on the field."

 

 No excuses 

 The frustrations have been high for the Texans, but not with each other as they've found ways to keep the team chemistry high during the adversity.

 "That's been one of our strongest points," defensive end Will Anderson Jr . said. "We've been together. Nobody has been energy vampires."

 Still, losing is hard, as shown by Lassiter finding himself in a familiar space following Sunday's game.

 He drew a 15-yard unnecessary roughness penalty with 1:18 left in the fourth quarter on second-and-11, giving the Browns a first-and-10 from the Texans' 35-yard line. The third-year corner unintentionally made contact with the helmet of wideout Tylan Wallace while trying to intercept quarterback Deshaun Watson , as both players got their hands on the ball.

 "It's very frustrating because it leaves you with indecision," Lassiter said. "I don't know what I'm supposed to do. I'm trying to go get the ball. If he's touching the ball, I'm trying to get the ball out of his hands. We play a violent sport. I don't know, I'm confused."

 On the next play, Watson completed a 30-yard dart to tight end Harold Fanning, and running back Quinshon Judkins scored one play later giving Houston 47 seconds to respond.

 

 But the drive ended with the same result as Week 1 did. No points.

 Even in the face of adversity, Houston continued to show unwavering loyalty.

 "What else are you supposed to do in that position," Bullock said. "You're supposed to just sit there and let them catch the ball?"

 Ryans echoed those sentiments during his postgame press conference.

 "It's only one way forward, and that's together," Ryans said. "I haven't seen it any other way. Our guys have been very good. Our guys have been together. That's never a message, or it's nothing that I have to talk about."

 Just like how Weeks 1 and 10 felt like déjà vu, the Texans are hoping to recreate their 2025 success -- where they turned a 3-5 record into a 12-5 finish with a postseason berth. But they know it's up to them to turn the tide.

 "We've put ourselves in this position, so we can't be mad at that,"…

title: Texans DE Hunter, RB Marks to miss TNF; Colts rule out CB Ward, starting OTs
summary: The Texans and Colts ruled out several key contributors for their Thursday night matchup.
full_text:
HOUSTON -- Key players for the Houston Texans and the Indianapolis Colts will be out for their AFC South matchup on "Thursday Night Football."
For the Texans, All-Pro defensive end Danielle Hunter is out with a hamstring injury after missing Houston's Week 10 loss to the Cleveland Browns , where they blew a 17-0 lead. That comes on the heels of Pro Bowl linebacker and team leader in tackles Azeez Al-Shaair being placed on injured reserve with a groin injury.
On the offensive side, the Texans will be without running back Woody Marks , who sustained a concussion on a second-down carry in the third quarter against the Browns. Browns defenders Emmanuel McNeil-Warren , Sam Kamara and Quincy Williams collided with Marks, leaving him on the ground for a few minutes.
A potential replacement for Marks is David Montgomery , but he has been out since Week 4 (groin). Montgomery practiced last week, and on Tuesday he said he's "trending in the right direction." He has no injury designation for the game.
Wideout Marvin Harrison Jr . is also out with a hamstring for the second straight game.
On the Colts' side, they will be without Pro Bowl starting cornerback Charvarius Ward , who sustained a knee injury in Sunday's win over the Miami Dolphins and did not practice this week.
Indianapolis also will be missing both starting tackles, a concerning development considering the impact that Houston defensive end Will Anderson Jr . had in the teams' first meeting in September. Left tackle Bernhard Raimann is still being treated for a concussion, and right tackle Jalen Travis will miss his second consecutive game with a knee injury. Tight end Will Mallory will not play because of a hamstring injury.
In the Colts' Week 3 win over Houston, Anderson dominated Indianapolis with 2.5 sacks, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery. He matched a career high with eight pressures in the game.
Cornerback Sauce Gardner , who has been dealing with calf issues off and on since last season, aggravated the injury Sunday and is listed as questionable. Another injury of note is the toe issue that has slowed receiver Anthony Gould . He took over the starting role in the slot after Josh Downs was traded to the Kansas City Chiefs earlier this month. Gould is listed as questionable.

title: Stroud: Texans' home skid and 17-point collapse fuel 'scary' urgency vs Colts
summary: — C.J. Stroud certainly isn’t thrilled with where his Houston Texans are entering Thursday night’s AFC South matchup with Indianapolis.
full_text:
HOUSTON -- — C.J. Stroud certainly isn’t thrilled with where his Houston Texans are entering Thursday night’s AFC South matchup with Indianapolis.
But the quarterback believes that he and the Texans respond well when their backs are against the wall.
“I’m not the happiest camper, but I think the motivated me is one of the best me’s that I’ve seen,” he said. “I think even as (a) team, the motivated Texans is a scary team. It’s up to us. We don’t need anybody else.”
The Texans will try and get back on track after squandering a 17-point lead in a 27-24 loss at Cleveland on Sunday dropped them to 3-6. They’ll meet a Colts team in a similar place at 3-7, but that snapped a five-game skid with a victory over the Dolphins last week.
“I think it’s big to get a win,” Colts coach Shane Steichen said. “It’s been five weeks and obviously we get one and so you get a little bit of momentum. Guys are feeling good ... so, it’s awesome to get that win, but we’ve got another challenge coming up.”
Steichen knows the key to success against the Texans will be to limit Stroud and he raved about his performance this season.
“He’s making a lot of big-time throws,” he said. “The ball’s coming out of his hands. Guys are separating and even when it’s tight coverage, the ball placement, the accuracy has been pinpoint.”
The Colts got a 19-17 win in the first meeting with Houston this season and a victory on Thursday will give them their first season sweep of the Texans since 2021 and leave them in second place in the division behind Jacksonville.
“Anytime you go against a division opponent, it means a little bit more,” Steichen said. “So, we’re excited for that challenge and that opportunity coming up on Thursday.”
Houston’s entire season has been disappointing, but perhaps the most disheartening is the team’s performance at home. The Texans are 0-4 at Reliant Stadium, capped by a 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants on Oct. 25.
After entering the season with Super Bowl aspirations, the Texans are now scrambling to try and hold onto their dwindling hopes of reaching the playoffs.
“It doesn’t feel good. It’s frustrating,” defensive end Will Anderson said. “Obviously, we’re not in a position that we want to be in, but we’re not going to waver. We’re not going to change anything for anybody. We’re going to continue to play our brand of ball.”
Indianapolis (3-7) at Houston (3-6).
When/where to watch: Thursday, 8:15 p.m. EST, Prime Video.
Latest odds: Texans by 12 ½.
Against the spread: Colts 5-5; Texans 3-6.
Last week: Colts beat Dolphins 24-22; Texans lost to Browns 27-24.
Last meeting: Colts beat Texans 19-17 on Sept. 27 in Indianapolis.
Series record: Colts lead 34-15-1.
Houston’s WRs led by Nico Collins vs. Indy’s banged-up secondary.
The Colts could be without starting cornerbacks Sauce Gardner (calf) and Charvarius Ward (knee) on Thursday after both missed practice this week with injuries. If they can’t play, Indy’s backups will have their hands full with a receiving group led by Collins and that features Xavier Hutchinson and got a boost by the recent return of Tank Dell . Collins, who missed the first meeting with the Colts this season, has 626 yards receiving and three touchdowns in seven games against Indy.
Dell also didn’t play in the earlier meeting this season and the Texans didn’t have Marvin Harrison Jr . yet. But Harrison is likely to miss a second straight game with a hamstring injury, so he won’t face the team where his father Marvin Harrison spent his entire Hall of Fame career.
— Indy’s win earlier this season snapped a five-game losing streak in the series. The Colts are 3-2-1 in their past six trips to Houston.
— Stroud ranks third in the NFL with 273.6 yards passing a game this season. He has nine TD passes and one scoring run with just one interception in seven games against the Colts.
— Indianapolis ranks 29th in the league in points allowed (271) and is on pace to give up the third-highest single-season total in franchise history. Opponents scored 533 points against the Colts in 1981 and 486 in 2001.
— Anderson leads the NFL with 10 ½ sacks and his 13 tackles for loss rank second. He had 2 ½ sacks, three tackles for loss, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery in the first meeting with Indy this season.
— Colts rookie RB Seth McGowan had his most productive game of the season last week, carrying 12 times for 77 yards and one touchdown.
— Houston RB David Montgomery is expected to return this week after missing four games with a groin injury. His return comes with Woody Marks out on Thursday after sustaining a concussion against the Browns.
— Kicker Spencer Shrader has already matched the Colts’ single-season franchise record by making nine field goals of 50 yards or longer. With one more, he’ll pass Chase McLaughlin who also made nine in 2022.
— Hutchinson has had a touchdown reception in three straight games. He’s had at least 50 yards receiving in his past two games against the Colts.
AP Sports Writer Michael Marot in Indianapolis contributed to this report.

title: Why can't Richardson beat out struggling Jones as Colts QB1?
summary: Daniel Jones has some of the worst numbers in the NFL, yet Anthony Richardson can't get on the field for the woeful Colts.
full_text:
INDIANAPOLIS --  Indianapolis Colts teammates Anthony Richardson Sr . and Grover Stewart have a playful rivalry that can be seen playing out during practice most days.

 Stewart, the 6-foot-4, 314-pound veteran nose tackle who anchors the middle of the defense, warns backup quarterback Richardson that today is the day he'll chase him down when he leaves the pocket.

 "Look," Stewart said, "he can move. But I always tell him, 'I'm gonna catch you.'"

 Stewart rarely does.

 "Hey, he's a hard guy to catch," Stewart said. "He's fast. That's a threat right there. Big arm, big legs."

 But lately, those practice reps running the scout-team offense are the closest Richardson has come to playing meaningful snaps. That remains true despite starting quarterback Daniel Jones ranking as the NFL's worst starter in numerous major categories, including QBR (30.3) and yards per attempt (5.6). He also leads the NFL in interceptions (12).

 Nevertheless, Jones remains the starter heading into Thursday's AFC South matchup against the  Houston Texans (8:15 ET, Prime Video). And Colts coach Shane Steichen continues to defend his handpicked starter who enjoyed the best stretch of his career under Steichen in the first half of the 2025 season.

 But most of what Jones has displayed in 2026 suggests that last season -- he at one point was the most efficient passer in the NFL -- was the exception, not the rule. Jones posted a 1.7 QBR in Sunday's win over the Miami Dolphins , the worst of any quarterback who has started a game in 2026. He's averaged 135 passing yards in his past four games and hasn't thrown for 200 yards in any game in the last month. It is arguably the worst Jones has played in his career, including his six tumultuous seasons with the New York Giants .

 But Steichen remains steadfast.

 

 "I think I take everything into account," he said when asked how he determines whether a quarterback change is warranted. "I always go back and look at the film and make sure on this play, was it his fault? Was it someone else's fault? I think there's a lot that goes into it.

 "Obviously, the biggest thing is taking care of the football moving forward."

 Jones hasn't done the latter, with a 7-to-12 touchdown-to-interception ratio and 13 fumbles over his 23 games as the Colts' starter. To be fair, the Colts are outmanned on offense, especially after trading receivers Josh Downs and Keenan Allen last week and All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson late last month.

 But there's no spinning Jones' performance, which was problematic even before the Colts' recent flurry of trades. The Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard  on Oct. 19, lost five of their past six games and are four games behind division-leading Jacksonville in the win column. If now isn't the time to try someone else at quarterback, when will it be?

 "It's not all about one guy," Steichen said this week. "I think it takes all 11 to do their job at a high level."

 It's a level of grace the Colts rarely afforded to Richardson.

 The No. 4 overall pick in the 2023 draft, Richardson's arrival in Indianapolis coincided with Steichen's. Together, the team envisioned Steichen doing for Richardson what he'd done for other young quarterbacks such as  Justin Herbert and Jalen Hurts while an offensive coordinator for the Chargers and Eagles, respectively.

 Steichen, along with Ballard and late owner Jim Irsay, were aligned on the selection of Richardson, who had just 13 college starts at Florida. He was one of the least-experienced quarterbacks ever to be drafted in the first round, but the Colts were undaunted.

 Richardson entered his first training camp in competition with veteran  Gardner Minshew II . Richardson started the team's preseason opener that summer against the Buffalo Bills and played about a quarter. Two days later, Steichen opened his post-practice media briefing with an announcement: He'd seen enough. Richardson would be the team's Week 1 starter.

 Steichen, it seemed, was all-in.

 

 Now, four seasons later, Richardson, who is in the last year of his contract, can't get on the field even when the team's starter is throwing perplexing interceptions and his coach's job is in serious jeopardy .

 Looking back, Steichen's belief in Richardson was short-lived. Steichen benched Richardson midway through the 2024 season following a loss at Houston that included the infamous "tap out," with Richardson leaving the game for a play after taking a knee on the field. He later said he was exhausted after the previous play.

 Steichen insisted then that backup Joe Flacco gave the Colts the best chance to win -- until that proved not to be true. Three weeks later, Steichen reinserted Richardson into the lineup. He went on to have some promising moments, authoring game-winning drives against the New York Jets and New England Patriots down the stretch.

 But Richardson's inconsistency -- he's a 50.9% career passer -- and his many injuries seemed to break Steichen's belief. It was clear to many in the organization that the coach had turned the page on the young quarterback. The Colts signed Jones the following spring and the rest is history. He has since signed a two-year, $88 million contract extension that might be a variable in Steichen's commitment to Jones.

 Richardson's performance was more than enough to prompt the Colts to look elsewhere. He was one of the lowest-rated quarterbacks in the league in his lone season as a full-time starter. But the same is now true of Jones, yet Steichen is staying the course.

 Steichen recently acknowledged that Richardson's electric running ability could possibly give the Colts a spark. Richardson has 10 rushing touchdowns in 15 career starts.

 "That's a real thing," Steichen said. "... We'll look at everything."

 The Colts have at least considered it. Richardson, according to multiple sources, currently has a package of plays in the playbook. But the Colts have yet to dust it off. If his exploits against Colts defenders in practice are any indication, perhaps they should.

 "He's so explosive," defensive end Jaylahn Tuimoloau said. "I don't think I've ever played against a quarterback that explosive. He gives us great looks on the scout team whenever we go against him."

 Richardson showed improvement during the preseason after coming back from a career-threatening eye injury that kept him out for much of last season. Still, it's difficult to imagine a future for him in Indianapolis. Recognizing his status with the franchise, Richardson requested a trade earlier this year. Ultimately, nothing materialized, according to team sources. But that the idea was even broached spoke volumes about Richardson's view of the situation. Now, Ballard, Richardson's biggest ally at Colts headquarters, has been ousted.

 Richardson was recently cited for marijuana possession in Carmel, Indiana, and faces a possible four-game suspension for violating the personal conduct policy, but there's no indication that is playing a role in lineup decisions.

 "I've just got to keep doing what I've been doing, coming in the building, showing up to work," Richardson said recently. "Just preparing like I was going to be the starter regardless of what decision [Steichen] makes. I've just got to make sure I'm prepared when my number's called."

 At this point, it's not clear whether that will ever happen.

title: Jaguars rule starting center Robert Hainsey (knee) out for Giants game

full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Jaguars starting center Robert Hainsey will miss Sunday's game against the New York Giants because of a knee injury, coach Liam Coen said Wednesday.
Second-year player Jonah Monheim , a seventh-round draft pick out of Southern California in 2025, will start.
Hainsey was hurt in the second half of last Sunday's 40-23 victory at the Tennessee Titans . Sources told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler that Hainsey has a knee sprain and is considered week-to-week.
Hainsey has started all nine games this season and started 15 of 17 games last season.
He signed with the Jaguars as a free agent in 2025 on a three-year, $21 million contract after spending four seasons with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .

title: Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce's top moments at Arrowhead Stadium
summary: Kelce's greatest Arrowhead moments include his first catch, lots of playoff magic, and meeting the love of his life, Taylor Swift.
full_text:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- Travis Kelce gets goosebumps every time, even though the drive from his home to his place of employment, at this point in his 14-year career, is routine.

 On game days, his car enters Gate 5, the road that leads to the entrance of the Kansas City Chiefs ' training facility. The destination of his journey always makes Kelce smile.

 "You come through the facility, and you just see Arrowhead [Stadium] pop up out of nowhere," Kelce said recently. "That's the best feeling for me."

 Few players in the Chiefs' 67-year history have entered Arrowhead to put on the team's red jersey, helmet and cleats as many times as Kelce. On Sunday, against the Arizona Cardinals (1 p.m. ET, CBS), Kelce will become only the fourth player in franchise history -- joining Hall of Fame right guard Will Shields, kicker Nick Lowery and punter Dustin Colquitt -- to play 100 regular-season games at Arrowhead, a venue that opened in 1972. Kelce considers Arrowhead a revered place, even before the venue was the site where his relationship with Taylor Swift, his wife, became public.

 Whenever Kelce's illustrious career ends -- which could happen after this season -- he will be remembered for being one of the franchise's greatest players and at minimum a three-time Super Bowl champion. He is also proud that his play, and most of his memorable highlights, will be synonymous with the history of Arrowhead, which is expected to have its final season in 2030.

 "The fans love to fill that stadium and create those memories and get away from the realities of what the world is," Kelce said. "I just love the fact that they pour so much into it. It just makes you want to play that much harder for them. That definitely makes Arrowhead special."

 Chiefs founder Lamar Hunt always said Arrowhead was his favorite place on earth. Kelce, 37, understands why Hunt, who died in 2006, had such a fond sentiment. Hours before kickoff, the expansive parking lots that surround the stadium host thousands of tailgating fans, many of them cooking the city's favorite cuisine: barbecue.

 When driving into the stadium, Kelce often rolls down his windows to enjoy the tantalizing smell of the many cookouts, and the brief moments he can interact with fans.

 "I like to just feel that feeling of being around the tailgate and the atmosphere," Kelce said. "It's just a part of the ballpark experience. I'm a fan of this game at heart, so getting that feeling of the moment building [before kickoff]. That's all a part of it for me."

 Kelce's career has coincided with the Chiefs' most successful period at Arrowhead. His Chiefs teams have won 76.5% of their games in the stadium, including 16 victories in the postseason. Fans inside the venue have also been privileged to see each stage of Kelce's transformation as a player, from a talented-but-sometimes-immature phenom to a certain future Hall of Famer.

 "Arrowhead's real magic is when you get inside," Kelce said. "It's something I know I'll cherish forever, those moments coming out of the tunnel or just making a big play for [fans] late in the game."

 

 

 Sept. 7, 2014: Kelce's first catch and the birth of a star 
 In the Chiefs' 2014 season opener against the Tennessee Titans , Alex Smith, Kansas City's quarterback at the time, hit Kelce on a corner route for a 27-yard gain. After the play, Kelce jumped up and showcased, for the first time, what would become one of his signature celebrations: mimicking firing an arrow from a bow, followed by a tomahawk chop.

 "He's a unique personality," Smith told "The Rich Eisen Show" of his first season playing with Kelce. Smith then added: "Travis is a knucklehead, just always smiling, always happy. I had never really seen a tight end who was just so smooth and fluid and he's a jokester and just talented in a lot of ways."

 Kelce signed a one-year, $12 million deal with the Chiefs in late March. As part of the team's celebration, a staff member handed Kelce a photo of himself during his second season in 2014. In the photo, he was wearing the Chiefs' red jersey and certain jewelry.

 "Aw man, this thing takes me back right here," Kelce said, looking at the picture. "That's back when they called me 'Hoopsie' because I had the hoops [earrings] and I used to mess up plays all the time.

 "Yeah, [I've] come a long way."

 

 Over two seasons together, Kelce and tight end Anthony Fasano built a relationship that proved to be instrumental in Kelce's development. As a mentor, Fasano, who played in the NFL for 12 seasons, taught Kelce about proper nutrition and how to recover each week from the physical demands of the position.

 "His professionalism was second-to-none, in terms of the scheme and understanding defenses, starting from the defensive coordinators to the position players and he understood how to really watch film," Kelce said of Fasano. "I took a lot from him on just how to be a professional."

 Kelce's first breakout performance occurred in Week 4 of the 2014 season, a primetime game at Arrowhead in which the Chiefs dominated the New England Patriots . Kelce, who finished with 93 receiving yards and a touchdown, outperformed Rob Gronkowski, who at the time was considered the league's best tight end. That night, Chiefs fans broke a mark recognized by the Guinness World Records for the loudest stadium. The fans roared to generate 142.2 decibels, a record that still stands.

 "The fans bring it every single game," Kelce said. "You can feel the kids and the generations of happiness and love that they have coming together and cheering for their team. It's a beautiful thing, man."

 The next season, Fasano was gone and Kelce became the No. 1 tight end for good.

 "You knew we had a tremendous talent," offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy said of Kelce. "But you never know how people's careers are going to shape themselves. Kelce had an opportunity to learn from Fasano, but you always knew that if he can just take the bull by the horns, and take the coaching, that he would have a tremendous career.

 "Did we think it would go this far? You probably didn't."

 

 

 Dec. 25, 2016: Kelce's routes change course 
 By 2016, Kelce had fully established himself in the league. He was a flamboyant celebrator in the end zone whenever he scored a touchdown and he was a pass catcher who, at 6-foot-5 and 250 pounds, was dynamic in the open field.

 Even though Kelce wasn't always a disciplined player -- he committed unsportsmanlike conduct penalties, criticized officials and was even ejected during that season for throwing a towel at an official -- he was also working on his route-running craft, an ability that would later become a secret weapon. Since he was in the fourth year of the Chiefs' playbook under coach Andy Reid, Kelce, who understood the entire passing concept of plays, began ad-libbing his routes in practice.

 "This guy just never ran the route on the paper," Smith said, smiling. "If the line on the paper was this corner [route] at 10 yards, Travis always put his own flare and stamp on things. At first, I had just never seen a tight end do that. Then all of a sudden, you realize it was this amazing superpower."

 Kelce and Smith both remember the exact moment the tight end used his rare skill for the first time in a game: The 2016 Christmas Day game at Arrowhead.

 Playing the Denver Broncos , the Chiefs faced a third-and-4 near midfield late in the third quarter. On the play, Kelce was supposed to run a whip route -- one that has deceptive breaks and double moves -- against rookie safety Will Parks.

 "[Parks] just sits hard on the outside, like he's not taking the cheese," Smith said last year in an episode of the "New Heights" podcast. "Well, Travis just kind of feels it, so he just keeps f---ing running, just runs all the way across the field -- and I threw him the ball for some reason."

 Kelce said he knew there wasn't another teammate running a route on the left side of the play, which helped him to…

title: 2027 NFL draft: Dolphins, Titans, Eagles, Jets, Chargers in race for No. 1 pick
summary: Five NFL teams have at least 5% odds to land the No. 1 pick in 2027, per ESPN's Football Power Index: the Dolphins, Titans, Eagles, Jets and Chargers.
full_text:
The race for the No. 1 pick in the  2027 NFL draft  is taking shape now that we're 10 weeks into the 2026 season .

 Five teams have at least a 5% chance at landing the top pick, according to ESPN's Football Power Index  projections. So we called on our experts and reporters to size up each of those bottom-tier franchises at midseason.

 NFL analyst Seth Walder used the FPI to make sense of each of the five teams' schedules the rest of the way. Our NFL Nation reporters looked at the biggest positional needs that could be addressed in the first round in April. And NFL draft analyst Jordan Reid spun it forward and suggested one prospect each front office could consider if it landed that top selection.

 Let's start with the Dolphins, who currently have the best odds at the No. 1 pick.

 

 
 Jump to a team: 
 LAC | MIA |  NYJ 
 PHI | TEN 

 
 

 

 Miami Dolphins  (1-8) 
 FPI chance to earn No. 1 pick:  41.2% 
 FPI chance to earn top-five pick:  93%

 What lies ahead in the schedule? Are they favored in any remaining games? 

 Not only are the Dolphins not favored by the FPI in a single remaining game this season, but the model also makes them at least a field-goal underdog in every game. Their best chances to win are  versus the Jets in Week 12 , versus the Chargers in Week 16  and  at the Patriots in Week 18 . But because the FPI believes the Dolphins are the worst team in the NFL, they are not likely to win any of those contests.   -- Walder 

 

 What is their biggest first-round need right now? 

 The Dolphins have needs across the board, but if we're narrowing down positions that make sense at their projected draft slot, it's edge rusher, quarterback and wide receiver. Chop Robinson has been excellent this season and could use a pass-rush partner to mix in with Josh Uche . However, pairing wide receiver Caleb Douglas in his second year with another receiver or a rookie quarterback is also tempting. -- Marcel Louis-Jacques 

 

 Who is the best prospect fit right now for them at No. 1? 

 Drew Mestemaker , QB, Oklahoma State. Free agent signee Malik Willis hasn't shown any signs of being the long-term answer moving forward, and Miami could use him as a bridge option. Mestemaker is a young and intriguing passer who won't be ready to start from Day 1; 2026 is only his second season as a starter in high school and college combined. Miami already has a productive foundation of youth, but Mestemaker could provide it the QB necessary to continue its rebuild.  -- Reid 

 
 

 Tennessee Titans  (1-8) 
 FPI chance to earn No. 1 pick:  36.9% 
 FPI chance to earn top-five pick:  92.4%

 What lies ahead in the schedule? Are they favored in any remaining games? 

 There are definitely some winnable games available for the Titans: Week 13 versus the Commanders , Week 15 versus the Colts  and Week 16 at the Raiders . The FPI favors the Titans only  against the Raiders in Week 16 (the model has fairly low confidence in rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza until proven otherwise), but there is a strong chance Tennessee wins at least one of those three games. Still, Tennessee has the second-best chance to earn the No. 1 pick. -- Walder 

 What is their biggest first-round need right now? 

 Pass rusher. Sure, Jacob Martin has gotten off to a great start with a career-high 7.5 sacks so far, but there's no guarantee he'll repeat that success next year, and his deal expires after 2027. Getting a running mate opposite Martin would improve the whole defense and give Tennessee an edge rusher to build its defense around in the future. A game-changing pass rusher would also allow coach Robert Saleh to rush with four and drop seven into coverage, which would help a struggling pass defense.  -- Turron Davenport 

 

 

 Who is the best prospect fit right now for them at No. 1? 

 Jeremiah Smith , WR, Ohio State. Even though the Titans have a huge need at edge -- where South Carolina's  Dylan Stewart  and Texas'  Colin Simmons  are  my top prospects  -- it shouldn't be at the expense of taking Smith, the best player in this class. Smith and Titans WR  Carnell Tate are very familiar with each other, combining for 2,118 receiving yards and 21 touchdowns at Ohio State in 2025. Quarterback  Cam Ward , who still hasn't solidified whether he's the long-term solution under center, has a risk-taking nature that would pair well with Smith's ability to be a three-level threat.  -- Reid 

 
 

 Philadelphia Eagles  (2-7) 
 FPI chance to earn No. 1 pick:  7.9% 
 FPI chance to earn top-five pick:  68.7%

 What lies ahead in the schedule? Are they favored in any remaining games? 

 Two games stand out as possible victories: Week 13 at the Cardinals and Week 14 versus the Colts . The FPI considers the Eagles as slight underdogs in both of them. I'll throw out one other game to keep an eye on:  Week 18 at the Giants . That's because the FPI is pretty bearish on New York, so it thinks the Eagles have a chance, and the Giants could sit their starters if they have the NFC East wrapped up at that point. -- Walder 

 What is their biggest first-round need right now? 

 Offensive tackle. The retirement of future Hall of Fame right tackle Lane Johnson created a major need along the offensive front. Rookie Markel Bell , the team's 2026 third-round pick, had a strong summer and took over when Johnson stepped away in early October, but Bell has yet to solidify himself as the right tackle of the future. The Eagles' long run of success is tied directly to their strength along the fronts. They need to invest early and often in the O-line. -- Tim McManus 

 Who is the best prospect fit right now for them at No. 1?  Jeremiah Smith. Right now, there isn't an offensive tackle worthy of a top-five pick. LSU's Jordan Seaton tops my position rankings right now at No. 11. That puts the Eagles in position to take the best player available, which is Smith in this scenario. He would add another outstanding option to an offense that includes RB  Saquon Barkley , WR  DeVonta Smith  and 2026 first-round pick  Makai Lemon . At 6-foot-4 and 220 pounds, Smith can glide past defenders or outmuscle them at the catch point.  -- Reid 

 

 

 
 

 New York Jets  (2-8) 
 FPI chance to earn No. 1 pick:  5.9% 
 FPI chance to earn top-five pick:  63.1%

 What lies ahead in the schedule? Are they favored in any remaining games? 

 The FPI favors the Jets to beat the Dolphins -- a high-leverage game for AFC East draft capital -- in Week 12 . But the Jets could also win next week at the Chargers , in  Week 15 at the Cardinals  and in  Week 16 against the Patriots (the FPI is assuming Tommy DeVito as the most likely quarterback in that game). Plus, if the Bills have the AFC's No. 1 seed locked up by Week 18 , it's possible the Jets' season finale in Buffalo could sneakily become a feasible win, too. -- Walder 

 What is their biggest first-round need right now? 

 Priority No. 1 is a franchise quarterback. This is their moment. This is why they traded defensive stars Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams in 2025. The objective was to accumulate draft capital for 2027, and now they have the means (three first-round picks) to wheel and deal. After four years of Aaron Rodgers , Justin Fields and Geno Smith -- all stopgaps, to varying degrees -- the Jets want to build around a young quarterback who can grow with the talent already in place. -- Rich Cimini 

 

 Who is the best prospect fit right now for them at No. 1? 

 Drew Mestemaker. At 6-foot-4 and 220 pounds, he is a strong-armed passer with plenty of mobility. Mestemaker still needs to become more consistent with his decision-making, but his tools and potential are an ideal fit for the Jets given the offensive personnel they already have in place.  -- Reid 

 
 

 Los Angeles Chargers  (1-8) 
 FPI chance to earn No. 1 pick:  5.5%

title: A Rams bye means time for rest and ramping up
summary: The bye "represents an opportunity to get recharged," but it also allows the team to improve.
full_text:
LOS ANGELES -- As Matthew Stafford relaxes and recovers during his bye week, the Los Angeles Rams quarterback has learned to expect a few texts from his head coach.

 Stafford and Sean McVay are headed into their sixth bye week together, and the quarterback knows how his head coach likes to use the time.

 "We'll definitely be texting with each other [and] talking to each other about how we move forward and how we try to help this team become the best version of itself," Stafford said.

 While the bye "represents an opportunity to get recharged [and] refreshed," McVay said Sunday after the Rams' victory over the Arizona Cardinals  that it also allows him to think about how he can continue to tweak and improve his offense.

 "What are the new iterations that you want to try to be able to build on or creatively come up with new ideas based on who's available and who's not," McVay said. "And so I know that'll be helpful for me for sure. It's an accelerated bye, but I am excited about what this group has done."

 McVay showed what might have been only a glimpse of that creativity in Week 10, when he had to game plan without wide receiver Puka Nacua  ( knee/toe ). The Rams were also without veteran receiver Davante Adams  ( hamstring ) and tight end Terrance Ferguson  ( hamstring/ankle ).

 

 Without their top two receivers, the Rams ran only three plays out of 11 personnel (three receivers on the field). Entering the game, they had run 53% of their plays this season out of that offensive grouping.

 While the Rams still leaned in to 13 personnel (three tight ends on the field) against the Cardinals, they also ran plays out of two personnel groupings they had not all season. The Rams ran 17 plays out of 20 personnel (two running backs). According to NFL Next Gen Stats, the Rams totaled 197 yards and a touchdown on those plays. They also ran a play out of 21 personnel (two running backs, one tight end).

 Since Adams injured a hamstring in Week 6, the Rams have leaned on their running game, led by the tandem of Blake Corum and Kyren Williams . During the four games without Adams, the Rams have outrushed their opponents 653-175 (478). According to ESPN Research, that is the team's largest rushing yards differential over a four-game span since 1984, the season Eric Dickerson ran for 2,105 yards.

 Without Adams and Nacua on Sunday, the Rams rushed for 202 yards, including 100 rushing yards and a touchdown for Corum. It was Corum's sixth straight game with a touchdown, and it came on a day the running back had a career-high 20 touches. For much of the season, Corum and Williams have split carries and both had success.

 After the game, Corum said he thought being in the backfield at the same time as Williams "was amazing."

 "It felt great," Corum said. "I was super excited. We share a backfield, but actually to be on the field together, I wish I was in the Cardinals' minds to see what they thought."

 McVay now has 10 days between games -- including a five-day bye week before players are back in the building -- to get ready for perhaps his team's biggest game of the season. The Rams host the Green Bay Packers in Week 12 ( 8 p.m. ET, Netflix ) the night before Thanksgiving.

 Both teams -- and the Seattle Seahawks -- are 6-4 going into a Week 11 bye. Given how close the race is for the three NFC wild-card spots, the head-to-head matchup against the Packers might be a key tiebreaker at the end of the season.

 The Rams have a 47.1% chance to make the playoffs, according to ESPN's FPI. The Packers' chances dropped to 33.3% after their loss to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 10. 

 McVay said Sunday that while the Rams dealt with adversity early in the season, it's something they're used to. The Rams have the hardest second-half schedule in the NFL, according to ESPN Analytics.

 In the previous three seasons, the Rams have gone a combined 23-7 after their bye, including 7-1 in 2023 after a 3-6 start and 9-3 in 2024 after a 1-4 start.

 "I think it's calloused us the right way," McVay said. "We've got a great challenge, and all I'm really worried about is the next game and that's going to continue to serve us well, but we got great challenges ahead. I don't know if I'd use the word relief, but it'd be good to be able to just take a step back and then attack it full speed ahead when we get back at it."

title: Three-win Saints, Kellen Moore face defining stretch of games
summary: Starting with the Bears on Sunday, the head coach's tenure and the team's season sits at a crucial crossroads.
full_text:
NEW ORLEANS -- The Saints (3-6) have a hill to climb if they want to get back to the top of the NFC South. At this point in the season, it almost feels insurmountable.

 The Saints had an opportunity to secure first place in a shaky division Sunday against the Carolina Panthers , however, they repeated many of their old mistakes, losing 20-17 after allowing two late scores.

 "Obviously we had plenty of opportunities in this game. We didn't get it done," a terse Saints coach Kellen Moore said postgame, mentioning the need to "get better" four times.

 But despite Moore repeating that phrase not just on Sunday but many times over the course of this rocky season, the Saints have failed to get better in key areas. Against the Panthers, New Orleans fell short in those areas again.

 

 They didn't score points in the first quarter for the seventh time this season, an issue Saints rookie Jordyn Tyson noted Moore has "harped on," without results. They had less than 100 net rushing yards for the sixth time and had at least two turnovers for the fifth time this season.

 The Saints now have an 0-2 record in the division and the feeling that they beat themselves yet again. Tight end Juwan Johnson said the Saints still believe things can be turned around, especially in a division in which no team has a winning record.

 "What we could all do is to learn from it, watch the film, move forward," Johnson said of Sunday's loss. "I know it sounds like a PR answer, but that's literally what we have to do in order to move forward because we say it every year, we're only a game back."

 While the Saints are only a few games out of contention now, that could easily slip away in the next few weeks. Not only do they have to account for those repeated mistakes that lost them games, but they have to fix them against some of the toughest opponents left on the schedule.

 "We definitely knew [what] was at stake," Saints running back  Travis Etienne Jr  said. "So it wasn't like we was unaware and it definitely hurt that we didn't capitalize on that moment. Win that game, we would've had control of our own destiny. So I feel like now we're putting our faith in someone else's hands."

 The next three games will be the most challenging stretch they've seen so far. The Saints will play at Chicago (7-2) on Sunday ( 1 p.m. ET, Fox ) against Dennis Allen's seventh-ranked Bears defense and at Cincinnati (7-2) against the Bengals' top-ranked passing offense and top-scoring offense. Then, in Week 13, the Saints will host the Green Bay Packers  (6-4), who have the second-ranked passing offense and a fourth-ranked scoring offense.

 If the Saints lose all three of those games, they'll have a 3-9 record and a losing season for the second straight year under Moore. It would drop the head coach's overall record to 9-20 and a win percentage of 31%, way behind former Saints coach Mike Ditka (1997-99), who was fired after a 3-13 season in 1999 and a 15-33 coaching record in New Orleans.

 Losing the next three would squarely put the team at a crossroads ahead of 2027: Continue with a third season under Moore or wipe the slate clean and look for their third long-term head coach since Sean Payton walked away after the 2021 season.

 

 The Saints haven't gotten the results they expected out of Moore. After stints as the offensive coordinator for the Dallas Cowboys (2019-22) and Los Angeles Chargers (2023), Moore was hired by the Saints after one season as the OC for the Philadelphia Eagles. The Eagles had a second-ranked rushing offense and top-10 overall offense en route to a Super Bowl win.

 That offensive prowess hasn't translated to New Orleans yet. The Saints have trailed in all 26 of Moore's games, and they rank last in first-quarter points scored dating to last season. Their run game ranked 28th last season (94.3 rushing yards per game) compared to 27th this season (90.1 rushing yards per game).

 The organization has sent out conflicting messages about how they feel about the current state of the Saints. Owner Gayle Benson read a statement to the New Orleans Quarterback Club following a 1-4 start and a humiliating primetime loss to the Atlanta Falcons that called out both Moore and Saints general manager Mickey Loomis by name, saying the losing record was "not acceptable."

 Benson sent out a public letter to fans two weeks later after the Saints rushed for 18 yards in a Week 7 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris that appeared to soften her previous words.

 "While the outcome on the field was not what we had hoped for, we have much to be proud of from our time together," she wrote . "We represented the New Orleans Saints, our beloved city and the entire state of Louisiana with class and pride on an international stage."

 During the Saints Week 8 bye, Benson told WDSU-TV at a charity event that she understood the "players were working as hard as they can. You know, at the end of the season, we'll kind of look at things and see what we need to change, but for right now, I think they're going to be OK. They're going to try the best they can and that's really all they can do."

 Loomis preached patience with the team during a news conference prior to the game in Paris, explaining they were excited about Tyler Shough , but said there's still a lot of development with both the second-year quarterback and the team.

 

 Loomis said Shough was "23 games into his career with a rebuilding team" -- using the term that he was so reluctant to use as recently as last summer. Loomis has said before that "rebuild" means different things to different people because of how fast things can turn around in the course of a season.

 "I think we're always in the mode of we're trying to win every game," Loomis said a few months after quarterback Derek Carr's sudden retirement in May 2025. "I don't look at it as a rebuild even though we might say we got a lot of positions of development, I should say. We've got a lot of young players that we want to develop and I'm excited about that but at the same time, look, there's always an opportunity for things to fall in place and be successful."

 Whether the Saints truly think the roster needs to be rebuilt would likely influence the length of time Moore is given to turn things around. So far, aside from a few scattered wins, the Saints haven't shown any consistent trend toward that goal in the past two seasons.

 Tyson was asked after the Panthers game if the players had confidence in Moore to put the offense in a position to be successful.

 "Yeah, I know for 100% certainty Kellen watches, like, a lot of tape," Tyson said. "He watches through every game, last year's games, the year before that, he watches a lot of tape, and I can promise you that he's giving ... his best shot."

 Is Moore the right person to coach going forward? The next three games will likely tell the tale. By the end of that stretch, the Saints will either be 6-6 and still in contention for the playoffs, or they'll be mulling over their next big steps for the future.

 That starts with the Bears (and Allen, the former Saints coach), in a few days.

 "Ultimately we all want the same thing. We all have the same goals and aspirations, want to win football games and put ourselves in position to have success," Moore said. "Now we really have to focus on eyes forward, getting better every day."

title: Giants RB Cam Skattebo to nix backflips in wake of Aidan Hutchinson's injury
summary: Giants RB Cam Skattebo said he is holding off on doing any more backflips after Lions DE Aidan Hutchinson suffered a major knee injury while leaping and celebrating a sack.
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo is retiring his trademark celebratory backflip for the time being.
This comes on the heels of Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson suffering a season-ending knee injury while leaping and celebrating a sack Sunday. Hutchinson was placed on injured reserve.
"It's hard to see," Skattebo told reporters Wednesday. "I'm saying, yeah, [no backflips]. Mentally, I'm like, 'I'm not doing that.'
"That s--- ain't going to happen to me."
Skattebo, the Giants starting running back, is coming off a serious ankle injury last year. But he returned for the start of the season and backflipped after scoring in New York's season-opening win over the Dallas Cowboys . He backflipped as recently as Thursday night in a loss to the Washington Commanders .
Skattebo isn't saying he won't backflip again. The likelihood is he will. He has done it his whole life. But he mentioned after the opener that he might put the celebration on the backburner, before it reemerged in Week 10.
Skattebo conceded Wednesday the backflip might resurface "if we go to the playoffs or something."
The backflip was a point of contention throughout the offseason, even before Hutchinson had his mishap. Skattebo did his flip for the first time since the injury after hitting a home run at the Brian Burns Celebrity Softball Game in late May.
Skattebo then stumbled while doing a backflip at Fanatics Fest over the summer, creating a stir.
Giants brass had a conversation with Skattebo afterward. They preferred he didn't do it leading into the season, especially coming off a major injury. They didn't mandate he never do it again.
"The big-picture message is you want to take care of yourself, take care of your team. Do everything you can do to be healthy, be back, be right, be good," Giants coach John Harbaugh said at the start of training camp. "What does that mean? It's not going to be the same situation the next time for anybody. It's going to be different. So, it's really the principle of it."
Skattebo, 24, leads the Giants with 496 yards rushing and four touchdowns on 116 carries so far this season.
Hutchinson, 26, isn't the first player to be injured while celebrating. Former Arizona Cardinals kicker Bill Gramatica tore his ACL while celebrating a made kick against the Giants in 2001. But the current Hutchinson situation has prompted some debate about whether coaches should talk to players about celebrations, potentially banning anything that could be deemed dangerous.
"No, I don't believe that," Lions coach Dan Campbell said. "I think what happened speaks for itself. We're not talking to 8-year-olds here."

title: Jets QB Geno Smith (ankle) intends to play vs. Chargers: 'That's the plan'
summary: Jets quarterback Geno Smith says he intends to play Sunday against the Chargers despite still walking with a noticeable limp due to an ankle injury.
full_text:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- Quarterback Geno Smith still was walking with a noticeable limp Wednesday, three days after injuring his left ankle, but he intends to play Sunday when the New York Jets try to snap their five-game losing streak.
"That's the plan," Smith said. "Obviously, you've got to take it day by day, but that's the plan."
Smith was listed as a limited participant in practice -- not a regular practice, but an extensive walk-through, as the Jets like to call it. Barring a setback, he expects to face the Los Angeles Chargers (1-8) at SoFi Stadium.
Embattled coach Aaron Glenn said he will let the week play out before announcing his plans. His options are a gimpy Smith or rookie Cade Klubnik , who replaced Smith in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills and was uneven in his NFL debut.
Glenn has made it clear that, even though the Jets are out of playoff contention with a 2-8 mark, he's not interested in turning the season over to the unproven Klubnik for evaluation purposes. Glenn, fighting for his job with a 5-22 record, said it would be "disrespectful" to bench Smith.
Smith has played reasonably well -- he's 19th in Total QBR (53.3) -- but the offense has gone nine straight quarters without a touchdown.
On Sunday, Smith was sidelined in the third quarter and never returned to the game. He went for a postgame X-ray and an MRI exam Monday, which showed no significant damage, a source said.
Smith wouldn't disclose the nature of the ankle injury, except to say it's "a little bit better [than Sunday]. I'm working through it." He took a few big hits in the game, acknowledging other aches and pains.
"Yeah, just working through some things, but just normal football stuff," he said.
When the starter is less than 100%, the distribution of practice reps can become an issue, especially if the backup is a rookie. Klubnik, who played only five series Sunday, had no practice reps with the starters before this week.
Glenn downplayed the matter, saying Klubnik will get a "fair amount of reps" in practice due to competition periods. In the game, the former Clemson star, a fourth-round pick, showed his inexperience. He led one field goal drive but also took three sacks and threw an interception. He completed 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards.
The sense in the locker room is that Smith will play.
"From what I know, Geno feels good to go," wide receiver Garrett Wilson said. "You would have to ask him. ... [but] from what I know, he's good to go. So, I'll say that."

title: Eagles' Sirianni sticking with Milton as QB1, Mannion as offensive playcaller
summary: QB Joe Milton will start again for the Eagles on Sunday and Sean Mannion will remain as the offensive playcaller against the Steelers, coach Nick Sirianni said.
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA -- Eagles quarterback Joe Milton will remain the starter and offensive coordinator Sean Mannion will retain playcalling duties as the team comes off the bye looking for an offensive turnaround, coach Nick Sirianni said Wednesday.
The Eagles signed Milton off the Dallas Cowboys ' practice squad in mid-October and thrust him into the starting lineup three weeks later against the New York Giants in place of Tanner McKee . Milton went 18-of-34 for 169 yards with no touchdowns, no interceptions and seven sacks, including one where he lost a fumble. He also ran for 64 yards on nine carries.
"He works extremely hard with everything, really love his approach, like his personality," Sirianni said. "He's a really hard worker, and I really value that."
Mannion, 34, oversaw an offense that led the league in three-and-out percentage (35.7%) and was bottom five in passing (171.7 YPG), rushing (88.6 YPG) and points per game (16.4) through nine games.
Some bumps were expected for Mannion, a first-time offensive coordinator who entered the season with just two years of coaching experience. The job of implementing a new scheme got tougher with the retirement of right tackle Lane Johnson , losing quarterback Jalen Hurts for the season, trade of center Cam Jurgens and multigame absence of wide receiver DeVonta Smith over the first half of the season.
Sirianni said he made no staff changes during the bye week outside of hiring former assistant offensive line coach and run game specialist T.J. Paganetti in a consulting role.
The Eagles (2-7), losers of seven straight games, will host the Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3) on Sunday.
"I think we have a good plan of action moving forward of things we want to do to move forward and to get better. Obviously we haven't been good enough on offense but I like our plan of attack and our process we went through last week," Sirianni said.
"I think [Sean] is very smart. I think he has a great football mind. He thinks through everything."
